Title: Speech at the Launch of the New Family of Metical Notes and Coins
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENCY THE GOVERNOR FROM THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, ADRIANO MALEIANE, On THE OCCASION OF THE RELEASE OF THE NOTES AND COINS OF THE NEW METICAL FAMILY MAPUTO, June 16 , 2006 Dear Guests , Ladies, Gentlemen , I would like on behalf of myself and on behalf of the members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique to thank you for your presence in this act of launching the notes and coins of the Metical of the new family, on the date that our coin completes 26 years of existence. This event constitutes the culmination of the process that began with the approval by the Assembly of the Republic of Law No . 7/2005 of 20 December, which creates and fixes the value of the metical conversion rate and authorizes the Governor the Bank of Mozambique to define the book designation of the new Metical family. The Metical of the new family will facilitate our commercial and financial operations and bring greater convenience and security thanks to the reduction of digits and the incorporation of more modern security elements in the notes and coins. The success of the process of introducing the new Metical family will continue to depend on a broad and participatory dissemination campaign that reaches our entire country. In this context, we have means of disseminating information, such as radio, television, newspapers and the Internet. In the case of radio, our message is being disseminated through Radio Mozambique and community radio, a total of 25 national languages. Also noteworthy is the distribution throughout the country of posters, brochures and leaflets. Tiscnicos do Banco de Mo8dambi que desl lo caram a todos districts of the country, for the public clarification of all the contours inherent in this process, having counted on the collaboration of state institutions, religious congregations, municipal authorities, community leaders and socio-professional organisations. We have also been making clarifications to our communities abroad, with a focus on the countries hosting most of our compatriots. Today we feel that the message about the Metical of the new family is present in the vast majority of the Mozambican population, including that of rural areas, which at the beginning of the process was our highest priority. Ladies, gentlemen , The notes and coins of the Metical of the new family enter into circulation from 1 July 2006. Today we begin the advertising of the characteristics and facial value of the notes and coins of the new metical family. With this act, pretend e-se iniciar o processo de familiariza8d8bo (d ) the p 9cblic with the new banknotes and coins, in particular in relation to the minimum security elements , to facilitate transactions to be from 1 July. As we have been reporting, the entry into circulation of the notes and coins of the new Metical family will not entail the immediate withdrawal of the banknotes and coins currently in circulation. On 1 July, a six-month period of simultaneous circulation of the banknotes and coins currently in circulation and the metical notes and coins of the new family begins. During this period of simultaneous circulation, we will have a process of gradual introduction of the Metical of the new family. By therefore, there will be no exchange posts. The metical notes and coins of the new family will be obtained normally in our commercial and banking transactions. July 1st is just the milestone for the beginning of the movement of the new Metical family and for the carrying out of conversion operations. Therefore, our behavior must be the same as what we have had when new facial values are introducing our currency. Until 31 December 2006, payments can be made using notes and coins from both the Metical currently in circulation and from the new family, and will receive change in both a Metical family and another. From 1 January 2007, metical banknotes and coins currently in circulation, which are still in the public's possession , may be exchanged for notes and coins of the New Family Metical in banking establishments during 2007 and at the Bank of Mozambique until 31 December 2012. 1 July 2006 is the day of effective conversion. This means that all bank accounts and the value of the goods and services expressed in Meticais will be converted to the Metical of the new family. In this regard, I would like to highlight the following aspects of Decree No 55/2005 of 27 December: a5 In order to adjust the accounting rules to the conversion process, in the 2006 financial year we will have two closures of the accounts, the first being presented in Meticais currently in circulation reported on 30 June 2006, and the second presented in Meticais of the new family, reported on December 31 , 2006; a5 The conversion of the Metical into circulation to the Metical of the new family does not call into question the existence, validity and effectiveness of contracts and other legal acts concluded before 1 July 2006. a5 The double price indication will remain mandatory until 31 December 2006. Prices of goods and services in markets, shops and service companies, bank account balances, exchange rate tables, to name a few examples, should continue to be indicated simultaneously in meticais of the new family and in Meticais currently in circulation. Dear guests, Ladies, Gentlemen, The characteristics of the metical notes and coins of the new family, in particular the colours, dimensions, motifs and others, are such that they are not confused with those of the Metical currently in circulation. In defining the characteristics of the notes and coins of the Metical of the new family we integrated elements about education, economy, history, culture and fauna of our country. The notes and coins of the new Metical family have benefited from technological advances in the field of banknote printing and coinage. In fact, they are part of elements that facilitate the identification of the various names through tact, which is an innovation and is endorsed with better quality and modern safety features. Nevertheless, it is up to all of us to be responsible for the dignification and good conservation of the national currency, the Metical. In this regard, allow me to quote the preamble to Law 2/80, The Metical Law, which says "The struggle for currency stability is an integral part of the struggle for economic development. Currency stability requires an ever-increasing increase in production and productivity, as well as the effort to watch over all acts and attempts to misuse our currency." (End of citation). Finally, I would like to draw your attention to the presentation by the technicians of the Bank of Mozambique of the notes and coins of the new Metical family. Thank you very much.
text_original: INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELNCIA O GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE, ADRIANO MALEIANE, POR OCASIO DO LANAMENTO DAS NOTAS E MOEDAS DA NOVA FAMLIA DO METICAL MAPUTO, 16 DE JUNHO DE 2006 Caros Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Gostaria de em meu nome e em nome dos membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique agradecer a vossa presena neste acto de lanamento das notas e moedas do Metical da nova famlia, na data em que a nossa moeda completa 26 anos de existncia. Este acontecimento constitui o culminar do processo que iniciou com a aprovao, pela Assembleia da Repblica, da Lei n 7/2005, de 20 de Dezembro, que cria e fixa o valor da taxa de converso do Metical e autoriza o Governador do Banco de Moambique a definir a designao escritural da nova famlia do Metical. O Metical da nova famlia vai facilitar as nossas operaes comerciais e financeiras e trazer maior comodidade e segurana graas  reduo de dgitos e  incorporao de elementos de segurana mais modernos nas notas e moedas. O sucesso do processo de introduo da nova famlia do Metical continuar a depender de uma campanha de divulgao ampla e participativa, que alcance todo o nosso Pas. Neste contexto, contamos com meios de disseminao de informao, tais como a rdio, televiso, jornais e Internet. No caso da rdio, a nossa mensagem est a ser difundida atravs da Rdio Moambique e das rdios comunitrias, num total de 25 lnguas nacionais. De destacar tambm a distribuio por todo o Pas de cartazes, brochuras e desdobrveis. Tcnicos do Banco de Moambique deslocaram-se a todos os distritos do Pas, para o esclarecimento pblico de todos os contornos inerentes a este processo, tendo contado com a colaborao das instituies do Estado, congregaes religiosas, autoridades municipais, lderes comunitrios e organizaes scio-profissionais. Temos igualmente estado a proceder a esclarecimentos junto das nossas comunidades no exterior, com enfoque para os pases que hospedam a maior parte dos nossos compatriotas. Hoje sentimos que a mensagem sobre o Metical da nova famlia est presente na grande maioria da populao moambicana, incluindo a das zonas rurais, que no incio do processo constitua a nossa maior prioridade. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, As notas e moedas do Metical da nova famlia entram em circulao a partir do dia 1 de Julho de 2006. Hoje iniciamos a publicitao das caractersticas e valor facial das notas e moedas da nova famlia do Metical. Com este acto, pretende-se iniciar o processo de familiarizao do pblico com as novas notas e moedas, em particular em relao aos elementos mnimos de segurana, para facilitar as transaces a partir de 1 de Julho. Como temos vindo a informar, a entrada em circulao das notas e moedas da nova famlia do Metical no implicar a retirada imediata das notas e moedas actualmente em circulao. A 1 de Julho, inicia um perodo de seis meses de circulao simultnea das notas e moedas actualmente em circulao e as notas e moedas do Metical da nova famlia. Durante esse perodo de circulao simultnea, teremos um processo de introduo gradual do Metical da nova famlia. Por conseguinte, no haver postos de troca. As notas e moedas do Metical da nova famlia iro sendo obtidas normalmente nas nossas transaces comerciais e bancrias. O dia 1 de Julho  apenas o marco para o incio da circulao da nova famlia do Metical e para a realizao das operaes de converso. Por isso, o nosso comportamento deve ser igual ao que temos tido quando h introduo de novos valores faciais da nossa moeda. At 31 de Dezembro de 2006, poder-se- efectuar pagamentos utilizando notas e moedas tanto do Metical actualmente em circulao como da nova famlia, e receber trocos tanto numa famlia do Metical como noutra. A partir de 1 de Janeiro de 2007, as notas e moedas do Metical actualmente em circulao, que ainda estiverem na posse do pblico, podero ser trocadas para notas e moedas do Metical da nova famlia nos estabelecimentos bancrios durante o ano de 2007 e no Banco de Moambique at 31 de Dezembro de 2012. 1 de Julho de 2006  o dia da converso efectiva. Isto significa que todas as contas bancrias e o valor dos bens e servios expressos em Meticais sero convertidos para o Metical da nova famlia. A este propsito, gostaria de destacar os seguintes aspectos do Decreto n 55/2005, de 27 de Dezembro:  Para ajustar as regras contabilsticas ao processo de converso, no exerccio econmico de 2006 teremos dois encerramentos das contas, sendo o primeiro a ser apresentado em Meticais actualmente em circulao reportado a 30 de Junho de 2006, e o segundo apresentado em Meticais da nova famlia, reportado a 31 de Dezembro de 2006;  A converso do Metical em circulao para o Metical da nova famlia no pe em causa a existncia, validade e eficcia dos contratos e demais actos jurdicos celebrados antes de 1 de Julho de 2006.  A dupla indicao de preos continuar a ser obrigatria at 31 de Dezembro de 2006. Os preos dos bens e servios nos mercados, estabelecimentos comerciais e empresas de servios, os saldos das contas bancrias, as tabelas cambiais, s para citar alguns exemplos, devero continuar a ser indicados simultaneamente em Meticais da nova famlia e em Meticais actualmente em circulao. Caros convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, As caractersticas das notas e moedas do Metical da nova famlia, nomeadamente as cores, dimenses, motivos e outras, so tais que no se confundem com as do Metical actualmente em circulao. Na definio das caractersticas das notas e moedas do Metical da nova famlia integrmos elementos sobre educao, economia, histria, cultura e fauna do nosso Pas. As notas e moedas da nova famlia do Metical beneficiaram dos avanos tecnolgicos na rea da impresso de notas e cunhagem de moedas. Com efeito, elas integram elementos que facilitam a identificao das vrias denominaes atravs do tacto, o que constitui uma inovao e so dotadas de melhor qualidade e modernos elementos de segurana. Apesar disso, cabe a todos ns a responsabilidade pela dignificao e boa conservao da moeda nacional, o Metical. A este propsito, permitam-me que cite o prembulo da Lei 2/80, Lei do Metical, que diz A luta pela estabilidade da moeda  parte integrante da luta pelo desenvolvimento econmico. A estabilidade da moeda exige o aumento sempre crescente da produo e produtividade, assim como o resforo de vigilncia contra todos os actos e tentativas de utilizar indevidamente a nossa moeda. (Fim da citao). A terminar, gostaria de atrair a vossa ateno para a apresentao, pelos tcnicos do Banco de Moambique, das notas e moedas da nova famlia do Metical. Muito obrigado.

Title: Speech at the 11th Meeting of Central Bank Jurists of CPLP by His Excellency the Governor of the Bank of Mozambique
text: Representatives of the Central Banks of the CPLP, Jurists of the Bank of Mozambique Dear Guests Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen Allow me that on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, the participants of this 11th Meeting of Jurists of the Central Banks of the Countries that have the Portuguese as their official language will be addressed. I extend a special greeting to the representatives of the Central Banks of Angola, Brazil, Portugal and Sao Tome and Principe who are joining us at this meeting in Maputo. Welcome to our country and we hope you have a great stay. We hope that this will be a good opportunity to reinforce the friendship that unites us and your knowledge about the socio-cultural reality of our country. I extend my greeting to the Jurists of the Bank of Mozambique aswes to different units, including the Regional Branches of Beira and Nampula and the representatives of our partner institutions, present at this meeting. The 11th Meeting of Jurists of the Portuguese-speaking Central Banks coincides with the 32nd Anniversary of the creation of the Bank of Mozambique, held yesterday, May 17th. The history of our institution, for historical and cultural reasons, is similar to that of many Central Banks represented here. The creation of the Bank of Mozambique on May 17, 1975, a month before the proclamation of National Independence, translated the clarity of our leaders on the role of the Central Bank in promoting the country's balanced development. The Bank of Mozambique in the last 31 years has had different stages, for which our workers have given their best. The first step was to consolidate our institution, ensuring the operation of its services, after the massive departure of many expatriate workers. This was followed by the stage of creating the appropriate legal framework for the development of the financial sector . This period coincided in time with the implementation of the Economic and Social Rehabilitation Program in the country, which was accompanied by a series of reforms in the various areas of political, economic and social life. It was at this stage that we autonomized the commercial function in the then Bank of Mozambique and then created a universal commercial bank, with its own identity and management, making the banking system become composed of 3 commercial banks, plus the Central Bank. Later and through appropriate legislation, our market opened up to private, domestic and foreign capital. An important milestone of this period was the approval of our Organic Law, Law 1/92, of January 3, which allowed us to focus exclusively on the functions of the Central Bank. The approval of Law 15/99, Law of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, gave a better framework to the activity of these institutions. The entry of new entrants into the Mozambican financial system required the improvement of monetary and exchange rate policy instruments, with the creation of interbank exchange and monetary markets, MCI and MMI, respectively. The transition from direct monetary to indirect control instruments, significant improvements in the activity of collecting and processing statistical and accounting information and the start of computerization of the Bank of Mozambique and other credit institutions, were also actions that contributed to the modernization of monetary and exchange rate policy management. In the current stage, we are consolidating the gains we have made during this long process in which we have learned how to make central bank, reinforcing our role as monetary authority, exchange rate and supervisor of the financial system. The sophistication of markets and financial instruments makes our challenges even greater, requiring us to continue to modernize our vision, adjust our mission and permanently strengthen the quality of our human resources. Over the past 31 years, we have modernised our payment system, created bank supervision equipped for the size of our financial market and started the process that will enable us to conduct monetary policy in a qualitatively new way, in terms of forecasting and transparency. Our system currently has 12 commercial banks, 3 leasing companies, 5 credit unions, more than four dozen microfinance operators and about thirty exchange offices, among other types of financial institutions. Ladies Gentlemen These meetings are of particular importance to all participants, as they help to improve the understanding of different phenomena that occur in our countries, facilitating the interaction between legal professionals. These meetings also serve to synthesize the experiences valid for our countries, even with different specificities. This forum is a sublime occasion for each of our institutions to assess the evolution of the legislative framework in which it operates and to draw valid lessons. The moment we live in is a great challenge for our institutions and the search for solutions leads us to be aware of new dynamics, combining synergies. In Mozambique, there are profound changes in the legal and normative framework, of which I can cite, as an example:  the recent adoption of a new Commercial Code  the amended Code of Civil Procedure  the revision of the Labor Law, the process of which is still taking place. As far as banking and financial legislation is concerned, reforms are also continuing. Very recently, at the initiative of the Bank of Mozambique, the Law of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations was revised, with the approval of Law 9/2004 of July 21. The Bank of Mozambique is also involved in the revision of the Foreign Exchange Law, the legal law regulating the liquidation of banking establishments and the creation of a Law of the National Payment System. Also in the context of the reforms, the process of revising the Organic Law of the Bank of Mozambique is ongoing, in coordination with the SADC countries. Indeed, the Bank of Mozambique is involved in the drafting of the model organic law for the Central Banks of the SADC countries, as part of the regional harmonisation and integration process which also provides for the creation of a single central bank for SADC countries in the near future. Even recognizing the different stages of development of each country represented here, I note with satisfaction that the choice of themes for this XI Meeting includes matters of interest and timeliness for the ongoing banking and financial legislation reform process. In the recent revision of the Law of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations in our country, the figure of microbanks, institutions created in order to provide the public with a framework of opportunities for access to credit, alternative to the formal system offered by commercial banks, was introduced. The introduction of microbanks is part of our strategy of creating incentives for a greater banking of our economy, recognised that in rural areas it is where the majority of the Mozambican population resides. Our payment system already allows the clientele of our banking system to have access to a range of services and products of international nature, such as visa international, ponto 24, multinetwork and pronto networks. Similarly, many institutions already have their financial services networks connected in online systems, offering modern telephone banking, mobile banking and home-banking services. The introduction of these financial products, the characteristics of which are clearly different from traditional products, requires appropriate legislation to strengthen the control and compliance with the rules, in particular those relating to money laundering, a phenomenon which would be important to share with those present. We hope that the frank and open debate that characterizes jurists will allow the systematization of the valuable contributions to the improvement of the regulatory activity of our institutions, which obviously go through a deep knowledge of their practices and pragmatic solutions to the various legal problems that our countries still face. Ladies Gentlemen The main challenge of the Bank of Mozambique this year is the implementation of Law 7/2005 of 20 December, and complementary regulation that creates the conversion rate of metical in circulation to the Metical of the new family. This reform is part of the economic reforms initiated in 1987 and aims to adapt the means of payment to the current stage of our economy and consists of a three-figure reduction in the current banknotes and coins in circulation. The introduction of the Metical of the new family assumes importance and practical scope, in the context of the process of stabilizing our economy and the attributions of the Bank of Mozambique, to provide the economy, good quality banknotes and coins and in the best conditions of safety and convenience. At the end, I hope that everyone will take advantage of this opportunity, to capitalize on the various legal and banking knowledge, through a wholesome exchange of knowledge and experience, with professionals who operate in similar conditions very much though in different geographical spaces and complexity. We hope that this meeting by enriching the knowledge and mastery that each one has will also serve to improve the quality of the normative activity of our institutions, thus contributing to the construction, in our countries, of increasingly sound financial systems. So, Ladies Gentlemen I declare open the 11th Meeting of Jurists of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries. Thank you very much. Maputo on 18 May 2006
text_original: Senhores Representantes dos Bancos Centrais da CPLP Senhores Juristas do Banco de Moambique Caros Convidados Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Permitam-me que em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, sade os participantes deste XI Encontro de Juristas dos Bancos Centrais dos Pases que tm o portugus como lngua oficial. Dirijo uma saudao especial aos representantes dos Bancos Centrais de Angola, Brasil, Portugal e So Tom e Prncipe que se juntam a ns nesta reunio de Maputo. Sejam bem-vindos ao nosso Pas e fazemos votos que tenham uma ptima estadia. Esperamos que esta seja uma boa oportunidade para reforarmos a amizade que nos une e o vosso conhecimento sobre a realidade scio-cultural do nosso Pas. Estendo a minha saudao aos Juristas do Banco de Moambique afectos a diferentes unidades, incluindo as Filiais Regionais da Beira e Nampula e os representantes de instituies nossas parceiras, presentes neste encontro. O XI Encontro de Juristas dos Bancos Centrais de lngua portuguesa coincide com o XXXI Aniversrio da criao do Banco de Moambique, celebrado ontem, dia 17 de Maio. A histria da nossa instituio, por razes histrico-culturais, assemelha-se a de muitos Bancos Centrais aqui representados. A criao do Banco de Moambique, a 17 de Maio de 1975, um ms antes da proclamao da Independncia Nacional, traduziu a clareza dos nossos dirigentes sobre o papel do Banco Central na promoo do desenvolvimento equilibrado do Pas. O Banco de Moambique nos ltimos 31 anos conheceu distintas etapas, para as quais, os nossos trabalhadores tm dado o seu melhor. A primeira etapa foi a de consolidao da nossa instituio, assegurando o funcionamento dos seus servios, aps a sada macia de muitos trabalhadores expatriados. Seguiu-se a etapa de criao do quadro legal apropriado ao desenvolvimento do sector financeiro. Este perodo coincidiu no tempo, com a implementao do Programa de Reabilitao Econmica e Social no Pas, que foi acompanhado de uma srie de reformas, nos vrios domnios da vida poltica, econmica e social. Foi nesta etapa que autonomizamos a funo comercial no ento Banco de Moambique e de seguida criamos um banco comercial universal, com identidade e gesto prpria, fazendo com que o sistema bancrio passasse a ser composto por 3 bancos comerciais, mais o Banco Central. Mais tarde e merc de legislao apropriada, o nosso mercado abriu-se aos capitais privados, nacionais e estrangeiros. Um marco importante deste perodo, foi a aprovao da nossa Lei Orgnica, Lei 1/92, de 3 de Janeiro, que nos permitiu concentrar, exclusivamente, nas funes de Banco Central. A aprovao da Lei 15/99, Lei das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras, veio dar um melhor enquadramento a actividade destas instituies. A entrada de novos operadores no sistema financeiro moambicano exigiu o aperfeioamento dos instrumentos de poltica monetria e cambial, com a criao dos mercados cambial e monetrio interbancrios, MCI e MMI, respectivamente. A transio de instrumentos directos de controle monetrio para indirectos, as melhorias significativas na actividade de recolha e tratamento de informao estatstica e contabilstica e o incio da informatizao do Banco de Moambique e demais instituies de crdito, foram tambm aces que concorreram para a modernizao da gesto da poltica monetria e cambial. Na actual etapa, estamos a consolidar os ganhos que obtivemos ao longo deste longo processo em que aprendemos a fazer Banco Central, reforando o nosso papel de autoridade monetria, cambial e de supervisor do sistema financeiro. A sofisticao dos mercados e instrumentos financeiros torna os nossos desafios ainda maiores, exigindo de ns a continua modernizao da nossa viso, ajustamento da nossa misso e permanente reforo da qualidade dos nossos recursos humanos. Ao longo dos ltimos 31 anos, modernizamos o nosso sistema de pagamentos, criamos uma superviso bancria apetrechada para a dimenso do nosso mercado financeiro e iniciamos o processo que nos habilitar a conduzir a poltica monetria de forma qualitativamente nova, em termos de previso e transparncia. O nosso sistema possui hoje 12 bancos comerciais, 3 sociedades de locao financeira, 5 cooperativas de crdito, mais de quatro dezenas de operadores de microfinanas e cerca de trinta casas de cmbio, entre outro tipo de instituies financeiras. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores, Estes encontros revestem-se de particular importncia para todos os participantes, pois ajudam a melhorar a compreenso de distintos fenmenos que ocorrem nos nossos pases, facilitando a interaco entre profissionais da rea jurdica. Estes encontros servem tambm para sintetizar as experincias vlidas para os nossos pases, mesmo com especificidades distintas. Este frum  uma ocasio sublime para cada uma das nossas instituies avaliar a evoluo do quadro legislativo em que opera e retirar ilaes vlidas. O momento em que vivemos,  de grandes desafios para as nossas instituies e a busca de solues leva-nos a estarmos atentos a novas dinmicas, juntando sinergias. Em Moambique, operam-se profundas mudanas no quadro jurdico-normativo, de que posso citar, a ttulo de exemplo:  a recente aprovao de um novo Cdigo Comercial  a alterado do Cdigo de Processo Civil  a reviso da Lei do Trabalho, cujo processo ainda decorre. No concernente  legislao bancria e financeira, as reformas tambm prosseguem. Muito recentemente, por iniciativa do Banco de Moambique, foi revista a Lei das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras, com a aprovao da Lei 9/2004, de 21 de Julho. O Banco de Moambique est igualmente envolvido na reviso da Lei Cambial, do diploma legal que regula a liquidao de estabelecimentos bancrios e na criao de uma Lei do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos. Ainda no mbito das reformas, est em curso o processo de reviso da Lei Orgnica do Banco de Moambique, em coordenao com os pases da SADC. Com efeito, o Banco de Moambique est envolvido na elaborao da lei orgnica modelo para os Bancos Centrais dos pases da SADC, no quadro do processo de harmonizao e integrao regional que prev, igualmente, a criao de um banco central nico para os pases da SADC, num futuro prximo. Mesmo reconhecendo os diferentes estgios de desenvolvimento de cada pas aqui representado, verifico com satisfao que a escolha dos temas para este XI Encontro contempla matrias de interesse e actualidade para o processo de reformas da legislao bancria e financeira em curso. Na recente reviso da Lei das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras no nosso pas, foi introduzida a figura de microbancos, instituies criadas com a finalidade de proporcionar ao pblico um quadro de oportunidades de acesso ao crdito, alternativo ao sistema formal oferecido pelos bancos comerciais. A introduo de microbancos insere-se na nossa estratgia de criar incentivos  uma maior bancarizao da nossa economia, reconhecido que nas zonas rurais  onde reside a maior parte da populao moambicana. O nosso sistema de pagamentos permite j que a clientela do nosso sistema bancrio tenha acesso a uma gama de servios e produtos de cariz internacional, como so os casos das redes Visa Internacional, Ponto 24, Multirede e rede Pronto. De igual modo, muitas instituies possuem j as suas redes de servios financeiros ligados em sistemas on-line, oferecendo servios modernos de telephone banking, mobile banking e home- banking. A introduo destes produtos financeiros cujas caractersticas so claramente diferentes dos produtos tradicionais, requer uma legislao adequada para reforar o controlo e o cumprimento das normas, em particular, as relativas  lavagem de dinheiro, fenmeno que importaria partilhar com os presentes. Esperamos que o debate franco e aberto que caracteriza os juristas, permitir a sistematizao das valiosas contribuies para a melhoria da actividade normativa das nossas instituies, que passam, obviamente, por um conhecimento profundo das suas prticas e por solues pragmticas para os diversos problemas de ordem legal que os nossos pases ainda enfrentam. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores, O principal desafio do Banco de Moambique no corrente ano,  o da implementao da Lei 7/2005, de 20 de Dezembro, e regulamentao complementar que, que cria a taxa de converso do Metical em circulao para o Metical da nova famlia. Esta reforma  parte das reformas econmicas iniciadas em 1987 e visa adequar os meios de pagamento ao estgio actual da nossa economia e consiste na reduo de trs dgitos nas actuais notas e moedas em circulao. Title: End of the Economic Year 2007
text: Presidents of the Boards of Commercial Banks; Distinguished Guests; Ladies and Gentlemen I once again have the honour to welcome you here for the traditional preliminary consideration of the financial year ending and outline prospects for the New Year. First of all, I would like to thank you, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Banco de Introduction & Mocambique for your presence in this ceremony and take this opportunity to express our Greetings deep recognition to all the institutions that you are worthy representatives, the various business associations we have relationship with, the economic agents from different sectors of activity, the Government, the international community and the media, for the invaluable support that have always provided, thus contributing to the development of our country and for the national agenda to fight against absolute poverty. The year 2007 was rich in terms of events that marked our existence as People and Nation. Among them, it is worth highlighting the successful completion of the process of reversion of Cahora Bassa Hydroelectric Plant to the Mozambican Government. We are all proud and rejoiced with this remarkable event provided that Cahora Bassa Plant can better liberate its potential while under control of the Mozambican authorities, assuming its role as a catalyst for the national development and fundamental instrument for the regional and continental economic integration. I congratulate the National Institute of Statistics, for having conducted the third general population census successfully, thus allowing the upgrading of the vital data of Mozambican population. We are also encouraged with the fact that the National Institute of Statistics have started to compile and publish the Gross Domestic Product quarterly data, the information of paramount importance for all users of national accounts, and especially the Central Bank. The more regular availability of infra-annual information on the GDP enhances our ability to analyze, explain and predict, more accurately, the status of our real economy, thus facilitating our performance. The year 2007 was also worthy in terms of remarkable events in the context of the relationship that Mozambique establishes with its partners of international cooperation, amongst which we would like to highlight the following:  The praiseworthy references on the countrys economic performance and macroeconomic management quality stressed again by the Bretton Woods institutions, which approved a new programme with our government named the Policy Support Instrument (PSI);  The hosting in Maputo of the XV Meeting for the Replenishment of Funds of the International Association for Development (IDA), a forum responsible for mobilizing and rising fiinds in order to ensure the achievement of the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). It is worth stressing that it was the first time that the Conference took place in the African Continent;  The hosting of the meetings of the Ministers of Finance and Governors of African Central Banks in July and August 2007, in the context of CAUCUS, an entity chaired by Mozambique for two years;  The completion in December, in London, of the fourth roiind of negotiations aimed to replenish resources for the African Development Fund for the term 2008-2010, which resulted in the Donors agreement to provide an amoiint estimated at USD 8.5 billion;  The selection of Mozambique by the African Development Bank to host its Annual Meeting in May 2008. These events testify the prestige and sympathy that Mozambique gained from the International Community and show its commitment with the Governmenfs performance in the implementation of development programmes and Macroeconomic stabilization. Ladies and Gentlemen; The political, economic, social and financial developments taking place in the region and worldwide concern us, given the characteristics of our country, of a small open economy, very sensitive to externai shocks. International & Regional Economic OverView Internationally, available information on the world advanced economies pointed out to growth rates in line with initial forecasts, although the latest prospects on the American economy showed a more moderate growth, especially due to the impact of the crisis affecting the sub-prime sector. The latest projections of the World Economic Outlook showed that the economic growth on the African continent may accelerate to 5.7 percent in 2007 and, for our satisfaction, whose major contribution will come from the SADC countries which, apparently, will record a joint annual growth of 9 per cent in 2007. The general prices rising trend has caused some concerns to the authorities in most of the economies in the world and particularly in our region, especially in this final part of the year, prompted by the sharp rise of crude oil and cereais prices in the international market. The boom of the Chinese economy which has resulted in increased demand for energy, the political problems in the major petroleum producer and exporting countries, especially those located in the Middle East, prevented from optimizing their production, and the global environmental problems that increasingly make the seasons of the year in the countries of the northern hemisphere unpredictable, have been creating conditions for a stronger pressure over crude oil price in the international market, which this year recorded a new historie peak of about USD 100 per barrei, thus increasing difficulties for the low- income countries entirely dependent on imports of this raw material. The sub-prime crisis affecting the real estate sector in the United States rapidly spread through other parts of the world as a result of the higher correlation between the markets. The central banks of the world advanced economies have taken extraordinary measures to ensure adequate leveis of liquidity and counter to the forecasts of inflationary pressure. In the United States, the Federal Reserve began a new round of reduction in its reference rate, while the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan, after the upward adjustments iindertaken in the first quarter of the year, made no more changes in their interest rates. In China, the Central Bank was forced to undertake successive upward adjustments of its reference rate and mandatory reserve coefficient. In the region, the economic problems in Zimbabwe remained unchanged, creating adverse side-effects on the Balance of Payments of the neighbouring countries such as Mozambique. In South africa, the most recent inflation rate exceeded the authoritys medium term expectation, a factor occurring in a context of the Rand strengthening, associated to Gold price rising trend. For the first time in the last four years, the South African Reserve Bank set its reference rate at 11 per cent in an attempt to counter to inflation rising trend. Yesterday, we received news about the elections within the ANC party that resulted in a change of leadership, element on which we hope the markets react with due serenity. Additionally, given the fali of the US dollar in the international market, the currencies of the most SADC countries appreciated during the course of current year. Ladies and Gentlemen; Economic Programme for 2007 Economic Programme for 2007 Economic & Financial Performance in 2007 Economic & Financial Performance in 2007 The exogenous shocks that hit our economy affected the behaviour of the general consumer price index of Maputo city such that the seasonal periods of the year that observe considerable inflation decline, did not reach the levei capable of softening the rise of prices that normally occurs in the last three months of the year. The foodstuff price has been the main reason behind the rise of prices, and our prospects point out to an inflation rate greater than the target set for the end of the year. However, we are encouraged by the fact that the average annual inflation throughout the year has slowed down from 13 per cent in late 2006 to 8 per cent in November 2007. Performance ofthe Banco de Mocambique Performance ofthe Banco de Mocambique During 2007, the Metical remained stable in the domestic foreign exchange market, thanks to the reforms, which led the market operators and economic agents, in general, to gain more confidence in the national currency. As a matter of fact, the foreign currency transactions among commercial banks amounted to USD 271 million, against USD 150 recorded in 2006, in a context where the spread of exchange rates between different market segments, remained below 2 per cent. Externai Sector Developmets in 2007 Externai Sector Developmets in 2007 The improvement of the current account coupled with the inflow of externai financial aid, contributed to the accrual of Net International Reserves to the tune of USD 1,470 billion, equivalent to 5.3 months of total imports of goods and non-factor Services, including major projects. Ladies Gentlemen; Monetary Policy Monetary Policy During the year under review, the monetary policy continued to focus on indirect instruments, especially for the open market operations that were reinforced in July 2007, with repo and reverse repo operations, along with the treasury bilis operations. As regards incentives for the expansion of financial Services to the rural areas, we have made adjustments in the mandatory reserves regime, expanding its base of incidence, and we have simultaneously reduced its coefficient to 10.15 per cent so as to align it with the average of the region. The exchange rate stability and the improved average annual inflation has allowed the expansion of the aggregate broad money - M3 - to stand in line with the outlined program, even in a year with increased inflow of foreign funds. This year, we revised our reference rate downwards, revealing to the market the sign of greater confidence on the trend of the market rates. Ladies Gentlemen; Expansion of Financial Services Expansion of Financial Services We are grateful that the credit institutions are responding positively, expanding their network of branches and financial Services through to new regions of the country. In effect, we have authorized 40 new branches in the current year, as well as the establishment of new credit institutions, and the transformation of one microfinance operator into a micro bank. Moreover, we witnessed the increase of the number of districts with bank Services to 32, which may grow in the short term, taking into account the banks and financial institutions high interest and expansion projects. Despite the concentration of our financial system in the urban areas and neighbourhoods, the Services it provides are increasingly broader, faster and effective, thus maximizing the large public investment that the Government is undertaking in infrastructures and Communications, which we should recognize and encourage. The national payment system has been the subject of major achievements, among which it is worth stressing the following:  Introduction of the cheque control digit and the mandatory use of the Bank Identification Number in interbank electronic transfers (TEI's), aimed at increasing security and efficiency of payment instruments.  Under the agreement signed between the VISA and BM in December 2006, we began in March of the current year, to perform the national settlement of domestic clearing transactions within this network. This agreement allowed us to save foreign currency over USD 7 million, until September. The cheque real time payments and settlement system is now available to the economic operators and the general public in many places of the country. In effect, by September 2007, more 200 thousand accounts were open in the national banking system, the number of Automated Teller Machines (ATM's) has increased by 14 and that of the Point of Sale (POS) devices by 154, an evolvement accompanied by an increase in the number of debit and credit cards, as well as the number of transactions performed through these instruments. Even though, we continue to work with the Government in order to identify other possibilities that encourage banks to extend their network throughout the country and in particular to the rural areas where the savers are forced to travei long distances to deposit their savings and access financial Services. Supervision & Regulatory Aspects Supervision & Regulatory Aspects Ladies Gentlemen, The Parliament approved very recently the Laws on the National Payment Systems and Financial Institutions Bankruptcy, which, including contributions of credit institutions, reinforces the legal framework for a more transparent and competitive performance. The growth and development of our financial system, the increased internationalization of our financial institutions and the challenges of regional integration that will culminate with the creation of a central bank and a single currency in 2018, has increased the challenges within our scope of performance. For better response, we have been equipping our institution with new materiais and human resources over the years. Ladies Gentlemen; Despite the improvements taking place, especially in macroeconomic stability domain, we are still faced with challenges such as the following: Future Challenges  Continue to improve the way we conduct our monetary policy, reinforcing the forecasting and modelling ability in order to minimize the risks and uncertainties of economic and financial climate and increase the effectiveness of our policies.  Strengthen our role as supervisors of the system and complete the process of transition to risk based supervision. We expect all credit institutions to report on the IFRS, as from 2008.  Pursue the multifaceted efforts aimed at further expansion of financial Services to rural areas. In this regard, we will also offer particular attention to the process of rural finance development already begun, as to extend the financial Services into the outskirts.  Prioritize joint work with our partners aimed to reduce the costs of transaction and turn the pricing of banking Services more transparent.  Implement the Law on the National Payment System and ensure entire operation of Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) System, which will promote faster transactions in the economy. Our mission is to ensure price stability, embodied in a low and stable inflation in line with the Governmenfs policy to fight against absolute poverty in the country. Prospects for 2008 The monetary policy in 2008 will continue to be conducted in order to contribute to the achievement of macroeconomic policy goals set by the Government, which point out to 7.0 per cent economic growth and a single digit inflation. Our intermediate goals point out to a monetary expansion to the tune of 18.1 per cent and growth in credit to the economy of 21.7 per cent in the year. Ladies Gentlemen; Allow me to take this opportunity to thank once again the economic agents, the society in general and the international community who have always contributed to the economic and social development of our country. 1 wish you all, Merry Christmas and Prosperous New Year together with your families. Thank you very much.

Title: End of the Economic Year 2005
text: Distinguished Guests; Ladies; Gentlemen In a few days, the year 2005 will end. As has been customary, at this time the Bank of Mozambique invites its partners in the financial system, representatives of economic associations and the banking workers' union, to take stock of the year ending and present its prospects for the new economic and financial year. On my own behalf and on the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, I would like to thank you for your presence at this ceremony. Let us first of all take this opportunity to congratulate the Government on the fact that very recently it has managed to formalize the agreement that reverts to the country the hydroelectric enterprise of Cahora Bassa, as well as the launch of the first stones that mark the beginning of the construction of important public works, namely the bridges over the rivers Zambezi, which will ensure the road connection between the center and the north of the country, Rovuma, already called the unit bridge and Limpopo. With these ventures, a great multiplier effect on the country's overall economic activity is expected in the coming years. Also in this wake, we welcome the decision of the IMF Board of Directors to include Mozambique on the list of the first 19 countries that qualified for the multilateral external debt forgiveness initiative. This decision, which is scheduled for 2006 , represents yet another gesture of trust of the international community in the country and an additional challenge for all of us with a view to reducing absolute poverty. When we met at the end of December 2004, we took stock of that year's financial and announced that the main targets for the 2005 financial year, Program consisted of 8% economic growth, single-digit inflation and a level of international economic reserves capable of covering around five months of imports of non-2005 non-2005 non-2005- Our intermediate targets were monetary expansion of not more than 14% and credit growth to the economy of 16%. At the 2004 ceremony, we witnessed the signing by operators of the Interbank Foreign Exchange Market (MCI) Code of Conduct. This was a necessary step to deepen and modernize the functioning of our foreign exchange market, implemented in January. International Economic Conjuncture in 2005 International Economic Conjuncture in 2005 It should be recalled that the price of a barrel of oil reached the historical peak of USD 70 in August, equivalent to a nominal increase of 70% compared to December 2004. After September, the price decreased to the 58 dollar a barrel, which still represents a high nominal change when compared to the late 2004 prices, the baseline scenario for the projections we made for 2005. The increase in the price of oil in the international market has changed the behavior of inflation on a global scale, and most countries have reviewed this indicator. In the US, annual inflation reached 4.7% in September, leading the Federal Reserve to set the interest rate nine times higher to the current level of 4.25%; in the Eurozone, estimates point to a inflation above 2%, with the ECB rising its interest rate to 2.25%, which was not the case three years ago; in Japan, after successive years of deflation, the authorities predict inflation for this year. In SADC countries, convergence criteria define that the annual inflation rate should, by 2008. According to projections for 2005, this goal will be more easily achieved only by South Africa. Ladies Gentlemen Economic and Financial Performance Internal in 2005 Economic and Financial Performance Internal in 2005 Preliminary information based on data from June 2005 indicates that domestic production could grow above 7%, which will represent an increase over the originally scheduled. Unlike 2004, when the contribution of major projects was decisive for overall performance (weight of 10% in total production and responsible for 56% of global growth), this year, the increase in production is being sustained by the dynamics of other sectors of activity, which grew 7.3%, against 1.3% in aluminum production. The monthly inflation of 2.8% recorded in November, the highest since 2001, makes our forecast of single-digit inflation for 2005 difficult to achieve, but we hope that it will not move too far away from this level if there is any price moderation in the days remaining until the end of this month. The exogenous shocks that our economy suffered have had a negative impact on the behaviour of the general consumer price index in Maputo City. With displeasure, we again observed in 2005 an atypical price behaviour in the last three months of the year, with food prices rising more than normal, representing about 50% of inflation for the whole year. As we have been mentioning, at the height of the festive season, economic operators should maximise their gains by means of the quantities sold and not by the increase in the piecos, which only creates disturbances in Mozambican families and in the inflation indicator. Throughout the year, the worsening CPI is explained by the effect of rising fuel prices, drought and the impact of imported inflation that the depreciation of IVbtical produces. The assessment of Metical in 2004 generated a strong propensity for imports, to the detriment of exports. As our balance of payments are structurally deficient and dependent on foreign aid, the replacement of external competitiveness gains required the market to correct and align the Metical exchange rate in 2005. Data reported in November indicate that the monetary aggregate designated M2, expanded in line with the program (16%). The economy's overall domestic banking financing increased by 26% in cumulative terms. We also recorded a drop of 3.5 percentage points in interest rates and the reduction in the amount of bad-stop credit that some banks have been carrying out. By October the total value of the saneada portfolio was 407.2 mdc, against 934.6 mdc in 2003 and 1063.8 mdc in 2004, which reveals improvement in the quality of the banks' loan portfolio. It has contributed to the increase in the volume of financing to the private sector, greater coverage of financial services at national level, dictated by the entry of new entrants and new products, which allow an improvement in access to credit. Moreover, the private sector of the economy also received USD 117 million in external funding until September, which is important for investment, job creation and economic activity in general. In order to safeguard credit institutions, borrowers and economic agents in general, in 2005 we published normative provisions that lend themselves to the prevention of foreign exchange risk, money laundering and improvement of the organization of processes involving foreign exchange operations. In the first nine months of the year, the country's external position measured by the Current Account increased by 2.2%, compared to the same period in 2004, in the face of a sharper increase in imports compared to exports. Until September, the country imported goods worth a total of US1.597 million, exporting US1.254 million, including yandes projects. If we exclude dwells, exports arose at US332.7 million (26.5% of the total value), against imports of US1.371 million. This scenario caused the rate of coverage of imports by exports to decrease by 2.4 percentage points to 78.6%. Pressure on the foreign exchange demand side has led to a wear and tear of liquid international reserves of around US40 million, but its balance is in line with the ultimate goal of accumulating sufficient reserves to cover 4.7 months of imports of non-factor goods and services. Ladies Gentlemen Reforms of the Financial System The reforms of the Mozambican financial system gained greater momentum with the approval in 1990 of the so-called General Lines for The Reform of the Financial System, which was based on three main pillars:  Transforming and strengthening the Bank of Mozambique  Enhance transparency in all central bank activities  Create banking supervision that is up to financial market developments. After 15 years of continuous work in this direction, we find that much has been done, even though we are aware of much to be done and consolidated. i) With regard to the transformation and strengthening of the Bank of Mozambique When the Government approved Decree 2/75, it had a clear perspective on the central role of the Bank of Mozambique in the national economy. The transformation of the WB to assume the exclusive missions of the Central Bank, made it necessary to review the Bank's Organic Law, through the approval of Law 1/92, which represented an important milestone in our activity and in the Mozambican financial system in general. This led to the institutional separation of commercial and central functions, with the Bank of mozambique to devote itself exclusively to the missions of monetary authority, foreign exchange and supervisor of the financial system. The objective of internal and external stability of the national currency which our Organic Law enshrines has become more clearly directed towards controlling inflation. The Bank's effort to create explanatory models of inflation, currency demand and models for predicting the system's liquidity variation factors was great useful for calibrating our market interventions. These tools are available today and we continue the work of constant improvement, as well as the technical and professional elevation of our employees, with the support of our international partners. The Bank's organic structure has been streamlined in order to adapt it to current practice in SADC's central banks and to allow greater efficiency in the circulation of information and in the decision-making and implementation process. (ii) With regard to enhanced transparency in the activities of the Central Bank The timing and credibility of the information provided is a success factor for greater effectiveness of the policy signals issued by the Central Bank. During this period, we have created a monetary and financial information infrastructure that is now collected, processed and disseminated at a daily frequency as a result of the significant investment in information and it solutions that we have been carrying out. This allows the market, analysts, academics and the general public to have access in real time to vital information needed to make various decisions, as well as to monitor and assess the degree of implementation of the monetary policy measures we implement. The quality of the monetary, financial and balance of payments statistics that we produce today contributed to the country being admitted in 2003 to the IMF data dissemination system, known as GDDS, which makes our information more comparable to that of other countries. In addition to statistical information, we offer the public various analytical information, in the form of regular editions that the Bank produces and disseminates, increasingly, in electronic support, through the page we have on the Internet. The exercise accounts and activity reports of the Bank of Mozambique are published annually, after rigorous evaluation and supervision by the Internal Audit Office, audit board and external audit firms we hire, following internationally established standards. The changes introduced in the framework of transparency and modernization of the Bank of Mozambique, today allow us to know, in real time, the financial situation of the institution and the accounts of the monetary authority, a crucial element for monitoring and decision-making by the Monetary and Exchange Rate Policy Committee. Indeed, transparency is now a acquis and a goal that we seek to preserve, extend and improve, for the sake of strengthening our role in the market and in the economy. In this way, we have also sought to involve all institutions operating under the Law of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, to promote a routine of greater transparency and discipline in their activity. It is in this context that the rules that we issue on the mandatory public disclosure of their reports and accounts, audited by independent entities, are framed. (iii) With regard to the creation of banking supervision at the level of the development of the financial market The opening up of the Mozambican economy to private initiative has led to new capital, both domestic and foreign, accessing our banking system, thereby increasing the range of existing institutions and their diversification. The separation of functions within the Bank of Mozambique and the change in the profile of our banking system through the sophistication of the financial products it offers, required, from the outset, the creation of a supervisory unit at the Central Bank. In 1994, when we created the Banking Supervision Department, it had only 4 technicians, a number that evolved into the current 47 analysts, increasingly able to perform on- and off-site inspections. In parallel to the strengthening of the technical framework, we have undertaken several actions aimed at strengthening banking supervision, with emphasis on the following:  Continuous training of technicians, in brazil and abroad;  Institutionalization of a system of inspections that takes into account the classification of each institution operating in our market;  Introduction of new methodologies and reports for inspections of the institutions, having a system of permanent monitoring of the corrective measures we recommend;  Review of several legislations, with emphasis on the Law of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations and their regulation, which accommodates the activity of new entrants and the creation of new financial products and services;  Updating and strengthening prudential ratios and limits, a process that by its nature has been implemented dynamically and progressively, in line with developments in the financial system, the government's programmatic objectives and international practices on the subject.  Development and entry into production of a specialized IT application to the banking supervision activity, which by its quality was adopted by the generality of the central banks of SADC. The work we have done in this direction has enabled our system to be more robust today and prepared to absorb the various risks that financial activity entails. To name a few examples, the ratio of bad-to-wage credit fell from 23.4% in 2001 to the current 4.6%, while the solvency ratio grew from 5.5% to 16.7% in the same period, against a required minimum of 8%, according to the terms of the Basel I convention or 12% under Basel II. Ladies Gentlemen The progress we have summing up here are only signs that encourage us to continue our concerted effort. We are aware of the challenges that are expected of us to be a Central Bank that is up to the imperatives of convergence in the SADC region and in the African continent challenges. Futures We will continue to improve the way we carry out monetary policy by improving aspects of communication and transparency. In this context, we have planned to reshape the functioning of monetary and exchange rate policy committee, meeting international standards. This process will undergo an adjustment in its analytical content, format, periodicity and the way we communicate the deliberations that this body takes. We will put into productive the computer application that we develop to support and support statistical activity on an online basis with banks and other information providers, which will allow us to focus, each time, on the analysis of information and on the evaluation of the impact of the measures we take. For your success, we invite our sources of information to work in this direction, providing us in a timely manner with your information. To our users, here is the invitation of permanent interaction, with comments and suggestions that help us greatly improve. We must strengthen our capacity to forecast and model the risks and uncertainties of the economic and financial environment to be minimised, with better results from the point of view of effectiveness of our policies. Moreover, such a programme is already underway, with the support and technical assistance of our partners, which provides for actions in the areas of the core inflation model for monetary policy purposes, the adoption of the monetary base as an instrumental variable and continuous improvement of the model for predicting factors for the variation of the system's liquidity, which will also involve the Ministry of Finance. Let me point out once again that the main objective of our monetary and exchange rate policy is to ensure low and stable inflation. This objective is in line with the Government's policy of combating absolute poverty in the country. Only with low inflation allows to preserve the purchasing power of families with lower incomes. The introduction of the multilateral exchange rate mechanism and the exchange auction is the objective of calibrating our market interventions through securities and Ide foreign exchange auctions in order to control the monetary base. I would like to point out that the MCI is extracting the practice of foreign exchange auctions. In addition to these, which should know new developments, such as the assumption of firm taking (bid and offer), we will regulate the framework of interventions that aim to align the exchange rate, having as an implicit anchor, the parity of purchasing power (PPC) of our currency in relation to the currencies of our partners. These changes require a continuous updating of the technical- professional skills of our staff. This will be the stance we will seek to maintain in order to achieve the final inflation and international reserve targets. Ladies Gentlemen Monetary policy in 2006 will continue to be designed to contribute to the government's macroeconomic policy objectives, which forecast economic growth of 7.9% and inflation of 7%. Our intermediate targets are a monetary expansion ( aggregate Outlook M2) of 14.5% and a growth of credit to the economy compatible with gdp growth for nominal 2006. Our mission as system supervisors will continue to require adequate vigilance to the soundness and stability indicators of the financial system, taking into account the timetable we have set for the gradual transition to the principles and good practices provided for in the IAS and IFRS. We will continue to work with the Government and the private sector on actions that stimulate further expansion of financial services to rural areas, where the degree of financial intermediation remains very low. In view of the approval by the Assembly of the Republic of Law No. 7/2005, on the Conversion Rate of the Metical to the Metical of the new family, the Bank of Mozambique, in coordination with other institutions, will prioritize its implementation in its actions for 2006. I would like to call for the collaboration of the whole society in this effort, participating in the civic education campaigns, which will be formally launched on 28 December, when we will give the details on this matter. Ladies Gentlemen We wish to express our deep gratitude for the support that the international community continues to provide to our country, providing us with the financial resources necessary for the plan to combat absolute poverty defined by the Government. Let me take this opportunity to thank with emphasis the economic agents and society at large who continue to believe and support our policies, as a contribution to the economic and social development of the country. Finally, I would like to thank the workers of the Bank of Mozambique and through you all the workers in our financial system for the dedication and commitment shown throughout the year. I wish you all happy holidays and a prosperous New Year with your families. Thank you very much. Maputo, 23 December 2005
