Acolhemos em Maputo este evento promovido pelo Banco Mundial num momento particularmente importante, em que o Banco de Moambique celebra, a 17 do ms em curso, 35 anos da sua criao. Este workshop acontece num cenrio em que a economia mundial paulatinamente se recompe duma situao generalizada de crise, com consequncias directas no crescimento global. Esta crise, considerada a mais severa desde a ecloso da 2^ Guerra Mundial, trouxe novos desafios para os pases desenvolvidos e em desenvolvimento, quer no contexto do combate ao desemprego, quer no processo da reestruturao econmico-financeira dos mercados a nvel global. O mercado internacional caracterizou-se pelo enfraquecimento de alguns dos seus segmentos, nomeadamente os ttulos colaterizados, por uma grande subida de spreads de crditos, incerteza dos investidores, reduo do volume de transaces e por uma expressiva descida das taxas de juro. Apesar de se registarem sinais de recuperao econmica, persiste a necessidade de os intervenientes nos mercados financeiros globais pautarem por um comportamento prudente. No obstante os efeitos transnacionais da crise, o ritmo de crescimento das reservas internacionais do Banco de Moambique manteve-se estvel. Factos elucidativos indicam que entre 2000 e 2009 o crescimento mdio anual das nossas reservas esteve  volta dos 15%, com o seu nvel mais elevado em Dezembro de 2009, quando, pela primeira vez na histria da instituio, o saldo das reservas se situou nos USD 2 bilies, correspondentes a 5.6 meses de cobertura das importaes. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores Apesar do cenrio estvel na gesto das reservas do Pas, importa destacar os efeitos da crise em duas fontes de produo das mesmas, nomeadamente as receitas de exportao e os rendimentos resultantes da sua gesto. No concernente s receitas de exportao, dois factores afectaram substancialmente a arrecadao de divisas, designadamente a contraco da demanda global e o declnio dos preos dos nossos produtos de exportao. Por outro lado, as receitas de exportao de produtos tradicionais, incluindo o algodo, camaro, castanha de caju e energia elctrica sofreram tambm, em 2009, uma reduo de 41% em relao ao ano de 2008. Por seu turno, o rendimento das reservas foi afectado pela brusca e inesperada volatilidade dos mercados financeiros. Por um lado, as nossas carteiras no mercado monetrio viram-se afectadas pela queda das taxas de juro. Por outro, a subida das taxas de retorno dos ttulos obrigacionistas (yields) afectou as nossas carteiras de activos de renda fixa (fixed income securities). Como resultado, os rendimentos da gesto de reservas registaram um declnio de 20% em 2009, contra um crescimento de cerca de 42% no ano 2007. Foi nesse contexto que comemos a empreender esforos no sentido de convencer os parceiros de cooperao multilateral da necessidade de disponibilizao de fundos de emergncia, de que resultou a aprovao, pelo FMI, do Exogenous Shocks Facility (ESF), no valor total de USD 176 milhes, para alm da alocao de SDR 108.8 milhes, correspondentes a cerca de USD 170 milhes para fazer face a perdas de liquidez pelo Pas. Hoje, o mundo confronta-se com o desafio decorrente do reforo das medidas regulamentares baseadas em princpios de boas prticas. transparncia, responsabilidade social, prestao de contas, boa governao e melhoria da prestao das nossas agncias de rating. Caros Convidados, A realizao deste evento em Moambique tem lugar num momento em que o Pas se associa aos esforos globais visando a superao da crise. Este  um momento importante para o Pas, uma vez que, apesar das marcas da crise na nossa economia, novos desafios se impem naquilo que chamaramos de nova gerao de reformas direccionadas ao financiamento de projectos estruturantes, que podero permitir retornos sustentveis no crescimento do PIB, no emprego e na melhoria da qualidade de vida da populao. Nestes termos, declaro aberto o Workshop On Credit Risk & Legal Issues e ao mesmo tempo desejo a todos uma participao activa e um debate frutfero. MUITO OBRIGADO! 10

Title: 35th Anniversary of the Bank of Mozambique
text: Speech OF S.EXCIA O GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, ON THE OCCASION OF THE MAYO DAY OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE MAPUTO, MAY 17, 2010 GALA DINNER OFFERED AT INDY VILLAGE Your Excellere Prime Minister Excellence Venerating Mr President of the Supreme Court, Excellence Venerating Mr President of the Constitutional Council Excellence Honourable Mr Attorney General of the Republic, Your Excellency, Members of the Assembly of the Republic Excellencies Honourable Members of the Council of Ministers Excellencies Your Excellency, Your Excellency, Your Excellency of Maputo Province Excellence Your Excellency, Governor of Maputo City Excellence Your Excellere, President of maputo City Council Excellency, Former Governors of the Bank of Mozambique Excellency, Mr. Executive Secretary of SADC Excellence Your Excellency, Representatives of the Diplomatic Corps and Multilateral Institutions, Excellencies Your Honourable Governors and Deputy Governors of the Central Banks represented here Excellencies Your Excelleres, Members of the Board of Directors and Former Directors of the Bank of Mozambique Your Excellere, President of the Bank of Mozambique Workers' Association, Your Honour, Mr. Representative of the Trade Union Committee of the Bank of Mozambique Honourable Members of the Board of Directors Administration of Commercial Banks; Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Distinguished Guests; Ladies; Gentlemen It is with high honor that I have the privilege of using the floor at this Bank of Mozambique Day ceremony. Let me, first of all, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and, on my own behalf, welcome all of you, Excellencies, because you have accepted the invitation we have made to witness this act that marks the highest moment of the commemorations of the day when the Bank of Mozambique marks its 35th Anniversary. Special greeting is addressed to you, Your Prime Minister, for being the personality to whom His Excellency the President of the Republic has appointed him to represent him at this ceremony. I also address a special greeting, with your permission, to my colleagues, Governors of the central banks represented here and to the other foreign guests, whose presence in this act has not only meant that this event has been prioritised in their agendas, but also to make long journeys to reach Maputo. Excellencies Ladies Gentlemen As part of the celebrations of its 35th Anniversary, the BM has programmed a set of activities of a scientific, historical, political, socio-economic and cultural nature, embodied in events generally open to the public, with national and international participation, in Maputo and in other cities where our institution is represented. We started the Commemorative Day last year, involving all the workers of the Bank of Mozambique in an internal competition that allowed us in December, to determine the motto of these celebrations: PROMOTING THE VALORIZATION OF METICAL AND THE GROWTH OF THE NATIONAL ECONOMY. At the same time, an external competition allowed us to select the 35-year-old BM logo. After the due disclosure of the programme of commemorations and after we launched a public tender on scientific research in the fields of financial economy and banking law, in January 2010, our XXXIV Council Advisory, it was already under the aegis of these celebrations, where we evaluated various topics, with emphasis on the evaluation of the stage of the bankroll of the economy and the extension of financial services to rural areas and the role of infrastructure in this process. The program of commemorations of our 35th anniversary, contemplated the holding of lectures of a technical- scientific nature, open to the public, on topics of the specialty of the central bank, in higher education establishments, in Maputo, Beira and Nampula, as well as the organization of sessions of "Historias Vividas", at our headquarters, where there was the presentation of testimonies on aspects of the history of the Bank of Mozambique, made by former governors and retired workers who had served as Directors and Directors of the Bank. This set of sessions began last February with the testimonies of personalities who were part of the delegation of the Mozambique Liberation Front to the Lusaka Agreements signed by FRELIMO and the Portuguese Government on 7 September 1974, in which the creation of a central bank was called for the first time in Mozambique's history. The sessions of "Lived Stories" proved important to our institutional memory and a far-reaching experience in the passage of testimony to the new generations. Here is present at this ceremony, individualities who witnessed the signing of the Lusaka Agreements, to whom, with the permission of His Excellency the Prime Minister, I request that you stand up so that we can pay you the deserved tribute. I ask you to accompany me in a round of applause. These men and women are, numerically, a modest representation of the thousands of Mozambicans who have been involved in the struggle for the liberation of our homeland. Our institution is inspired by them for the difficult missions ahead. Our thanks! We have also organised sports tournaments that have moved various modalities, individual and collective, which have provided a wholesome relationship between ourselves and colleagues in the banking system and of different companies that have sympathetically agreed to join us. For them, our thank you! The exhibition of fine arts that has been on display under the seal of the Bank of Mozambique since last Friday at the National Museum of Art, is the corollary of a contest we launched within the framework of these festivities, through our Cultural Center. Beautiful works by Mozambican artists consecrated by us invited and interesting works by the young people who have competed are exhibited side by side, revealing a promising future in many of them. Excellencies Ladies Gentlemen In the performance of its functions, the Bank of Mozambique relates to a number of foreign entities and has the legally established responsibility to promote international financial relations. In view of this aspect, we include in the Commemorative Day international and regional events held in Maputo, namely a seminar on Credit Risk, co-organized by the World Bank and the MEFMI, the XXX Session of the SADC Central Bank Governors Committee and the International Symposium on the lessons of the financial crisis. These celebrations have also allowed us to promote the image of our country, the beauty of Maputo City, the richness, delight and variety of our gastronomy, the tourist itinerary of our historical monuments and other attractions that our beautiful Mozambique exhibits. It was imbued with this spirit that we included in the Commemorative Day a Cultural Gala brightened by the National Dance Company and performances of Timbila and Nyau, by groups purposely brought from Inhambane and Tete, taking into account the fact that these cultural manifestations were proclaimed by UNESCO, a world heritage site. From the north of the country, we had a show of N'ganda, from Metangula, Niassa province. For posterity, we made image and sound records and invited the press to report on each event; we produce a commemorative medal marking our 35th anniversary; we distribute the Catalogue of the Exhibition of Fine Arts and two compact discs that bring together, respectively, a selection of mozambican light music and songs from the Choral and Musical Groups of the BM; the Chronology of the Bank of Mozambique 1975-2010 was launched, in addition to the 35-year-old capulana of the Bank of Mozambique, which is present at this Gala Dinner, in the costumes displayed by the protocol agents. The balance we make of these six months of intense celebration through diverse events is positive and encouraging. In this process, we have consolidated the institutional culture of the Bank of Mozambique and our knowledge of the history of our country and the challenges of the international economy, in addition to having contributed to the strengthening of the love of each worker for our institution. Your Excellency Prime Minister Ladies Gentlemen Here are holders and members of the sovereignty bodies, and the governments of the province and city of Maputo, members of the Council of State, municipal leaders, leaders of political parties with parliamentary seats, governors and representatives of central banks of sadc, CPLP and other countries, ambassadors of countries with investments in the Mozambican financial sector, representatives of international bodies, representatives of financial institutions operating in Mozambique, representatives of professional associations, the private sector and civil society, academics, renowned individualities from the spheres of the economy, culture, sport and the media, as well as representatives of various media. From the Bank of Mozambique, we present the members of the Board of Directors, the Former Governors and Directors, Directors, Assistant Directors, Agency Managers and representatives of our Trade Union Committee and workers, as well as the members of our Coral Group. We are happy, I must say, to have you all, Excellencies, as part of our celebrations, of the 35th anniversary of the Bank of Mozambique. I hope that you will feel infected by the atmosphere of celebration and excitement that animates us. Thank you very much! Maputo, 17 May 2010.

Excelncias Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores No quadro das comemoraes do seu 35 Aniversrio, o BM programou um conjunto de actividades de carcter cientfico, histrico, poltico, scio-econmico e cultural, consubstanciadas em eventos geralmente abertos ao pblico, com participao nacional e internacional, em Maputo e nas demais cidades onde a nossa instituio est representada. Inicimos a Jornada Comemorativa no ano transacto, envolvendo todos os trabalhadores do Banco de Moambique num concurso interno que permitiu em Dezembro, apurarmos o lema destas celebraes: PROMOVENDO A VALORIZAO DO METICAL E O CRESCIMENTO DA ECONOMIA NACIONAL. Ao mesmo tempo, um concurso externo possibilitou que seleccionssemos o logotipo dos 35 anos do BM. Aps a devida divulgao do programa das comemoraes e depois de termos lanado um concurso pblico sobre investigao cientfica nos ramos de economia financeira e direito bancrio, em Janeiro de 2010, o nosso XXXIV Conselho Consultivo, realizou-se j sob a gide destas celebraes, onde aprecimos temas diversos, com destaque para a avaliao do estgio da bancarizao da economia e da extenso dos servios financeiros s zonas rurais e o papel das infraestruturas nesse processo. O programa de comemoraes do nosso 35 aniversrio, contemplou a realizao de palestras de carcter tcnico- cientfico, abertas ao pblico, sobre temas da especialidade do banco central, em estabelecimentos do ensino superior, em Maputo, Beira e Nampula, bem como a organizao de sesses de "Histrias Vividas", na nossa sede, onde houve a apresentao de depoimentos sobre aspectos da histria do Banco de Moambique, feita por Antigos-Governadores e por trabalhadores reformados que haviam exercido as funes de Administradores e Directores do Banco. Este conjunto de sesses iniciou em Fevereiro ltimo com os testemunhos de personalidades que integraram a delegao da Frente de Libertao de Moambique aos Acordos de Lusaka assinados pela FRELIMO e o Governo Portugus a 7 de Setembro de 1974, em cujo texto se preconizou, pela primeira vez na histria de Moambique, a criao de um banco central. As sesses de "Histrias Vividas" revelaram-se importantes para a nossa memria institucional e uma experincia de grande alcance na passagem do testemunho s novas geraes. Esto aqui presentes, nesta cerimnia, individualidades que testemunharam a assinatura dos Acordos de Lusaka, a quem, com a permisso de Sua Excelncia o Primeiro Ministro, solicito que se levantem para que lhes possamos prestar o tributo merecido. Peo que me acompanhem numa salva de palmas. Estes homens e mulheres so, numericamente, uma modesta representao dos milhares de moambicanos que se envolveram na luta pela libertao da nossa ptria. A nossa instituio inspira-se neles para as difceis misses que tem pela frente. O nosso muito obrigado! Organizmos tambm torneios desportivos que movimentaram vrias modalidades, individuais e colectivas, que proporcionaram um conviver salutar entre ns mesmos e os colegas do sistema bancrio e de diferentes empresas que simpaticamente aceitaram juntar-se a ns. Para eles, o nosso muito obrigado! A exposio de belas artes que est patente sob a chancela do Banco de Moambique desde a ltima sexta-feira no Museu Nacional de Arte,  o corolrio de um concurso por ns lanado no mbito destas festividades, atravs do nosso Centro Cultural. Esto expostos, lado a lado, belssimas obras de artistas moambicanos consagrados por ns convidados e interessantes trabalhos dos jovens que concorreram, revelando-se j um futuro promissor em muitos deles. Excelncias Minhas senhoras Meus senhores No exerccio das suas funes, o Banco de Moambique relaciona-se com uma srie de entidades estrangeiras e tem a responsabilidade legalmente estabelecida de promover relaes financeiras internacionais. Atentos a este aspecto, inserimos na Jornada Comemorativa eventos de carcter internacional e regional realizados em Maputo, nomeadamente, um seminrio sobre Risco de Crdito, co-organizado pelo Banco Mundial e o MEFMI, a XXX Sesso do Comit dos Governadores dos Bancos Centrais da SADC e o Simpsio Internacional sobre as lies da crise financeira. Estas celebraes tm tambm permitido promover a imagem do nosso pas, a beleza da Cidade de Maputo, a riqueza, delcia e variedade da nossa gastronomia, o roteiro turstico dos nossos monumentos histricos e outros atrativos que o nosso belo Moambique exibe. Foi imbudos desse esprito que inclumos na Jornada Comemorativa uma Gala Cultural abrilhantada pela Companhia Nacional de Dana e espectculos de Timbila e de Nyau, por grupos trazidos propositadamente de Inhambane e de Tete, tendo em conta o facto de estas manifestaes culturais terem sido proclamadas pela UNESCO, patrimnio da humanidade. Do norte do pas, tivemos um espectculo de N'ganda, de Metangula, provncia de Niassa. Para a posteridade, fizemos registos de imagem e de som e convidmos a imprensa a fazer reportagens de cada evento; produzimos uma medalha comemorativa que assinala o nosso 35 aniversrio; procedemos  distribuio do Catlogo da Exposio de Artes Plsticas e de dois discos compactos que reunem, respectivamente, uma seleco de msica ligeira moambicana e canes dos Grupos Coral e Musical do BM; foi lanada a Cronologia do Banco de Moambique 1975-2010, para alm da capulana dos 35 anos do Banco de Moambique, que se faz presente neste Jantar de Gala, nos trajes exibidos pelos agentes de protocolo. O Balano que fazemos destes seis meses de intensa comemorao atravs de diversificados eventos,  positivo e encorajador. Neste processo, consolidmos a cultura institucional do Banco de Moambique e o nosso conhecimento da histria do nosso pas e dos desafios da economia internacional, para alm de termos contribudo para o reforo do amor de cada trabalhador para com a nossa instituio. Excelentssimo Senhor Primeiro Ministroncias Minhas senhoras Meus senhores Esto aqui presentes titulares e membros dos rgos de soberania, e dos governos da provncia e cidade de Maputo, membros do conselho de Estado, dirigentes municipais, dirigentes dos partidos polticos com assento parlamentar, governadores e representantes de bancos centrais da SADC, da CPLP e de outros pases, embaixadores de pases com investimentos no sector financeiro moambicano, representantes de organismos internacionais, representantes das instituies financeiras que operam em Moambique, representantes de associaes profissionais, do sector privado e da sociedade civil, acadmicos, individualidades de renome das esferas da economia, da cultura, do desporto e da comunicao social, assim como representantes de diversos rgos de comunicao. Da parte do Banco de Moambique, presentes temos os membros do Conselho de Administrao, os Antigos Governadores e Administradores, Directores, Assistentes de Direco, Gerentes de Agncias e representantes do nosso Comit Sindical e dos trabalhadores, assim como os membros do nosso Grupo Coral. Estamos felizes, devo dizer, por vos termos a todos, Excelncias, como parte das nossas comemoraes, dos 35 anos do Banco de Moambique. Fao votos que se sintam contagiados pela atmosfera de festa e de entusiamo que nos anima. Muito Obrigado! Maputo, 17 de Maio de 2010.

Title: Agreement Signing with KFW
text: Lady Ute Heinbuch, Head of Cooperation at the German Embassy; Mr Ralf Orlik, Director of KfW; Representatives of the Ministries of Finance and Planning and Development, the Administrative Court and the Tax Authority of Mozambique; Distinguished Guests; Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen On behalf of the Government of Mozambique, I would like to express my thanks to the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany for the valuable and continuous contribution to the economic and social development of our country. We have just signed a financial contribution agreement for the participation of the Federal Republic of Germany in the Joint Macroeconomic Support Programme , in the amount of 18,000,000.00 (eighteen million euros). The partial amount of 15,000,000.00 (fifteen million euros) is intended for direct contribution to the State Budget and the remaining 3,000,000.00 (three million euros) is aimed at institutional capacity building and will be allocated to other priority areas of cooperation, ministry of planning and development (EUR 800,000), the Administrative Court (EUR 800,000), the Tax Authority of Mozambique (1 million), the Assembly of the Republic and Civil Society (EUR 400,000). The support of the German Government, represented by KFW, is part of the recommendations and commitments made between the Government of Mozambique and the 19 cooperation partners (G-19), whose Memorandum was signed in September 2009, aimed at implementing the Mozambican poverty reduction strategy. This is the fourth funding granted by the German Government under the joint macroeconomic support programme. This financial contribution complements the strategy of Mozambique-Germany, which defines education, decentralisation for rural development and sustainable economic development as priorities . It should be recalled that the Budget Aid Programme began, in its first phase, in 2004, with the signing of the Financing Agreement in the framework of Germany's agreement to the Joint Macro-Financial Support Mechanism for government, amounting to 7,500,000.00 (seven million and five hundred thousand euros). In the second stage, in June 2006, the Financial Contribution Agreement in the framework of Budget Aid was signed, in the amount of 20,000,000.00 (twenty million euros) and, in the third, in October 2008, in the amount of 30,000,000.00 (thirty million euros) all of these contracts take the form of donations to the country. German cooperation in Mozambique, in addition to support for the State Budget, takes place in other areas, namely the financial sector and technical assistance. In the financial system, it is worth highlighting the support in the creation and operation of GAPI, Socremo and Banco Terra, institutions focused on small and medium-sized enterprises. German cooperation also covers support for microfinance. In the field of technical assistance, we highlight the co-financing of studies and pilot projects for banks and microfinance institutions. The German contribution aims at poverty reduction in all its dimensions, supporting the implementation and monitoring of government-defined programmes. Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen With this contract we signed today, the German Government's support for the State Budget totals 77,000,000.00 (seventy-seven million euros), which represents a great commitment by the Government of Germany to the development purposes of our country, and it is expected that this support will translate into greater growth of the economy, reduction of poverty and unemployment levels. Finally, I would like to assure the German Government represented here by the Head of Cooperation of the German Embassy that the Government of Mozambique will mobilise all its means and efforts for the proper and speedy implementation of the resources made available to achieve the objectives set by the Government. Thank you very much
text_original: Excelentssima Senhora Ute Heinbuch, Chefe da Cooperao da Embaixada Alem; Excelentssimo Senhor Ralf Orlik, Director do KfW; Senhores representantes dos Ministrios das Finanas e da Planificao e Desenvolvimento, do Tribunal Administrativo e da Autoridade Tributria de Moambique; Distintos Convidados; Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores Em nome do Governo de Moambique, gostaria de expressar o meu agradecimento ao Governo da Repblica Federal da Alemanha, pela valiosa e contnua contribuio para o desenvolvimento econmico e social do nosso Pas. Acabmos de assinar um contrato de contribuio financeira referente  participao da Repblica Federal da Alemanha no Programa Conjunto de Apoio Macroeconmico, no montante de 18,000,000.00 (dezoito milhes de euros). Esta contribuio financeira complementa a estratgia da cooperao Moambique-Alemanha, que define como prioridades a Educao, a Descentralizao para o Desenvolvimento Rural e o Desenvolvimento Econmico Sustentvel. Importa recordar que o Programa de Ajuda ao Oramento teve incio, na sua primeira fase, em 2004, com a assinatura do Contrato de Financiamento no quadro da adeso da Alemanha ao Mecanismo Conjunto de Apoio Macro-Financeiro ao Governo, no valor de  7.500.000,00 (sete milhes e quinhentos mil euros). A cooperao alem em Moambique, para alm do apoio ao Oramento do Estado, desenrola-se em outras reas, nomeadamente, o sector financeiro e a assistncia tcnica. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores Com este contrato que hoje assinmos, o apoio do Governo alemo ao Oramento do Estado totaliza  77.000.000,00 (setenta e sete milhes de euros), o que representa um grande comprometimento do Governo da Alemanha para com os propsitos de desenvolvimento do nosso Pas, esperando-se que este apoio se traduza em maior crescimento da economia, reduo da pobreza e dos nveis de desemprego. Muito Obrigado

Title: End of the Economic Year 2009
text: Former Governors of the Bank of Mozambique; Members of the Board of Directors of the BM; Presidents of the Boards of Directors of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations; Mr. Delegated Directors of financial institutions; Former Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Distinguished Guests; Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen First of all, I would like to thank you for your honorable presence at this year-end toast ceremony, which we usually organise to carry out the preliminary balance sheet for the year that is about to end and to disclose to our partners in the financial system, to the market and to the general public our prospects for the new economic and financial year. Allow me on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf to take this opportunity to greet our Government for the achievements achieved in the year and for the bold economic policy measures it has adopted to mitigate the impact of the global financial and economic crisis on our economy, ensuring that Activities economic and financial developments were not greatly affected, which contributed to Mozambique being part of a limited group of developing countries that was able to ensure a robust growth rate. I also greet the credit institutions and financial corporations operating in our country for having been able to correctly interpret the policy signals that the Central Bank issued throughout the year, aimed at maintaining macroeconomic stability, in an adverse environment and of strong uncertainty. I am also responsible for the support and collaboration we have received from the business sector, economic and socio-professional associations, economic actors, the academic community, our multilateral and bilateral cooperation partners and the media. This interaction has enriched our strategic vision and the way we carry out our mission. My greetings extend still To bretton woods institutions and other international cooperation partners for having decided, in the face of the international crisis, to allocate additional funds to our country, strengthening our capacity to cover foreign trade, improving the position of our international reserves and contributing to greater leverage of the State budget. The committing of our international partners to the country's strategic objectives remains important for the successes that have been achieved in the various areas of activity economic and social impact. It is also worth mentioning other important events that took place in 2009, namely the holding of the fourth general and multi-party elections that open a new political cycle, which we want to take place, as well as the previous ones, in full harmony, peace and stability. Our appreciation also deserves the completion of important public enterprises of a structuring nature for the national economy, such as the bridge over the Zambezi River, which fills an important space in the process of consolidating the national market, more integrated and less asymmetric, from Rovuma to Maputo and from Zumbo to the Indian Ocean. Ladies, my dear guests The global financial crisis and recession in the more developed economies have reduced aggregate demand, spreading to African economies, mainly through larger deficits in their balance of payments. Phenomena such as the fall in commodity prices we export, the reduction in emigrant remittances, the low flow of foreign direct investment, the difficulties in accessing external credit by the business sector and the reduction of official financial aid to development programmes undermine the march of social and human development on our continent, as well as the millennium goals. Despite the various exceptional and incentive measures taken by governments and central banks around the world since the outbreak of the crisis in 2007, the challenges to be overcome in order to repay the aggregate demand curve to the desired level of equilibrium, in an environment of historically low interest rates, of inflation on negative ground, remain enormous, unemployment to reach alarming proportions and deficits in the budgets of states that perithet the sustainability of public debt. In fact, the current problems of the world macroeconomics closely resemble, in essence, the intricate labyrinth of the "liquidity trap" theorized by John Keynes in the context of the great depression of 1929. However, optimism seems to emerge from more recent information showing that the global recession tends to slow, based on forecasts from many reputable institutions, despite the cautions with which such forecasts should be read, given the high degree of uncertainty and risk that still hangs. Today, the impetus for global growth comes from emerging market economies, notably China, Brazil and India, countries that a few decades ago thickened the global statistics of poor and underdeveloped nations. In Africa and particularly in non-exporting countries of oil and precious metals, the crisis tends to erode the balance of payments and GDP growth, whose rates slowed to an average of 5.5% in 2008, compared to 6.4% in 2007, with growth of just 1.3% projected for 2009. In SADC countries, the general trend is one-digit inflation stability, lower interest rates and a reversal of the behavior of different currencies against the US Dollar, to the sense of appreciation, especially rand, which valued 27% until last November. The region continues, however, to be influenced by events that do little to optimize its high production and wealth potential. We hope that the ongoing actions, some of which will be the initiative of our statesmen, will provide the conditions for rapid governance stability in Zimbabwe and Madagascar, an important factor for rapid and harmonious economic development in the region. The strategic objectives of the region require large investments and these will only reach the desired proportion, let alone united, skilled and bold are our governments and economic agents operating in our countries. Ladies Distinguished Ladies Guests In 2008, when the international financial crisis manifested itself with greater acuity, the country was already experiencing a crisis resulting from rising fuel and food prices. Therefore, the mitigation measures adopted focused on stimulus on the budgetary and exchange rate side, reflecting our international reserves. The tax package then approved aimed to keep the economy functioning with relative normality, while interventions in the interbank foreign exchange market aimed to ensure internally offset the prices of imported products in the face of their rampant rise in the international market. In 2009, we negotiated with multilateral agencies access to additional resources, and the IMF granted a concessional loan of approximately USD 176 million, whose first tranche of USD 132 million was disbursed at the beginning of the second half of the year under the Exogenous Shock Facility. More recently, as part of the IMF's decision to improve the liquidity conditions of its members, the country received SDR 108.8 million, equivalent to about USD 170 million. This year, the reduction of our exports and the flow of foreign exchange to our economy, combined with difficulties in accessing external credits by companies operating in the country, has led the Bank of Mozambique to make available to the economy, through the Interbank Foreign Exchange Market, a total of USD 757 million to date, usd 89 million more than net sales made in the whole of 2008. In addition, we have made a relative relaxation of monetary policy, reducing, twice (in February and August), the coefficient of Mandatory Reserves and reviewing, also twice, our interest rates, placing them at 11.5% for the Ease of Transfer, and 3% for the Deposit Facility. These measures have made room for further expansion of credit to the economy, ensuring that many companies and economic projects meet their financing needs, maintaining their functioning and ensuring employment and income for thousands of families. Just to illustrate, by October 2009, credit to the economy had expanded annually by 55.5%, which represents the highest rate in recent years. At the level of the foreign exchange market, after a strong stability of the Metical in 2008, this year the exchange rate of the Metical against the US dollar recorded a depreciation of around 10%, a result that will certainly have contributed to the recovery of the competitiveness of our exports, in an international situation characterized by the fall in oil prices and import products. The exchange rate pressure that our market faced in 2009 is justified by a larger currency deficit recorded in our economy, in the face of the sharp reduction in our exports, combined with greater difficulties in accessing foreign credit by domestic companies. By the crossing of rates with the Rand, we found that the Metical accumulated a higher nominal depreciation (46%), explained, in part, by the strengthening of the South African currency against the U.S. dollar, by about 27%, favored by the increase in the prices of precious metals that that country produces, especially gold whose price was set over the year new historical highs. Rand's situation contributed to the long part of 2009, domestic prices in South Africa remained relatively low and the inflation band set as a target by the authorities would be respected. However, it is a challenge for all of us to monitor the sustainability of a strong Rand. In addition to interventions via the Interbank Foreign Exchange Market, the objective of managing liquidity and the Monetary Base, an instrumental variable of monetary policy, also counted on the contribution of interbank money market operations. As part of the reforms we have been making to increase the effectiveness of our monetary policy instruments, we have reviewed interbank money market regulations, easing the criteria for the association of banking institutions, the adequacy of the minimum amounts of market operations of the banks' initiative, the introduction of infra-weekly maturity operations in reverse reps and the operationalization of purchases of securities with resale agreement between bm and commercial banks, as well as the execution of reversible transactions between banks. These changes have brought new dynamism and deepening of the money market. Ladies My Distinguished Guest Lords Despite the adverse situation we face, the National Institute of Statistics found for the first nine months of 2009 a real growth of the economy above the initial forecasts, registering an annual expansion of 6.5%, supported primarily by the dynamics of agriculture, construction, hotels and restaurants, transport and communications, financial services and public administration. The good performance of the sector agricultural comfort us, for being the main source of employment and income for thousands of families, in addition to generating consumer goods for the vast majority of the population Mozambican. Moreover, this growth is consistent with the government's strategic option of making the country's development district a hub, in addition to being the initial reflection of the implementation of the Action Plan for Food Production (PAPA). As is common knowledge, the main mission of the WB is to ensure price stability, embodied in low and controlled inflation. Throughout 2009, inflation, obtained from the Maputo City Consumer Price Index, registered a downward trend: annual and average inflation was 2.6% and 3.4% in November, respectively, against 6.2% and 10.3% in December 2008. This trend has extended to The IPC Mozambique, which aggregates the cities of Maputo, Beira and Nampula, with annual inflation reduced from 11.8% in December 2008 to just 0.78% in October 2009. The core inflation indicator monitored by the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Mozambique, which excludes fruit and vegetable prices, also evolved in the same direction, from 5.8% in December 2008 to 2.1% in November 2009. The slowdown in inflation in the year in the past year reflects the combination of factors, highlighting the positive impact of macroeconomic measures taken by the authorities in the context of international financial and cereal crises, GDP growth above forecasts, the sharp fall in international commodity prices that the country imports and the slowdown in inflation in the Republic of South Africa. Ladies Gentlemen Distinguished Guests In 2009, pressure on demand for banknotes and coins in circulation was notorious. This phenomenon is linked to the changes taking place in the economy, greater financial decentralisation of the State, the implementation of local initiative investment budgets and greater use of Metical in the agricultural marketing of some products previously traded in the currencies of neighbouring countries. As a consequence, the expansion of the Monetary Base was significant in the period, although it did not generate inflation. As assessing provisional data for the first nine months of 2009, it is noted that the country's Balance of Payments was particularly affected by the effects of the financial crisis. Indeed, the value of foreign trade in goods, when compared to the period of 2008, fell by 26.5%, due to the sharp reduction in exports of goods by USD 760.5 million (down 37.2%), compared to a less sharp drop in imports, in the amount of USD 483.7 million (minus 18.3%). The country's current account deficit increased by USD 300 million to USD 861 million when transactions from major projects were excluded, reflecting the increase in deficits in partial accounts of goods and services by 46% and 14%, respectively, together with a 7% reduction in the inflows of external financial resources in the form of unilateral transfers. Despite the magnitude of the interventions we have made in the foreign exchange market, our Net International Reserves increased by USD 127 million, with their balance set at USD 1.770 million on 15 December 2009, corresponding to about 6 and 8 months of coverage of total imports of non-factor goods and services, when the operations of major projects are included and excluded , respectively. This strengthens the country's payment capacity abroad and the appropriate safeguards to meet the challenges of the future. I would like to take this opportunity once again to remind all economic actors that only by combining synergies to increase production and progressively replace imports by multiplying foreign exchange-generating activities for the country, we will be able to successfully face the current economic crisis and continue with the programme to combat poverty. Ladies Gentlemen Dear Guests The strengthening of banking supervision measures combined with the adoption of good practice sums by the managers of our credit institutions and financial corporations has proved important for minimising the impact of the crisis on our financial sector, with the main indicators of financial soundness maintaining the profile of a sound and stable system. In addition to regular inspections of credit institutions and financial corporations operating in the country, in order to improve the banking supervision methodology now in force, we have developed several tools that have now allowed the adoption of the risk-oriented supervision process, in addition to having produced the Manual of Good Practices of Corporate Govemance, which was distributed for consideration by the banking system. In addition to the vigilance we had on the system, the rigor and professionalism manifested by managers and employees of banking institutions allowed it to continue to show signs of solidity and robustness. Despite the strong expansion of credit to the economy in the year to September 2009, the ratio of non-domestic credit stood at 2%, the same as December 2008. The solvency ratio of the system increased to 16.6%, compared to 14% in December 2008, demonstrating that our system is relatively well capitalised and with enough antibodies to cope with the effects of the crisis. During the year and as part of our strategy for extending financial services To less favoured areas, we have once again witnessed the continued expansion of the network of bank counters to rural areas, with a but mozambicans have access to financial services and can channel their savings to the banking system. In the last 12 months, we have authorized the opening of 57 new bank branches in all provinces, thus moving to a total of 398 authorized branches, of which 340 are already in operation, covering all capital cities, municipal towns and 44 of the country's 128 districts, a number that could soon increase to 53 districts, as soon as the installation works are complete. Additionally, during the year we authorized the establishment of another Bank, passing the national total to 16, a Credit Cooperative and two Exchange Offices and the registration of five Savings and Loan Organizations and 23 Microcredit operators. After a long process of technical work and consultations with our banking partners, we hereby approve Notice No. 5/GBM/2009 of 10 June on the commission and other charges. This regulation plays a major role in credit institutions and financial corporations with a view to the adoption of good practices that promote competition, transparency and fairness in setting and publicising their commissions and other charges charged for the provision of financial services. The advent of the international financial crisis - it must be noted - has brought numerous challenges to financial institutions, financial managers, the governance bodies of the institutions and the regulatory and supervisory authorities that we have to interpret and internalise, challenges that will certainly make the financial systems different from those we had been having until 2007. In this context, Notice 5/GBM/2009 also establishes the duty of information to users of financial services about prices and conditions of services and products they hire, in a standardized and accessible manner, through the adoption of the common nomenclature, in addition to preventing the collection of some commissions and charges in the provision of essential banking services related to deposit accounts. We continued in 2009 with actions aimed at the creation of an interbank service company, and the respective memorandum of understanding between the BM and credit institutions was signed yesterday, yesterday, the 16th of this month, representing more than 90% of the banking business in the country. We intend with this society to guarantee economies of scale in access to banking services, reflecting the expected reduction of associated costs, speed and security in the various banking operations. With the shared use of the payment infrastructure, it will also be possible for customers of the banking system to make use of ATM or POS services in any of the banks operating in the country, with evident efficiency gains, in addition to the possibility of access to more and varied correlated services. Ladies My Distinguished Guest Lords As we have said, the forecasts suggest an optimistic scenario for 2010 with regard to the recovery of the world economy. The October 2009 World Economic Outlook points to an expansion of 3.1%, after a contraction of 1.1% expected for this year. Internally, monetary policy management will continue to take account of developments in the international environment, monitoring the potential out-of-the-way effects of the international financial crisis on the national economy in general and on the financial sector in particular. Monetary policy will be managed with a view to maintaining the low inflation gains achieved in 2009, in a regime of flexible exchange rates and prioritization of more robust real growth in our economy. We therefore believe that monetary policy will have to be managed cautiously, bearing in mind that it will be necessary to cushion the impact of the alignment of liquid fuel prices on the domestic market, which results from the gradual withdrawal of subsidies pre-announced by the Government. Our performance in 2010 will also be in line with the economic objectives set by the Government, which establish GDP growth of between 5.9% and 6.4%, an average annual inflation of 9.5% and a position of net international reserves that guarantees 5 months of coverage of total imports, when included in major projects. Our intermediate targets are a monetary expansion of 18.3%, compatible with a growth in credit to the economy slightly above the nominal GDP expansion and a growth of the Monetary Base, around 16%. We have also planned for the coming year a set of actions, and the following should be highlighted: a5 Continue to strengthen our model of forecasting and managing monetary and liquidity policy in particular, with a view to increasing the effectiveness of our interventions; a5 Continue with actions aimed at consolidating the operations of the interbank money market. In this context, greater emphasis will be on the operationalization of the permanent sale/purchase of securities on the secondary market between bm and commercial banks and the strengthening of human capital, at the level of the system, with a view to contributing to the greater professionalization of the interaction between operators through the certification of dealers; a5 Continue to monitor the developments and activities of the financial sector as a whole. The financing conditions for the State Budget and Balance of Payments for 2010 were previously negotiated during this year. With the completion of the first evaluation of this Facility, Mozambique now has at its disposal an amount equivalent to DES 14.2 million (approximately US22.6 million) With the group of programmatic support partners to the State budget, the G-19, we held important discussions throughout the year on strategic aspects of bilateral and global cooperation, and the monitoring and evaluation framework was improved. Ladies Distinguished Ladies Guests In 2010, the country completes 35 years of independence and the Bank of Mozambique will also mark the 35th anniversary of its existence, a fact that fills us with pride, because we are an institution that is born from the process of achieving national independence itself. In order to mark this event, allow me to take this opportunity to formally announce the launch of the celebrations of the 35th anniversary of the Bank of Mozambique, whose central activities will take place on 17 May. The commemoration initiative will be identified by a logo and a slogan, exhibited in this place where we are and the respective program will be filled by a set of cultural, sporting, scientific events, of historical evocation among others, being highlighted: a5 The 34th Advisory Board of the Bank of Mozambique, between 27 and 29 January 2010, is the last day reserved for the public debate on the theme " The Role of Infrastructure in the Promotion of Economic Development and in the Implementation of the Financial Sector and Services"; a5 The host of the Ordinary Meeting of the SADC Central Bank Governors Committee (CCBG); a5 The holding of an international symposium on the theme: "Framework of the International Financial Crisis, Challenges, Perspectives and Impact on African Economies", which will have the participation of the International Monetary Fund; a5 Holding an international seminar of the World Bank on the theme d2Credit Risk and Legal Issues"; a5 Lectures to be held in several cities of our country dealing with current themes of our economy; a5 Sporting events and cultural days, with emphasis on timbila and nyau, two numbers of our cultural mosaic considered world heritage; a5 Scientific research, literature and Fine Arts competitions, open to the public, as well as an exhibition of fine arts with the participation of some renowned Mozambican artists. Ladies Gentlemen Distinguished Guests Finally, I would like once again to thank all of you for accepting our invitation to share this moment of reflection. To all those present and their families, to the staff and other employees of the Bank of Mozambique and the financial sector, as well as to their families, go to my wishes for Happy Holidays and a Prosperous New Year. I invite you to accompany me in a toast to the health of all and to the prosperity of the Mozambican financial system. Thank you very much.
