Title: Speech at the National Seminar on the Evaluation of Programs of the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)
text: 1 Honourable Ambassadress of Mozambique in Italy, Honourable President of the International Fund for Agricultural Development Assessment Committee, Distinguished Members of the Board of the International Fund for Agricultural Development, Distinguished Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Planning & Development, Distinguished National Directors, Representatives of the Partners of Cooperation, Distinguished Members of the Assessment Committee of the International Fund for Agricultural Development, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, As we reached the end of the work under the National Seminar on the Assessment of Programs of the International Fund for Agricultural Development - IFAD, I would like to address my gratitude to all the participants for the valuable contributions herein presented. I am particularly very pleased to see in this conference room, apart from my fellow countrymen with whom I interact in the implementation of projects, our friends from the IFAD with whom I was in Rome during the analysis of the Assessment Report by the Board. I hope you are enjoying to be in Mozambique. The IFAD is one of the Governments main partner in pursuant to the rapid economic growth objective and poverty reduction, primarily that affecting the rural areas. I should highlight that IFAD projects are within the top priority activities of the Government Economic and Social Program. We have managed to join together in the same agenda, the IFAD members of the Board, Members of the IFAD Assessment Committee, IFAD staff members directly involved in the Fund operations to Mozambique, members and representatives of the Government in the key areas for the success of the programs agreed and financed by the IFAD, project coordinators, direct beneficiaries of the IFAD financed programs and managers of funds disbursement processes. After about a day and half of work, I think the objectives of this Seminar have been satisfactorily achieved. 2 We are grateful for the satisfactory evaluation assigned by the Assessment Committee. However, we recognize the new approaches, replication of experiences of success and increased efforts to overcome the problem of poor program sustainability and to achieve more satisfactory results, including the systemic performance perspective on the chain of values in rural area. Ladies and Gentlemen, In the course of our work, we divided ourselves in groups in order to enable the debate of topics of great importance such as the relationship between IFAD and other stakeholders, the impact and relevance of IFADs programs and the recommendations for future actions. The working groups recommend us to proceed with the actions and programs underway, with the relevant adjustments. This new approach requires greater involvement of the private sector and the civil society as implementers of development programs, which implies its institutional capacity building, technical assistance, and assignment of responsibilities in accordance with the mandate of each stakeholder. It has been considered important to define better the target group, in order to maximize the impact of IFAD programs, as well as to replicate the well succeeded pilot-projects, extending IFAD actions to more regions of the country. In this context, the experience of the Support Program for Agricultural Markets and the Project of Banco de Sofala, should be focused and replicated. As regards the relevance and pertinent adjustments for IFAD programs better results in Mozambique, the discussion pointed to the need of a clear definition of the role of each stakeholder and the target groups capacity building, through training programs, extension services, association for a major program adequacy, maximization of benefits and defense of its interests. This adjustment should focus on its economic, social and ecological dimensions, allowing the target group major productivity, diversification, access to energy, infrastructures, financial services, education, health and knowledge for adaptation to climate changes and environment protection. For such purpose, it is important that the design and implementation of projects takes into account the need of space for entrepreneurship and innovation. 3 Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, This seminar allowed us a frank dialogue and identification of problems and challenges of future cooperation with the IFAD. The lack of connection between the producers and the markets is still an enormous challenge in the rural area. Therefore, the improvement of public infrastructures is the major challenge to materialize the so expected linkage between both segments and, to increase agricultural productivity. I wish a pleasant journey to the team going to Sofala Province and wish it be a good opportunity to know other realities of our beautiful country, apart from the visit to the existing projects in that region. For those who continue with discussions this afternoon, on the Country Strategic Opportunities Programme (COSOP) for the period 2011-2015, I wish the debate to bring positive results. I wish all participants to proceed with good work towards rural development and Mozambique continuous progress. Maputo, May 25, 2010.

Title: Speech at the Official Announcement of the Coordinated Direct Investment Survey (CDIS)
text: Dear Sir Arthur Cousins, SWIFT Board Member Esteemed Sir David Pryce, Regional Director for Africa Dear Guests My Ladies and Gentlemen I welcomed the invitation addressed to me to address this opening ceremony of the SWIFT African Regional Conference, which takes place under the motto "Transforming the future: optimising the market, local, regional and global". I would like to welcome all the delegates present in this room, especially the representatives of african countries. As hosts of the SWIFT African Regional Conference, we are deeply honoured to welcome you to Maputo and wish you a great stay. The high interest and participation in this Conference attests to the sensitivity of our governments and financial institutions to the current information technology issues that we use to better prepare our countries to meet the challenges of globalisation and regional and continental integration. Information technologies are now an indispensable platform for the activity of various sectors of activity, including the financial sector and payment systems. SWIFT is an integral part of the technological infrastructure that our institutions use for the settlement and clearing of values, with a view to better serving customers, to safeguard risks associated with our activity and, in general, to contribute to the improvement of the business environment in our countries, an important factor to attract the investment we need to comply with our economic and social development plans. In the globalised world in which we live, information technology supports are increasingly harmonised, so it is urgent to improve them in order to reduce transaction costs and enable adequate risk management, both domestically and regionally and internationally. Ladies Gentlemen Our economies are still too small in the context of world production and trade. Our countries are generally very sensitive to exogenous shocks, whether they are from adverse natural factors, such as those induced by conjunctural changes or international trade rules. Our position in the world economy remains, roughly speaking, of producers of primary products, whose access to international markets still faces various barriers and inequalities. This makes our countries highly dependent on the help of the international community, especially in the form of donations. Mozambique, began in 1987 deep reforms, the results of which, at the level of the financial sector, are already visible, either by evaluating the number of operators, as well as of financial products available on the market. In fact, thanks to substantial changes that we have been making, today we have a diverse range of credit institutions and financial corporations offering competitive products and services in the national and international markets. In the field of information technologies, we have now evolved into a financial system where most transactions are done in real time, when until the early 1990s, they were carried out using telex and other rudimentary data transmission mechanisms. The management of nostros accounts improved after our addition to SWIFT in 1995. At that time, only 3 banks operated with SWIFT, but after about 10 years, we can say with satisfaction that all credit institutions authorized to operate in the country, make their operations with the outside through this system, which is symptomatic the improvement of the management of the country's operations with abroad. The entry of new operators into our banking system, with strong implementation abroad, brought added value to the national financial system, given that the square of Maputo and other provincial capitals, have become connected with the main international financial markets. The evolution of the financial system has placed the Bank of Mozambique, as central bank, the challenge of introducing monetary and exchange policy management instruments more suited to the dynamics of our market and its transformations. We continue to modernise our payment, clearing and settlement system, as well as strengthening banking supervision, to the size of our financial market. Ladies Gentlemen Improving the efficiency of financial services is an important lever for the attraction of more foreign investment and other financial flows to our countries. A strong and solid infrastructure is now an important factor in creating new opportunities for our countries to find alternative sources of funding. In this context, the SWIFT system is an important element of this infrastructure and should therefore be prepared to participate in the definition of development strategies for our markets that have been carried out in many countries and in the various sub-regions of Africa. Other challenges facing the SWIFT system and other banking management solutions today is ensuring adequate integration between front, middle and back office systems of operations, to enable efficient management, as well as access to information on nostros accounts, in real time. At sadc level, some countries have already implemented or are in an advanced implementation phase of RTGS payment systems. SWIFT should be an important partner for improving the efficiency of payment systems and above all for risk minimisation. Recognizing the importance of having good infrastructure in Africa, it is up to us Africans to develop common and/or harmonised projects in this area. In the region of which we are a part, particularly at the level of the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the preconditions for the process of harmonising some financial infrastructures are already in place. In fact, there are several projects for harmonisation of procedures at central bank level, such as payment systems, settlement and clearing, information and communication technologies and banking supervision. To finish, I am convinced that this meeting will produce the expected results and that cooperation between our institutions in the field of interbank telecommunications for the development of a modern, reliable and compatible financial platform in the main international markets is strengthened. The topics to be addressed and the level of the presenters are a guarantee that the debates will be frank and from here we will all be enriched. Once again, I wish you a good stay in Maputo and in this way, I officially declare the Regional Conference open Africana da SWIFT. Thank you very much. Maputo, 22 May 2006.
text_original: Estimado Senhor Arthur Cousins, Membro do Board da SWIFT Estimado Senhor David Pryce, Director Regional Para frica Caros Convidados Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores Aceitei com agrado o convite que me foi endereado para dirigir esta cerimnia de abertura da Conferncia Regional Africana da SWIFT que se realiza sob o lema Transformando o futuro: optimizando o mercado, local, regional e global. Quero desejar as boas-vindas a todos os delegados presentes nesta sala, em especial os representantes dos pases africanos. Na qualidade de hospedeiros da Conferncia Regional Africana da SWIFT, sentimo-nos profundamente honrados por acolher-vos em Maputo e desejamos que tenham uma ptima estadia. O elevado interesse e participao nesta Conferncia, atesta a sensibilidade dos nossos Governos e das instituies financeiras para as questes actuais de tecnologias de informao que utilizamos para melhor preparar os nossos pases para enfrentar os desafios da globalizao e de integrao regional e continental. As tecnologias de informao so hoje uma plataforma indispensvel para a actividade de vrios sectores de actividade, incluindo o sector financeiro e os sistemas de pagamentos. O SWIFT  parte integrante da infra- estrutura tecnolgica que as nossas instituies utilizam para a liquidao e compensao de valores, na perspectiva de melhor servir os clientes, acautelar riscos associados  nossa actividade e, de uma maneira em geral, contribuir para a melhoria do ambiente de negcios nos nossos pases, factor importante para atrair o investimento que necessitamos para o cumprimento dos nossos planos de desenvolvimento econmico e social. No mundo globalizado em que vivemos, os suportes das tecnologias de informao so cada vez mais harmonizados, da que urge aperfeio-los com vista  reduo dos custos de transaco e permitir uma adequada gesto dos riscos, tanto no plano domstico, como nos planos regional e internacional. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores, As nossas economias continuam a ser demasiado pequenas no contexto da produo e do comrcio mundial. Os nossos pases so, no geral, bastante sensveis a choques exgenos, seja os que decorrem de factores naturais adversos, como os induzidos por alteraes conjunturais ou ainda das regras do comrcio internacional. O nosso posicionamento na economia mundial continua a ser, grosso modo, de produtores de produtos primrios, cujo acesso aos mercados internacionais, enfrenta ainda vrias barreiras e desigualdades. Esta caracterstica torna os nossos pases altamente dependentes da ajuda da comunidade internacional, sobretudo sob forma donativos. Moambique, iniciou em 1987 profundas reformas, cujos resultados, ao nvel do sector financeiro, so j visveis, seja avaliando a quantidade de operadores, como de produtos financeiros disponveis no mercado. Com efeito, merc de alteraes substanciais que temos vindo a realizar, contamos hoje com um leque diversificado de instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras que oferecem produtos e servios competitivos nos mercados nacional e internacional. No domnio das tecnologias de informao, evolumos hoje para um sistema financeiro em que a maior parte das transaces so feitas em tempo real, quando at principio dos anos 90, as mesmas eram efectuadas com recurso a telex e outros mecanismos de transmisso de dados rudimentares. A gesto das contas nostros melhorou, aps a nossa adeso  SWIFT, em 1995. Nessa altura, somente 3 bancos operavam com o SWIFT, mas volvidos cerca de 10 anos, podemos afirmar com satisfao que todas as Instituies de Crdito autorizadas a operar no Pas, fazem as suas operaes com o exterior atravs deste sistema, o que  sintomtica a melhoria da gesto das operaes do Pas com o exterior. A entrada de novos operadores ao nosso sistema bancrio, com forte implantao no exterior, trouxe valor acrescentado ao sistema financeiro nacional, dado que a praa de Maputo e de outras capitais provinciais, passaram a estar conectadas com as principais praas financeiras internacionais. A evoluo do sistema financeiro colocou ao Banco de Moambique, na sua qualidade de Banco Central, o desafio de introduzir instrumentos de gesto de polticas monetrias e cambiais mais adequados  dinmica do nosso mercado e s suas transformaes. Continuamos a modernizar o nosso sistema de pagamentos, de compensao e liquidao de valores, para alm de termos reforado a superviso bancria, para a dimenso do nosso mercado financeiro. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores, A melhoria da eficincia dos servios financeiros  uma importante alavanca para a atraco de mais investimentos estrangeiros e outros fluxos financeiros para os nossos pases. Uma infra-estrutura forte e slida  hoje um factor importante para a criao de novas oportunidades para os nossos pases encontrarem fontes alternativas de financiamento. Neste contexto, o sistema SWIFT assume-se como sendo um importante elemento dessa infra-estrutura, devendo por isso, estar preparada para participar na definio de estratgias de desenvolvimento dos nossos mercados que vem sendo levado a efeito em muitos pases e nas diversas sub regies de frica. Outros desafios que hoje se colocam ao sistema SWIFT e outras solues de gesto bancria,  a garantia de integrao adequada entre os sistemas front, middle e back office das operaes, para permitir uma gesto eficiente, bem como o acesso de informao sobre as contas nostros, em tempo real. Ao nvel de SADC, alguns pases j implementaram ou esto numa fase avanada de implementao, dos sistemas de pagamentos RTGS. A SWIFT deve assumir-se como um parceiro importante para a melhoria da eficincia dos sistemas de pagamentos e sobretudo para a minimizao do risco. Reconhecendo-se a importncia de termos em frica boas infra-estruturas, cabe a ns, os Africanos, o desafio de desenvolvermos projectos comuns e/ou harmonizados nesta rea. Na regio de que fazemos parte, particularmente a nvel da Comunidade de Desenvolvimento da frica Austral (SADC), esto j criadas as pr-condies para o processo de harmonizao de algumas infra-estruturas financeiras. Com efeito, encontram-se numa fase de implementao, vrios projectos de harmonizao de procedimentos a nvel dos Bancos Centrais, de que so exemplos, os sistemas de pagamentos, liquidao e compensao, tecnologias de informao e comunicao e superviso bancria. Para terminar, manifesto a minha convico de que este encontro produza os resultados esperados e que sai reforada a cooperao entre as nossas instituies, no domnio das telecomunicaes interbancrias para o desenvolvimento de uma plataforma financeira moderna, fivel e compatvel com as utilizadas nas principais praas internacionais. Os temas a abordar e o nvel dos apresentadores so uma garantia de que os debates sero francos e daqui sairemos todos enriquecidos. Mais uma vez, desejo-vos boa estadia em Maputo e deste modo, Declaro oficialmente aberta a Conferncia Regional Africana da SWIFT. Muito Obrigado. Maputo, 22 de Maio de 2006.

Title: Intervention at a Business Dinner hosted by the High Commission of the Republic of South Africa in Maputo on Nelson Mandela Day
text: President of the National Institute of Statistics Vice-President of the National Institute of Statistics Executive Director and Board Member of the Banco de Mocambique Executive Directors of Credit Institutions General and Financial Managers of Non-Financial Institutions Ladies and Gentlemen First of all, allow me on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Banco de Mocambique and in my personal name, to thank you for your presence in this ceremony for official announcement of the Coordinated Direct Investment Survey - CDIS. Coincidently, this ceremony takes place in a date of particular importance for the people of africa. Therefore, I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate our Government for the diligence that has demonstrated, either within the SADC region as well as within the Continent as whole, in the context of the African Union, in combined efforts with other African countries for a more united africa around the common purposes, namely the fight against poverty, amongst other current challenges. Ladies and Gentlemen, We are very grateful for your presence since it consolidates the institutional relationship between the National Institute of Statistics and the Banco de Mocambique, two entities of the Statistical National System, as well as the institutions herein present, which are generally information providers. Your presence also confirms your commitment in relation to the improvement of the quality, timeliness and coverage of Mozambiques official statistics, a relatively young country that still has a long way to go in this domain. I particularly thank, in this occasion, the presence of the President and Vice-President of the National Institute of Statistics, the institution with which the Banco de Mocambique has a strategic cooperation in their capacity as the leading entities of the Statistical National System. The official announcement of the Coordinated Direct Investment Survey taking place today is a clear evidence of this relationship. The Banco de Mocambique, on the basis of a protocol of cooperation signed with the National Institute of Statistics, has been compiling and publishing externai sector statistics, described in our Balance of Payments, an important instrument for macroeconomic management, formulation of policies and for entrepreneurial activity, provided that it details the transactions performed by the resident business operators with the rest of the world. The measures to mitigate the effects of the economic and financial crises worldwide recently adopted by our Government took into account the statistical information of all sectors of the economy, especially the externai sector statistics, considering the countrys externai dependence. The Central Bank permanent activity and, precisely, the analysis and projections conducted by its Monetary Policy Committee are based on data produced by the institutions herein present, which shows, once again, the relevance of information in decision taking process. Hence, we, as the Statistical National System, address special attention to the continuous improvement of the process of collection, compilation, analysis and timely dissemination of statistical information, with minus costs and efficiency gains deriving from a coordinated action, likewise we did in the preparation of the survey announced today focused on direct investment information. The direct investment multiplying effect is recognized in the increase of the countrys productive capacity, employment opportunities, promotion of technological progress and improvement of externai position, either via exports or via substitution of imports. In economies with characteristics like ours, direct investment also constitutes one of the competitive forms of externai financing. Besides, I recall that in the Consultative Annual Meeting of the Banco de Mocambique held in Beira city, in January 2009, we discussed with different sectors the forms to increase competitiveness of the Mozambican economy. We have concluded that the structuring projects, which add value, generate new jobs, more public revenues and improve our international reserves, are the ones to be prioritized and treated with prudence. Ladies and Gentlemen The survey that we are announcing today derives from the need to update information on direct investment, which will contribute for the authorities to be aware of its role and impact on our economy, either during the course, as well as in the subsequent stage when the projects enter into operation. We are pleased to note that, notwithstanding the current international adverse situation, the foreign direct investment in Mozambique has grown at an annual average of 44% over the three last years ended in 2009, having the cumulative inflow in the period amounted to USD 3.4 billion, including mega projects, or USD 1.7 billion, excluding their contribution. We need to proceed with economic reforms, improve the business environment in order to be competitive in investment attraction and regain the inflow leveis recorded before the international economic and financial crisis break out. The Coordinated Direct Investment Survey is a global initiative aimed to collect information on the stock of direct investment and other supplementary information regarding private externai debt, holdings abroad, amongst other financial assets and liabilities of the country in relation to the rest of the world, supported by the International Monetary Fund, in partnership with the World Bank, European Central Bank, the Eurostat, amongst other institutions. Mozambique was selected together with 130 countries to conduct this survey, which should observe the same methodological principies and reference period, December 31, 2009. Besides the feeling of honour for the inclusion of our country in the leading group, our responsibilities and commitment are also enormous as regards the improvement of the coverage, quality and comparability of our statistics, especially those of the externai sector. In this context, there will be a collection of broad covering and harmonized data on (i) Direct investment in Mozambique; (ii) granted and received loans; (iii) deposits of residents at non- residents; (iv) granted and received commercial credits; and (v) foreign bilis held by residents. Likewise, the companies in possession of data on direct investment abroad should report it in the same basis, so as to allow its comparability with other countries involved in the initiative. The survey will not only contribute to improve the externai sector statistics, but it will also provide important elements for analysis of direct investment dynamics in Mozambique, thus enabling the authorities to reinforce the analytical framework of externai sustainability, or yet the analysis of the trend of private capital flows, in which the exchange rate is an important variable. Therefore, I would like to invite everyone to participate, between May 26 and June 24, 2010, in the survey that we announce together with the National Institute of Statistics, covering a sample of financial and non-financial institutions, with externai assets and/or liabilities, located in Maputo City and in Nampula, Sofala and Tete Provinces. The survey will be conducted by technical staff of the Banco de Mocambique. The survey detailed technical presentation is planned for the second part of this session. In conclusion, in the context of the celebrations of the 35th anniversary of the Banco de Mocambique, allow me to address special thanks to all our partners and the public and private institutions for their collaboration and, wish that we proceed with our efforts for the benefit of our economy and the country as a whole. Thank you for your attention and wish everyone a good work

Title: Intervention at the Agreement Signing with the German Development Bank (KFW)
text: High Commissioner of South Africa, Excellency; Former Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique Distinguished Guests; Ladies Gentlemen. Let me, first of all, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, welcome and thank the High Commissioner of South Africa for the organisation of this event, bringing together in the same room, entrepreneurs from South Africa and Mozambique, two neighbouring countries with a long history of economic connection, to jointly reflect on the integration process that takes place in our countries and, above all, to assess existing investment opportunities, particularly in Mozambique which, once exploited, can contribute to overcoming the challenges of poverty and underdevelopment. This meeting takes place at a time when at international level the signs of recovery in global economic activity are beginning to be robust after years of great economic and financial crisis, the effects of which in countries such as ours have been stronger in the external sector, particularly through the drop in export revenue stemming from the fall in international prices of almost all export products. The fall in prices was accompanied by a reduction in their demand, which made evident the need to strengthen south-south partnerships, as a way to minimize, in the future, the problems of access to international markets and price volatility in those squares. This initiative is therefore not only timely, but it is also extremely important because it will allow us to discuss informally what can be done in order to create a favourable environment for the development of the private sector of the SADC member countries. Dear Guests; Ladies; Gentlemen Mozambique is a small open economy and heavily dependent on abroad, a factor that makes it very vulnerable to external shocks, a situation that became more evident in the last three years when we were confronted, first by the worsening prices of cereals, after fuels and very recently, with the impact of the global economic and financial crisis. Despite this adverse context, thanks to fiscal, monetary and sectoral measures taken by the authorities, gross domestic product continued to grow at robust rates, with an annual expansion of 9.5% in the First quarter of 2010, justified by the strong dynamism in the agriculture, manufacturing, trade and repair services and transport and communications sectors. Inflation and the exchange rate, which after a period of strong stability, have been a relatively bullish development throughout 2010, basically reflecting developments in indicators, taking into account the anti-crisis measures taken in 2008/9 aimed at protecting the economy from external shocks. Available data show that in the First quarter of this year, exports grew in annual terms by 13.3% which, in the face of a 9.5% drop in imports and an increase in net inflows of external income, resulted in an improvement in the current account deficit by about 39%, thus offsetting the decrease in capital inflows in the form of Foreign Direct Investment which was around USD 175 million. Distinguished Guests, Ladies Gentlemen The financial sector plays an important role in reducing the country's external dependence. In this context, the Central Bank has been adopting monetary and exchange rate policies aimed at contributing to the maintenance of macroeconomic stability. In addition, as supervisors of commercial banks and non-financial banking institutions we will continue to require institutions to maintain adequate capitalization levels and to observe internationally acceptable prudential ratios, in addition to professional management according to international standards. We also promote financial inclusion by taking advantage of the Government's effortto provide infrastructure through the extension of energy networks, fibre optics and other media, as well as the physical expansion of commercial bank branches, with the aim of promoting savings in rural areas. I can share with you the fact that since the launch of the strategy to bankroll our economy, national banking has responded positively to the challenges, extending its presence in the districts, supporting the productive sector and granting credit to the private sector. For example, the average annual growth of credit to the economy has been above 40% in the last two years. In addition, the Central Bank and Commercial Banks are involved in the creation of an interbank service company that will manage atm's network infrastructure, POS, as well as the development of mobile banking and other financial products and services at low costs, taking advantage of economies of scale resulting from the combination of synergies. Dear Guests, Ladies Gentlemen The geographical location of Mozambique gives the country immense responsibilities to its people and also to the vile countries. In fact, Mozambique extends from north to south on a coast of about 3,000 kilometers, which has beautiful seascapes and deep-water ports, from which development corridors depart that facilitate foreign trade in the hinterland countries. Inside it has extensive areas of arable soils, forests and savannas, with precious woods and wildlife and an underground that hosts immense known and other undiscovered natural resources, among minerals and hydrocarbons. The big questions that arise are among others the following: a5 Why do we remain poor with all this tourist, agricultural, mineral resource and geographical location advantages? a5 Why does the country remain a net importer of cereals and other agricultural products when we have extensive areas of arable land to produce the same products locally and thereby alleviate the deficit in our balance of payments? a5 Why does our region with more than 200 million inhabitants have intra-regional trade of less than 10%? a5 Why the level of investment, as a percentage of GDP, is in Africa and particularly in SADC, below 20%, creating a large infrastructure gap. The questions are easy to ask, but the answers not at all. However, I interpret this meeting of South African investors with Mozambicans as part of the solution or answer to the questions behind the issues. I think we need to be together. We need to eliminate information asymmetries. We need to share our vast experiences and talk about what each one can do or offer to develop our countries. We need to embody and shape the ongoing regional integration process by implementing the existing strategic plan and carrying out common and integrated projects, particularly cross-border trade that could boost regional trade. In this context, the authorities of sadc member countries need to proceed with macroeconomic and institutional reforms that allow more investment to be made to the region. It is also imperative to boost and deepen the financial sector so that it can develop a modern and strong capital market in order to bridge the financial gap in the region's crucial infrastructure projects. The Bank of Mozambique considering national, regional and international developments has been continuously reviewing the main financial legislation in order to adapt it to new challenges and trends, as well as allowing more financial institutions to enter the sector , thereby promoting greater competition. Also in the framework of the ongoing reforms, let me inform you that we already have a draft regulation of the foreign exchange law in the assessment phase by the various stackholders of the country, including cta and it is intended that the regulation to be approved is an important instrument in the dynamic of foreign trade and in the discipline of the functioning of the foreign exchange market. These are the points I wanted to share with your Excellencies Thank you and a good dinner for everyone. Maputo, 17 May 2010
text_original: Senhor Alto Comissrio da frica do Sul, Excelncia; Exmos Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique Distintos Convidados; Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores. Permitam-me, antes de mais, que em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, saude e agradea ao Alto Comissrio da frica do Sul pela organizao deste evento, juntando numa mesma sala, empresrios da frica do Sul e Moambique, dois pases vizinhos e com uma longa histria de ligao econmica, para em conjunto reflectirem sobre o processo de integrao que tm lugar nos nossos pases e, sobretudo, avaliar as oportunidades de investimento existentes, particularmente, em Moambique que, uma vez exploradas, podem contribuir para venceremos os desafios da pobreza e do subdesenvolvimento. Este encontro tem lugar num perodo em que a nvel internacional comeam a ser robustos os sinais de recuperao da actividade econmica mundial aps anos de grande crise econmica e financeira, cujos efeitos em pases como o nosso foram mais forte ao nvel do sector externo, particularmente atravs da baixa da receita de exportaes devido  queda dos preos internacionais de quase todos os produtos de exportao. A queda dos preos foi acompanhada pela reduo da procura dos mesmos, o que tornou evidente a necessidade de se reforar as parcerias sul-sul, como forma de se minimizar, no futuro, os problemas de acesso aos mercados internacionais e a volatilidade de preos naquelas praas. Por isso, esta iniciativa, no s se revela oportuna, como tambm  de extrema importncia pois, ir nos permitir discutir de forma informal o que pode ser feito de modo a criar um ambiente favorvel para o desenvolvimento do sector privado dos pases membros da SADC. Caros Convidados; Minhas Senhoras; Meus Senhores, Moambique  uma pequena economia aberta e fortemente dependente do exterior, factor que o torna bastante vulnervel aos choques externos, situao que se tornou mais evidente, nos ltimos trs anos, quando fomos confrontados, primeiro pelo agravamento dos preos dos cereais, depois dos combustveis e muito recentemente, com o impacto da crise econmica e financeira mundial. Apesar deste contexto adverso, merc das medidas de mbito fiscal, monetrio e sectorial tomadas pelas autoridades, o Produto Interno Bruto continou a crescer a taxas robustas, tendo registado uma expanso anual de 9.5% no I trimestre de 2010, justificada pelo forte dinamismo registado nos sectores de agricultura, indstria transformadora, servios de Comrcio e Reparao e Transportes e Comunicaes. A inflao e a taxa de cmbio, que aps um perodo de forte estabilidade, tm ao longo de 2010 conhecido uma evoluo relativamente altista, reflectindo, basicamente, a evoluo correctiva destes indicadores, tendo em conta as medidas anti-crise tomadas em 2008/9, que visavam proteger a economia dos choques externos. Dados disponveis mostram que no I trimestre do corrente ano, as exportaes cresceram em termos anuais em 13.3% o que, perante uma queda das importaes em 9.5% e aumento das entradas lquidas de rendimentos externos, resultou na melhoria do dfice da conta de transaces correntes em cerca de 39%, compensando, deste modo, o decrscimo registado na entrada de capitais na forma de Investimento Directo Estrangeiro que foi de cerca de USD 175 milhes. Distintos Convidados, Minhas senhoras, Meus senhores, O sector financeiro desempenha um papel importante na reduo da dependncia externa do Pas. Neste particular, o Banco Central, tem vindo a adoptar polticas no domnio monetrio e cambial, tendentes a contribuir para a manuteno da estabilidade macroeconmica. Adicionalmente, na qualidade de supervisor dos bancos comerciais e das Instituies bancrias no financeiras continuaremos a exigir que as instituies mantenham nveis de capitalizao adequados e observem rcios prudenciais aceitveis internacionalmente, para alm de uma gesto profissional segundo padres internacionais. Promovemos igualmente a incluso financeira, tomando vantagens do esforo do Governo na disponibilizao de infra-estruturas, atravs da extenso das redes de energia, fibra ptica e demais meios de comunicao, bem como a expanso fsica dos balces dos bancos comerciais, com o intuito de promover a poupana nas zonas rurais. Posso partilhar com os presente o facto de que desde o lanamento da estratgia de bancarizao da nossa economia, a banca nacional tem respondido positivamente aos desafios, alargando a sua presena nos distritos, apoiando o sector produtivo e concedendo crdito ao sector privado. Por exemplo, o crescimento mdio anual do crdito  economia situou-se nos ltimos dois anos acima de 40%. Adicionalmente, o Banco Central e os Bancos Comerciais esto envolvidos na criao de uma sociedade interbancria de servios que ir gerir a infra-estrutura de rede de ATMs, POS, bem como o desenvolvimento de mobile banking e outros produtos e servios financeiros a custos baixos, tirando vantagens das economias de escala resultantes da conjugao de sinergias. Caros Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, A localizao geogrfica de Moambique atribui ao Pas imensa responsabilidades para com o seu povo e tambm para com os pases visinhos. Com efeito, Moambique extende-se do norte ao sul numa costa com cerca de 3 mil quilmetros, a qual dispe de lindas paisagens martimas e portos de guas profundas, donde partem corredores de desenvolvimento que facilitam o comrcio externos dos pases do hinterland. No interior detm extensas reas de solos arveis, florestas e savanas, com preciosas madeiras e fauna bravia e um subsolo que hospeda imensos recursos naturais conhecidos e outros ainda no descobertos, entre minerais e hidrocarbonetos. As grandes questes que se colocam so entre outras as seguintes:  Porqu  que continuamos ento pobres com todo este potencial turstico, agrcola, de recursos minerais e vantagens de localizao geogrfica?  Porqu  que o pas continua sendo um importador lquido de cereais e outros produtos agrcolas quando se tem extensas reas de terras arveis para produzirmos localmente os mesmos produtos e, deste modo, aliviar o dfice da nossa balana de pagamentos?  Porqu  que a nossa regio com mais de 200 milhes de habitantes tem um comrcio intra-regional inferior a 10%?  Porqu  que o nvel de investimento, como percentagem do PIB,  em frica e particularmente na SADC, inferior a 20%, criando uma grande lacuna de infra- estruturas. As perguntas so fceis de colocar, porm as respostas nem por isso. Todavia, interpreto este encontro de investidores sul-africanos com moambicanos como parte da soluo ou resposta s questes atrs elencadas. Julgo que precisamos de estar juntos. Precisamos de eliminar assimetrias de informao. Precisamos de partilhar as nossas vastas experincias e de falar do que cada um pode fazer ou oferecer para desenvolvermos os nossos pases. Precisamos de dar corpo e forma ao processo de integrao regional em curso, implementando o plano estratgico j existente e realizando projectos comuns e integrados, particularmente os de comrcio transfronteirio que podero impulsionar o comrcio regional. Neste contexto, as autoridades dos pases membros da SADC precisam de prosseguir com as reformas macroeconmicas e instituicionais que permitam a atraco de mais investimentos para a regio. Torna-se igualmente imperioso potenciar e aprofundar o sector financeiro para que possa desenvolver um mercado de capitais moderno e forte, de modo a colmatar a lacuna financeira existente nos projectos de infra-estruturas cruciais da regio. O Banco de Moambique considerando os desenvolvimentos nacionais, regionais e internacionais tem vindo a proceder  reviso permanente da principal legislao financeira por forma a adequ-la aos novos desafios e tendncias, bem como permitir a entrada no sector de mais instituies financeira, promovendo, deste modo, maior concorrncia. Ainda no quadro das reformas em curso, permita-me informar que temos j um projecto de regulamento da lei cambial na fase de apreciao pelos diversos stackholders do pas, incluindo a CTA e pretende-se que o regulamento a ser aprovado constitua um instrumentro importante na dinamizao do comrcio externo e na disciplina do funcionamento do mercado cambial. Estes so os pontos que pretendia partilhar com Vossas Excelncias Muito Obrigado e um bom jantar para todos. Maputo, 17 de Maio de 2010

text: Lady Ute Heinbuch, Head of Cooperation at the German Embassy; Mr Ralf Orlik, Director of KfW; Honourable Representatives of the Ministries of Education and Finance; Distinguished Guests; Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen On behalf of the Government of Mozambique, I would like to express my thanks to the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany for the valuable and continuous contribution to the economic and social development of our country. We have just signed a contract amounting to EUR 47 million for the participation of the Federal Republic of Germany in the Common Fund, which co-finances the implementation of the Strategic Plan for the Education Sector for the years 2010-2013. This agreement, as we concluded on 21 June 2010, is an important support from the German Government, represented by the German Development Bank (KFW), which is part of the recommendations and commitments made between the Government of Mozambique and the 19 cooperation partners (G-19). This is the fourth funding granted by the German Government under the joint sectoral support programme. This financial contribution complements the Mozambique-Germany cooperation strategy, which prioritises Education, Decentralisation for Rural Development and Sustainable Economic Development. It should be recalled that the Strategic Plan for the Education Sector received a contribution of EUR 5 million in its first phase in 2001. In the second stage, in 2003, the contribution was 13 million and 700 thousand Euros. In the third stage, in 2005, the amount made available by the Germany was 46 million Euros, and today, as we enter the fourth phase, the amount involved is, as I announced behind, 47 million Euros, totaling about 112 million Euros. The provision of these funds is particularly important because it comes at a time when some European countries, including Germany, are in the process of re-balancing the fiscal balance, affected by measures to stimulate economic activity in the context of mitigating the financial crisis. It is therefore a sign of confidence which the German Government sends not only to us but also to the other partners for international cooperation. The German Government's support for the Education sector represents a great commitment to the purposes of our country's development, and is expected to result in improved access to education, particularly for women, as well as the quality of education, strengthening institutional capacity building, education policies, planning, management and administration system. Economic and social development cannot be conceived without adequate investment in the human factor. From this perspective, this German support represents a gesture of profound significance for our country, which still faces the challenge of ensuring a solid and comprehensive formation of our youth, as an essential premise for the eradication of poverty. In addition to direct support to the Education sector, the entry of these funds will have a multiplier effect on the rest of the economy as part of these will be applied to the building of new infrastructure, which in itself contributes to the generation of new jobs and consequent generation of income for Mozambican families. It should be reported that German cooperation in Mozambique, in addition to support for education, takes place in other areas, including support for the State Budget, the financial sector and technical assistance. Support for the State Budget aims to reduce the Balance of Payments deficit. In the financial system, it is worth highlighting the support in the creation and operation of GAPI and Banco Terra, institutions focused on financing small and medium-sized enterprises. German cooperation also covers support for the microfinance sector. In the field of technical assistance, we highlight the co-financing of studies and pilot projects for banks and microfinance institutions. Finally, I would like to assure the German Government, represented here by the Head of Cooperation of the German Embassy and the Director of KFW, that the Government of Mozambique will mobilise all its means and efforts for the proper and speedy implementation of the resources made available to achieve the objectives set. Thank you very much
text_original: Excelentssima Senhora Ute Heinbuch, Chefe da Cooperao da Embaixada Alem; Excelentssimo Senhor Ralf Orlik, Director do KfW; Excelentssimos Senhores Representantes dos Ministrios da Educao e das Finanas; Distintos Convidados; Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Em nome do Governo de Moambique, gostaria de expressar o meu agradecimento ao Governo da Repblica Federal da Alemanha, pela valiosa e contnua contribuio para o desenvolvimento econmico e social do nosso Pas. Acabmos de assinar um contrato no montante de 47 milhes de Euros referentes  participao da Repblica Federal da Alemanha no Fundo Comum que co-financia a implementao do Plano Estratgico do Sector da Educao para os anos 2010-2013. O presente acordo,  semelhana do que celebrmos a 21 de Junho de 2010, constitui um importante apoio do Governo alemo, representado pelo Banco Alemo de Desenvolvimento (KFW), que se enquadra nas recomendaes e compromissos assumidos entre o Governo de Moambique e os 19 parceiros de cooperao (G-19). Trata-se do quarto financiamento concedido pelo Governo alemo no mbito do programa conjunto de apoio sectorial. Esta contribuio financeira complementa a estratgia da cooperao Moambique-Alemanha, que define como prioridades a Educao, a Descentralizao para o Desenvolvimento Rural e o Desenvolvimento Econmico Sustentvel. Importa recordar que o Plano Estratgico do Sector da Educao recebeu na sua primeira fase, em 2001, uma contribuio de 5 milhes de Euros. Na segunda etapa, em 2003, a contribuio foi de 13 milhes e 700 mil Euros. Na terceira fase, em 2005, o montante disponibilizado pela Alemanha foi de 46 milhes de Euros, e hoje, que entramos na quarta fase, o valor envolvido , como atrs anunciei, de 47 milhes de Euros, totalizando cerca de 112 milhes de Euros. A disponibilizao destes fundos ganha especial relevo por ocorrer num momento em que alguns pases da Europa, incluindo a Alemanha, se encontram no processo de reposio do equilbrio fiscal, afectado pelas medidas de estmulo  actividade econmica no quadro da mitigao da crise financeira. Trata-se, por isso, dum sinal de confiana que o Governo alemo transmite, no s a ns, como tambm aos demais parceiros de cooperao internacional. O apoio do Governo alemo ao sector da Educao representa um grande comprometimento para com os propsitos do desenvolvimento do nosso Pas, esperando-se que se traduza numa melhoria no acesso  educao, particularmente para as mulheres, e ainda na qualidade de ensino, fortalecimento da capacitao institucional, nas polticas de ensino, planeamento, gesto e sistema de administrao. No se pode conceber o desenvovimento econmico e social sem um adequado investimento no factor humano. Nessa perspectiva, este apoio alemo representa um gesto de profundo significado para o nosso pas, que ainda enfrenta o desafio de assegurar uma formao slida e abrangente da nossa juventude, como premissa essencial para a erradicao da pobreza. Para alm do apoio directo ao sector da Educao a entrada destes fundos ter um efeito multiplicador sobre o resto da economia uma vez que parte destes sero aplicados na edificao de novas infra-estruturas, o que em si concorre para a gerao de novos postos de trabalho e consequente gerao de rendimentos para as famlias moambicanas. Refira-se que a cooperao alem em Moambique, para alm do apoio  Educao, desenrola- se em outras reas, nomeadamente apoio ao Oramento do Estado, ao sector financeiro e  assistncia tcnica. O apoio ao Oramento do Estado visa reduzir o dfice da Balana de Pagamentos. No sistema financeiro, merece realce o apoio na criao e funcionamento do GAPI e do Banco Terra, instituies viradas para o financiamento a pequenas e mdias empresas. A cooperao alem abrange tambm o apoio ao sector de microfinanas. No domnio da assistncia tcnica, destaca-se o co-financiamento de estudos e projectos-piloto para bancos e instituies de microfinanas. Para finalizar, gostaria de assegurar ao Governo alemo, aqui representado pela Chefe da Cooperao da Embaixada Alem e pelo Director da KFW, que o Governo de Moambique mobilizar todos os seus meios e esforos para uma adequada e clere aplicao dos recursos disponibilizados com vista ao cumprimento dos objectivos traados. Muito Obrigado

Title: Speech at the 5th National Microfinance Conference
text: Your Excelleres Gentlemen Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique Separate representatives of the institutions members of the Coordination Committee of the National Payment System Distinguished Representatives of Mozambique Electricity and Telecommunications companies of Mozambique Dear Directors of Banco Dear Guests Ladies Gentlemen First of all, I would like to thank you for your honorable presence at this First Session of the Coordination Committee of the National Payment System. Allow me, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, to welcome the dear representatives of the Ministry of Finance, the National Communications Institute, the Mozambican Stock Exchange, the Mozambican Association of Banks and the commercial banks present here. I also address my greetings to the Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company Telecommunications of Mozambique and to the representative of Electricity of Mozambique. I would like to congratulate the members of the CCSNP who have just been sworn in and wish them many successes in the tasks that are legally committed to them. Pursuant to Law No. 2/2008 of 27 February, which establishes the National Payment System, the CCSNP, the advisory body of the Governor of the Bank of Mozambique on payment systems matters, is chaired by the Bank of Mozambique and is also composed by representatives of the Ministry of Finance, National Communications Institute, Mozambique Stock Exchange, Mozambican Association of Banks, commercial banks and payment service providers. It is for the CCSNP, in particular, to rule on matters relating to the improvement or modernisation of the National Payment System; submit to the Bank of Mozambique studies, suggestions or recommendations that contribute to the continuous development of the National Payment System; constitute sub-groups with a technical nature to collaborate in the preparation of studies and assessment of specific matters on the National Payment System and to exercise other powers that may be assigned to it. As can be seen, the Committee has the important challenge of contributing to Mozambique having a modern national payment system, which ensures the expansion of financial services throughout the national territory, an essential factor for the continuous growth of our economy and for the integration of our country into the regional and global economy. This session, which marks the formal start of the activities of the Coordination Committee of the National Payment System, provides an opportunity for newly sworn members to learn and reflect on the current stage of our National Payment System, as well as on the state of play of the project for the creation of the Interbank Society of Mozambique. In fact, in addition to the aspects inherent in the formalization and functioning of the CCSNP, we have taken these two points to our agenda of today's session, taking into account the importance of the National Payment System for our country, including the existence of an interbank company owned by all banking institutions operating in Mozambique. In 2007, we launched the challenge of bankising our economy and consequently extending financial services to less favoured areas. Over the last three years, we have registered the entry into operation of new financial institutions, as well as the expansion of those that already existed throughout the national territory. The banking system is now composed of 373 bank branches, covering all provincial capitals, municipal villages and 52 districts of the country in rural areas, and provides our economy with a park of 665 ATMs and 4 976 POSs. In addition to increasing the number of institutions and physical and territorial expansion of their activities, there is also a broad and profound process of modernization of the financial sector , taking advantage of the developments of new information and communication technologies to which the diversification of financial products is associated, comparable to those existing in the most developed countries and financial systems. In this context, examples of modernisation of the sector are the establishment of mobile agencies operating in rural areas, the creation of a technological infrastructure for the electronic transfer of state funds (STF) in the context of the process of decentralization of the state's financial administration and the ongoing process of creation of the interbank company of Mozambique, with the aim of promoting economies of scale in access to banking services, reflecting the expected reduction of associated costs, speed and security in the various banking operations. In fact, with the shared use of the payment infrastructure ensured by the Interbank Society of Mozambique, it will also be possible for customers of the banking system to make use of ATM or POS services of any of the banks operating in the country, with evident efficiency gains, in addition to accessing more and varied correlated services. The consolidation, modernization and development of our National Payment System is a strategic objective of the Bank of Mozambique with a structuring and comprehensive nature, given its benefits for the desired improvement of the efficiency of financial intermediation within the framework of the objectives of the policy 2 economic impact, combating poverty and promoting Mozambique's growth and economic development. Ladies Gentlemen This First Session of the CCSNP takes place a week after the announcement by our Government of a number of important macroeconomic, sectoral and financial measures, following the riots earlier this month in the nation's capital, which disrupted the functioning of the institutions, markets and the economy. The evolution of the Metical exchange rate and the Consumer Price index in 2010 had been denoting the existence of anomalies in the overall behavior of our economy. In a market economy environment, sudden variations, of great magnitude and with an upward trend in exchange rates, spreads and inflation, are unequivocal flags of an economy's health state that requires adequate intervention. Our economy continues to produce less than it consumes and so, in aggregate terms, the country's imports exceed the level of our exports, which reflects the structural problem we are struggling with because the level of public spending is higher than the level of revenue collected by the State. In these circumstances, the pressure on the internal foreign exchange market is permanent, reflecting on the evolution of the exchange rate, which requires the macroeconomic authorities to increase and also permanent rigor, coordination and consistency in the management of public policies. Our economy still resents the global food crisis and the international fuel price crisis triggered in 2007, a situation aggravated by the international financial crisis that began in 2007/2008, whose primary, secondary and delayed effects still overlap the world economy, creating further complications for many economies, including ourown. About a month ago, in the face of the persistent depreciation of the Metical and after an in-depth diagnosis of the situation, the Bank of Mozambique announced bold measures to stabilize the foreign exchange market and exchange rates. The available data show a strong and consistent reduction in spreads and a coherent alignment of the exchange rate, which has ceased to depreciate. However, when we took these measures, we were aware that the desired effects required the undertaking of additional actions to ensure increased production and productivity, containment and in some cases the reduction of expenditure. In an environment characterized by a balance of payments and a structurally deficient General State Budget, external shocks such as those we live in resulting from the international financial and economic crisis, rigour, financial discipline and austerity are the fundamental pillars of macroeconomic management. The challenge for us is to achieve these objectives without losing sight of the unavoidable social side of the economy, which requires appropriate policies that meet the needs of the extremely vulnerable layers. The measures announced by our Government aim, on the one hand, at immediate impacts on prices and, on the other hand, macroeconomic objectives focused on rigour, containment and reduction of public expenditure and strengthening the stabilisation of the Metical. This week, the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Mozambique met in ordinary session and decided to take additional measures aimed at the intended objectives of macroeconomic rebalancing. It is in this context that the increase in the reference interest rate of the Bank of Mozambique, the Permanent Ease of Service, and the increase by 0.25 percentage points in the mandatory reserve rate that banks must constitute with the WB are framed. Ladies Gentlemen The payment system is a structured set of actors, services, subsystems, payment instruments, technology and procedures that facilitate the transfer of funds or monetary values for the finalisation of payments and their circulation in the economy. Payment systems must meet public interest objectives, including security, reliability , transparency and efficiency. Achieving these objectives requires the commitment of all Mozambicans and the existence of a communications infrastructure and a policy of expanding electricity networks that are in line with the challenges that result from the advancement of the financial system. Therefore, we decided to invite the representatives, at the level of the respective Boards of Directors, of the companies Telecommunications of Mozambique and Electricity of Mozambique. In addition to the points to which I mentioned above, the Code of Conduct, the RULES of procedure, the proposal for technical working subgroups and the Regulation of plenary meetings, technical subgroups and the work of the secretariat will also be considered at this session. To finish, I would like to take this opportunity to thank the presence of the CCSNP member institutions and that we make this body a forum for the exchange of ideas that contribute to the consolidation of a safe, reliable, transparent and efficient National Payment System. Thank you very much Maputo, 15 September 2010
text_original: Excelentssimos Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique Distintos Representantes das Instituies Membros do Comit de Coordenao do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos Ilustres Representantes das empresas Electricidade de Moambique e Telecomunicaes de Moambique Estimados Directores do Banco Caros convidados Minhas senhoras Meus senhores Quero, em primeiro lugar, agradecer a vossa honrosa presena nesta Primeira Sesso do Comit de Coordenao do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos. Permitam-me que, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, sade os prezados representantes do Ministrio das Finanas, do Instituto Nacional de Comunicaes, da Bolsa de Valores de Moambique, da Associao Moambicana de Bancos e dos bancos comerciais aqui presentes. Endereo igualmente as minhas saudaes ao senhor Presidente do Conselho de Administrao da empresa Telecomunicaes de Moambique e ao representante da Electricidade de Moambique. Gostaria de enderear os meus parabns aos membros do CCSNP que acabam de ser empossados e desejar-lhes muitos sucessos nas tarefas que lhes esto legalmente cometidas. Nos termos da Lei n 2/2008, de 27 de Fevereiro, que estabelece o Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos, o CCSNP, rgo de consulta do Governador do Banco de Moambique em matrias de sistemas de pagamentos,  presidido pelo Banco de Moambique e  ainda integrado pelos representantes do Ministrio das Finanas, Instituto Nacional de Comunicaes, Bolsa de Valores de Moambique, Associao Moambicana de Bancos, bancos comerciais e empresas prestadoras de servios de pagamentos. Compete ao CCSNP, nomeadamente, pronunciar-se sobre matrias relacionadas com o aperfeioamento ou modernizao do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos; submeter ao Banco de Moambique estudos, sugestes ou recomendaes que contribuam para o contnuo desenvolvimento do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos; constituir subgrupos com carcter tcnico para colaborar na elaborao de estudos e apreciao de matrias especficas sobre o Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos e exercer outras competncias que lhe vierem a ser atribudas. Como se pode observar, o Comit tem pela frente o importante desafio de contribuir para que Moambique tenha um sistema nacional de pagamentos moderno, que assegure a expanso dos servios financeiros por todo o territrio nacional, factor essencial para o crescimento contnuo da nossa economia e para a integrao do nosso Pas na economia regional e mundial. A presente sesso, que marca o incio formal das actividades do Comit de Coordenao do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos, constitui uma oportunidade para os membros recm-empossados se inteirarem e reflectirem sobre o actual estgio do nosso Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos, bem assim sobre o ponto de situao do projecto de criao da Sociedade Interbancria de Moambique. Com efeito, alm dos aspectos inerentes  formalizao e ao funcionamento do CCSNP, elegemos estes dois pontos para a nossa agenda da sesso de hoje, tendo em conta a importncia de que se reveste o Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos para o nosso Pas, incluindo a existncia duma sociedade interbancria participada por todas as instituies bancrias que operam em Moambique. Em 2007, lanmos o desafio da bancarizao da nossa economia e consequente alargamento dos servios financeiros para zonas menos favorecidas. Ao longo dos ltimos trs anos, registmos a entrada em funcionamento de novas instituies financeiras, bem assim a expanso das que j existiam pelo territrio nacional. O sistema bancrio  hoje composto por 373 balces de bancos, cobrindo todas as capitais provinciais, vilas municipais e 52 Distritos do pas nas zonas rurais, e disponibiliza  nossa economia um parque de 665 ATMs e 4 976 POSs. Para alm do incremento do nmero de instituies e expanso fsica e territorial das suas actividades, assiste-se, ainda, a um amplo e profundo processo de modernizao do sector financeiro, tirando vantagens dos desenvolvimentos das novas tecnologias de informao e comunicao a que a diversificao de produtos financeiros se associa, comparveis aos existentes nos pases e sistemas financeiros mais desenvolvidos. Nesse mbito, constituem tambm exemplos de modernizao do sector o estabelecimento de agncias mveis a operar nas zonas rurais, a criao de uma infra-estrutura tecnolgica para a transferncia electrnica de fundos do Estado (STF) no quadro do processo de descentralizao da administrao financeira do Estado e o processo em curso de criao da sociedade interbancria de Moambique, com o objectivo de promover economias de escala no acesso aos servios bancrios, com reflexo na esperada reduo de custos associados, rapidez e segurana nas diversas operaes bancrias. Na verdade, com a utilizao partilhada da infra-estrutura de pagamentos assegurada pela Sociedade Interbancria de Moambique, ser ainda possvel que os clientes do sistema bancrio faam uso de servios de ATM ou POS de qualquer dos bancos a operar no Pas, com ganhos de eficincia evidentes, para alm de acederem a mais e variados servios correlacionados. A consolidao, modernizao e dinamizao do nosso Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos  um objectivo estratgico do Banco de Moambique com carcter estruturante e abrangente, dados os seus benefcios para a almejada melhoria da eficincia da intermediao financeira no quadro dos objectivos da poltica 2 econmica do Governo, de combate  pobreza e promoo do crescimento e do desenvolvimento econmico de Moambique. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores Esta Primeira Sesso do CCSNP realiza-se uma semana aps o anncio, pelo nosso Governo, de um conjunto de importantes medidas macroeconmicas, sectoriais e financeiras, na sequncia dos tumultos registados, no incio deste ms, na capital do Pas, os quais perturbaram o funcionamento das instituies, dos mercados e da economia. A evoluo da taxa de cmbio do Metical e do ndice de Preos no Consumidor, em 2010, vinham denotando a existncia de anomalias no comportamento geral da nossa economia. Em ambiente de economia de mercado, variaes bruscas, de grande magnitude e com tendncia ascendente nas taxas de cmbio, nos seus spreads e na inflao, constituem sinalizadores inequvocos de um estado de sade da economia que requer adequada interveno. A nossa economia continua a produzir menos do que consome e por isso, em termos agregados, as importaes do pas superam o nvel das nossas exportaes, o que traduz o problema estrutural com que nos debatemos de o nvel da despesa pblica ser superior ao nvel das receitas cobradas pelo Estado. Nestas circunstncias, a presso sobre o mercado interno de divisas  permanente, com reflexos sobre a evoluo da taxa de cmbio o que exige das autoridades macroeconmicas redobrado e igualmente permanente rigor, coordenao e consistncia na gesto das polticas pblicas. A nossa economia ainda se ressente da crise alimentar mundial e da crise dos preos internacionais dos combustveis despoletadas em 2007, situao agravada pela crise financeira internacional iniciada em 2007/2008, cujos efeitos primrios, secundrios e retardados pairam ainda sobre a economia mundial, criando complicaes acrescidas a muitas economias, incluindo a nossa. H cerca de um ms atrs, perante a persistente depreciao do Metical e aps um aprofundado diagnstico da situao, o Banco de Moambique anunciou medidas arrojadas de estabilizao do mercado cambial e das taxas de cmbio. Os dados disponveis mostram uma forte e consistente reduo dos spreads e um alinhamento coerente da taxa de cmbio, que deixou de depreciar. No entanto, ao tomarmos essas medidas, estvamos conscientes de que os efeitos desejados requeriam o empreendimento de aces adicionais que garantam o aumento da produo e da produtividade, a conteno e nalguns casos a reduo da despesa. Num ambiente caracterizado por uma balana de pagamentos e um Oramento Geral do Estado estrutural mente deficitrios, choques externos como os que vivemos, resultantes da crise financeira e econmica internacional, o rigor, a disciplina financeira e a austeridade so os pilares fundamentais da gesto macroeconmica. O desafio que se nos coloca  a prossecuo desses objectivos sem perdermos de vista o incontornvel lado social da economia, o que requer polticas apropriadas, que alcancem a satisfao das necessidades das camadas extremamente vulnerveis. As medidas anunciadas pelo nosso Governo visam, por um lado, impactos imediatos nos preos e, por outro, objectivos de mbito macroeconmico centrados no rigor, na conteno e reduo da despesa pblica e no reforo da estabilizao do Metical. Esta semana, o Comit de Poltica Monetria do Banco de Moambique reuniu-se em sesso ordinria e decidiu tomar medidas adicionais visando os objectivos pretendidos de reequilbrio macroeconmico.  neste mbito que se enquadra o incremento em um ponto percentual na taxa de juro de referncia do Banco de Moambique, a Facilidade Permanente de Cedncia, e a subida em 0.25 pontos percentuais na taxa de reserva obrigatria que os bancos devem constituir junto do BM. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores O sistema de pagamentos  um conjunto estruturado de intervenientes, servios, subsistemas, instrumentos de pagamento, tecnologia e procedimentos que facilitam a transferncia de fundos ou de valores monetrios para a finalizao de pagamentos e a circulao destes na economia. Os sistemas de pagamentos devem cumprir com os objectivos de interesse pblico, nomeadamente, segurana, fiabilidade, transparncia e eficincia. O alcance destes objectivos requer o empenho de todos os moambicanos e a existncia de uma infra- estrutura de comunicaes e de uma poltica de expanso de rede elctrica que estejam em linha com os desafios que resultam do avano do sistema financeiro. Por isso, decidimos convidar os representantes, a nvel dos respectivos Conselhos de Administrao, das empresas Telecomunicaes de Moambique e Electricidade de Moambique. Alm dos pontos a que anteriormente fiz meno, sero tambm objecto de apreciao, na presente sesso, o Cdigo de Conduta, o Regimento do CCSNP, a proposta de subgrupos tcnicos de trabalho e o Regulamento das reunies do plenrio, dos subgrupos tcnicos e dos trabalhos do secretariado. Para terminar, queria aproveitar esta oportunidade para agradecer a presena das instituies membros do CCSNP e que faamos deste rgo um frum de troca de ideias que contribuam para a consolidao de um Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos seguro, fivel, transparente e eficiente. Muito obrigado Maputo, 15 de Setembro de 2010

Title: End of the Economic Year 2010
text: DISCOURSE DESUAEXCELeNCIATHE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE ON THE OCCASION OF THE V NATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MICROFINANCE MATOLA, NOVEMBER 24, 2010 Madam Minister of State Administration, Excellency, Madam Governor of Maputo Province, Excellency, Mr National Director for the Promotion of Rural Development Mr President of the Matola City Council Dear guests My ladies My lords I would first like, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, to greet all those present at this conference and to express my gratitude for the invitation addressed to me to participate in this important forum for joint reflection on a matter of such high interest and timeliness. Let me also health, in particular, the Ministry of State Administration, for its initiative to organize this event and for the continued support it has provided to the development of microfinance and rural finance in general, in the country contributing significantly to the increase in our financial sector and to the increase in financial intermediation, which represents a stimulus to the growth of the economy, an essential condition for poverty reduction in our country. The theme that I have been asked to present at this conference is the vision on the development of the national financial sector. This is a very broad and complex subject, which has received a deep treatment in the Medium and Long-term strategy of the Bank of Mozambique. That is why my intervention will be based on the aspects most related to the implementation and operation of banking and financial institutions in general in the country and the role that microfinance operators can play in the context of our economy. Dear Guests My Ladies My Lords Recent data on developments in our financial sector show that since the opening of the market to domestic and foreign private investors, following the implementation of economic and financial reforms initiated in the 1980s and which had greater momentum since 1990, this has grown at a significant pace, having passed from a total of three banks that the country had in the early 1990s, for the current 16 banks, 7 credit unions, 6 microbanks, 117 microcredit operators and 10 savings and loan organisations. The strategy of banking the economy that we launched in 2007 and the revision we have been carrying out over time of the country's main financial legislation were to change the scenario then prevailing. The results achieved so far are positive and encouraging. Indeed, out of a total of 229 bank branches operating in the country covering 28 districts, as of December 31, 2006, the country now has 385 branches of banks and the number of districts served increased to 52. However, despite this development, both in terms of increasing the number of institutions and from the point of view of further diversification of the range of operations and financial operators, the tendency for the concentration of institutions and services provided by them in the main cities of the country continues to prevail in the country, given that it is in the districts where the majority of our population is concentrated. In fact, to illustrate, the three main cities of the country (Maputo, Beira and Nampula) continue to be responsible for most of the branches, and maputo city absorbs 38% of the total, a situation that becomes more evident when considering the location of micfrofinance institutions, since of the 117 microcredit operators legally constituted, 66% of these are located in the City and Province of Maputo, the same with credit unions and other types of microfinance institutions operating in the country. Other indicators of coverage of the country's bank branches reinforce this trend towards the concentration to which I refer. For example, while in Maputo City each agency covers about 7,000 inhabitants in Montepuez and Milange, this coverage covers 153,000 and 498,000 inhabitants, respectively. From a territorial perspective, it is observed that in Maputo City there is one agency for every 2 square kilometers against about 10,000 square kilometers in Milange and 15,800 square kilometers in Montepuez. Nationally, the average coverage of each counter is about 2,271 km and 57,000 inhabitants. The study produced by FinScope in 2009 found that in Mozambique only 22.2% of the adult population has access to financial services, below 46% in Tanzania or even 45% in Malawi, countries with socio-economic characteristics very close to ours. The same study also states that the situation of exclusion is more serious in rural areas where 86.5% of the population has no connection with financial institutions, compared to 61% in urban areas. The low level of access to financial services is, in our view, attributable to a number of factors, particularly of a macroeconomic nature, associated with the low level of income and high poverty rate of Mozambican families, which prevents them from saving in considerable amounts, as well as institutional constraints relating to the weak geographical deployment of financial institutions in the country. To these circumstances, socio-cultural factors are added, namely poor financial information and poor infrastructural conditions in some regions of the country, which lead to high installation and transaction costs in these areas, which ultimately affects the institutions' fixing process and even the movement of populations from production sites to the nearest bank counter. In addition to the data to which I referred above, it should also be mentioned that the country has 128 districts and of these 76 have no banking representation. This also helps to explain part of the conclusions of the FinScope assessment, according to which only 5.3% of adults save via bank and that most people use unconventional schemes to save their savings, namely in-case, formal schemes, 11.2% of adults and keep at home, 8.6%, equally identical when analysed from the perspective of access to credit, where the use of the informal sector and family and friends are considered the main sources. Dear Guests My Ladies And Gentlemen The situation described above makes it clear that we all face the mission and the challenge of building a comprehensive and inclusive financial sector. Modernising the sector is also one of our objectives, as we believe that it has a direct impact on increasing the efficiency of the sector, while being a strong tool for expanding financial services in the country as it can allow the extension of services to take place without necessarily having a physical bank presence. The fiscal and monetary incentives contained in the said strategy of banking the economy, combined with that of the Government to make the district the hub of planning and development of our economy, the allocation of financial resources to districts and middle and higher level staff and the maintaining of the commitment, by the Government, to continue to adopt policy measures to ensure macroeconomic stability, an essential condition for increasing savings and attracting more domestic and foreign private investments, sources of employment and income, are also important instruments to support the process of extending financial services to rural areas, for capturing the savings that is being generated in these places or for the financing of new investments needed for exploitation of the wealth potential that the country boasts.
