Este nvel de acesso aos servios financeiros que Moambique possui mostra a elevada excluso de utilizao dos servios e produtos financeiros pela populao. O mesmo estudo concluiu que a situao de excluso  mais acentuada nas zonas rurais onde 86.5% da populao no tem nenhuma relao com as instituies financeiras contra 61% nas zonas urbanas. Com vista a superar estes desequilbrios e deficincias, tornando o nosso sistema financeiro mais inclusivo, registamos com satisfao que a actividade do sistema bancrio continuou em 2009 a ser marcada pelo desenvolvimento de novos produtos de poupana e crdito e pela expanso dos canais de distribuio como a rede de caixas multibanco (ATMs) e de agncias bancrias. Estes desenvolvimentos enquadram-se no contexto da modernizao do sistema bancrio, processo em que todos ns, banco central e bancos comerciais continuamos envolvidos, de forma a garantir, com economias de escala, atravs da utilizao partilhada da infra-estrutura de pagamentos, a eficincia, rapidez e segurana no fornecimento dos servios financeiros, o acesso mais alargado aos mesmos por parte dos clientes e a custos associados relativamente mais reduzidos. Em 2010, foram dados importantes passos para a entrada em funcionamento da Sociedade Interbancria de Servios (SIMO) e espera-se que no primeiro semestre de 2011 as ATM's e os POS's passem a estar conectados  mesma rede e se realize um exerccio piloto em que os bancos estejam ligados aos agentes prestadores de servios financeiros mesmo nas zonas em que no tenham uma presena fsica. Com esta sociedade pretende-se garantir economias de escala no acesso aos servios bancrios, com reflexo na esperada reduo de custos associados, rapidez e segurana nas diversas operaes bancrias. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores, A estabilidade macroeconmica e o propcio ambiente de negcios de que o pas goza tem atrado investimentos de vulto e criado espao apropriado para o desenvolvimento das pequena e mdias empresas, o que prognostica para os anos que vm um robusto crescimento econmico com impactos positivos no emprego e na reduo da pobreza. Os desafios que temos pela frente so, todavia, ingentes. A escalada dos preos dos cereais e do petrleo no mercado internacional ir pressionando a nossa balana de pagamentos e outras variveis da economia domstica. O aumento da produo e da produtividade internas deve ser a resposta de todos ns; produzir para substituirmos as importaes e produzir para alargarmos as receitas de exportao. Neste exerccio, a banca deve continuar a desempenhar o seu papel de alavanca de desenvolvimento econmico, alinhando as suas estratgias comerciais com os objectivos do governo de combate  pobreza e reduo da dependncia externa. O nmero de bancos e sociedades financeiras de capitais nacionais e estrangeiros que temos vindo a licenciar cresce de ano para ano. Este grande entusiasmo dos investidores, que encontra respaldo na confiana criada pelas persistentes e exitosas polticas de reformas macroeconmicas, precisa de ser acarinhado e orientado para aces de promoo da poupana e extenso dos servios financeiros para todo o nosso Pas. A entrada de novos operadores no nosso sector financeiro permitir ainda a disperso do risco associado a concentrao do volume dos activos globais e da carteira de crdito. Com efeito, a actual situao caracteriza-se por uma significativa concentrao do sistema bancrio onde os quatro maiores bancos detm quase 90% dos activos do sistema. A concentrao na rea do crdito tambm  notria, sendo que os quatro maiores bancos continuam a atrair para si e a conceder crdito a grandes empresas, que tm contribudo significativamente para o incremento das suas carteiras e, consequentemente, das respectivas quotas de mercado. Termino agradecendo a vossa ateno e reiterando os meus parabns  KPMG e  Associao Moambicana de Bancos pelo trabalho que hoje nos apresentaram. Muito Obrigado

Title: Speech at the Opening of the BCI Branch in Ressano Garcia - Moamba
text: Natural Resource Management - Options and Policy ImplicationsNOTAS INTRODUTeeRIASErnesto Gove, Governador do Banco de Mo8dambique Minister for Planning and Development, Excellency Ministers, Deputy Ministers, Deputy Governors of Central Banks and Permanent Secretaries of african countries represented here, Excellencies Dear Professor and Friend William Lyakurwa, Executive Director of AERC Dear Guests, Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen I take the opportunity of host and co-organizer of this Seminar, to welcome to Maputo on my own behalf and the Bank of Mozambique, all participants in this XIII International Seminar of the African Economic Research Consortium (AERC), the first held on Mozambican soil. As a member of the AERC Programme Committee, when i was attending our annual mombassa meeting last November, I launched the challenge of hosting this event, recognizing the high quality of the debates that the AERC promotes, in view of its extensive network of partnerships with Governments, Central Banks, Universities and Advanced Research Centres on various specialties, always valuing African institutions and brains in the dialectics of scientific and technical exchange with entities from other quadrants. The theme that brings you to Maputo and that brings us together in this room is current and relevant for countries like Mozambique, which begin the epic of more active and intensive exploitation of their non-renewable natural resources. Therefore, I did not hesitate to invite this recognized institution to hold this meeting in Mozambique. I also believe that it is our mission, as the Central Bank, to facilitate access to knowledge and rich experiences, to Mozambican leaders and cadres of different public and private institutions present here, in an action of exchange of ideas and training on the complex phenomenon of natural resource management, options and policy implications, more even when we are fully aware of the implications of these processes in our balance of payments, at the level of our country's external reserves and, consequently, in the course of the desired political, social and macroeconomic stability. Our real expectations regarding this event are that we will at least be more enlightened and aware of what other countries have been doing in this area, which helps us to know better the phenomenon, the success stories and the most appropriate policies for the management and exploitation of natural resources that take into account intergenerational aspects, beyond the short- and medium-term horizon of the sector's development-oriented policies or its contribution to inclusive and sustainable development. Despite the adverse situation that the world economy has been experiencing over the past few years, the Mozambican economy has maintained robust growth rates of around 7.0% over the past five years, ranking among the 10 fastest growing economies on the planet we inhabit; the average inflation indicator for this period has been single-digit; our international reserves provide comfortable levels of coverage of our imports, budgeted at three billion U.S. dollars. However, in the last twelve months, due to exogenous causes unequivocally attributable to the delayed effect of the financial and economic crisis on a global scale, we have faced an inflatable pressure, which has led to the adoption of a more prudent monetary policy adjusted to macroeconomic objectives, short and medium term. Unfortunately, the further escalation in the international price of oil and food is an additional challenge, not only for us, but also for the governments and central banks of sub-Saharan Africa, regardless of whether or not they are oil producers. More than eternal victims of the vicissitudes of adverse endogenous and exogenous conjunctures, Africa has the resources and a recognized potential to turn the crisis into opportunities. Our human and natural resources are the instrument that can catapult the march of our development, generating the financial resources we need to sovereignly define our development priorities, which I believe are focused on the infrastructure of our economies, the education of our youth, the health of our children, the consolidation of institutions and democracy and the improvement of the appropriate environment for the development of our private sector . This is the strategic platform of a tomorrow that will make us competitive and able to integrate globalization as active participants and not as mere observers, let alone as subordinates of the process. It is in the inclusive and sustainable exploitation of natural resources that we also seek the means to reduce external dependence, increasing the domestic production of goods and services, replacing imports and boosting exports. The proper exploitation of natural resources involves integrated public policies, public-private partnerships aimed at multiplying income generation and attracting investment in our development programs and anti-poverty programs. It is from the exploitation of natural resources that the state budget becomes less dependent and catalyst for a fairer income redistribution and the more robust exchange rate fund. It is from the exploitation of natural resources that we must create the basis of our sovereign wealth fund, with a perspective of macroeconomic and market stability, long-term investment and intergenerational exchange reserve. We are fully aware that our continent in general, and each of our countries in particular, has not yet been able to provide the world, in quantity and desired quality, companies specializing in the exploitation, transformation and marketing of non-renewable natural resources. It is important that this segment of the market operates in a fairer, transparent and inclusive manner, to the extent that the resources of our subsoil are instruments with constitutional dignity that bind them to our sovereignty. That is why we have been introducing reforms that ensure greater transparency in the process of exploiting natural resources. But there is also an effort to be made on the other side, from those who have the know-how, from whom it actually exploits resources. That is why I believe that triology transparency, ethics and justice contain essential factors of stability in the process of managing natural resources that must be scrupulously observed by host countries and also by the companies involved in the exploitation. Once this framework of principles is respected, truly genuine and inclusive partnerships will be in place; partnerships that ensure not only adequate and profitable exploitation of our natural resources and a visible economic empowerment of our countries, but also ensure an increasing participation of the national private sector and experts and managers of our countries in this process, side by side with the experienced companies, experts and international managers we have. Excellencies I just wanted to stress in my brief notes how important it is for us Central Banks and not only on this current and urgent issue. We hope that this seminar will deepen our network and open the channels of communication and exchange of experiences between the different stakeholders who somehow participate in the management of this public and valuable thing that are our natural resources, such as oil, coal, natural gas, heavy sands and other minerals. Thank you very much. Maputo, 28 March 2011.

Title: Signing of the Social Pact of the Interbank Society of Mozambique (SIMO)
text: Mr. Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency, Your Excellese St. Bank of Mozambique Administrators; Members of the Coordination Committee of the National Payment System; Representatives of credit institutions and the Mozambican Association of Banks; Members of simo's Interbank Operationalisation Commission; Mr. Representative of KfW; Representatives of SIBS, simo's technology implementer; Mr. Representative of the consulting firm EMC; Representative of the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique; Directors and other managers of the Bank of Mozambique; Dear Guests, Ladies Gentlemen It is with great satisfaction that I address you at this signing ceremony of the Social Pact of the Interbank Society of Mozambique (SIMO). On this occasion, I would like to greet, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, the distinguished representatives of the Coordination Committee of the National Payment System, credit institutions, the Mozambican Association of Banks and the Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique. I extend my warm greetings to the members of the Interbank Commission for the Operationalisation of SIMO and the SIMO Installer Commission, as well as to the other guests present in this act. If there are particularly important occasions in the life of our institutions, surely this is one of them. In fact, today is a special day, in which we come together to give body to the work that, with selflessness, we have been doing for a little over three years aiming at the constitution of this society. In this process now knows one of its most important moments, I point out, among other achievements, the preliminary contacts with our partners with a view to the advocacy of the project, the working meetings with the various stakeholders, in particular the credit institutions operating in our country, and the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding between the Bank of Mozambique, as the promoter of the initiative, and credit institutions, on 16 December 2009. It is also necessary in this context to mention the identification of the technological implementer of the project, which is developing the migration model of existing networks, as well as the choice of the firm "Sociedade Interbancaria de Mocambique, SA", abbreviated by SIMO, the approval of the SIMO logo, the attribution of the SIMOrede designation for the agglutinating network, the creation of conditions at the level of facilities for the functioning of society, as well as the implementation of the process of recruitment and selection of human resources that are already working in this company. It was a long process, during which each signatory institution, represented in the Interbank Commission for The Operationalization of SIMO, brought its experience and comparative experiences, which proved of enormous value for us to reach the current phase. I would even say that the results of the work done compensated for this time spent. It is now appropriate to remind the public, in particular our fellow citizens, of the economic and social foundations behind the creation of this society; it is time to inform us about what are already certainties and what can be expected of SIMO, whose social contract we sign today. As is clear, our network of banking establishments is booming, especially if we take into account the situation we were in in 2007, when we launched, in partnership with the Government, the strategy of banking the economy of our country. In fact, the number of credit institutions and financial corporations that the Bank of Mozambique has been licensing is continuously growing, from year to year. It is recalled, in this regard, that the study prepared by FinScope in August 2009 concluded that in Mozambique only 22.2% of the adult population had access to financial services, a level considered quite low when compared to other countries with similar economic characteristics to Those of Mozambique, namely Tanzania (46%) and Malawi (45%). This level of access to financial services that our country has shows the high exclusion of use of financial services and products by a significant part of the population. The same study concluded that the situation of exclusion is more pronounced in rural areas where 86.5% of the population has no relation to financial institutions versus 61% in urban areas. However, we are pleased to note that this scenario of poor access to financial products and services is gradually changing. The results achieved so far encourage us to take more steps towards a more inclusive banking system. In fact, our financial system currently has 16 banks and 417 branches, spread over 58 of the 128 districts of the national territory, against coverage of only 28 districts until just over 4 years ago. To these figures, there are 7 credit unions, 132 microcredit operators and 8 microbanks. It should also be reported that data reported for April 2011 reported that the country had a total of 747 ATM's and 5,051 POS's, against 367 ATM's and 3,243 POS's until September 2006. Distinguished Guests Ladies Gentlemen In the last three to four years, the world has experienced one of the most severe economic and financial crises in memory, with harmful repercussions, particularly on foreign trade in developing countries, which have seen their exports falling considerably, worsening the current account of their countries. This factor, in addition to producing instability in macroeconomic management, also caused economic recessions in some countries, undermining the efforts they had been making in the implementation of policies and strategies to combat poverty. Mozambique has not been immune to these adversities. However, the bold economic and legislative reforms aimed at creating an adequate business environment have enabled average rates of economic growth in the period to be above the African average. In this effort, the financial sector has always been present, aligning its business strategies with government economic policies, always looking for solutions to the problem of financing the economy, providing innovative and quality financial services and reaching an increasing number of Mozambican citizens. It is in this context that the initiative of the creation of the Interbank Society of Mozambique is part of the initiative, which comes at a time when, in addition to the growth in terms of the number of banking establishments, the activity of the banking system is marked by the development of new savings and credit products and the expansion of distribution channels such as the POS's and ATM's network. However, 6 electronic payment networks coexist that work in a non-integrated way. With the entry into operation of this interbank company, ATM's and POS's will cease to operate in isolation, being connected to a single national network. In turn, banks, in view of the reduction in costs that will result from the sharing of technological infrastructure, will be better able to expand, even to areas where they do not have a physical presence. This desiderato is in line with this strategy of banking our economy, whose objective is the financial inclusion of Mozambicans, providing them with diversified and good quality financial services. Ladies Gentlemen With the implementation of SIMO and the start of its activities, we will certainly have significant economic gains of scale, implying the reduction of unit costs of financial transactions. Multifaceted gains are expected for commercial banks, customers, society and the economy at large. For commercial banks, the gains will result in greater efficiency in the provision of their services, in the rationalisation of costs, once served by a common technological network, with universal access, which allows the satisfaction of the needs of domestic customers and those travelling outside national borders. For their part, consumers will benefit from universal access to a variety of financial products and services. Another gain for customers will be the possibility of using terminals of different financial products and services indistinctly (namely POS's, ATM's, internet banking, mobile phone banking), without burdening your pocket. The customer who only needs a card for home use will not be required to have a card whose compensation is made outside the national territory, as are the cases of Visa or MasterCard. Another valence that will come from the entry into operation of SIMO services will be the increase in the number of available products. In fact, with the shared use of the payment infrastructure ensured by the Interbank Society of Mozambique, it will also be possible for customers of the banking system to make use of ATM or POS services of any of the banks operating in the country, with evident efficiency gains, in addition to accessing more and varied correlated services. For society and the economy in general, there will also be significant gains, which will result, inter alia, in the increase in the number of banked customers, implying greater social inclusion in terms of benefits in access to information and communication technologies. There is no doubt that increasingly mass access to information and communication technologies is ultimately a contribution to the common fight against poverty. In short, SIMO has the role of boosting the bankof the economy, as well as massising the use of electronic payment instruments alternative to cash, thereby contributing to improving the conditions for the provision of payment services at national level and increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of financial intermediation. Ladies Gentlemen It was in view of the multiplicity of advantages to which I have mentioned that the initiative to create SIMO has deserved the adherence of the banking system, which from an early age has understood that competition will not be hampered by the fact that technological infrastructure is shared. In fact, competition is a function of the efficiency, creativity, innovation and quality of the services provided and the products provided by each institution. In the financial sector, these differentiating factors are always present and legislation promotes and defends competition. Therefore, I cannot finish my speech without first expressing my appreciation to the fifteen credit institutions that embody this project, integrating, alongside the Central Bank, simo's shareholder structure, namely: African Banking Corporation, Commercial and Investment Bank, Mercantile and Investment Bank, Banco Oportunidade de Mocambique, Banco Terra, Barclays Bank, Cooperative of Poupanca e Credito, First National Bank, International Commercial Bank, Millennium BIM, Moza Banco, Procredit, Socremo, Standard Bank e The Mauritius Commercial Bank. I also greet The Single Bank and TCHUMA, which have recently joined this project. Nor would I fail to express my word of gratitude to the members of the Coordination Committee of the National Payment System and to the members of simo's Interbank Commission for the Operationalisation of SIMO, whose involvement allowed the company's draft constitution to be implemented. Recognizing that the achievement of SIMO's objectives requires the call for a communication infrastructure and a policy of expansion of electricity grid swelled with the challenges arising from the advancement of the financial system, I would like to express my encouragement to the Presidents of the Boards of Directors of Telecommunications of Mozambique and Electricity mozambique, also present here, to whom I welcome the progress that has been made in both sectors. I also express my gratitude to the workers of the Bank of Mozambique and the other institutions that are part of SIMO, as well as to all those who directly or indirectly collaborated until we reach the stage in which we are today. The future Directorate and simo workers, my appeal to devotion to work, the spirit of teamwork and professionalism. Finally, I would like, on the one hand, to remind SIMO shareholders of the great challenge that we face in materialising the objectives outlined with the creation of this society and, on the other hand, to take the opportunity to reiterate the invitation to the other Commercial Banks that have not yet done so to join this joint initiative that will certainly improve banking services in the country. Thank you very much.

Nesse processo que conhece agora um dos seus momentos mais importantes, destaco, dentre outras realizaes, os contactos preliminares com os nossos parceiros tendo em vista a advocacia do projecto, os encontros de trabalho com as diversas partes interessadas, em particular as instituies de crdito que operam no nosso pas, e a assinatura do Memorando de Entendimento entre o Banco de Moambique, na sua qualidade de promotor da iniciativa, e instituies de crdito, havida em 16 de Dezembro de 2009. Cumpre ainda neste mbito referir a identificao do implementador tecnolgico do projecto, o qual se encontra a desenvolver o modelo de migrao das redes existentes, bem como a escolha da firma Sociedade Interbancria de Moambique, SA, abreviadamente designada por SIMO, a aprovao do logtipo da SIMO, a atribuio da designao SIMOrede para a rede aglutinadora, a criao de condies a nvel de instalaes para o funcionamento da sociedade, bem como a realizao do processo de recrutamento e seleco dos recursos humanos que j se encontram a trabalhar nesta empresa. Foi um processo longo, durante o qual cada instituio subscritora, representada na Comisso Interbancria de Operacionalizao da SIMO, trouxe a sua experincia e experincias comparadas, que se mostraram de enorme valia para que chegssemos  actual fase. Diria mesmo que os resultados do trabalho realizado compensaram esse tempo despendido. Agora,  oportuno recordarmos o pblico, em particular os nossos concidados, os fundamentos econmicos e sociais que esto por detrs da criao desta sociedade;  chegado o tempo de informarmos sobre o que j so certezas e o que podem esperar da SIMO, cujo contrato social hoje assinamos. Como  notrio, a nossa rede de estabelecimentos bancrios est em franca expanso, sobretudo se tivermos em linha de conta a situao em que nos encontrvamos em 2007, quando lanmos, em parceria com o Governo, a estratgia de bancarizao da economia do nosso pas. Com efeito, o nmero de instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras que o Banco de Moambique tem vindo a licenciar cresce continuamente, de ano para ano. Recorde-se, a este propsito, que o estudo elaborado pelo FinScope, de Agosto de 2009, conclura que em Moambique apenas 22.2% da populao adulta tinha acesso aos servios financeiros, nvel considerado bastante baixo quando comparado com o de outros pases com caractersticas econmicas similares s de Moambique, nomeadamente a Tanznia (46%) e o Malawi (45%). Este nvel de acesso aos servios financeiros que o nosso pas possui mostra a elevada excluso de utilizao dos servios e produtos financeiros por parte significativa da populao. O mesmo estudo concluiu que a situao de excluso  mais acentuada nas zonas rurais onde 86.5% da populao no tem nenhuma relao com as instituies financeiras contra 61% nas zonas urbanas. Todavia, apraz-nos observar que este cenrio de fraco acesso aos produtos e servios financeiros est a ser progressivamente alterado. Os resultados at aqui alcanados encorajam-nos a darmos mais passos, por um sistema bancrio mais inclusivo. Com efeito, o nosso sistema financeiro conta actualmente com 16 bancos e 417 balces em funcionamento, distribudos por 58 dos 128 distritos do territrio nacional, contra uma cobertura de apenas 28 distritos at h pouco mais de 4 anos. A estes nmeros, acresce 7 cooperativas de crdito, 132 operadores de microcrdito e 8 microbancos. Refira-se tambm que dados reportados ao ms de Abril de 2011 davam conta de que o pas dispunha de um total de 747 ATM's e 5.051 POS's, contra 367 ATM's e 3.243 POS's at Setembro de 2006. Distintos Convidados Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores O mundo conheceu nos ltimos trs a quatro anos uma das mais severas crises econmicas e financeiras de que se tem memria, com repercusses nefastas, particularmente a nvel do comrcio externo dos pases em desenvolvimento, que viram as suas exportaes a baixarem consideravelmente, agravando a balana de transaces correntes dos respectivos pases. Este factor, para alm de produzir instabilidade na gesto macroeconmica, tambm provocou em alguns pases recesses econmicas prejudicando os esforos que vinham realizando na implementao de polticas e estratgias de combate  pobreza. Moambique no ficou imune a essas adversidades. Todavia, as corajosas reformas econmicas e legislativas visando a criao de adequado ambiente de negcios permitiram que as taxas mdias de crescimento econmico no perodo se situassem acima da mdia africana. Neste esforo, o sector financeiro sempre esteve presente, alinhando as suas estratgias empresariais s polticas econmicas governamentais, sempre  procura de solues para o problema do financiamento  economia, provimento de servios financeiros inovadores e de qualidade e alcanando um nmero cada vez maior de cidados moambicanos.  neste contexto que se enquadra a iniciativa da criao da Sociedade Interbancria de Moambique, que surge numa altura em que, para alm do crescimento a que se assiste em termos de nmero de estabelecimentos bancrios, a actividade do sistema bancrio  marcada pelo desenvolvimento de novos produtos de poupana e crdito e pela expanso dos canais de distribuio como a rede de POS's e ATM's. No entanto, coexistem 6 redes de pagamentos electrnicos que funcionam de forma no integrada. Com a entrada em funcionamento desta sociedade interbancria, as ATMs e os POS's vo deixar de operar de forma isolada, passando a estar conectados a uma nica rede nacional. Por seu turno, os bancos, face  reduo dos custos que resultaro da partilha da infra-estrutura tecnolgica, estaro em melhores condies para se expandirem, mesmo para as zonas em que no tenham uma presena fsica. Esse desiderato est em linha com a referida estratgia de bancarizao da nossa economia, cujo objectivo  a incluso financeira dos moambicanos, provendo-lhes servios financeiros diversificados e de boa qualidade. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Com a implantao da SIMO e incio das suas actividades, teremos seguramente importantes ganhos econmicos de escala, implicando a reduo dos custos unitrios das transaces financeiras. Esperam-se ganhos multifacetados para os bancos comerciais, para os clientes, para a sociedade e a para a economia em geral. Relativamente aos bancos comerciais, os ganhos traduzir-se-o numa maior eficincia na prestao dos seus servios, na racionalizao dos custos, uma vez servidos por uma rede tecnolgica comum, de acesso universal, o que permite a satisfao das necessidades dos clientes domsticos e dos que viajam para fora das fronteiras nacionais. Por seu turno, os consumidores iro beneficiar de acesso universal duma variedade de produtos e servios financeiros. Outro ganho para os clientes consistir na possibilidade de usarem indistintamente terminais dos diferentes produtos e servios financeiros (nomeadamente POS's, ATM's, internet banking, mobile phone banking), sem com isso onerar o seu bolso. O cliente que apenas precise de carto para uso domstico no ser obrigado a possuir um carto cuja compensao  feita fora do territrio nacional, como so os casos da Visa ou MasterCard. Outra valncia que decorrer da entrada em funcionamento dos servios da SIMO ser o incremento do n de produtos disponveis. Com efeito, com a utilizao partilhada da infra-estrutura de pagamentos assegurada pela Sociedade Interbancria de Moambique, ser ainda possvel que os clientes do sistema bancrio faam uso de servios de ATM ou POS de qualquer dos bancos a operar no Pas, com ganhos de eficincia evidentes, para alm de acederem a mais e variados servios correlacionados. Para a sociedade e a economia em geral, haver tambm ganhos significativos, que se traduziro, nomeadamente, no aumento do nmero de clientes bancarizados, implicando uma maior incluso social em termos de benefcios no acesso s tecnologias de informao e comunicao.  indubitvel que o acesso cada vez mais massificado s tecnologias de informao e comunicao representa, em ltima instncia, um contributo no combate comum contra a pobreza. Em suma, a SIMO tem o papel de impulsionar a bancarizao da economia, bem assim o de massificar a utilizao de instrumentos de pagamento electrnicos alternativos ao numerrio, contribuindo, deste modo, para a melhoria das condies de prestao de servios de pagamentos a nvel nacional e aumentar a eficincia e a eficcia da intermediao financeira. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores, Foi tendo em conta a multiplicidade de vantagens a que exemplificativamente me referi que a iniciativa de criao da SIMO mereceu a aderncia do sistema bancrio, que desde cedo compreendeu que a concorrncia no ficar prejudicada pela circunstncia de haver partilha da infra-estrutura tecnolgica. Na verdade, a concorrncia  funo da eficincia, criatividade, inovao e qualidade dos servios prestados e dos produtos disponibilizados por cada instituio. No sector financeiro, estes factores diferenciadores esto sempre presentes e a legislao promove e defende a concorrncia. Por conseguinte, no posso terminar a minha interveno sem antes manifestar o meu apreo s quinze instituies de crdito que corporizam este projecto, integrando, a par do Banco Central, a estrutura accionista da SIMO, designadamente: African Banking Corporation, Banco Comercial e de Investimento, Banco Mercantil e de Investimento, Banco Oportunidade de Moambique, Banco Terra, Barclays Bank, Cooperativa de Poupana e Crdito, First National Bank, International Commercial Bank, Millennium BIM, Moza Banco, Procredit, Socremo, Standard Bank e The Mauritius Commercial Bank. Sado ainda o Banco nico e o TCHUMA, que recentemente se juntaram a este projecto. No deixaria tambm de expressar a minha palavra de reconhecimento aos membros do Comit de Coordenao do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos e aos membros da Comisso Interbancria de Operacionalizao da SIMO, cujo envolvimento permitiu a concretizao do projecto de constituio da sociedade. Reconhecendo que o alcance dos objectivos da SIMO requer o concurso duma infra- estrutura de comunicaes e de uma poltica de expanso de rede elctrica alinhados com os desafios decorrentes do avano do sistema financeiro, gostaria de manifestar o meu encorajamento aos senhores Presidentes dos Conselhos de Administrao das Telecomunicaes de Moambique e da Electricidade de Moambique, tambm aqui presentes, a quem sado pelos progressos que se tm vindo a registar em ambos os sectores. Expresso ainda a minha gratido aos trabalhadores do Banco de Moambique e das demais instituies que integram a SIMO, bem assim a todos quantos de forma directa ou indirecta prestaram a sua colaborao at que chegssemos  fase em que hoje nos encontramos. A futura Direco e aos trabalhadores da SIMO, o meu apelo  devoo ao trabalho, ao esprito de trabalho em equipa e ao profissionalismo. Para terminar, queria, por um lado, recordar aos accionistas da SIMO o grande desafio que temos pela frente na materializao dos objectivos traados com a criao desta sociedade e, por outro, aproveitar o ensejo para reiterar o convite aos outros Bancos Comerciais que ainda no o fizeram para aderirem a esta iniciativa conjunta que certamente ir melhorar os servios bancrios no pas. Muito obrigado.

Title: Speech at the 31st Anniversary of the Metical Celebrations
text: SPEECH OF YOUR EXCIA. THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE ON THE OCCASION OF METICAL's 31 ANNIVERSARY CELEBRATIONS MAPUTO, JUNE 16, 2011 Mr. Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency, Your Excellese St. Administrators of the Bank of Mozambique; Representatives of credit institutions; Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Dear Guests; Ladies; Gentlemen; On behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, I would like to begin by addressing all my words of welcome to all and thanking you for your presence, which greatly honors and sensitizes me. Today, June 16th, is a particularly remarkable day in our history. Indeed, throughout the country is commemorated by the31st anniversary of the creation of the national currency, the Metical, one of the constitutionally enshrined elements of our nation. The creation of the Metical on June 16, 1980, through Law No2 2/80, represented a major milestone in the process of consolidating national independence and sovereignty and affirming our identity and our Mozambicanity. It underscores the historical symbolism of June 16 the fact that it marked the 51-year-old passage of the Mueda Massacre, in which several Mozambicans were savagely murdered when they claimed their legitimate rights. For the reasons mentioned above, a special greeting is due to all our compatriots, who, in various forms and at different stages, have been involved in this long process of consolidation of the Metical. I extend my warm greeting to the Mozambicans who on June 16, 1980 made their contribution in the exchange of the Portuguese Shield for the Metical, going from les-a-les to the national territory, within the framework of what became known as Operation Zero. It is legitimate to pay homage to them in the spirit of mission and dedication to the national cause that these fellow citizens have demonstrated in this delicate process. Today we also remember and pay a fitting tribute to the martyrs of Mueda. On this occasion, I would also like to congratulate the Government of Mozambique, the economic agents, financial institutions and our compatriots in general for their great contribution, ensuring that the Metical fully fulfils the functions that are legally reserved for it, namely that of a unit of value with legal course in the national territory, intermediary of exchange, payment and value reservation. Dear Guests Ladies Gentlemen The preservation of the value of our currency is the main missionthat Law No . 1 and 1/92 of January 3nd assigns to the Bank of Mozambique. In order to carry out this mission, we have taken concerted actions to stimulate savings, so that investment flourishes, as well as to defend the purchasing power of citizens, especially the poorest layers, in the general context of combating poverty in our country. It is a source of joy that our Government, in the person of the Head of State, has chosen june for the launch of the national campaign to promote savings. June is the month of the proclamation of national independence; June is the month of glory, June is also the month of hope. We warmly welcome this government initiative because we recognise the importance of attracting more savings from the public, businesses and families. In fact, with the channeling of these savings to the financial sector, the capacity of banks to support the various investment initiatives, with quality credit, that will increase economic growth, increase the level of employment and contribute to the external sustainability of our country. We are confident in the role and place of Metical in our economy, which requires synergies from all, aimed at increasing domestic production, replacing imports, increasing and diversifying our exports and investing in innovation and increasing the productivity of businesses and economic actors in general. We are pleased to note the contribution of various government bodies in the meta-investigation of our economy, by raising awareness that service providers and suppliers of goods understand, take and take to the last consequences that Metical, in banknotes and coins, has mandatory legal course and unlimited and full liberatory value within the national territory and also, in the same perspective, so that invoicing and pricing for domestic transactions are made in national currency. In this case, conditions are created for greater price stability and consequent improvement of our standard of living. Our commitment to Metical - the national currency of the Republic of Mozambique - is to implement monetary policy measures to ensure the reduction and control of inflation and the stability of interbank markets; measures that result in an increasingly comprehensive preference of economic agents in our country's currency; measures to improve our balance of payments. We do not want - and would never act in this direction - to interfere with the financial assets of citizens. The law allows economic agents to have accounts denominated in foreign currency and this is therefore guaranteed. The ongoing efforts of coordinated implementation of consistent macroeconomic policies have resulted in gross domestic product growth rates above the African average, such as the 8.4% annual recorded in the first quarter of 2011, thus enabling, alongside the trend towards reducing inflation and appreciation of the exchange rate, a greater preference for the Metical in domestic transactions that occur in our economy. We must continue with economic reforms that lead to more investment, more employment and greater competitiveness in the country. The liberalisation of the current account balance, the main desideratum of the new foreign exchange law and its regulation, offers a unique opportunity for the external sector of our economy to assert itself, grow and expand. But the affirmation in foreign trade requires, in addition to increasing production and productivity, modernization innovation and quality. We therefore call for this period, characterised by general liquidity shortages worldwide, to be able to make efficient use of the resource windows available in the national financial sector and multilateral financial institutions. The investments that the financial sector, under the guidance of the Bank of Mozambique, is making within the framework of the Interbank Society of Mozambique (SIMO), officially created on 6 June, are also part of the global strategy to strengthen the use of Metical in Mozambique. Dear guests. Ladies Gentlemen. Since the creation of metical on 16 June 1980, the country has undergone many socio-economic transformations. The result of peace, the consequent macroeconomic policies and especially the selfless work of all Mozambicans, Mozambique has experienced significant stability in recent years. Against this backdrop, in 2006, the Bank of Mozambique introduced an adjustment in the national currency, adopting the third metical family, i.e. the "Bank of Mozambique" family, which follows the first two, namely the "People's Republic of Mozambique" family and the "Republic of Mozambique" family. The Bank of Mozambique has taken care of the introduction of the latest banknote printing and coining technologies in the design of the new Metical family and has assumed the need to raise and immortalize some values representative of our vast historical, cultural, economic and faunistic heritage. Some five years after the introduction, with recognised success, of the third Metical family and in view of the ongoing expansion of the financial sector by the national territory, as well as the increase in the number of monetary transactions, the volume of monetary circulation and the economic agents involved in those transactions, it is necessary to ensure protection metical banknotes by adjusting their safety elements and production material. I therefore have the honour of, under the special powers conferred on me by Article 47 of Law No. 1/92 of 3 January - Organic Law of the Bank of Mozambique - to announce the introduction of a new series of banknotes, endortined with improved safety devices and elements that facilitate the identification of the various denominations through tact. Another milestone in the improvements made is the alteration of the substrate of the notes of 20 MT, 50 MT and 100 MT. The choice of these names results from the fact that they are the most rotating and therefore exhibited the relatively greater wear. After a specialised study we carried out, the option for enhancing the consistency of banknotes was to replace the paper substrate with polymer, which is a synthetic material, particularly adjusted to humid climates, currently in use in banknotes from more than thirty countries, namely Zambia, Nigeria, Australia, Chile, Paraguay, Honduras, Singapore, Malaysia and Mexico, and is expected to be released this year also in Canada. With the adoption of this type of substrate, we hope to significantly reduce the costs in which we incur with the replacement of degraded banknotes, prolonging the longevity of banknotes and also complying with our legal duty to provide the public, in the best conditions of safety and convenience, good quality notes and hardly imitable. For the 200 MT, 500 MT and 1,000 MT banknotes, they maintain the paper substrate, but improvements to the safety elements have been introduced. In the meantime, I would like to draw your special attention to the fact that the reasons for the Metical notes of the third family remain, thus keeping present the expression of these values of our historical, cultural, economic and faunistic heritage. The new banknotes will enter circulation later this year. However, the entry into circulation of the improved banknotes does not mean the introduction of a new family, nor will it entail the withdrawal of the banknotes currently in circulation. There will therefore be simultaneous movement, during which time we will have a gradual process of introducing the improved banknotes, which the public will normally obtain in commercial and banking transactions and there is therefore no place in exchange. Today we begin the process of disseminating the new notes. We are convinced that the success of this work will depend on a broad and participatory dissemination campaign that reaches our entire country and Mozambican communities abroad, through the resources available, including the media. Dear Guests, Ladies Gentlemen I could not finish my speech without reiterating my call to contest everyone in the dignification and conservation of the Metical notes and coins. By properly preserving our Metical, we save the country's currency. In this regard, allow me to quote the preamble to Law 2/80, The Metical Law: "The struggle for currency stability is an integral part of the struggle for economic development. Currency stability requires an ever-increasing increase in production and productivity, as well as increased surveillance against all acts and attempts to misuse our currency." (End of quote). At this time, I would like to draw your attention to the presentation of the following notes. Thank you very much!
text_original: DISCURSO DE SUA EXCIA. O GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE POR OCASIO DAS COMEMORAES DO 31^ ANIVERSRIO DO METICAL MAPUTO, 16 DE JUNHO DE 2011 Senhor Vice-Governador do Banco de Moambique, Excelncia, Excelentssimos Senhores Administradores do Banco de Moambique; Senhores Representantes das Instituies de Crdito; Senhores Directores do Banco de Moambique; Caros Convidados; Minhas Senhoras; Meus Senhores; Em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, gostaria de, neste dia festivo, comear por dirigir a todos as minhas palavras de boas-vindas e por agradecer a vossa presena, que muito me honra e sensibiliza. Hoje, 16 de Junho,  um dia particularmente marcante da nossa Histria. Com efeito, comemora-se, em todo o pas, o 319 aniversrio da criao da moeda nacional, o Metical, um dos elementos identitrios da nossa Nao, constitucionalmente consagrado. A criao do Metical a 16 de Junho de 1980, atravs da Lei n2 2/80, representou um marco de grande relevo no processo de consolidao da independncia e soberania nacionais e da afirmao da nossa identidade e da nossa moambicanidade. Alicera o simbolismo histrico do 16 de Junho o facto de marcar a passagem de 51 anos sobre o Massacre de Mueda, no qual vrios moambicanos foram barbaramente assassinados quando reivindicavam seus legtimos direitos. Pelas razes mencionadas, uma saudao especial  devida a todos os nossos compatriotas, que, sob diversas formas e em diferentes etapas, se tm vindo a envolver neste longo processo de consolidao do Metical. Estendo a minha calorosa saudao aos moambicanos que no dia 16 de Junho de 1980 deram o seu contributo na troca do Escudo portugus pelo Metical, percorrendo de ls-a-ls o territrio nacional, no quadro do que ficou conhecido por Operao Zero.  legtimo render-lhes homenagem, face ao esprito de misso e dedicao  causa nacional que esses nossos concidados demonstraram nesse delicado processo. Recordamos e rendemos tambm hoje uma justa homenagem aos mrtires de Mueda. Nesta oportunidade, gostaria igualmente de felicitar o Governo de Moambique, os agentes econmicos, as instituies financeiras e os nossos compatriotas em geral, pela grande contribuio que tm prestado, garantindo que o Metical cumpra na ntegra as funes que lhe esto legalmente reservadas, nomeadamente a de unidade de valor com curso legal no territrio nacional, intermedirio de troca, meio de pagamento e reserva de valor. Caros Convidados Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores A preservao do valor da nossa moeda  a principal misso que a Lei ne 1/92, de 3 de Janeiro, atribui ao Banco de Moambique. Para o cumprimento dessa misso, temos levado a cabo aces concertadas tendentes a estimular a poupana, para que o investimento floresa, bem assim para a defesa do poder de compra dos cidados, sobretudo das camadas mais pobres, no mbito geral de combate  pobreza no nosso pas. Constitui motivo de regozijo o facto de o nosso Governo, na pessoa do Chefe do Estado, ter escolhido o ms de Junho para o lanamento da campanha nacional de promoo da poupana. Junho  o ms da proclamao da Independncia nacional; Junho  o ms da glria, Junho  tambm o ms da esperana. Saudamos vivamente esta iniciativa do Governo porque reconhecemos a importncia da captao de mais poupanas do pblico, das empresas e das famlias. Na verdade, com a canalizao dessas poupanas ao sector financeiro, multiplicar-se- a capacidade dos bancos de apoio s diversas iniciativas de investimento, com crdito de qualidade, que alavanque o crescimento econmico, eleve o nvel de emprego e contribua para a sustentabilidade externa do nosso Pas. Estamos confiantes no papel e no lugar do Metical na nossa economia, o que exige sinergias de todos, direccionadas ao aumento da produo interna, que substitua as importaes, ao incremento e diversificao das nossas exportaes e ao investimento na inovao e na elevao da produtividade das empresas e dos agentes econmicos em geral. Apraz-nos notar o contributo de vrios organismos do Governo na meticalizao da nossa economia, atravs da sensibilizao para que as instituies prestadoras de servios e fornecedoras de bens compreendam, assumam e levem at s ltimas consequncias que o Metical, em notas e moedas metlicas, tem curso legal obrigatrio e valor liberatrio ilimitado e pleno dentro do territrio nacional e tambm, na mesma perspectiva, para que a facturao e a fixao de preos pela realizao de transaces domsticas sejam feitas em moeda nacional. Assim procedendo-se, criam-se condies para uma maior estabilidade dos preos e consequente melhoria do nosso nvel de vida. A nossa aposta no Metical - a moeda nacional da Repblica de Moambique -  no sentido de implementarmos medidas de poltica monetria que garantam a reduo e o controlo da inflao e a estabilidade dos mercados interbancrios; medidas que resultem numa cada vez mais abrangente preferncia dos agentes econmicos na moeda do nosso pas; medidas que possibilitem a melhoria da nossa balana de pagamentos. No pretendemos - e jamais actuaramos nesse sentido - interferir nos activos financeiros dos cidados. A lei permite que os agentes econmicos possuam contas denominadas em moeda estrangeira e isso est, portanto, garantido. Os esforos em curso de aplicao coordenada de polticas macroeconmicas consistentes tm resultado em taxas de crescimento do produto interno bruto acima da mdia africana, tal como os 8,4% anuais registados no primeiro trimestre de 2011, possibilitando, assim, a par da tendncia para a reduo da inflao e a apreciao da taxa de cmbio uma maior preferncia pelo Metical nas transaces internas que ocorrem na nossa economia. Devemos prosseguir com reformas econmicas que induzam mais investimentos, mais emprego e maior competitividade do Pais. A liberalizao da balana de transaces correntes, principal desiderato da nova lei cambial e do seu respectivo regulamento, oferece uma oportunidade nica ao sector externo da nossa economia para afirmar-se, crescer e expandir. Mas a afirmao no comrcio externo requer, para alm do aumento da produo e produtividade, modernizao inovao e qualidade. Por isso, apelamos para que neste perodo, caracterizado por escassez geral de liquidez a nvel mundial, saibamos utilizar eficientemente as janelas de recursos disponveis a nvel do sector financeiro nacional e de instituies financeiras multilaterais. Os investimentos que o sector financeiro, sob a orientao do Banco de Moambique, est a levar a cabo no quadro da Sociedade Interbancria de Moambique (SIMO), oficialmente criada no dia 6 de Junho corrente, constituem tambm parte da estratgia global de reforo do uso do Metical em Moambique. Estimados convidados. Minhas Senhoras, Meus senhores. Desde a criao do Metical a 16 de Junho de 1980, o pas conheceu muitas transformaes scio-econmicas. Fruto da paz, das polticas macroeconmicas consequentes e sobretudo do trabalho abnegado de todos os moambicanos, Moambique tem vivido nos ltimos anos uma significativa estabilidade. Perante este cenrio, em 2006, o Banco de Moambique introduziu um ajustamento na moeda nacional, adoptando a terceira famlia do Metical, ou seja a famlia "Banco de Moambique", que sucede s primeiras duas, designadamente a famlia "Repblica Popular de Moambique" e a famlia "Repblica de Moambique". O Banco de Moambique socorreu-se da introduo das ltimas tecnologias de impresso de notas e cunhagem de moedas metlicas na concepo da nova famlia do Metical e assumiu a necessidade da elevao e da imortalizao de alguns valores representativos do nosso vasto patrimnio histrico, cultural, econmico e faunstico. Decorridos cerca de 5 anos aps a introduo, com reconhecido xito, da terceira famlia do Metical e face  expanso em curso do sector financeiro pelo territrio nacional, bem assim ao incremento do nmero de transaces monetrias, do volume da circulao monetria e dos agentes econmico envolvidos nessas transaces, mostra-se necessrio assegurar proteco mais eficaz das notas do Metical, ajustando os seus elementos de segurana e o respectivo material de produo. Tenho, pois, a honra de, ao abrigo das competncias especiais que me so conferidas pelo artigo 47 da Lei ne 1/92, de 3 de Janeiro - Lei Orgnica do Banco de Moambique - anunciar a introduo de uma nova srie de notas, dotadas de dispositivos de segurana melhorados e de elementos que facilitam a identificao das vrias denominaes atravs do tacto. Outro marco assinalvel nos melhoramentos efectuados  a alterao do substrato das notas de 20 MT, 50 MT e 100 MT. A escolha destas denominaes resulta do facto de serem as de maior rotao e expostas, por conseguinte, a relativamente maior desgaste. Aps um estudo especializado que efectumos, a opo para o reforo da consistncia das notas foi de substituio do substrato de papel pelo polmero, que  um material sinttico, particularmente ajustado a climas hmidos, actualmente em uso em notas de mais de trinta pases, nomeadamente Zmbia, Nigria, Austrlia, Chile, Paraguai, Honduras, Singapura, Malsia e Mxico, prevendo-se para este ano a sua introduo tambm no Canad. Com a adopo deste tipo de substrato, esperamos reduzir significativamente os custos em que incorremos com a reposio das notas degradadas, prolongando a longevidade das notas e tambm cumprir com o nosso dever legal de fornecer ao pblico, nas melhores condies de segurana e comodidade, notas de boa qualidade e dificilmente imitveis. Relativamente s notas de 200 MT, 500 MT e 1.000 MT, elas mantm o substrato de papel, tendo sido, porm, introduzidos melhoramentos dos elementos de segurana. Entretanto, gostaria de chamar a vossa especial ateno para o facto de que permanecem os motivos das notas do Metical da terceira famlia, mantendo-se, assim, presente a expresso dos referidos valores do nosso patrimnio histrico, cultural, econmico e faunstico. As novas notas entram em circulao ainda este ano. No entanto, a entrada em circulao das notas melhoradas no significa a introduo de uma nova famlia, nem implicar a retirada das notas actualmente em circulao. Haver, portanto, uma circulao simultnea, perodo durante o qual teremos um processo gradual de introduo das notas melhoradas, que o pblico obter normalmente nas transaces comerciais e bancrias, no havendo, por isso, lugar a postos de troca. Iniciamos hoje o processo de divulgao das novas notas. Estamos convictos de que o sucesso deste trabalho depender de uma campanha de divulgao ampla e participativa, que alcance todo o nosso Pas e as comunidades moambicanas no exterior, atravs dos recursos disponveis, incluindo os meios de comunicao social. Estimados Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, No poderia terminar esta minha interveno sem reiterar o meu apelo ao concurso de todos na dignificao e conservao das notas e moedas do Metical. Conservando condignamente o nosso Metical, poupamos divisas ao Pas. A este propsito, permitam-me que cite o prembulo da Lei 2/80, Lei do Metical: "A luta pela estabilidade da moeda  parte integrante da luta pelo desenvolvimento econmico. A estabilidade da moeda exige o aumento sempre crescente da produo e produtividade, assim como o reforo de vigilncia contra todos os actos e tentativas de utilizar indevidamente a nossa moeda." (Fim da citao). Neste momento, gostaria de atrair a vossa ateno para a apresentao das notas que se segue. Muito obrigado!

Title: End of the Economic Year 2011
text: Mr Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency Mr President of THE INE, Excellency Former Governors of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellencies; Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Presidents of the Boards of Directors of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations; Presidents of Executive Committees of Financial Institutions; Members of the Audit Board of the Bank of Mozambique; Dear Directors, Assistant Directors and Managers of the Bank of Mozambique; Distinguished Guests; Ladies; and Gentlemen. It is with renewed honor that we welcome you to this house, for the usual preliminary balance sheet meeting of the economic and financial year that is about to end and presentation of our prospects for next year and the main monetary policy lines related to the achievement of the economic and financial policy objectives set by the Government of Mozambique. I would first of all like to express our gratitude to you all on behalf of the Board of Directors and in Introduction and my personal name. Greetings partners, including credit institutions and financial corporations operating in the country, economic and socio-professional associations, trade unions, academic community, international cooperation partners and the media, whose collaboration has greatly contributed to the fulfilment of our mission. Allow me to address a special greeting to our Government for the important measures and actions taken throughout this year in the various areas of activity, including the consolidation of the culture of peace and tolerance, the numerous acts to strengthen the country's credibility in Africa and the world, social and economic measures aimed at alleviating the suffering of thousands of our compatriots affected by natural disasters or the effects of the economic and financial crisis that marks the global situation, the strategic orientation for public investments and public-private partnerships to catapult the country's infrastructure, the reforms undertaken to attract new investments, both domestic and foreign, and the attention it has paid to the complex process of exploiting the enormous potential of natural resources available to the country, to accelerate the march of our development, promoting rapid, robust and inclusive economic growth. This year, the collective effort of millions of Mozambicans and Mozambicans and the commitment of their institutions has been positively appreciated by international financial institutions monitoring the economic and financial programme that Mozambique maintains with them, as part of our participation in the International Monetary Fund, World Bank, African Development Bank, Islamic Bank, among others. There have been numerous support and supervision missions we have received from these institutions, most nodding to the visits of the Director-General of the World Bank, the Executive Director of our constituent office at the IMF, and the fact that we have hosted, for the first time, a meeting of the Islamic Bank, following the appointment of a Mozambican to its Board of Directors. This demonstrates the interest and commitment of the international community to ongoing reforms, macroeconomic management and policies that have been implemented in the country, within the national agenda of prioritizing the fight against poverty. Distinguished Guests Ladies, and My Lords Performance of the Monetary and Exchange Policy Performance of the Monetary and Exchange Policy On the other hand, inflation measured by the annual change in the Maputo City Price Index, which reached 16.6% at the close of 2010, has shown a clear trend for the slowdown since January , having retreated to 7.74% in November, the same with average inflation falling to 11.27% in the same period, after 15.37% in April. The slowdown in inflation throughout the year was supported by a more stable and desirable Metical in domestic transactions , the increased domestic supply of fruits and vegetables, products with considerable impact on the behaviour of this indicator, and the increased confidence of economic agents in the future of our economy. The performance of the financial indicators also reflects the impact of the corrective measures we adopted from August 2010 and which were embodied in the downward revision of our interest rates for intervention in the Interbank Money Market, in the adjustment of the Compulsory Reserve coefficient, as well as in the strengthening of our interventions in interbank markets, especially at the level of the foreign exchange market, providing an increasing volume of foreign exchange, part of which for the coverage of a higher import invoice for liquid fuels and other essential products for the operation of our economy. These measures proved necessary for the replacement of the macroeconomic balance, an important factor for economic growth gains to be more noticeable and for the country to continue to attract more domestic and foreign investment, in addition to being our main mission to ensure low and stable inflation that protects the purchasing power of households, especially from the less favoured layers of our vast Mozambique. Last week, there was less than a month of the end of the year - in view of the positive results obtained and based on the forecasts that we have of an alignment of inflation with the target set for 2012, without losing sight of the prevailing risks internally and externally, we will relieve monetary policy conditions by lowering the rate of the Permanent Ease of Transfer (FPC) by 100 bp to 15% and reducing the Mandatory Reserve coefficient by 25 bp to 8.5%, measures aimed at ensuring the release of bank liquidity, to support a further expansion of bank credit to the private sector, with more attractive rates, and thus consolidate the foundations of economic growth in progress, generating higher income and creating new jobs, in a context where we need to be more cautious about the contagion of the international financial crisis and the expectations of new restrictions on access to foreign finance and the international market. Monetary sector data show that the balance of credit to the economy at the end of October was 94,261 million Meticais, corresponding to an annual expansion of 11.4%. When the effect of metical's assessment on the foreign currency denominated credit component is expunged, this indicator grows to 17%. The Monetary Base - the operational variable of monetary policy - stood in November at 31,380.4 million Meticais, corresponding to an annual expansion of 2.8%, justified by substantial changes in the demand for Banknotes and Coins in Circulation and their more appropriate management by credit institutions, which is in line with our objectives of massify the use of alternative means of payment for the execution and settlement of transactions, the result of the immense investment being made in the modernization of the national payment system and in the banking of our economy and the expansion of financial services. In September, the current account balance including major projects deteriorated by 38% compared to the same period in 2010, justified by expenditure associated with investments taking place in the country, especially in the area of mineral resource exploration. When transactions are withdrawn from major projects, the current account deficit improves by 2.1% as a result of improved exports compared to increased imports. The entry of foreign exchange in the country, derived from export revenues, whether from private transfers, private external loans, foreign direct investment, in the amount of USD 381.2 million, and unilateral current transfers to the public sector in amounts higher than those recorded in 2010, not only provided the accumulation of International Liquid reserves of the WB in a total amount of USD 280 million, causing the balance to be USD 2200 million, until December 15, as well as contributing to the Bank of Mozambique selling less foreign currency compared to 2010, and there were periods in which, seeking to mitigate the appreciation of the exchange rate, it positioned itself as a buyer in the MCI. Total MCI sales as of last week were 549 million, about 30% less than the same period in 2010, while purchases amounted to about 152 million, representing an increase of 111 million compared to the whole of last year. Ladies Gentlemen In the year about to end, we prepared the necessary conditions for the implementation of the new exchange rate legislation. The new regulation completely liberalises current transactions, but creates appropriate registration mechanisms for the purposes of verifying and building the balance of payments. The current framework represents a further advance in the speed of transactions that economic agents carry out with the outside world and has been in line with international standards and good practice, facilitating the free movement of people, goods and services. After a long and careful process of preparation of the regulation, its implementation had as fundamental components the dissemination and training of the main foreign exchange operators, private sector, importers, exporters, public and private institutions that intervene in trade with abroad, media consulting companies, among others. Platforms for consultation and permanent clarification were established, through dedicated lines, correspondence, various meetings and work meetings. All these actions have been done in such a way as to mitigate potential negative impacts on the economy and on the expectations of economic operators and the general public. In order to make it faster and faster to realization of foreign exchange operations, where this proved necessary, we assume a posture of making the procedural matter more flexible, through the issuance of Notices and Circulars. It is worth remembering that the delegation of powers to commercial banks to license current transactions was generally welcomed by the public and economic agents. Since the entry into force on 11 July of this new device, the preference for the use of Metical in domestic transactions has grown and consolidated, as has the use of electronic means of payment; alternatives to cash. It should be noted that, in the wake of our forecasts, exchange rate stability based on greater availability of foreign exchange is also associated with the process of implementing the new exchange rate regulation, which provides, among others, for faster payment mechanisms for foreign operations, less circulation of foreign currency in the form of cash in the domestic market and greater availability of foreign exchange in the banking system. Ladies Gentlemen The Mozambican financial system continues to strengthen in terms of the number, diversity and quality of services provided. In fact, in 2011 we saw the entry of two new banking institutions, bringing the national total to 18 banks. In addition, 3 microbanks, 43 microcredit operators and a considerable number of other financial operators have entered into operation in our financial market. We also registered the opening of new bank branches, with the total in operation running from 416 in December 2010 to 440 in 2011, covering all provincial capitals, municipalities and a total of 58 districts. It is important to note that this growth in our financial sector occurs in a context where the situation is characterised by the closure and bankruptcy of numerous financial institutions. Furthermore, the ongoing expansion respects the standards of prudential balance and health of our institutions, thanks to the professionalism and responsibility of managers and employees of credit institutions, without neglecting the regulatory action and supervision of the Bank of Mozambique. In this context, we have to inform you that despite the strong expansion of credit between 2008 and 2010, the unsubstantiated credit this year remains below 3% and the solvency ratio remains above the minimum levels required by the practices enshrined under the Basel I Agreement. The modernization of our national payment system remains one of the main objectives to be achieved in the short and medium term, because we recognize that this is the only way we can have a wider scope of banking services without necessarily implying the physical presence of banks in the various remote areas of the country. The formal constitution of the Interbank Service Society (SIMO) that occurred in June of this year is also in this light. Its implementation will mean greater efficiency for banks in providing their services, once served by a common technological infrastructure that allows universal access to a variety of financial products and services. Also in the wake of the modernization of our national payment system, the Bank of Mozambique has been following with satisfaction the growing use of bank cards in the Mozambican financial system, as a way to ensure speed, security and flexibility in carrying out various bank transactions by the citizen. Attempts at bank fraud, through the use, in some ATMs, of electronic card cloning devices, have deserved a rapid and professional response from the Bank of Mozambique, commercial banks, police authorities and other partners of the national banking system, with no risk being envisaged that compromises the process of modernizing the current national payment system. Ladies Gentlemen Distinguished Guests The world economy continues to show signs of slowing, with forecasts of moderate growth in 2011 and 2012, a situation justified by the unencouraging performance of major economies, which this year, unlike previous ones, has not been sufficiently opposed by the robust growth of emerging economies, given the increasing volatility and risk aversion on the part of investors. The worsening sovereign debt crisis in some eurozone countries has dominated the attention of the markets, and today it is pointed out as one of the factors for spreading risk and pessimism about the effectiveness of fiscal consolidation measures adopted by the European authorities. It is on this basis that the latest projections from the World Economic Outlook point to a low revision of global economic growth by around 30bp to 4.0%, determined by the slowdown in economic activity in the advanced (US and Eurozone) and emerging economies (China and India). For sub-Saharan Africa, the same source prospects a generalincrease in production and projects for 2012 an acceleration of the economic growth rate by 50bp to 5.75%, which will be accompanied by the iinence of risks of inflationary pressures throughout the year. The international financial crisis and market volatility also affect the Mozambican economy and its financial system. Assessing the data reported in November 2011, it is noted that the portfolio of investments of our international reserves has been affected, either by means of exchange rate fluctuations pronounced in the parity of the various currencies vis-a-vis the US Dollar, as a part of the continuous fall in interest rates in the international market, leading to the yields obtained this year, portfolio larger than in 2010, are slightly lower. Successive rating downgrades of countries and banks have required us to manage more cautiously by diversifying the instruments and markets for applying our reserves and more conservative risk exposure postures. Distinguished Guests Monetary policy in 2012 will continue to meet the government's final economic policy objectives, which forecast average annual inflation of 7.2%, GDP growth of 7.5% and 4.6 months of coverage of imports of non-factoriary goods and services by gross international reserves. The intermediate monetary policy target will allow an annual expansion of total means of payment (M3) around 18.9% and the possibility of increasing credit expansion to the economy by up to 22.2%. The monetary base - an instrumental variable of monetary policy - is expected to grow by not more than 17.5% and we anticipate that the balance of Net International Reserves will be USD 2.279 million. In order to achieve these objectives, the Bank of Mozambique will focus on the use of instruments available in the monetary and foreign exchange markets, complemented by moral persuasion actions and banking supervision to credit institutions. Our main challenges are summarized in the following: Continue to improve monetary policy management by strengthening our forecasting and response capacity to minimise the risks and uncertainties of the economic and financial environment and increase the effectiveness of the measures we have been taking; Continue to strengthen our role as supervisor and regulator of the financial system through risk-based supervision; Maintain ongoing efforts to adapt the practices and procedures already underway in the region regarding the specialty of the Central Bank; In partnership with credit institutions, continue the effort to bankare the national economy, modernize the national payment system and seek pricing for the most competitive financial services; Given the scenario of volatility in the international market, adopt a posture of greater prudence in the application of our international reserves, with a view to reducing the risk; In line with other institutions and bodies, continue to encourage the opening of more bank branches in rural areas with a view to creating an inclusive financial sector , on the one hand, and increasing the collection of savings in rural areas, on the other, an essential condition for increasing the resources available to the banking system for financing investment in our country. In achieving the objectives inherent in our central bank mission, we are aware of other actions that will require increased attention from us, including the physical expansion of our institution to provinces where we are not resettled, namely Gaza and Manica. Still on this treadmill, in view of the to address the growing need to better serve the financial system, state institutions and the economy in general, as well as improving the working conditions of our employees, we have started the construction of two root buildings adjacent to the bank's current head office. It is in the same perspective of improving working conditions that today we inaugurated the Bank of Mozambique Health Post. Ladies Gentlemen The challenges that 2012 holds for us, taking into account the prognoses of an adverse and uncertain international situation. Nevertheless, we believe in the capacity of government institutions and Mozambicans to face the risks that are envisioned as opportunities to maximize our potential, producing more to meet the needs of the internal market, diversifying our export products and exploring new markets and partnerships. On January 31, 2012, we will mark the 25-year period since the implementation of the first exchange rate reform measure in Mozambique, in the context of the Economic Rehabilitation Program, the PRE, which began that year. Twenty-five years later, we have a national currency that has been able to earn respect among economic agents and in our region, reflecting the economic growth effort we have all maintained over the years. I would like to challenge the bm's staff and the scholars of our economy in general to take this opportunity for scientific reflection on the adjustment process, the behaviour and role of the exchange rate in Mozambique. At the end, I would like to express my appreciation to the workers of the Bank of Mozambique and, through you, to all the workers of our financial system, for the dedication and commitment shown throughout 2011, and to renew my thanks to all of you, to economic agents, to society in general and to the international community. To all present and their families, I wish Happy Holidays and a prosperous New Year. I invite you to accompany me in a toast for the health of our financial system, of all of us and of our families! Thank you very much.
text_original: Senhor Vice-Governador do Banco de Moambique, Excelncia Senhor Presidente do INE, Excelncia Senhores Antigos Governadores do Banco de Moambique, Excelncias; Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique; Senhores Presidentes dos Conselhos de Administrao de Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras; Senhores Presidentes de Comisses Executivas de Instituies Financeiras; Senhores Membros do Conselho de Auditoria do Banco de Moambique; Caros Directores, Assistentes de Direco e Gestores do Banco de Moambique; Distintos Convidados; Minhas Senhoras; e Meus Senhores.  com renovada honra que vos acolhemos nesta casa, para o habitual encontro de balano preliminar do exerccio econmico e financeiro que est prestes a findar e de apresentao das nossas perspectivas para o prximo ano e das principais linhas de poltica monetria atinentes  consecuo dos objectivos de poltica econmica e financeira traados pelo Governo de Moambique. Quero, em primeiro lugar, em nome do Conselho de Administrao e em Introduo e meu nome pessoal, agradecer a vossa presena nesta cerimnia e aproveitar esta ocasio para expressar o nosso reconhecimento a todos Saudaes os parceiros, nomeadamente instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras que operam no pas, associaes econmicas e scio- profissionais, sindicatos, comunidade acadmica, parceiros de cooperao internacional e os rgos de comunicao social, cuja colaborao em muito tem contribudo para o cumprimento da nossa misso. Permitam-me que enderece uma saudao especial ao nosso Governo pelas importantes medidas e aces levadas a cabo ao longo do presente ano nos vrios domnios da actividade, nomeadamente a consolidao da cultura de paz e tolerncia, os inmeros actos para reforar a credibilidade do pas em frica e no mundo, as medidas sociais e econmicas visando aliviar o sofrimento de milhares de compatriotas nossos afectados por calamidades naturais ou pelos efeitos da crise econmica e financeira que marca a conjuntura mundial, a orientao estratgica para que os investimentos pblicos e as parcerias pblico- privadas catapultem a infra-estruturao do pas, as reformas empreendidas para atrair novos investimentos, nacionais e estrangeiros, e a ateno que tem prestado ao complexo processo de explorao do enorme potencial de recursos naturais de que o pas dispe, visando acelerar a marcha do nosso desenvolvimento, promovendo um crescimento econmico rpido, robusto e inclusivo.
