No presente ano, o esforo colectivo de milhes de moambicanas e moambicanos e o empenho das suas instituies voltaram a ser apreciados positivamente pelas instituies financeiras internacionais que monitoram o programa econmico e financeiro que Moambique mantm com as mesmas, no quadro da nossa participao no Fundo Monetrio Internacional, Banco Mundial, Banco Africano de Desenvolvimento, Banco Islmico, entre outras. Foram inmeras as misses de apoio e superviso que recebemos destas instituies, sendo de destacar as visitas da Directora-Geral do Banco Mundial, do Director Executivo da nossa constituncia no FMI, e o facto de termos hospedado, pela primeira vez, uma reunio do Banco Islmico, na sequncia da indicao de um moambicano para o seu Conselho de Administrao. Fica assim demonstrado o interesse e cometimento da comunidade internacional s reformas em curso,  gesto macroeconmica e s polticas que tm sido implementadas no pas, no mbito da agenda nacional de priorizar o combate  pobreza. Ilustres Convidados Minhas Senhoras, e Meus Senhores Desempenho da Poltica Monetria e Cambial Desempenho da Poltica Monetria e Cambial Por outro lado, a inflao medida pela variao anual do ndice de Preos da Cidade de Maputo, que atingiu 16,6% no fecho de 2010, mostrou, desde Janeiro, uma tendncia clara para a desacelerao, tendo recuado para 7.74% em Novembro, sucedendo o mesmo com a inflao mdia que baixou para 11,27% no mesmo perodo, aps 15,37% em Abril. A desacelerao da inflao ao longo do ano foi suportada por um Metical mais estvel e apetecvel nas transaces domsticas, pela maior oferta interna de frutas e vegetais, produtos com impacto considervel no comportamento deste indicador, e pela maior confiana dos agentes econmicos no futuro da nossa economia. O desempenho dos indicadores financeiros reflecte ainda o impacto das medidas correctivas que adoptmos a partir de Agosto de 2010 e que se consubstanciaram na reviso em alta das nossas taxas de juro de interveno no Mercado Monetrio Interbancrio, no ajustamento do coeficiente de Reserva Obrigatria, bem assim no reforo das nossas intervenes nos mercados interbancrios, sobretudo ao nvel do mercado cambial, disponibilizando um volume cada vez maior de divisas, parte das quais para a cobertura de uma maior factura de importao de combustveis lquidos e outros produtos essenciais para o funcionamento da nossa economia. Estas medidas mostraram-se necessrias para a reposio do equilbrio macroeconmico, factor importante para que os ganhos do crescimento econmico sejam mais perceptveis e para que o pas continue a atrair mais investimentos nacionais e estrangeiros, para alm de ser nossa misso principal assegurar uma inflao baixa e estvel, que proteja o poder de compra das famlias, sobretudo das camadas menos favorecidas do nosso vasto Moambique. Na semana passada, havia menos de um ms do fim do ano - em face dos resultados positivos obtidos e com base nas previses que temos de um alinhamento da inflao com o objectivo estabelecido para 2012, sem perder de vista os riscos prevalecentes interna e externamente, aligeirmos as condies de poltica monetria, baixando a taxa da Facilidade Permanente de Cedncia (FPC) em 100 pb, para 15% e reduzindo o coeficiente de Reserva Obrigatria em 25 pb, para 8,5%, medidas que visam garantir a libertao de liquidez bancria, para apoiar uma maior expanso do crdito bancrio ao sector privado, com taxas mais atractivas, e deste modo consolidarmos as bases do crescimento econmico em curso, a gerao de maior renda e a criao de novos postos de trabalho, num contexto em que precisamos de ter maiores cautelas para o efeito contgio da crise financeira internacional e das expectativas de novas restries no acesso ao financiamento externo e ao mercado internacional. Dados do sector monetrio mostram que o saldo do crdito  economia no final do ms de Outubro foi de 94.261 milhes de Meticais, correspondente a uma expanso anual de 11.4%. Quando expurgado o efeito da apreciao do Metical sobre a componente do crdito denominada em moeda estrangeira, este indicador cresce para 17%. A Base Monetria - varivel operacional da poltica monetria - situou-se, em Novembro, nos 31.380,4 milhes de Meticais, correspondente a uma expanso anual de 2.8%, justificada por alteraes substanciais na demanda por Notas e Moedas em Circulao e pela sua gesto mais adequada por parte das instituies de crdito, o que vai ao encontro dos nossos objectivos de massificar a utilizao de meios alternativos de pagamento para a realizao e liquidao das transaces, fruto do imenso investimento que est sendo realizado na modernizao do sistema nacional de pagamentos e na bancarizao da nossa economia e alargamento dos servios financeiros. Em Setembro, o saldo da conta corrente incluindo os grandes projectos deteriorou em 38% quando comparado com o perodo homlogo de 2010, justificado pelas despesas associadas aos investimentos que esto a ter lugar no pas, sobretudo na rea de explorao de recursos minerais. Quando retiradas as transaces dos grandes projectos, o dfice da conta corrente melhora em 2,1% em resultado da melhoria das nossas exportaes em relao ao acrscimo das importaes. A entrada de divisas que se verifica no pas, seja derivada das receitas de exportao, seja de transferncias privadas, emprstimos externos privados, investimento directo estrangeiro, no valor de USD 381,2 milhes, e transferncias correntes unilaterais para o sector pblico em montantes superiores aos registados em 2010, no s propiciaram a acumulao de Reservas Internacionais Liquidas do BM num montante total de 280 milhes de USD, fazendo com que o saldo se situasse nos 2200 milhes de USD, at ao dia 15 de Dezembro, como tambm contribuiu para que o Banco de Moambique vendesse menos divisas comparativamente a 2010, havendo inclusive perodos em que, procurando atenuar a apreciao da taxa de cmbio, posicionou-se como comprador no MCI. O total das vendas no MCI at  semana passada foi de USD 549 milhes, cerca de menos 30% relativamente a igual perodo de 2010, enquanto que as compras ascenderam a cerca de USD 152 milhes, representando um aumento de USD 111 milhes quando comparadas com todo o ano passado. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores No ano prestes a findar, preparmos as condies necessrias para a implementao da nova legislao cambial. O novo normativo liberaliza por completo as transaces correntes, criando, todavia, mecanismos adequados de registo para fins de verificao e construo da balana de pagamentos. O quadro actual representa um avano para maior celeridade das transaces que os agentes econmicos realizam com o exterior e veio conformar-se com os padres e boas prticas internacionais, facilitando a livre circulao de pessoas, mercadorias e servios. Aps um longo e aturado processo de preparao da regulamentao, a sua implementao teve como componentes fundamentais a divulgao e formao dos principais operadores cambiais, sector privado, importadores, exportadores, instituies pblicas e privadas que intervm no comrcio com o exterior, empresas de consultoria comunicao social, entre outros. Foram estabelecidas plataformas de consulta e esclarecimento permanente, atravs de linhas dedicadas, correspondncia, diversas reunies e encontros de trabalho. Todas estas aces foram feitas de forma a atenuar potenciais impactos negativos na economia e nas expectativas dos agentes econmicos e pblico em geral. Com o intuito de tornar cada vez mais clere a realizao das operaes cambiais, onde tal se mostrou necessrio, assumimos uma postura de flexibilizar a matria procedimental, atravs da emisso de Avisos e Circulares. Vale a pena lembrar que a delegao de competncias aos bancos comerciais para licenciarem as transaces correntes foi em geral bem acolhida pelo pblico e agentes econmicos. Desde a entrada em vigor, a 11 de Julho, deste novo dispositivo, a preferncia pelo uso do Metical nas transaces domsticas cresceu e consolidou-se, o mesmo acontecendo com o uso de meios electrnicos de pagamento; alternativos ao numerrio.Convm realar que, na esteira das nossas previses, a estabilidade cambial baseada numa maior disponibilidade de divisas tambm se associa ao processo de implementao da nova regulamentao cambial, que prev, entre outros, mecanismos mais cleres de pagamentos das operaes com o exterior, menor circulao de moeda estrangeira sob forma de numerrio no mercado domstico e maior disponibilidade de divisas no sistema bancrio. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores O sistema financeiro moambicano continua a fortalecer-se em termos de nmero, diversidade e qualidade dos servios prestados. Com efeito, assistimos, em 2011,  entrada de duas novas instituies bancrias, elevando o total nacional para 18 bancos. Adicionalmente, entraram em funcionamento no nosso mercado financeiro mais 3 microbancos, 43 operadores de microcrdito e um nmero considervel de outros operadores financeiros. Registmos tambm a abertura de novos balces de bancos, tendo o total em funcionamento passado de 416 em Dezembro de 2010 para 440 em 2011, cobrindo todas as capitais provinciais, municpios e um total de 58 distritos. Importante notar que este crescimento do nosso sector financeiro ocorre num contexto em que a nvel mundial a situao  caracterizada pelo encerramento e falncia de inmeras instituies financeiras. Mais ainda, a expanso em curso respeita os padres de equilbrio prudencial e sade das nossas instituies, merc do profissionalismo e responsabilidade dos gestores e colaboradores das instituies de crdito, sem descurar a aco reguladora e a superviso do Banco de Moambique. Neste contexto, temos a informar que apesar da forte expanso do crdito entre 2008 e 2010, o crdito malparado no presente ano continua abaixo dos 3% e o rcio de solvabilidade mantm-se acima dos nveis mnimos exigidos pelas prticas consagradas no mbito do Acordo de Basileia I. A modernizao do nosso sistema nacional de pagamentos continua a ser um dos principais objectivos a alcanar no curto e mdio prazos, por reconhecermos que s assim poderemos ter, a breve trecho, uma maior abrangncia dos servios bancrios sem, contudo, implicar necessariamente a presena fsica de bancos nas diversas zonas recnditas do pas. A constituio formal da Sociedade Interbancria de Servios (SIMO) ocorrida em Junho do presente ano enquadra-se igualmente neste prisma. A sua implementao ir significar maior eficincia para os bancos na prestao dos seus servios, uma vez servidos por uma infraestrutura tecnolgica comum que permite o acesso universal a uma variedade de produtos e servios financeiros. Ainda na esteira da modernizao do nosso sistema nacional de pagamentos, o Banco de Moambique tem acompanhado com satisfao o crescente uso de cartes bancrios no sistema financeiro moambicano, como forma de garantir rapidez, segurana e flexibilidade na realizao de diversas transaces bancrias por parte do cidado. As tentativas de fraudes bancrias, atravs da utilizao, em algumas ATM's, de dispositivos electrnicos de clonagem de cartes, tm merecido uma resposta rpida e profissional por parte do Banco de Moambique, bancos comerciais, autoridades policiais e demais parceiros do sistema bancrio nacional, no se vislumbrando qualquer risco que comprometa o processo de modernizao do sistema nacional de pagamentos em curso. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Distintos Convidados A economia mundial continua a mostrar sinais de abrandamento, com previses de crescimento moderado em 2011 e 2012, situao justificada pelo desempenho pouco animador das principais economias, que este ano, diferentemente dos anteriores, no tem sido suficientemente contrariado pelo crescimento robusto das economias emergentes, dada a crescente volatilidade e averso ao risco por parte dos investidores. O agravamento da crise da dvida soberana em alguns pases da Zona Euro tem dominado as atenes dos mercados, sendo hoje apontada como um dos factores de propagao do risco e pessimismo quanto  efectividade das medidas de consolidao fiscal adoptadas pelas autoridades europeias.  nesta base que as ltimas projeces do World Economic Outlook apontam para uma reviso em baixa do crescimento econmico mundial em cerca de 30pb, para 4,0%, determinada pelo abrandamento da actividade econmica nas economias avanadas (EUA e Zona Euro) e emergentes (China e ndia). Para a frica Subsahariana, a mesma fonte perspectiva um aumento generalizado da produo e projecta para 2012 uma acelerao da taxa de crescimento econmico em 50pb para 5,75%, o que ser acompanhado pela iminncia de riscos de presses inflacionrias ao longo de todo o ano. A crise financeira internacional e a volatilidade dos mercados tambm atingem a economia moambicana e o seu sistema financeiro. Avaliando os dados reportados a Novembro de 2011, constata-se que a carteira de aplicaes das nossas reservas internacionais tem sido afectada, seja por via de oscilaes cambiais pronunciadas na paridade das diversas moedas vis--vis o Dlar dos EUA, como por efeito da contnua queda das taxas de juro no mercado internacional, levando a que os rendimentos obtidos este ano, ainda que uma carteira maior que a de 2010, sejam ligeiramente mais baixos. Os sucessivos downgrades de rating de pases e bancos tm exigido de ns uma gesto mais cautelosa, mediante a diversificao dos instrumentos e mercados de aplicao das nossas reservas e posturas mais conservadoras de exposio ao risco. Distintos Convidados A poltica monetria em 2012 continuar a respeitar os objectivos finais de poltica econmica do Governo, que prev uma inflao mdia anual de 7,2%, um crescimento do PIB de 7,5% e 4,6 meses de cobertura de importaes de bens e servios no factoriais por reservas internacionais brutas. O objectivo intermdio da poltica monetria vai permitir uma expanso anual dos meios totais de pagamento (M3) em torno dos 18,9% e a possibilidade de aumento da expanso do crdito  economia at 22,2%. A base monetria - varivel instrumental da poltica monetria - dever ter um crescimento no superior a 17,5% e prevemos que o saldo de Reservas Internacionais Lquidas seja de USD 2,279 milhes. Para a consecuo destes objectivos, o Banco de Moambique privilegiar o uso de instrumentos disponveis nos mercados monetrio e cambial, complementados com aces de persuaso moral e superviso bancria s instituies de crdito. Os nossos principais desafios resumem-se nos seguintes: Continuar a melhorar a gesto da poltica monetria, reforando a nossa capacidade de previso e de resposta tendo em vista minimizar os riscos e incertezas da conjuntura econmico-financeira e aumentar a eficcia das medidas que temos vindo a tomar; Continuar a fortalecer o nosso papel de supervisor e regulador do sistema financeiro, atravs da superviso baseada no risco; Manter os esforos em curso visando adequar as prticas e procedimentos j em curso na regio em matria de especialidade do Banco Central; Em parceria com as instituies de crdito, prosseguir o esforo de bancarizao da economia nacional, modernizao do sistema nacional de pagamentos e a busca de prerios dos servios financeiros mais competitivos; Perante o cenrio de volatilidade a que se assiste no mercado internacional, adoptar uma postura de maior prudncia na aplicao das nossas reservas internacionais, tendo em vista a reduo do risco; Em sintonia com outras instituies e organismos, continuar a incentivar a abertura de mais agncias bancrias nas zonas rurais, tendo em vista a criao de um sector financeiro inclusivo, por um lado, e o aumento a captao de poupana nas zonas rurais, por outro, condio essencial para o aumento dos recursos ao dispor do sistema bancrio para o financiamento do investimento no nosso pas. Na consecuo dos objectivos inerentes  nossa misso de banco central, temos conscincia de outras aces que exigiro da nossa parte uma ateno acrescida, incluindo a expanso fsica da nossa Instituio para as provncias onde no estamos reperesentados, designadamente Gaza e Manica. Ainda nesta esteira, tendo em vista fazer face  crescente necessidade de melhor servir o sistema financeiro, as instituies do Estado e a economia em geral, bem assim a melhoria das condies de trabalho dos nossos colaboradores, inicimos a construo de dois edifcios de raiz contguos  actual sede do Banco.  na mesma perspectiva de melhorar as condies de trabalho que hoje inaugurmos o Posto de Sade do Banco de Moambique. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores So enormes os desafios que nos reserva o ano de 2012, tomando em conta os prognsticos de uma conjuntura internacional adversa e incerta. Ainda assim, acreditamos na capacidade das instituies do Governo e dos moambicanos para encararem os riscos que se vislumbram como oportunidades para maximizar as nossas potencialidades, produzindo mais para suprir as necessidades do mercado interno, diversificando os nossos produtos de exportao e explorando novos mercados e parcerias. No dia 31 de Janeiro de 2012, vamos assinalar a passagem de 25 anos desde a implementao da primeira medida de reforma das taxas de cmbio em Moambique, no contexto do Programa de Reabilitao Econmica, o PRE, iniciado naquele ano. Vinte e cinco anos depois, temos uma moeda nacional que vem conseguindo granjear respeito entre os agentes econmicos e na nossa regio, reflectindo o esforo de crescimento econmico que temos todos mantido ao longo dos anos. Gostaria de lanar um repto aos quadros do BM e aos estudiosos da nossa economia em geral para que aproveitem esta oportunidade para uma reflexo cientfica sobre o processo de ajustamento, o comportamento e o papel da taxa de cmbio em Moambique. Ao terminar, quero manifestar o meu apreo aos trabalhadores do Banco de Moambique e, por vosso intermdio, a todos os trabalhadores do nosso sistema financeiro, pela dedicao e empenho demonstrados ao longo do ano de 2011, e renovar os meus agradecimentos a todos vs, aos agentes econmicos,  sociedade em geral e  comunidade internacional. A todos os presentes e suas famlias, desejo Festas Felizes e um Ano Novo prspero. Convido-vos a acompanharem-me num brinde pela sade do nosso sistema financeiro, de todos ns e das nossas famlias! Muito Obrigado.

Title: Intervention at the IMF African Department Meeting in Maputo
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENCY THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK FROM MOZAMBIQUE, DR. ERNESTO GOUVEIA GOVE, ON THE OCCASION OF MEETING OF THE AFRICAN IMF DEPARTMENT IN MAPUTO MAPUTO, JANUARY 25, 2012 Ms Antoinette Sayeh, Director of the Imf's African Department, Sir Roger Nord, Deputy Director of the African Department, Dear IMF Representatives of the sub-Saharan region of Africa, Ladies and Gentlemen, Gentlemen It is my first, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and in my own name, to wish you a welcome to our country, making you hope of a great stay in Maputo and enjoying the wonders that this city offers, from its landscape beauty, to the hospitality of its inhabitants, without neglecting its gastronomic richness and so many other attributes that are part of our national cultural mosaic, represented in every corner of this capital. I greet in particular Ms Antoinette Sayeh, Director of the African Department of the International Monetary Fund, for deciding to hold this meeting in Mozambique, which brings together all the representatives of your institution in sub-Saharan Africa. For our Government, which had repeatedly made the invitation to Director Sayeh to visit Mozambique, it is a great honor for her presence in Maputo, as well as her companions and all the participants of this forum. Your stay will be a sublime opportunity for, once again and on the spot, the IMF, notably the African Department, to interact with the reality of Mozambique, to see live what is happening in this corner of the world, to witness our achievements, our progress and our difficulties, in the most varied areas, especially those of macroeconomic stability, promoting robust and increasingly inclusive economic growth, expanding and consolidating the financial sector, attractiveing quality investment and generating jobs and income, as well as the challenging reform process underway aimed at improving the business environment and strengthening good governance, which has contributed, at every moment, to strengthen and resilience the Mozambican economy in the face of the effects of the various waves of the international economic and financial crisis that has been affecting the world economy in recent years. I would also like to thank you for the invitation made to join this great meeting on this occasion and to draw your attention to the theme proposed by us, which I consider current and far-reaching for us, particularly in the exercise of our mission as central bank, and in view of the fact that the reforms underway in this country, programmes with the support of the IMF, complete, precisely in 2012, twenty-five years of continuous implementation and consolidation. The approach to the challenges of monetary policy, in the Mozambican case and in the context of the international financial crisis we are experiencing, is, in itself, a real challenge, either from a purely academic or policy makers point of view. In accepting the invitation, I have already made it clear that it would be a moment of sharing, with this illustrious audience, our humble experience of designing and implementing monetary policy which generally reflects the case of a small economy, in the context of the world economy, but sufficiently open and therefore sufficiently exposed to external shocks. Despite the impact of the international financial crisis on our economy, I believe that countries like ours should see it as an opportunity to catapult growth with macroeconomic stability, exploiting new markets, strengthening international cooperation, including South-South cooperation, and diversifying the productive base through the common and sustainable use of the enormous natural resources we have and the widening of business opportunities to new sectors and branches of activity. Dear Guests, The Mozambican experience is well known by the IMF and particularly its African Department, with whom, moreover, we have had the pleasure of dialogue and discuss, throughout all these years that we maintain a programme with you, so that in the end the ideal does not necessarily prevail, but above all the possible and more appropriate to our reality, essential conditions for the desired formulation and ownership of programmes by national authorities. Over the course of two and a half decades of conception, adoption and implementation of economic and financial programs, monetary policy in Mozambique has been going through several phases, since the adjustment period and subsequent liberalization of interest and exchange rates, moving on to the period of quantitative limitation of credit aggregates. Currently, the Bank of Mozambique conducts a monetary policy based on indirect control, through open market operations, which take place in the context of the Interbank Money Market - where treasury bills are placed, both for monetary policy purposes and for the purpose of financing temporary deficits in the state treasury - and the Interbank Exchange Market - where meticais are traded against US dollars. Each year, the explicit final objectives of the Government's economic policy are: a rate of economic growth, a level of inflation and net international reserves, assuming that the achievement of these targets contributes in the medium term to the reduction of absolute poverty, the increase and stabilisation of employment and the reduction of external dependence. The Bank of Mozambique's contribution focuses on controlling inflation, adopting measures with an impact on the variation of gross domestic product and the coverage of imports by external reserves, through interbank markets and a properly capitalized and functional financial sector. For the correct performance of its main mission, the Bank of Mozambique prioritizes policy coordination, especially between monetary and fiscal/fiscal policies, as well as the correct internal articulation between interbank, monetary and exchange markets, based on its performance on a thorough economic research work based on scientific and technical studies, including field research in the sector which have been published in the various publications we maintain and through the advisory councils and scientific days that we organize annually. We understand that the independence of the central bank is an essential requirement for the success of our mission. But the practice of several years teaches us that this independence should not be an objective in itself, but the result of continuous and consistent work widely recognized by society and cemented in transparency, humility, professionalism and permanent contact with economic agents. In countries such as Mozambique, the issue of the adequacy of central bank capital to sustain its operational independence must be viewed realistically, and it is up to us to advise the Government on the most pragmatic ways for this desire to be realized with tranquility and sustainability. The institutional culture of the Bank of Mozambique is based on an expression that is the binomial TEA-CHA, inspired by the anthropological meaning of tea in our society, not only as an indispensable food, but also as a medicine, as an assimilation of positive values and as an apanagio of good education. TEA- CHA summarizes the institutional values of transparency, involvement, self-development, competence, honesty and attendance. The pillar of transparency is therefore paramount in the actions of the Bank of Mozambique. Transparency about what we do, why we do it, how we do it, when we do it, who we do it and what we do it for. Therefore, we have not only an internal audit unit and our Audit Board, but we also subject the audit accounts to the Bank of Mozambique to specialized external audit and we systematically publish our reports. We therefore maintain an active communication policy with economic actors and the general public through the media and internal media developed by the bank. Esteemed Director Sayeh Dear guests, Our experience of managing the crisis is not much different from that of other African countries with similar characteristics, from small open economies, but heavily dependent on abroad. Our dependence is not limited to the financial resources necessary for the budgetary and balance of payments balance; it extends to the vicissitudes of the international market that establishes the terms of exchange and prices of the products we export and import. Our dependence also makes this economy sensitive to variations in external demand for the products we promote for export. Moreover , our dependence tends to worsen in the face of natural calamity, given Mozambique's vulnerability to drought and flood phenomena, which requires greater regional coordination in the management of existing water resources in Southern Africa. When the international crisis in fuel and cereal prices hit us between late 2006 and 2007, we quickly realized that the weaknesses of our economy would not help us cope with that situation by reserving central bank policies an important role in creating shock absorbers that would avoid the effects of severe slowdown economic growth. It was important to intervene in the markets in order to ensure the stability of the exchange rate and even admitting a certain appreciation of the Metical at the end of 2007 to counterbalance the cross-cutting shocks on our entire production structure, which would result from the absorption of the international price increase if nothing was done. This stance, supported by adequate coordination with the fiscal aspect of fiscal policy, also favoured the containment of domestic inflation, resulting in alleviating the impact of the crisis on the most disadvantaged layers and allowing the authorities to focus on medium-term programmatic objectives. With the outbreak of the international financial crisis at the end of 2007 and with severe global systemic effects since 2008, we soon made sure that our financial system was not exposed to toxic assets created and traded in the northern hemisphere, and therefore no direct reflection is expected through the banks operating in Mozambique. However, we were careful to foresee that the likely impacts could come from the balance of payments side, through the fall in exports by reducing external demand for our products and/or by contracting foreign exchange flows to finance our economy. Thus, we decided, on the monetary side, for softer measures, reducing the coefficient of mandatory reserves and changing lower our interest rates of intervention in the interbank money market, to allow greater fluidity of liquidity in the system, namely an adequate provision of credit to the economy, on a scale that domestic transactions demanded for companies to continue to contribute to GDP and revenue collection Tax. In addition to these measures, we have agreed with our state partners to relocate temporary budgetary measures to the few financial resources available in order to support and stimulate domestic production and cope with the effects of the international crisis. Also in this context, it was important to receive the support we received from the IMF, in the context of the Exogenous Shock Facility and the allocation of Special Reasite Rights, which contributed to safeguarding the prudential condition of our international reserves and their estimated wear iness in the face of the deterioration of our balance of payments. These measures have enabled the expansion of credit to the economy to levels close to 60% per year, supporting the growth of productive activity and the functioning of the business fabric, the maintenance of jobs, income generation and GDP growth at levels we all applaud, which place Mozambique in the fastest growing group of countries on the African continent. The validity of these measures was unquestionable in the concrete conjuncture that we faced in 2008 and 2009, although they also produced side effects. It should be held that, in 2010 and early 2011, signs of inflationary pressure were visible, reflecting the worsening of the annual inflation indicator, which were the case of misadjustments in the liquidity injected into the economy. We then adopted, from August 2010, corrective measures, which were embodied in a more prudent monetary policy, through the rising revision of our intervention interest rates, complemented by an increase in the coefficient of compulsory reserves and our interventions in interbank markets, especially in the foreign exchange market, in order to cope with a higher import bill for liquid fuels and other essential products for the functioning of our economy. Combined with the effort made by our state partners in public revenue collection and budget management, we can now say that in 2011 we managed to stify the inflationary pressure that the country registered in 2010 and re-achieve macroeconomic balance. Indeed, inflation, which had reached 16.6% in 2010, started a downward trend since January, setting at 5.46% in December 2011, in a context where the expansion of the Monetary Base decreased to 8.5%, after 29.2% at the end of 2010 and where the stability of the Metical in relation to the currencies of the main partners was maintained. The main macroeconomic objectives established for 2011 were met, inter alia, inflation, monetary base and net international reserves, thanks to adequate policy coordination and opportunity in the measures taken throughout the year. We have to point out that in 2011 the exchange rate stability was accompanied by lower interventions of the Central Bank in the foreign exchange market and by a record accumulation of net international reserves, in the amount of USD 310 million, for a balance corresponding to about 5.8 months of coverage of total imports of non-factorial goods and services. Consolidating macroeconomic stability and ensuring, at the same time, accelerating economic growth to the 7.5% levels set by the Government are new challenges ahead. Our action will take into account the external economic forecasts still associated with the sovereign debt crisis that some eurozone countries face and the prospect of a slowdown in global economic activity, which, like 2008 and 2009, will have repercussions on the Mozambican economy, through a probable deterioration of the country's current account, either by reduction of export revenues, or by new difficulties in external financing for structural, public and private investment projects. These risks require enhanced policy coordination and, on our side, appropriate measures to minimise their impacts and not jeopardise the gains achieved so far, particularly in terms of macroeconomic growth and stability. That is why at the end of 2011 we started a new policy cycle, with alignments that signal greater possibility of credit expansion and other monetary aggregates, to stimulate economic activity and the private sector. In this cycle, we hope to establish adequate balancing in the policy instruments available, while respecting our commitments inflation, monetary base and international reserves, as well as the stability and soundness of the banking system. We continue to monitor the implementation of the new exchange rate regulation that entered into force in July 2011, which enshrines the full liberalization of current transactions and introduces the principle of sending export revenues to the country and converting at least 50% into national currency. Part of the excess foreign exchange that the banking system recorded in 2011, absorbed by purchases from the Central Bank, results from the greater availability of foreign exchange in the market due to the implementation of this regulation. In addition, the start of the exploitation of mineral resources in the country will also contribute to the increase of tax revenues and the constitution of foreign exchange reserves, in an environment of greater exchange rate stability. The Mozambican experience with regard to the dollarization of the economy teaches us that, in periods immediately after those of great financial repression such as those we experienced until the end of the 1980s, adopting measures to restore the confidence of economic agents in financial institutions and in the functioning of markets is the most even if in this process it is tolerated and even given room for dollarization. In the meantime, regaining confidence in the functioning of the financial sector and achieving a reasonable degree of financial stability, we must move to strengthen the internalisation of the economy, since a persistently dollarized environment reduces the effectiveness of monetary policy and seriously undermines the central bank's action. Ladies Gentlemen The challenges of monetary policy in the context of the international financial crisis are enormous, some of which are difficult to forecast, and it is therefore not possible to exhaust them in my speech. We believe in the capacity of the institutions of our Government and mozambicans to know how to transform risks into opportunities, continuing the implementation of our economic agenda. We are aware of the importance of the IMF's role in this process and its timely advice for making the most appropriate decisions at every stage and at this stage of the crisis. Broad bilateral and multilateral coordination remains the vital tool for mitigating the contagion effect, ensuring stability and soundness of our financial system, which, as we all know, is also exposed, by the composition of its capital, to the unwanted effects of the sovereign debt crisis and the ongoing fiscal consolidation effort in many countries. Our clarity regarding the relevance of the stability of the financial sector leads us to be constantly aware of what happens in other quarters of the world with direct links with financial institutions operating in Mozambique. The gains achieved so far and with great sacrifice in the area of consolidation and expansion of the Mozambican financial sector cannot be wasted without taking any concrete action. In this regard, let me share with you the information that, for our 2012 annual meeting this week, we have called, for public debate, a study carried out at the Bank of Mozambique on the impacts of financial stability on macroeconomic stability and these two variables on economic growth, to scientifically demonstrate and based on domestic and international experience the fundamentals of our policy option for financial and macroeconomic stability. I end my speech by thanking, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique, the commitment and the IMF's support to our country, in the three aspects, namely surveillance, technical assistance and shock financing, which have allowed us to improve the design and implementation of macroeconomic policies, strengthen institutional capacity and the formation of Mozambican staff, which favors greater appropriation and empowerment. I hope that this maputo meeting will enrich your knowledge of our reality, including with regard to vulnerability in the face of variations climate change, so that we all benefit from macroeconomic policy advice more adjusted to the current international crisis situation. Thank you very much. Maputo, 25 January 2012
text_original: INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELNCIA O GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE, DR. ERNESTO GOUVEIA GOVE, POR OCASIO DA REUNIO DO DEPARTAMENTO AFRICANO DO FMI EM MAPUTO MAPUTO, 25 DE JANEIRO DE 2012 Senhora Antoinette Sayeh, Directora do Departamento Africano do FMI, Senhor Roger Nord, Director-Adjunto do Departamento Africano, Caros Representantes do FMI da regio sub-sahariana de frica, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Cumpre-me, em primeiro lugar, em nome do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, desejar-vos as boas-vindas ao nosso pas, fazendo votos de uma ptima estadia em Maputo e que desfrutem das maravilhas que esta cidade oferece, desde a sua beleza paisagstica,  hospitalidade dos seus habitantes, sem descurar a sua riqueza gastronmica e outros tantos atributos que so parte do nosso mosaico cultural nacional, bem representados em cada canto desta capital. Sado em particular a Senhora Antoinette Sayeh, Directora do Departamento Africano do Fundo Monetrio Internacional, por ter decidido realizar em Moambique este encontro que rene todos os representantes da vossa instituio na frica sub- sahariana. Para o nosso Governo, que, por diversas vezes, havia formulado o convite  Directora Sayeh para visitar Moambique,  uma grande honra a sua presena em Maputo, assim como dos seus acompanhantes e de todos os participantes deste frum. A vossa estadia ser uma sublime oportunidade para, mais uma vez e in loco, o FMI, nomeadamente o Departamento Africano, interagir com a realidade de Moambique, perceber em directo o que se passa neste canto do mundo, testemunhar os nossos feitos, os nossos progressos e as nossas dificuldades, nos mais variados domnios, com destaque para os da estabilidade macroeconmica, de promoo de um crescimento econmico robusto e cada vez mais inclusivo, de expanso e consolidao do sector financeiro, de atraco de investimento de qualidade e gerador de emprego e de renda, bem assim o desafiante processo de reformas em curso visando a melhoria do ambiente de negcios e o reforo da boa governao, o que tem contribudo, a cada momento, para o fortalecimento e resilincia da economia moambicana face aos efeitos das diversas vagas da crise econmica e financeira internacional que vem afectando a economia mundial nos ltimos anos. Aproveito tambm para agradecer pelo convite feito para me juntar, nesta ocasio, a esta magna reunio e atrair a vossa ateno para o tema por ns proposto, que considero actual e de grande alcance para ns, particularmente no exerccio da nossa misso de Banco Central, e atendendo ao facto de as reformas em curso neste pas, inseridas em programas com o apoio do FMI, completarem, precisamente em 2012, vinte e cinco anos de contnua implementao e consolidao. A abordagem dos desafios da poltica monetria, no caso moambicano e no quadro da crise financeira internacional que vivemos, constitui, de per si, um verdadeiro repto, seja na ptica puramente acadmica, seja na de policy makers. Ao aceitar o convite, tive desde logo em mente que este constituiria um momento de partilha, com esta ilustre audincia, da nossa humilde experincia de concepo e implementao da poltica monetria que reflecte, genericamente, o caso de uma economia pequena, no contexto da economia mundial, mas suficientemente aberta e, por isso, bastante exposta aos choques externos. Apesar do impacto da crise financeira internacional na nossa economia, sou da opinio de que pases como os nossos devem ver nela uma oportunidade para catapultar o crescimento com estabilidade macroeconmica, explorando novos mercados, reforando a cooperao internacional, incluindo a cooperao sul-sul, e diversificando a base produtiva, atravs do uso regrado e sustentvel dos enormes recursos naturais de que dispomos e do alargamento das oportunidades de negcios a novos sectores e ramos de actividade. Caros Convidados, A experincia moambicana  sobejamente conhecida pelo FMI e particularmente pelo seu Departamento Africano, com quem, alis, temos tido o grato prazer de dialogar e discutir, ao longo de todos estes anos que convosco mantemos um programa, para que no final prevalea no necessariamente o ideal, mas sobretudo o possvel e mais adequado  nossa realidade, condies essenciais para a desejada formulao e apropriao dos programas pelas autoridades nacionais. Ao longo de duas dcadas e meia de concepo, adopo e implementao de programas econmicos e financeiros, a poltica monetria em Moambique vem passando por vrias fases, desde o perodo de ajustamento e posterior liberalizao das taxas de juro e de cmbios, seguindo para o perodo de limitao quantitativa dos agregados creditcios. Actualmente, o Banco de Moambique conduz uma poltica monetria baseada no controle indirecto, atravs das operaes de mercado aberto, que tomam lugar no contexto do Mercado Monetrio Interbancrio - onde so colocados bilhetes do tesouro, tanto para fins de poltica monetria, como para fins de financiamento de dfices temporrios na tesouraria do Estado - e do Mercado Cambial Interbancrio - onde se transaccionam meticais contra dlares americanos. Anualmente, os objectivos finais explcitos da poltica econmica do Governo so: uma taxa de crescimento econmico, um nvel de inflao e de reservas internacionais lquidas, assumindo-se que a consecuo dessas metas concorre, a mdio prazo, para a reduo da pobreza absoluta, o aumento e estabilizao do emprego e a reduo da dependncia externa. A contribuio do Banco de Moambique concentra-se no controle da inflao, adoptando medidas com impacto na variao do Produto Interno Bruto e na cobertura das importaes pelas reservas externas, atravs dos mercados interbancrios e de um sector financeiro adequadamente capitalizado e funcional. Para o correcto desempenho da sua misso principal, o Banco de Moambique prioriza a coordenao de polticas, sobretudo entre as polticas monetria e fiscal/oramental, bem como a correcta articulao interna entre os mercados interbancrios, monetrio e cambial, baseando a sua actuao num aturado trabalho de investigao econmica fundada em estudos cientfico-tcnicos, incluindo pesquisas de campo no sector real, que vm sendo divulgados nas diversas publicaes que mantemos e atravs dos conselhos consultivos e das jornadas cientificas que anualmente organizamos. Entendemos que a independncia do banco central  um requisito essencial para o sucesso da nossa misso. Mas a prtica de vrios anos ensina-nos que essa independncia no deve ser um objectivo em si, mas o resultado de um trabalho contnuo e consistente amplamente reconhecido pela sociedade e cimentado na transparncia, na humildade, no profissionalismo e no permanente contacto com os agentes econmicos. Em pases como Moambique, a questo da adequao dos capitais do banco central para a sustentao da sua independncia operacional deve ser encarada com realismo, cabendo-nos aconselhar ao Governo as formas mais pragmticas para que esse desejo se realize com tranquilidade e sustentabilidade. A cultura institucional do Banco de Moambique assenta numa expresso que  o binmio TEA-CHA, inspirada no significado antropolgico do ch na nossa sociedade, no s como alimento indispensvel, mas tambm como medicamento, como assimilao de valores positivos e como apangio da boa educao. TEA- CHA sintetiza os valores institucionais de transparncia, envolvimento, auto- desenvolvimento, competncia, honestidade e assiduidade. O pilar da transparncia , pois, primordial na actuao do Banco de Moambique. Transparncia em relao ao que fazemos, porqu fazemos, como fazemos, quando fazemos, com quem fazemos e para qu fazemos. Por isso, temos no s uma unidade de auditoria interna e o nosso Conselho de Auditoria, mas tambm sujeitamos as contas do Banco de Moambique  auditoria externa especializada e publicamos sistematicamente os nossos relatrios. Por isso, mantemos uma poltica de comunicao activa com os agentes econmicos e com o pblico em geral, atravs dos rgos de comunicao social e dos meios internos desenvolvidos pelo banco. Estimada Directora Sayeh Caros convidados, A nossa experincia de gesto da crise no difere, em muito, da de outros pases africanos com caractersticas semelhantes, de pequenas economias abertas, mas bastante dependentes do exterior. A nossa dependncia no se limita aos recursos financeiros necessrios ao equilbrio oramental e de balana de pagamentos; ela estende-se s vicissitudes do mercado internacional que estabelece os termos de troca e preos dos produtos que exportamos e importamos. A nossa dependncia torna tambm esta economia sensvel a variaes da procura externa dos produtos que promovemos para exportao. Mais ainda, a nossa dependncia tende a agravar-se perante situaes de calamidade natural, dada a vulnerabilidade de Moambique a fenmenos de seca e de cheias, o que impe uma maior coordenao regional na gesto dos recursos hdricos existentes na frica Austral. Quando a crise internacional dos preos dos combustveis e dos cereais se bateu sobre ns entre finais de 2006 e ao longo de 2007, rapidamente percebemos que as fragilidades da nossa economia no nos ajudariam a enfrentar aquela situao reservando s polticas do banco central um papel importante para criar amortecedores que evitassem efeitos de grave desacelerao do crescimento econmico. Era importante intervir nos mercados de forma a assegurar a estabilidade da taxa de cmbio e admitindo at uma certa apreciao do Metical, em finais de 2007, para contrabalanar os choques transversais sobre toda a nossa estrutura produtiva, que decorreriam da absoro da alta internacional dos preos dos combustveis caso nada fosse feito. Esta postura, suportada por uma adequada coordenao com a vertente oramental da poltica fiscal, favoreceu tambm a conteno da inflao domstica, traduzindo-se no aliviar do impacto da crise sobre as camadas mais desfavorecidas e permitindo que as autoridades se concentrassem nos objectivos programticos de mdio prazo. Com o deflagrar da crise financeira internacional de finais de 2007 e com efeitos severos de nvel sistmico mundial desde 2008, cedo nos certificmos de que o nosso sistema financeiro no se encontrava exposto aos activos txicos criados e transaccionados no hemisfrio norte, no se prevendo por isso qualquer reflexo directo atravs dos bancos que operam em Moambique. Todavia, tivemos o cuidado de antever que os provveis impactos poderiam vir do lado da balana de pagamentos, atravs da queda nas exportaes por reduo da procura externa pelos nossos produtos e/ou pela contraco dos fluxos de divisas para financiar a nossa economia. Assim, decidimos, do lado monetrio, por medidas mais brandas, reduzindo o coeficiente de reservas obrigatrias e alterando em baixa as nossas taxas de juro de interveno no mercado monetrio interbancrio, para permitir maior fluidez da liquidez no sistema, designadamente uma adequada disponibilizao do crdito  economia, numa escala que as transaces domsticas demandavam para que as empresas continuassem a dar o seu contributo para o PIB e para a arrecadao de receitas fiscais. A par dessas medidas, concertmos com os nossos parceiros do Estado medidas temporrias de cariz oramental, de realocao dos poucos recursos financeiros disponveis, de modo a apoiar e estimular a produo interna e fazer face aos efeitos da crise internacional. Ainda neste contexto, foi importante o apoio que recebemos do FMI, no mbito da Facilidade de Choques Exgenos e da alocao de Direitos Especiais de Saque, que contriburam para salvaguardar a condio prudencial das nossas reservas internacionais e o seu desgaste estimado, em face da deteriorao da nossa balana de pagamentos. Estas medidas permitiram a acelerao da expanso do crdito  economia para nveis prximos de 60% ao ano, apoiando a dinamizao da actividade produtiva e o funcionamento do tecido empresarial, a manuteno de postos de trabalho, a gerao de rendimento e o crescimento do PIB nos nveis que todos aplaudimos, que colocam Moambique no grupo de pases que mais rapidamente crescem no continente africano. A validade daquelas medidas foi inquestionvel na conjuntura concreta que enfrentmos em 2008 e 2009, embora tambm tenham produzido efeitos colaterais. Retenha-se que, em 2010 e princpios de 2011, foram visveis os sinais de presso inflacionria, com reflexos no agravamento do indicador de inflao anual, que decorriam de desajustes na liquidez injectada na economia. Adoptmos ento, a partir de Agosto de 2010, medidas correctivas, que se consubstanciaram numa poltica monetria mais prudente, atravs da reviso em alta das nossas taxas de juro de interveno, complementadas por um aumento no coeficiente de reservas obrigatrias e das nossas intervenes nos mercados interbancrios, sobretudo no mercado cambial, para fazer face a uma maior factura de importao de combustveis lquidos e outros produtos essenciais para o funcionamento da nossa economia. Conjugado com o esforo realizado pelos nossos parceiros do Estado, na arrecadao de receitas pblicas e gesto do oramento, podemos hoje afirmar que em 2011 logrmos estancar a presso inflacionria que o pas registou em 2010 e repor o equilbrio macroeconmico. Com efeito, a inflao que havia atingido 16,6% em 2010, iniciou uma tendncia para a desacelerao desde Janeiro, fixando-se em 5.46% em Dezembro de 2011, num quadro em que a expanso da Base Monetria reduziu para 8,5%, aps 29,2% em finais de 2010 e em que a estabilidade do Metical em relao s moedas dos principais parceiros foi mantida. Os principais objectivos macroeconmicos estabelecidos para 2011 foram cumpridos, nomeadamente, de inflao, base monetria e reservas internacionais lquidas, merc de uma adequada coordenao de polticas e oportunidade nas medidas tomadas ao longo do ano. Temos a assinalar que em 2011 a estabilidade cambial foi acompanhada por menores intervenes do Banco Central no mercado cambial e por uma acumulao recorde de reservas internacionais lquidas, num montante de USD 310 milhes, para um saldo correspondente a cerca de 5.8 meses de cobertura de importaes totais de bens e servios no factoriais. Consolidar a estabilidade macroeconmica e assegurar, em simultneo, a acelerao do crescimento econmico para os nveis de 7.5% definidos pelo Governo constituem desafios novos que temos pela frente. A nossa actuao ter em conta as previses de conjuntura externa ainda associadas  crise de dvida soberana que alguns pases da Zona Euro enfrentam e a perspectiva de desacelerao da actividade econmica mundial, o que,  semelhana de 2008 e 2009, ter reflexos na economia moambicana, atravs de uma provvel deteriorao da conta corrente do pas, seja por reduo de receitas de exportao, seja por novas dificuldades no financiamento externo para projectos de investimento estruturantes, pblicos e privados. Estes riscos requerem o reforo da coordenao de polticas e, do nosso lado, medidas adequadas para minimizar os seus impactos e no comprometer os ganhos at aqui alcanados, particularmente em termos de crescimento e estabilidade macroeconmica. Da que j em finais de 2011 inicimos um novo ciclo de poltica, com alinhamentos que sinalizam maior possibilidade de expanso do crdito e outros agregados monetrios, para estimular a actividade econmica e o sector privado. Neste ciclo, esperamos estabelecer o balanceamento adequado nos instrumentos de poltica disponveis, respeitando os nossos compromissos quantitativos de inflao, base monetria e reservas internacionais e ainda a estabilidade e solidez do sistema bancrio. Continuamos a monitorar a implementao da nova regulamentao cambial que entrou em vigor em Julho de 2011, a qual consagra a total liberalizao das transaces correntes e introduz o princpio de remessa de receitas de exportao ao pas e converso de pelo menos 50% em moeda nacional. Parte dos excessos de divisas que o sistema bancrio registou em 2011, absorvidos por compras do Banco Central, resulta da maior disponibilidade de divisas no mercado por fora da implementao desta regulamentao. Adicionalmente, o incio da explorao dos recursos minerais no pas ir tambm concorrer para o incremento das receitas fiscais e a constituio de reservas cambiais, num ambiente de maior estabilidade cambial. A experincia moambicana relativamente  dolarizao da economia ensina-nos que, em perodos imediatamente posteriores aos de grande represso financeira como os que vivemos at finais da dcada de 80 do sculo passado, adoptar medidas de recuperao da confiana dos agentes econmicos nas instituies financeiras e no funcionamento dos mercados  o caminho mais apropriado, mesmo que nesse processo se tolere e at se conceda espao  dolarizao. Entretanto, reconquistada a confiana no funcionamento do sector financeiro e atingido um grau razovel de estabilidade financeira, devemos trilhar pelo reforo da meticalizao da economia, uma vez que um ambiente persistentemente dolarizado reduz a eficcia da poltica monetria e compromete seriamente a actuao do banco central. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores So enormes os desafios da poltica monetria no contexto da crise financeira internacional, sendo alguns de difcil prognstico, no sendo, por isso, possvel esgot-los nesta minha interveno. Acreditamos na capacidade das instituies do nosso Governo e dos moambicanos para saber transformar riscos em oportunidades, prosseguindo a implementao da nossa agenda econmica. Temos conscincia da importncia do papel do FMI neste processo e dos seus aconselhamentos oportunos para a tomada de decises mais adequadas em cada etapa e nesta fase da crise. A ampla coordenao bilateral e multilateral continua a ser o instrumento vital para mitigar o efeito contgio, assegurando estabilidade e solidez do nosso sistema financeiro, que, como todos sabemos, tambm est exposto, por fora da composio dos seus capitais, aos efeitos indesejados da crise de dvida soberana e do esforo de consolidao fiscal em curso em muitos pases. A nossa clareza relativamente  pertinncia da estabilidade do sector financeiro leva-nos a estar permanentemente atentos ao que acontece noutros quadrantes do mundo com vnculos directos com as instituies financeiras que operam em Moambique. Os ganhos at aqui alcanados e com muito sacrifcio, no domnio da consolidao e expanso do sector financeiro moambicano, no podem ser desperdiados sem que tomemos alguma aco concreta. A este respeito, permitam-me que partilhe convosco a informao de que, para a nossa reunio anual de 2012, a decorrer esta semana, elegemos, para tema de debate pblico, um estudo desenvolvido no Banco de Moambique sobre os impactos da estabilidade financeira na estabilidade macroeconmica e destas duas variveis no crescimento econmico, para demonstrar cientificamente e com base na experincia domstica e internacional os fundamentos da nossa opo de poltica pela estabilidade financeira e macroeconmica. Termino a minha interveno agradecendo, em nome do Banco de Moambique, o cometimento e o apoio do FMI ao nosso pas, nas trs vertentes, nomeadamente, surveillance, assistncia tcnica e financiamento a choques, que nos tm permitido aprimorar o desenho e implementao de polticas macroeconmicas, reforar a capacidade institucional e a formao dos quadros moambicanos, o que favorece uma maior apropriao e empoderamento. Fao votos de que este encontro de Maputo enriquea o vosso conhecimento da nossa realidade, incluindo no tocante  vulnerabilidade diante de variaes climatricas de grande vulto, para que todos beneficiemos de aconselhamentos de polticas macroeconmicas mais ajustadas  conjuntura actual de crise internacional. Muito Obrigado. Maputo, 25 de Janeiro de 2012

Title: Speech at the Ordinary Meeting of the SADC Banks Association
text: Dr. Mario Machungo, President of the Mozambican Association of Banks Distinguished Representatives of the SADC Banking Association Distinguished Guests Ladies and Gentlemen, On behalf ofthe Banco de Mocambique I would like to welcome all participants ofthis magna meeting ofthe SADC Banking Association. I particularly address my greetings to our guests from different countries of our region, wishing them a great stay in this beautiful Maputo city, the capital of Mozambique. I expect you to take this opportunity to associate the intense work during the following two days, with a more direct contact with our cultural, landscape and gastronomic reality. I salute the SADC Banking Association for having chosen Maputo to host this meeting and I am convinced that all participants will deepen their understanding about the Mozambican reality, witnessing our progress, our difficulties and the challenges ahead in various domains, especially as regards macroeconomic stability, promotion of an inclusive and robust economic growth, expansion and consolidation of financial sector, attraction of quality investment and jobs and income raising, as well as the challenging process of reforms underway aimed to improve the business environment and reinforcement of good governance. I would like to thank you for the opportunity given to share, in this occasion, our ideas and vision in relation to the topic "development ofthe regional integration process in the SADC", which I consider up-to-date for our countries. The regional integration can be assumed in different approaches, namely in terms of international trade, sharing of natural resources and infrastructures, or also in terms of harmonized vision as regards food security programs or environment protection. Ladies and Gentlemen, lt seems consensual that the financial and economic approach gains particular emphasis in this process of convergence and integration that our countries are embracing. The key indicators of macroeconomic convergence established for the SADC constitute the focus of my speech, with incidence on the expected goals set for the year 2012. However, taking into account the audience, allow me to start my remarks giving brief information about the status of our economy and the health of our financial sector, as a hosting country ofthis event. Our economies have been facing since 2007 the combined effects of the International financial crisis, oil price hikes, foodstuff crisis and countless natural adversities that have cyclically affected our countries. The endeavours of our Governments and Central Banks to mitigate the impact of these exogenous shocks have been enormous, concurrently ensuring price stability, GDP growth in a desired scale and promoting a favourable business environment to attract new investments. In Mozambique, we have been achieving positive results in the macroeconomic management domain, thanks to adequate coordination of the monetary and fiscal-budgetary policies, as inflation decelerated to 6.14% at the end of 2011 and having kept the same trend in February of the current year, and fell again to 3.5%, while the preliminary information regarding our real GDP growth in 2011 is close to 7.4%, figures that position us within the goals set in the SADC convergence indicators. Within the banking sector, we have witnessed the increase in the number of licensed financial institutions in the country, inherently accompanied by the physical expansion of bank branches throughout the country, as well as the innovation and diversification of financial products and Services for economic and social development. In effect, from a total of 14 banks in 2008, today we have 18 commercial banks operating in the country. It is also worth highlighting that when we announced the strategy on the expansion of banking activities in 2007, of the total 128 districts of the country, only 28 were being served by bank agencies in a total of 228. Today, with enormous efforts and dedication of every market stakeholders, the banks serve 56 districts, with a total of 462 branches all over the country. Although the figures are encouraging, it is to recognize that the banking sector has yet many challenges, where it is worth highlighting among others, the need to become financial Services more inclusive, through the expansion of the physical presence in rural areas, and also, through the modernization of the national payments System towards more competitive financial Services. The indicators of financial System stability point to a major soundness, having as reference the capital adequacy at around 17.1% in December 2011, against 13.9% during the sub-prime crisis in 2008. In 2011, overdue credit stood at 2.6%, which shows endeavours of commercial banks in the selection and decision over proposals, weighed the related inherent risks. In the light of the recent evolution of the key financial and economic indicators, with emphasis on favourable inflation results, combined with its short and medium term forecasts, as well as the financial sector stability environment as I previously mentioned, the Monetary Policy Committee of the Banco de Mocambique considered that there are conditions for liquidity increase in the market, in order to promote banking finance to the private sector, thus contributing to the goals of GDP growth set for the current year, in a scenario of lower and controlled inflation. Therefore, the Committee decided to revise the reference interest rates downward, in its last ordinary meeting of the current year held on March 12. Ladies and Gentlemen, With respect to macroeconomic convergence indicators, it is worth reminding you that within our region, the indicators were defined, for the first time in 2003, with intermediate goals set for the time period between 2008 and 2012. For the current year, the macroeconomic convergence criterion establish the following goals - an average inflation below 5%, real GDP growth rate not below 7%, a fiscal deficit as percentage of GDP in a range between 1% and 3%, a public debt ratio as percentage of GDP below 60% and ratio of imports coverage by international reserves not below 6 months. In various meetings of the Committee of the SADC Central Bank Governors, in which I have the privilege to participate, each of our countries are asked to report on these indicators. In the last presentation, the countries were also asked to present the projections of macroeconomic convergence key indicators for the end of 2012. I would like to stress that the majority of countries expressed reserves in relation to inflation target, given the international adverse environment, which leads to uncertain fluctuations in oil prices and its derivatives and in foodstuff prices, with impact on adjustments of domestic prices, and yet, as a result of natural shocks deriving from climate changes. These have been, at present, the main elements of pressure on inflation in our region. Further in relation to inflation target, some countries suggest that the alternative should be to establish a range, for example, between 2% and 7%, instead of a fixed target. Such range would take into account a set of elements, such as the impact of externai shocks that has been identified as the main risk factor in the region for a single digit inflation, as established in the macroeconomic convergence plan. Likewise, we have observed that some countries have difficulties in complying with the imports coverage convergence goal, given the current levei of reserves, weighing the pressure over its demand to cater the importation of goods and Services, in an environment of financial and economic crisis worldwide. On the opposite side, we have noted with satisfaction that the overall SADC countries have fulfilled the convergence goal regardingthe fiscal deficit as percentage of GDP and real GDP growth rate. Besides a clear political will reaffirmed in many occasions by the leaders of our Governments, it is worth stressing that there are enormous challenges for the alignment and accomplishment of convergence goals in the SADC, considering the significant differences in economic framework of our countries, and mainly, assuming the shortage of financial resources that would levei such differences. Even so, the macroeconomic management institutions in our countries have been striving in order to become the harmonization and the respective convergence indicators and policies and the necessary reforms more perceptible and fortheirthorough fulfillment. The regional integration process is dependent on the adoption of policies that reinforce the convergence goals and their monitoring, as well as the implementation of specific programs, within the legal approach, aimed to the harmonization of the legal framework for central banks, the integration of national payments systems, alignment of information for banking supervision; strengthening of coordination between the central banks and treasuries; and the development of financial sector indicators. Distinguished Guests, The implementation of the Protocol of Finance and Investment is a major challenge for harmonization and convergence success. However, other challenges are associated, namelythe harmonization of regulations and banking supervision, harmonization ofthe regulatory framework on capital flows and the norms relating to foreign exchange regimes, development of capital markets and the promotion of financial literacy and educational programs. On the other hand, the SADC Banking Association performs a very important role in this process, as it offers opportunities to its members to exchange information and experiences on ethical and good practices, mainly at this distressing moment in which the world seeks Solutions in order to recover after the global financial and economic crisis that is not yet totally healed, and which is currently assuming the sovereign debt crisis in the Euro Zone. I also understand that it is possible to minimize the difficuIties of necessary liquidity to finance the enterprises, if we work together in the creation of a stock exchange of the region and in the process of gradual removal of the prevailing barriers within capital operations. Another important challenge that commercial banks have forward, which should be discussed in this meeting, in an approach of exchange of experiences, is related to the matter of money laundering. We need to create the necessary defenses so that our respective banking systems are not used for such illegal practices, whereby the principie "Know your Client", should be diligent and strictly followed. Ladies and Gentlemen, In conclusion of my remarks, I wish all participants a very good work and I expect this meeting to be very productive in terms of discussions and exchange of experiences so that the banking system ofthe region gains value. Thank you very much Maputo, March 29, 2012

Title: Intervention at the Annual Meeting of the World Bank and IMF in Tokyo
text: Recent Experience of Financial Development in Mozambique Dear Dr. Anselmo Teng, President of the Monetary Authority of Macao Dear Governors of Distinguished Central Banks Invited Ladies Gentlemen First of all, let me address a fraternal and friendly greeting, on behalf of myself and the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, to the President of the Monetary Authority of Macao for the invitation he has asked me to be present at this forum and for the opportunity given to me to present our experience in this event. I warmly greet all the Central Bank Governors and their delegations, as well as to those present at this forum for dialogue and prospecting for the opportunities that the market Chinese and Asian offer to our countries. I would also like on this occasion to congratulate the President of the Monetary Authority of Macao on this initiative which reinforces our solidarity and institutional cooperation. This space is a unique opportunity to highlight our potential and the comparative advantages that we have, in the context of the excellent relationship we have with China, with the guiding vein of this autonomous region of Macao, with which we have deep ties of history, language and culture. We are meeting in a particularly difficult international economic and financial environment, where the countries of the northern hemisphere continue to be buffeted by the effects of the international economic and financial crisis that has dragged on for more than five years, infecting our countries in various ways in the face of increasing market integration, even if some of our economies are small in the context of the global economy. We see this meeting as an excellent opportunity to diversify the foundation of our economy, exploring new opportunities and deepening our knowledge of the Asian market. Mozambique's cooperation with China currently covers different areas of mutual interest, with emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, fisheries, energy and the burgeoning mining industry that emerges in the Mozambican economy. Although Mozambique is part of the Group of IDA countries, in which it is financed in concessional terms, China already takes the lead of our official creditors, with credits exceeding US1.8 billion, for strategic infrastructure construction projects such as roads, airports, bridges, with vital importance for deepen the integration of the national market, which enables us to better face the enormous challenges in the context of regional and international integration. The deepening of the economic and trade relations we have with China is of particular importance at this stage when our country emerges for the research and exploitation of non-renewable natural resources, such as coal, gas and different minerals, whose economic potential demands high investments, solid partnerships and greater rigour in its sustainable management. Dear Guests The theme that was proposed to me is about the experience of Financial Development in Mozambique. I am convinced that our experience does not differ substantially from that of the friends present here, who follow a path of reforms monitored by international financial institutions. Allow, as an introduction to the theme, to briefly present some macro-financial indicators of the Mozambican economy. Mozambique is part of low-income nations, based on international statistical criteria, with a GDP per capita of less than 1,000 US Dollars and a population of approximately twenty-two million inhabitants, according to the last population census conducted by our National Institute of Statistics in 2007. However, our country's economic growth has seen real rates above 7% in a row in the last five years, with real growth around 7.3% projected this year. Macroeconomic stability, translated into an average annual single-digit inflation, over the past five years, a public external debt ratio as a percentage of GDP considered controlled and a level of external reserves above five months of coverage of imports of non-factorial goods and services, have crystallized the confidence of domestic and foreign investors to increasingly bet on Mozambique as a safe destination for their investments. To exemplify, in 2011 foreign direct investment reached a record figure of US2.1 billion in different sectors of economic activity, especially the mining, energy, tourism and agriculture sectors. The Mozambican financial sector has experienced significant development in the last two decades, thanks to the legal-institutional reforms that have been introduced since the late 1980s and which gained greater momentum after 1990, with constitutional and regulatory changes that have opened up political space to multi-party, market and private initiative. From a financial sector consisting of three banks and one insurance company in 1992, we currently have a total of 18 banks, eight microbanks, seven credit unions, ten savings and loan organisations, thirteen insurers, as well as other financial corporations, including 185 microcredit operators. The first phase of opening and consolidating the financial system with the participation of private, national and foreign capital was characterized by a concentration of financial institutions and services in the main urban centers, namely Maputo, the capital of the country and other provincial capital cities. In 2007, we launched the strategy of banking and extending financial services to the most remote areas of the country with a view to reversing this situation by encouraging institutions to expand their coverage in places with high income and employment potential. The results obtained are frankly encouraging, although this process has begun in the course of the international financial crisis. We are currently experiencing an increase in bank coverage to 470 branches, covering all provincial capital cities and municipalities, covering 58 districts in the country, when in 2007 the branches were only 274 to 28 districts. Monetization indicators of our economy rose to 41% at the end of 2011, compared with about 20% in 1999, and in the same period, financial savings and bank financing to the private sector doubled to 35% and 28% of GDP, respectively. In addition to this effort to bankeat the economy, access to financial services by the Mozambican population has become possible more recently through electronic means using mobile telephone networks or by banks that specialize in the provision of these services. Currently, the Bank of Mozambique is leading the process of implementing the Interbank Services Society (SIMO) to ensure interoperability of electronic payment networks with a common technological infrastructure with universal access and more competitive transaction costs, taking advantage of economies of scale in the provision of various financial services. Despite these advances, we recognize that the current levels of financial services provision are below the desired, and our objective is the massification of financial intermediation, through Internet banking, mobile banking, delegation of banking skills by specialized post companies and microfinance institutions. Dear Guests The current context of international financial crisis obliges us to be attentive to the robustness and financial balance of the institutions under our supervision, ensuring that the expansion of the business of financial institutions takes place in close harmony with their prudential balance. The stability of the financial sector also leads us to be alert to what is occurring in other quarters of the world, whose institutions have links with the financial institutions operating in our market. The gains achieved so far in the consolidation and expansion of the Mozambican financial sector cannot be overlooked. In this context, we have been adjusting the operational framework with which we guide monetary and exchange rate policy, balancing our interventions in the monetary and foreign exchange markets in line with the macroeconomic objectives established and implementing supervisory mechanisms that respect international good practice, with a view to creating greater resilience of the Mozambican financial sector to external shocks, confidence of the public and economic operators in our financial system. The advent of the exploitation of natural resources in the country poses new challenges to the central bank, with a view to preserving macroeconomic and financial sector stability, with low and controlled inflation, improvement of the external position, strengthening the use of Metical, our currency, in domestic transactions. The greater variation of our exports, coupled with a greater availability of foreign exchange from capital generated by foreign direct investment combined with the impacts of the implementation of the new exchange rate regulation in force since mid-2011, impose increasing creativity in the manipulation of the policy instruments at our disposal. Ensuring more robust gdp growth with safeguarding the external competitiveness of our economy is a permanent challenge for macroeconomic management. Ladies, gentlemen, I have just summarized our experience of developing the financial sector, also focusing on the enormous economic potential that Mozambique has to continue to attract investment in the various sectors. Despite all the reported efforts, we remain a country where absolute poverty still reaches high figures, reflecting domestic savings deficits, which condition the pace of economic expansion on the desired scale. It is up to us, the financial sector, to seek the partnerships and financing necessary to leverage the dynamics of the private and public sectors of the economy, in a logic of judicious, responsible and sustainable indebtedness. For us, this forum lends itself to strengthening economic and financial cooperation between our institutions, our countries and our peoples, with a view to boosting trade and investment, with a concrete perspective of facilitating the movement of people, goods and capital. In an international context of increased risks, the management of the Republic's foreign exchange reserves entrusted to our institutions requires on our side of the refined sensitivity, rigour and professionalism. Our institutions apply a considerable share of these resources to traditional markets in Europe, the USA and Japan, where return rates are virtually nil or extremely low. In this context, let us also use this forum to deepen our knowledge of the advantages and opportunities of China's financial market as an alternative to diversify ing the resources entrusted to central banks. Before I finish, may I talk about the importance of training our technicians. Training focused not only on the field of banking techniques, but essentially on the knowledge of the functioning of our respective systems policies, legislation and financial institutions, as it can serve as a real lever in the field of economic cooperation between our countries, where trade is large. Among the central banks of portuguese speaking countries cooperation in the area of training is already a reality. We need to extend it to one of the largest economies in the world, China, with Macau as a bridge and platform connecting this country to our respective countries. Let me conclude my speech by reiterating my thanks to the Monetary Authority of Macao and its President, Dr. Anselmo Teng, for this opportunity that has given us to share our experience of building a strong, inclusive, integrated and transparent financial sector. I could not fail to praise the excellent organization and hospitality that has been reserved for us, conditions that will provide the success of this event. To all present we reiterate our invitation for direct investment or, in partnerships, in Mozambique, our pearl of the Indian Ocean, in the most varied sectors of activity, including the financial sector. Thank you so much for your attention! Ernesto Gouveia Gove

Title: Investment Forum in Mozambique
