text: BRIEF INFORMATION ABOUT The RECENT EVOLUTION OF THE MO82AMBICANECONOMY INTERVENTION OF YOUR EXCELLENCY THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE ON THE OCCASION OF THE INVESTMENT FORUM IN MOZAMBIQUE MAPUTO, 18 OCTOBER 2012 Minister for Industry and Trade of Mozambique Minister for Industry and Trade uk Members of the Government, Excellencies Dear Guests, Ladies Gentlemen Allow me to express my deep gratitude for the honour i am given to participate in this forum and for the opportunity given to me to present the Bank of Mozambique's vision on the recent developments in the Mozambican economy, focusing on the variables that are the subject of the central bank's mandate or related to them. I take this opportunity to greet, on my own behalf and on behalf of the Board of Directors, the organisers of this event for this initiative, which is an important vehicle for strengthening the fruitful cooperation between Mozambique and the United Kingdom of Great Britain. I must encourage our government to continue with actions of this nature, which promote the immense potential of the country, internally and internationally, boosting investments, strengthening existing partnerships and creating an appropriate space for the exchange of information and experiences on various matters. The government should also be recognized for the effort to maintain political and macroeconomic stability and the strategic orientation in line with its Five-Year Plan, which has made it possible to infrastructure the Country of Rovuma to Maputo, deepening the internal market, in the current framework in which we have started the exploitation of important natural resources that will accelerate the march of our development, robust, balanced and inclusive growth. I would also like to take this opportunity to address my compliments to the distinguished panelists, the dignitaries present in this forum and to the investors representing various productive sectors, who, at a particularly difficult time, characterized by an unprecedented economic and financial crisis, have decided to visit us, which shows their interest in knowing the numerous business opportunities that the country offers. Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen Despite an adverse international situation, marked by consecutive years of persistent economic and financial crisis on a global scale, Mozambique remains resilient, gaining the confidence of entrepreneurs of different latitudes, which has made it a safe and preferred destination for investment, even occupying a prominent place of direct investment africa and the world. The epic exploitation of non-renewable natural resources that we have come to follow presents new and exhilarating challenges for all of us, public and private institutions, economic agents and civil society. It seems important to us to continue to empower our institutions to lead this process, in defence of the national interest and future generations, as well as to calibrate our policies, so that they exercise more effectively the role that is expected of them on the national agenda for development and which has the fight against poverty as a scope. Respecting the theme that the organizers have proposed to me, my intervention focuses on the recent evolution of the Mozambican economy, focusing on the variables that constitute the mandate of the Bank of Mozambique. In this context, I will try to share with you the recent trends of the real, financial and external sectors of the economy, as well as our main perspectives. As I have pointed out, since 2007 the world has been experiencing a long economic and financial crisis, and the economic outlook is dominated by sharp risks and uncertainties. Mozambique is a small economy, within the framework of the world economy, but open enough to be affected by the side effects of contagion of this adverse conjuncture. Still, it has managed to maintain appreciable economic growth rates in recent years, positioning itself even in the fastest growing group of economies, in Africa and in the world. The peace that the country is experiencing, macroeconomic stability, policies to promote economic growth, good governance and the structural reforms that have been undertaken by the government are the pillars of our resilience to the crisis. Indeed, the Mozambican economy has been growing over the past five years at an average annual rate of more than 7%, well above the average for SADC and the African continent. Economic activity growth has outsgrown the natural population growth for several years, causing our real Gross Domestic Product per capita to grow at an average annual rate of 4%, reaching 500 U.S. dollars in 2011, equivalent to 1,000 when adjusted for purchasing power parity. The agriculture, construction, transport and communications sectors, leveraged by high public investment in close partnership with private investment, have been the main driver of our economic growth. It should be noted that these data do not yet weigh the dynamism of the mining industry that emerges in the country. From 1990 to 1996, we lived with inflation levels in the band of 50%. However, in recent years the country's good economic performance has occurred in an environment of stability, translated into annual single-digit inflation, a level that is in line with the average of the countries in the SADC region. Recent inflation developments show a path of stability, with the average annual rate of 3.3% in September 2012, i.e. the lowest in the SADC region. Price stability is the main objective of monetary policy, as it is believed that with low inflation it is guaranteed the promotion of domestic savings and private investment, in addition to helping to preserve the purchasing power of thousands of Mozambican families still living on the threshold of absolute poverty, without neglecting that a low and controlled economic environment also favors the attraction of more and new investments for the country. Nevertheless, we are fully aware that the stability of inflation mainly reflects the good performance of the real sector of the economy, the increase in domestic food production, under the Action Plan for Food Production (PAP), an initiative of our Government aimed at reducing the food deficit and external dependence in the long term. Metical's stability in the foreign exchange market, good public finance performance and closer coordination between fiscal and monetary policy also play its part in macroeconomic stability at every stage. In this regard, I must stress the efforts of the Government which has gradually made the State Budget less and less dependent on resources from abroad, whose availability and access, in an environment of international financial crisis, becomes more difficult. Indeed, the weight of foreign aid in the State Budget has declined considerably in the last five years to current levels of around 40%, offset by an increase in revenue collection which as a percentage of GDP has gone from around 15% in 2006 to the current 22%. This is a clear sign of the performance of our real economy, but also of the improvement of the fiscal machine, without neglecting the citizenship of all taxpayers to do the part that is due to them to the State, allowing it to be more sovereign in the definition and implementation of policies for the development and redistribution of income. At a time when the sovereign debt of many countries is a factor of concern and subject to severe restrictions, Mozambican public debt as a percentage of GDP fell from 74.2% in 2005 to around 32% in 2011, thus being considered sustainable, which also opens up fiscal space for the contracting of new loans that could leverage other projects and infrastructure, employment promoters and income generation. Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen At the level of the financial sector, we have been carrying out a set of actions aimed at encouraging the increase and diversification of financial institutions operating in the country, as well as the expansion and scope of the services provided. The legal and institutional transformations introduced in the late 1980s and the opening of the market to private, national and foreign financial institutions allowed only three banks in 1992 to have 18 banks, 8 microbanks, 7 cooperatives, 10 savings and loan organisations, as well as other types of credit institutions and financial corporations, from only three banks in 1992, a total of 185 microcredit operators. Faced with the finding that the national financial system tended to focus on major cities in 2007, together with the government, we launched the strategy of banking the economy, which includes a set of actions aimed at promoting the expansion of financial services, especially for areas of the country with lower density of these services. The results are very encouraging, as the number of branches in operation increased to 470 bank branches, about double that of 2007, covering all capital cities, municipalities and 58 districts. Additionally, the use of new information technologies is disseminated and consolidated, with clear advantages, with emphasis on the easy access to financial services by the population, even in areas where there is no physical representation of banks. In the face of improved levels of internal financial savings and the capitalization levels of the banking system, financing to the private sector of the economy, which in 1990 represented 13% of GDP, increased to 28% in 2011, a figure that is in line with the average of SADC countries. The degree of monetization of the economy grew from 20% in 1999 to 41% at the end of 2011. Despite the turbulence that characterizes the global financial markets, the Mozambican financial system is resilient to the indirect effects of the international financial crisis, with the solvency ratio above the 8% established by the Basel I criterion and the non-non-non-credit ratio below 4%. Our country's external position, measured by the current account balance in relation to GDP, also shows a persistent deficit situation consistent with the degree of external dependence on our economy. With the exception of the last two years, attributable to growing foreign investment in the mining sector, there is an improvement in the current account deficit, reducing from 17% of GDP in 2003 to around 10% in 2009, rising again to 13.2% in 2011 for the reasons listed. We expect this position to be reversed as mining and gas projects begin exporting their production. The global situation is characterized by the decline in direct investment, but in our case it grew from 5% of GDP in 2007 to 17.1% in 2011, with a record entry of more than US2 billion into our economy. Net International Reserves managed by the Bank of Mozambique have doubled in the last five years to a total of US2.7 trillion by September 2012, corresponding to about 5.3 months of non-factor import coverage of non-factor goods and services. In 2011, we started the implementation of the new exchange rate regulation that enshrines the principle of liberalization of current transactions and the strengthening of the national banking system in the intermediation of operations with abroad. We have observed that under this reform our foreign exchange market presents itself with greater availability of foreign exchange, a fact that poses new challenges to monetary and exchange rate policy in order to ensure an exchange rate that is competitive for exporters, but does not penalize imports, in the face of empirical evidence already tested of its rapid impact on domestic inflation. Ladies Gentlemen We do not neglect to be enormous the efforts and challenges that are ahead, especially if we take into account the forecasts that point to the prevalence of an adverse and uncertain international situation, the effects of which can affect us, either on the side of our exports, or the sudden fluctuation of international prices of the main commodotties. The process of exploiting non-renewable natural resources that our country has initiated involves additional challenges for public and private institutions and for the entire Mozambican society. Let us not be content with the export of raw materials, which is a preliminary step in the march of our development. Indeed, our prospect remains to optimise the exploitation of these resources, fuelling the emergence of new sectors of the economy, which add value to our raw materials. In our field, we must continue to adjust the action of monetary and fiscal policy to the reality of every moment, to ensure that the increase in export revenues, foreseen with the implementation of projects now in the implementation phase, does not call into question the external competitiveness of the exchange rate. We will have to continue to consolidate macroeconomic and financial sector stability in order to attract more investment to the country. Mozambique has a huge potential for attraction of investments in various sectors of the economy, with emphasis on agriculture, agro-industry, tourism, fishing and mining. In the meantime, because we are in constant competition with other countries and regions of the world, our policies must be geared towards consolidating the results already achieved, continuing structural and sectoral reforms for the permanent improvement of the business environment. I end my speech by reiterating that Mozambique has room to receive new and more investments in the various sectors of the economy, including the financial sector. Cooperation between the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Mozambique can help to minimise the saturation problems observed in the European market and, at the same time, that of underdevelopment of our country, supporting it to stop being a mere producer and exporter of raw materials to become a processing country for part of these raw materials, which implies its industrialisation. The existence of abundant energy sources, minerals, high agricultural potential, fishing and others only shows that it is possible to develop such industrialization, promoting more employment, adding value to our products and significantly improving the terms of exchange. From this perspective, what we hope and hope is that the knowledge that the UNITED KINGDOM has and the capital it has can be made available to a project and development strategy of the country, in which we all win. Once again, I express my thanks for the invitation and for this space that I have been given to share with this great Assembly the recent panorama of our economy and the emerging challenges. Thank you so much for your attention! Maputo, on 18 October 2012
text_original: BREVE INFORMAO SOBRE A EVOLUO RECENTE DA ECONOMIA MOAMBICANA INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELNCIA O GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE POR OCASIO DO FRUM DE INVESTIMENTO EM MOAMBIQUE MAPUTO, 18 DE OUTUBRO DE 2012 Senhor Ministro da Indstria e Comrcio de Moambique Senhor Ministro da Indstria e Comrcio do Reino Unido Senhores Membros do Governo, Excelncias Estimados Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Permitam-me que manifeste o meu profundo agradecimento pela honra que me  concedida de participar neste frum e pela oportunidade que me  dada de apresentar a viso do Banco de Moambique sobre a evoluo recente da economia moambicana, com enfoque para as variveis que so objecto do mandato do Banco Central ou com estas correlacionadas. Aproveito esta ocasio para saudar, em meu nome pessoal e em nome do Conselho de Administrao, os organizadores deste evento por esta iniciativa, que constitui um importante veculo para o reforo da profcua cooperao existente entre Moambique e o Reino Unido da Gr Bretanha. Cumpre-me encorajar o nosso governo a prosseguir com aces desta natureza, que promovam o imenso potencial do Pas, no plano interno e internacional, dinamizando os investimentos, reforando as parcerias existentes e criando um espao adequado para a troca de informaes e vivncias sobre diversas matrias. O governo deve igualmente ser reconhecido pelo esforo de manuteno da estabilidade poltica e macroeconmica e pela orientao estratgica plasmada no seu Plano Quinquenal, que tem possibilitado infraestruturar o Pas do Rovuma ao Maputo, aprofundando o mercado interno, no actual quadro em que iniciamos a explorao de importantes recursos naturais que iro acelerar a marcha do nosso desenvolvimento, atravs de um crescimento robusto, equilibrado e inclusivo. Gostaria ainda de aproveitar esta oportunidade para enderear os meus cumprimentos aos ilustres painelistas, aos dignitrios presentes neste frum e aos investidores representando diversos sectores produtivos, que, num momento particularmente difcil, caracterizado por uma crise econmica e financeira sem precedentes, decidiram visitar-nos, o que demonstra o seu interesse em conhecer as inmeras oportunidades de negcio que o pas oferece. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Apesar de uma conjuntura internacional adversa, marcada por anos consecutivos de uma persistente crise econmica e financeira  escala global, Moambique mantm-se resiliente, granjeando a confiana de empreendedores de diferentes latitudes, o que o tem tornado um destino seguro e preferido do investimento, ocupando mesmo um lugar de destaque do investimento directo estrangeiro, em frica e no Mundo. A epopeia de explorao de recursos naturais no renovveis que passamos a trilhar apresenta novos e exaltantes desafios para todos ns, instituies pblicas e privadas, agentes econmicos e sociedade civil. Parece-nos importante continuar a empoderar as nossas instituies para liderarem este processo, em defesa do interesse nacional e das futuras geraes, assim como calibrar as nossas polticas, para que elas exeram mais eficazmente o papel que delas se espera na agenda nacional pelo desenvolvimento e que tem a luta contra a pobreza como escopo. Respeitando o tema que os organizadores me propuseram, a minha interveno debrua-se sobre a evoluo recente da economia moambicana, com enfoque para as variveis que constituem o mandato do Banco de Moambique. Neste contexto, procurarei partilhar com os presentes as tendncias recentes dos sectores real, financeiro e externo da economia, bem como as nossas principais perspectivas. Como sublinhei, desde 2007 o mundo atravessa uma longa crise econmica e financeira, sendo as perspectivas econmicas dominadas por acentuados riscos e incertezas. Moambique  uma pequena economia, no quadro da economia mundial, mas aberta o suficiente para ser afectada pelos efeitos colaterais de contgio desta conjuntura adversa. Ainda assim, tem conseguido manter, nos ltimos anos, taxas de crescimento econmico apreciveis, posicionando-se mesmo no grupo de economias que mais crescem, em frica e no mundo. A paz que o pas vive, a estabilidade macroeconmica, as polticas de promoo do crescimento econmico, a boa governao e as reformas estruturais que tm vindo a ser empreendidas pelo governo so os pilares da nossa resilincia  crise. Com efeito, a economia moambicana tem vindo a crescer nos ltimos cinco anos a uma taxa mdia anual superior a 7%, bem acima da mdia da SADC e do continente africano. O crescimento da actividade econmica tem superado, h vrios anos, o crescimento natural da populao, fazendo com que nosso Produto Interno Bruto real per capita cresa a uma taxa mdia anual de 4%, tendo atingido em 2011 quinhentos dlares americanos, equivalentes a mil dlares quando ajustados  paridade de poder de compra. Os sectores da agricultura, construo, transportes e comunicaes, alavancados por elevados investimentos pblicos, em estreita parceria com o investimento privado, tm-se afirmado como os principais propulsores do nosso crescimento econmico. Importa destacar que estes dados no ponderam ainda o dinamismo da indstria de extraco mineira que desponta no Pas. No perodo de 1990 a 1996, convivemos com nveis de inflao na banda de 50%. No entanto, nos ltimos anos o bom desempenho econmico do pas tem ocorrido num ambiente de estabilidade, traduzida numa inflao anual de um dgito, nvel que est em linha com a mdia dos pases da regio da SADC. A evoluo recente da inflao comprova uma trajectria de estabilidade, tendo no ms de Setembro de 2012 a taxa mdia anual sido de 3,3%, ou seja, a mais baixa da regio da SADC. A estabilidade de preos  o principal objectivo da poltica monetria, pois acredita-se que com uma inflao baixa se assegura a promoo da poupana interna e do investimento privado, para alm de ajudar a preservar o poder de compra de milhares de famlias moambicanas que vivem ainda no limiar da pobreza absoluta, sem descurar que um ambiente econmico de inflao baixa e controlada tambm favorece a atraco de mais e novos investimentos para o Pas. Ainda assim, temos a plena conscincia de que a estabilidade da inflao espelha sobretudo o bom desempenho do sector real da economia, o aumento da produo interna de bens alimentares, no mbito do Plano de Aco para a Produo de Alimentos (PAP), iniciativa do nosso Governo que tem em vista reduzir o dfice alimentar e a dependncia externa a prazo. A estabilidade do Metical no mercado cambial, o bom desempenho das finanas pblicas e a coordenao mais estreita entre a poltica fiscal e monetria tambm jogam o seu papel na estabilidade macroeconmica em cada etapa. A este propsito, devo sublinhar os esforos do Governo que tem permitido paulatinamente tornar o Oramento do Estado cada vez menos dependente de recursos provenientes do exterior, cuja disponibilidade e acesso, num ambiente de crise financeira internacional, se torna mais difcil. Com efeito, o peso da ajuda externa no Oramento de Estado regrediu consideravelmente nos ltimos cinco anos, para os nveis actuais em torno dos 40%, compensado pelo aumento da arrecadao da receita que em percentagem do PIB passou de cerca de 15% em 2006 para os actuais 22%. Este  um claro sinal da performance da nossa economia real, mas tambm da melhoria da mquina fiscal, sem descurar a cidadania de todos os contribuintes de fazerem a parte que lhes  devida para com o Estado, permitindo que este seja mais soberano na definio e implementao de polticas de desenvolvimento e de redistribuio da renda. Num momento em que a dvida soberana de muitos pases constitui factor de preocupao e objecto de severas restries, a dvida pblica moambicana em percentagem do PIB baixou de 74,2% em 2005 para cerca de 32% em 2011, sendo assim considerada sustentvel, o que tambm abre espao fiscal para a contratao de novos emprstimos que podero alavancar outros projectos e infra-estruturas, promotores de emprego e gerao de renda. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, A nvel do sector financeiro, temos vindo a levar a cabo um conjunto de aces visando incentivar o aumento e diversificao de instituies financeiras que operam no Pas, bem assim o alargamento e abrangncia dos servios prestados. As transformaes jurdico-institucionais introduzidas em finais dos anos 80 e a abertura do mercado a instituies financeiras privadas, nacionais e estrangeiras, permitiu que de apenas trs bancos em 1992, o nosso sistema passasse a contar na actualidade com 18 bancos, 8 microbancos, 7 cooperativas, 10 organizaes de poupana e emprstimos, para alm de outros tipos de instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras, de entre as quais figura um total de 185 operadores de microcrdito. Perante a constatao de que o sistema financeiro nacional tendia a concentrar-se nas principais cidades, em 2007, juntamente com o governo, lanmos a estratgia de bancarizao da economia, que contempla um conjunto de aces com o intuito de promover o alargamento de servios financeiros, em especial para as zonas do pas com menor densidade destes servios. Os resultados so bastante encorajadores, pois o nmero de agncias em funcionamento incrementou para 470 balces de bancos, cerca do dobro do existente em 2007, cobrindo todas as cidades capitais, municpios e 58 distritos. Adicionalmente, dissemina-se e consolida-se o uso de novas tecnologias de informao, com claras vantagens, com destaque para o fcil acesso aos servios financeiros pela populao, mesmo nas zonas onde no haja uma representao fsica de bancos. Em face da melhoria dos nveis de poupana financeira interna e dos nveis de capitalizao do sistema bancrio, o financiamento ao sector privado da economia, que representava, em 1990, 13% do PIB, incrementou para 28% em 2011, cifra que est em linha com a mdia dos pases da SADC. O grau de monetizao da economia cresceu de 20% em 1999 para 41% em finais de 2011. No obstante as turbulncias que caracterizam os mercados financeiros globais, o sistema financeiro moambicano mostra-se resistente face aos efeitos indirectos da crise financeira internacional, situando-se o rcio de solvabilidade acima dos 8% estabelecidos pelo critrio de Basileia I e o rcio do crdito malparado abaixo de 4%. A posio externa do nosso pas, medida pelo saldo da conta corrente em relao ao PIB, mostra ainda uma situao de dfice persistente, consistente com o grau de dependncia externa da nossa economia.  excepo dos ltimos dois anos, imputvel ao crescente investimento estrangeiro no sector de explorao mineira, observa-se uma melhoria no dfice da conta corrente, ao reduzir de 17% do PIB em 2003 para cerca de 10% em 2009, voltando a subir para 13,2% em 2011, pelas razes enumeradas. Esperamos que esta posio se inverta  medida que os projectos de explorao mineira e de gs iniciem a exportao da sua produo. A conjuntura global  caracterizada pela retraco no investimento directo, mas no nosso caso o mesmo cresceu de 5% do PIB em 2007 para 17,1% em 2011, com uma entrada recorde de mais de dois mil milhes dlares americanos na nossa economia. As Reservas Internacionais Lquidas geridas pelo Banco de Moambique duplicaram nos ltimos cinco anos, para um total de 2,7 bilies de dlares at Setembro de 2012, o que corresponde a cerca de 5.3 meses de cobertura de importao de bens e servios no factoriais. Em 2011, inicimos a implementao da nova regulamentao cambial que consagra o princpio da liberalizao das transaces correntes e do reforo do sistema bancrio nacional na intermediao das operaes com o exterior. Temos observado que por fora desta reforma o nosso mercado cambial se apresenta com maior disponibilidade de divisas, facto que coloca novos desafios  poltica monetria e cambial visando assegurar uma taxa de cmbio que seja competitiva para os exportadores, mas que no penalize as importaes, em face de evidncias empricas j testadas do seu rpido impacto na inflao domstica. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores No descuramos serem enormes os esforos e desafios que temos pela frente, sobretudo se tomarmos em considerao os prognsticos que apontam para a prevalncia de uma conjuntura internacional adversa e incerta, cujos efeitos nos podem atingir, seja do lado das nossas exportaes, seja da flutuao brusca dos preos internacionais das principais commodotties. O processo de explorao de recursos naturais no renovveis que o nosso pas iniciou envolve desafios adicionais para as instituies pblicas e privadas e para toda a sociedade moambicana. No nos contentemos com a exportao de matrias-primas, que constitui uma etapa preliminar da marcha do nosso desenvolvimento. Com efeito, a nossa perspectiva continua a ser a de optimizar a explorao destes recursos, dinamizando o surgimento de novos sectores da economia, que acrescentem valor s nossas matrias-primas. No nosso domnio, temos que continuar a ajustar a actuao da poltica monetria e fiscal  realidade de cada momento, para assegurar que o incremento de receitas de exportaes, previsto com a implementao dos projectos ora em fase de implantao, no ponha em causa a competitividade externa da taxa de cmbio. Teremos que continuar a consolidar a estabilidade macroeconmica e do sector financeiro, tendo em vista atrair mais investimentos para o pas. Moambique possui um enorme potencial de atraco de investimentos em vrios sectores da economia, com destaque para a agricultura, agroindstria, turismo, pesca e minerao. Entretanto, porque estamos em concorrncia permanente com outros pases e regies do mundo, as nossas polticas devem estar orientadas para a consolidao dos resultados j alcanados, prosseguindo as reformas estruturais e sectoriais para a melhoria permanente do ambiente de negcios. Termino a minha interveno reiterando que Moambique tem espao para receber novos e mais investimentos nos diversos sectores da economia, incluindo o financeiro. A cooperao entre o Reino Unido da Gr-Bretanha e Moambique pode contribuir para minimizar os problemas de saturao que se observa no mercado europeu e, em simultneo, o de subdesenvolvimento do nosso pas, apoiando-o para que deixe de ser um mero produtor e exportador de matrias-primas para se tornar num pas de processamento de parte destas matrias- primas, o que implica a sua industrializao. A existncia de abundantes fontes energticas, minerais, elevado potencial agrcola, pesqueiro e outros s mostra que  possvel desenvolvermos tal industrializao, promovendo mais emprego, adicionando valor aos nossos produtos e melhorando significativamente os termos de troca. Nesta perspectiva, o que esperamos e desejamos  que o conhecimento que o Reino Unido tem e o capital que possui possam ser postos  disposio de um projecto e estratgia de desenvolvimento do pas, em que todos saiamos a ganhar. Uma vez mais, manifesto os meus agradecimentos pelo convite e por este espao que me foi proporcionado para partilhar com esta magna assembleia o panorama recente da nossa economia e os desafios emergentes. Muito obrigado pela Vossa ateno! Maputo, aos 18 de Outubro de 2012

Title: 2012 Scientific Days
text: Mr Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency, Members of the Board of Directors, Directors, Assistant Directors and Technicians of the Bank of Mozambique; Representatives of Government Institutions Dear academics and researchers Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen I would first like, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, to greet all those who have deigned to honour us with their presence in these Fourth Scientific Days of our institution. Allow me to address a special greeting to all the researchers who have accessed the invitation of the Bank of Mozambique, accepting the challenge of participating and sharing with us their research projects, around the central theme that we have selected for these Scientific Days. To the five finalist participants, go to the congratulations of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, for the quality demonstrated in your research, which certainly required you many hours of work and study for the preparation of your projects, two of which will be presented here today publicly, after being selected by the designated Jury. Address to the President and the other members of the Jury our thanks for their prompt collaboration with the Mozambique in the arduous mission they have carried out to evaluate and select the papers submitted, strictly respecting the parameters established by the Regulation of Scientific Days. To all those present in these IV Scientific Days, we are interested in this initiative and consideration for our institution, which you express with your presence, in order to share with us points of view, sensitivities and contributions in relation to the selected theme, which we classify as current, timely and relevant, either in the perspective of pure economic research and in the field of economic policy-making. Dear guests, When in 2009 the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique decided to organize, on an annual basis, the scientific days had in mind a structured technical debate forum, making use of available tools of economic and financial theory, as well as the properly analyzed practice of the activity of central banks, through specialty communications made by our staff or experts, academics and policy makers who are dedicated to the analysis of the phenomena of the universe of our performance, functions and mandate. We have reiterated each year that for us the scientific days are another moment of openness of our institution to society and our partners, to reflect together on information of our specialty, technical-scientific studies related to our activity, which allows us to be attentive to other sensitivities and perceptions, maintaining visual and analytical contact with opinions even contrary, in a dialectic of permanent learning, aiming to improve our performance in the areas of the design and implementation of monetary and exchange rate policies, in our role as regulators and supervisors of credit institutions, financial corporations and the national payment system. The first Days took place in 2009, having been analyzed two topics authored by bank of Mozambique staff and before a reduced audience to managers and technicians of the institution, although we invited discussions external to the Bank. In 2010, the scientific days focused on the analysis and dissemination of our research in the formulation and management of monetary policy, in the face of substantial changes that we have undertaken in the organic and content of our Monetary Policy Committee (CPMO). This year, we selected three papers for debate, all by our managers and technicians, before an audience that already had the participation of guests from government institutions and academia. Following the gradualism we adopted last year, the Third Scientific Days were extended to representatives of government institutions, academic institutions and economic research , specialty analysts and higher education students. At this event, we addressed three topics authored by the Staff of the Bank of Mozambique, namely" The Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism: An Investigation of the Interest Rate Channel in Mozambique", "Reflection on Monetary Goals in Mozambique" and the "Effectiveness of the Taylor Rule in Mozambique". For the present edition of the Scientific Days, the Board of Directors has elected as the central theme "The Exchange Rate in Mozambique", which is justified by the fact that we mark this year the 25th anniversary of the implementation of the first exchange rate reform in Mozambique, inserted in the implementation of the PRE - Economic Rehabilitation Program. As I mentioned, this theme is always current and transversal, attracting the interest of a wide range of sensitivities and perceptions, from academics to ordinary citizens, and it is therefore important to debate and know how to listen to the voice of structured research on this subject. Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen Since the proclamation of independence in 1975, our country has experienced different exchange rate regimes, in view of the specific economic conditions of each moment, as well as the economic policy objectives pursued at each stage. The period from 1975 to 1986 was characterized by a fixed exchange regime, in the context of a central planning economy marked by numerous economic difficulties, deterioration of national production, worsening of public indebtedness and scarcity of foreign exchange. In eleven years of fixed exchange rate regime, the accumulated fluctuation approached 46%, corresponding to an average annual depreciation of only 1.42%. International reserves in this period were only US39.5 million, an amount capable of covering less than a month of imports that the country was carrying out at that time. I would like to point out, however, that this period should not be evaluated without contextualizing the war economy environment in which it was immersed. In 1987, following Mozambique's participation in the International Monetary Fund in 1984, the implementation of the Economic Rehabilitation Programme (PRE) began. This programme followed the typical model of structural adjustment and economic liberalisation and the exchange rate correction was the most visible face of the programme, with two distinct steps:  The first, of high intensity devaluations (also known as shock therapy), carried out between 1987 and 1988, on a semiannual basis. It is recalled that the first devaluation occurred on January 31, 1987, when, by the voice of the then Prime Minister of our government, the Metical suffered the first devaluation of 442.5% against the US Dollar, which was traded on the official market at the exchange rate of 38.28 Meticais when it moved to 200 Meticais. This process continued until 1988, with the exchange rate reaching 620 Meticais per Dollar in October, resulting in an administrative correction of 1,520% in our currency in about two years.  The period of peg crawling or sliding devaluation followed between 1989 and 1992, without, however, changing the substance of the existing exchange rate regime which continued to be of administered or fixed rates. The process consisted of small monthly devaluations, until 1990, followed by daily devaluations, between 1991 and 1992, with the accumulated devaluation in this interval totaling 59.9% in the first period and 13% in the second. It was during this period that the Secondary Foreign Exchange Market was created, a legal space that attracted private operators to a new segment of the foreign exchange market, many of which until then linked to the parallel foreign exchange market. Between 1992 and 1993, we carried out the process of exchange unification, a step that was marked by a narrowing of the spread between the official exchange rate and that of the secondary market. This was followed by the period from 1993 to 2000, when we began to prepare the conditions and foundations for the transition to the flexible exchange regime, in the context of the deepening of the political and economic liberalisation that the country experienced, with the peace reached in 1992 and the holding of the first multi-party elections in 1994. In 1996, we formally created the Interbank Foreign Exchange Market, which operated for four years in a face-to-face regime and without major technological support. We started trading foreign exchange currencies on the foreign exchange market with existing commercial banks, resulting in an exchange rate which was the genesis of the current rate of MCI quotes. It should be noted that in 2000 we started the transition to indirect monetary control instruments, abandoning the system of credit limits and net domestic asset limits, and monetary policy is made exclusively by the instruments of the markets, including monetary and exchange rates. The entry of new private banks into the banking system required the deepening of the functionalities of the interbank foreign exchange market. In 2005, with the technical assistance of international experts, we introduced the Bid and Offer quotation system in the interbank foreign exchange market and rules of conduct to guide the posture and ethics of dealers, supported by a computer system that was constantly improved in time, which allows to carry out operations in real time, with any financial square in the world. This was the culmination of a long process of reforms of our exchange rate regime and from then on we consolidated the regime in which the exchange rate is determined by the conditions of demand and supply in the market. It should be recalled that in the framework of this reform, in 2005 we rehearsed the holding of foreign exchange auctions on the foreign exchange market, with the aim of better assessing the price discovering mechanism. This was an experience that produced less positive results, with Metical that year recording a high nominal depreciation of close to 20%. Metical's quotes, at each time of the day, are determined by the conditions of demand and supply of foreign exchange expressed by operators authorized to carry out activities in our foreign exchange market. Since then, our market interventions have taken into account market conditions and their objectives are closely linked to the macroeconomic objectives set, based on three essential pillars: liquidity regulation, inflation and the position of international reserves. Thus, when we intervene in the foreign exchange market, more than meeting the revealed demand for foreign exchange, we also pursue monetary policy objectives or alignments necessary in our exchange rate to its most desired trend in the medium term. The flexible exchange rate regime was reiterated and reinforced with Law No. 11/2009, of March 11, Exchange Law, which consecrated the complete liberalization of current transactions in the country, the exclusivity of the national banking system for the intermediation of transactions with abroad, keeping under the tutelage and jurisdiction of the foreign exchange authority all capital transactions. Prior to the adoption of this regulation, the country was subject to the scrutiny of international financial institutions to assess and verify the existence of exchange rate restrictions and multiple exchange rate practices. It was concluded that Mozambique actually adopts a flexible exchange rate regime, enabling us to be adhering to Article VIII of the IMF Statutes. These developments were accompanied by the growth in total exports of goods and services at an average annual rate of 16% over the last ten years, which had a positive impact on the improvement of the country's external position, reflected in the fall in the current account deficit ratio to GDP, to less than 10% in 2009, rising to 13.2% in 2011, in view of the large volume of imports associated with the high influx of Foreign Direct Investment that has been taking place in recent years. The country's Net International Reserves increased year on year, up to around USD 2.7 trillion last September, equivalent to 5.9 months of coverage of imports of non-factor goods and services and 6.5 months excluding imports from major projects. Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen The process of reforms in Mozambique, with direct and indirect impact on the exchange rate regime, is well documented and reasonably analyzed in our institution. In addition to specialty studies also carried out by other national and foreign researchers. We are proud that our staff have already made analytical and scientific contributions on the subject, some of which I am summarizing for the benefit of our debates. Thus, we find in de Sousa, W. (1993), an analysis of the impact of exchange rate unification in Mozambique, which occurred in 1992 and the finding that the process was characterized by significant real actual devaluations, with real gains in external competitiveness for the country, concluding that competitiveness is only effective when all the factors that determine it are weighed, in addition to the exchange rate, in particular the rate and tariff scheme, labour productivity and innovation. Pimpao, A. (1996) makes a chronology of the evolution of foreign exchange policy in Mozambique, from 1975 to 1996, highlighting the objectives that guide it. For his part, Saranga, J. in his work "Real Exchange Rate and Agricultural Export Products" (1996), analyzed the impact of the real exchange rate on the volume of exports of agricultural products, with emphasis on cotton and cashew nuts, having concluded that the effect was marginal, thus showing the fact that the low competitiveness of agricultural products is not dependent on the behavior of the exchange rate. On the issue of exchange rate alignment in Mozambique, there is also the point of note relevant scientific papers already published, highlighting the work of Fabrizio, S. (1998), which assessed mozambique's external competitiveness for the period 1980 to 1996, and found that in net terms metical recorded an effective real assessment between 1980 and 1986, resulting in real losses of external competitiveness vis-a-vis the main partners the region, a situation that was reversed since mid-1987. The author concludes that the real exchange rate re-recorded between 1993 and 1997, periods of relative appreciation, but generally without expression in the perspective of misalignment, since fluctuations turned around its balance, on average, 7%. Francis V. (2007), in his article "Export Performance and Competitiveness in Mozambique", evaluating the misalignment of the real exchange rate between 1999 and 2006, concludes that despite the misalignments observed, in general the exchange rate was in line with the country's economic fundamentals. More recently, as part of the improvement of the monetary policy implementation framework, our Department of Economic and Statistical Studies has made several estimates, including econometrics, the results of which converge on those already presented in other studies on the determinants of inflation in Mozambique, which show that the transmission of the effects of the exchange rate to inflation is rapid and of considerable magnitude. This means that we are always aware of the movements of this variable to prevent its short-term dynamics from having negative effects on the overall price level, but also does not provide persistent losses in the external competitiveness of our export products. Dear Guests This debate takes place at a time characterised by an unprecedented economic and financial crisis. Still, the Mozambican economy has considerable resilience, with growth rates above 7%, higher than the average for SADC and the African continent. The growth of economic activity in the country has been sustained by the good performance of the agriculture, construction, transport and communications sectors, leveraged by high public and private investments, particularly foreign investment, in the mining industry, a dynamism that has not yet been fully weighted in the country's total production statistics. In turn, inflation measured by the annual change in the Maputo city price index, which decreased to 5.46% in 2011, it was in the nine months of this stable and low year, setting at 1.23%, similar to the average inflation that decreased to 3.31%, after 10.3% in December 2011. We have seen considerable exchange rate stability in recent years, supported, on the one hand, by the good coordination of monetary and fiscal policies, as well as by the massive entry of capital into the national banking system, associated with foreign direct investment that takes place in the country, with the advent of the exploitation of natural resources. The exchange rate is an important variable of macroeconomic management and stimulates economic activity, impacting in particular in our case, with the behavior of the general price level. For countries such as ours, excessive depreciation in addition to not ensuring long-term competitiveness gains can have harmful effects on domestic production if economic operators, in the face of the extraordinary gains made by the exchange rate, stop investing in the innovation and modernisation of their production units, aimed at promoting productivity and competitiveness. The exchange rate study offers several approaches, ranging from understanding dynamics, determinants, effects on other macroeconomic variables, determining the level of balance and its misalignment, as well as the effect and magnitudes of the transmission mechanism for inflation and growth, including the phenomenon of Dutch disease. Our history of reforms in the foreign exchange area is long as well as technical analysis on this topic. Some of the work developed on the Mozambican reality addresses two main issues related to the behavior of the Metical, namely the issue of alignment or misalignment of the exchange rate versus evaluation of the occurrence of dutch desease. Much has been said recently about the phenomenon of "Dutch disease" in the Mozambican case. There are several analysts and perceptions about this phenomenon, but I must stress that we Banco de Mocambique have not yet seen the occurrence of this phenomenon in the Mozambican economy. Since the beginning of the recent exploitation of natural resources, everything that is happening is still in the sphere of direct investment, and revenues are expected to leverage greater independence of our State Budget and greater robustness of our international reserves. In the article "The Macroeconomic Challange of More Aid" published by the IMF in Finance and Development Magazine, paragraph 3 of volume 43 of September 2005, it was concluded that the Mozambican economy has been able to absorb foreign aid intake, which has allowed the avoidance of episodes of real appreciation, and there is therefore no evidence of the "Dutch disease". In this line, Wazela, T. and Ornar, J. (2009), both technicians of the Bank of Mozambique, conclude that despite the considerable entry of foreign aid funds are tenuous the signs of occurrence of Dutch desease or "Dutch disease", results compatible with the work of the IMF published in 2006, with the title "Aid and the Equilibrium Exchange Rate - The case of Mozambique". The discussion around the "Dutch disease", which was previously related to the entry of foreign aid for direct support to the State Budget, is now shifting to the exploitation of natural resources and the strong associated investments. Take this respect on the recent inferences of Professor Tyler Biggs. Even so, for the case of Mozambique, respecting the results and opinions of different scholars and analysts, we have been guided by prudent exchange rate management, adjusting our interventions in the markets, always with the intention of influencing and not determining, the behavior of the exchange rate, to levels that ensure in the medium term, real gains of competitiveness. Thus, since the liberalization of the rate in 1993, it has fluctuated freely and around its level of equilibrium, and there are no signs of the so-called Dutch disease in our country for now. However, we are aware that the process of exploiting non-renewable natural resources that our country has just started will require us to make considerable adjustments in the action of monetary and exchange rate policy, in order to ensure that the expected massive increase in export revenue stemming from the implementation of the projects under implementation will not the external competitiveness of the exchange rate, or result in the proposed Dutch disease. In this area, I reaffirm our predisposition and commitment to do everything in order to preserve and consolidate macroeconomic stability in the country, including foreign exchange, an essential condition for the realization of more and greater investments and consequent promotion of economic growth. For this edition, the jury selected for public presentation the following papers: "Impact of Exchange Rate Variations on Mozambique's Trade Balance" and "Exchange Crises in Mozambique and its Determinants". Before concluding, allow me to express our pride in maintaining our Stable and Competitive Metical on time. We are also proud that we have maintained our national currency, the Metical, which is increasingly universally accepted, not only for its liberating power but also for the intrinsic strength it represents in the global, regional and cross-border trade, without underaltering its growing weight in transactions Domestic. The robustness of the Metical is a reflection of all the multisectoral reforms that the country has been carrying out in the last 25 years and expresses the new dynamics and balance of forces that are generated in our economy and its positioning in the region and in the world, coming to the world with new attributes and resources and, thereby attracting high interest and direct investment foreigner. I cannot lose sight of the reforms we have made in the monetary circulation since 1987, introducing three new Metical households and relieving the economy and national accounting with the three-digit cut in 2006. I end by renewing our expectation that the work that will be presented here will provide us with fruitful debates and exchange of views around the issue of the exchange rate in Mozambique. I hereby declare the Fourth Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique open and wish all participants a good working session. Thank you very much. Maputo, 30 October 2012
text_original: Senhor Vice-Governador do Banco de Moambique, Excelncia Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao Senhores Directores, Assistentes de Direco e tcnicos do Banco de Moambique; Senhores Representantes de Instituies do Governo Caros acadmicos e investigadores Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Gostaria em primeiro lugar, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, de saudar a todos os que se dignaram honrar-nos com a sua presena nestas Quartas Jornadas Cientficas da nossa instituio. Permitam-me que enderece uma saudao especial a todos os investigadores que acederam ao convite do Banco de Moambique, aceitando o desafio de participar e compartilhar connosco os seus projectos de investigao, em torno do tema central que seleccionmos para estas Jornadas Cientficas. Aos cinco participantes finalistas, vo as felicitaes do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique, pela qualidade demonstrada nas vossas pesquisas, que por certo exigiu de vs muitas horas de trabalho e estudo para a elaborao dos vossos projectos, dois dos quais sero hoje aqui apresentados publicamente, aps terem sido seleccionados pelo Jri designado. Endereo ao Presidente e aos demais membros do Jri os nossos agradecimentos pela pronta colaborao com o Banco de Moambique na rdua misso que desempenharam de avaliar e seleccionar os trabalhos submetidos, respeitando estritamente os parmetros estabelecidos pelo Regulamento das Jornadas Cientficas. A todos os presentes nestas IV Jornadas Cientficas vai o nosso apreo pelo interesse por esta iniciativa e considerao para com a nossa instituio, que expressam com a vossa presena, com o intuito de partilhar connosco pontos de vista, sensibilidades e contribuies em relao  temtica seleccionada, que classificamos de actual, oportuna e relevante, seja na ptica de pesquisa econmica pura como na vertente de fazedores de poltica econmica. Caros convidados, Quando em 2009 o Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique deliberou organizar, com periodicidade anual, as jornadas cientficas tinha em vista um frum de debate tcnico estruturado, fazendo uso de ferramentas disponveis da teoria econmica e financeira, bem assim a prtica devidamente analisada da actividade dos bancos centrais, atravs de comunicaes de especialidade feitas pelo nosso staff ou por peritos, acadmicos e policy makers que se dedicam  anlise dos fenmenos do universo da nossa actuao, funes e mandato. Temos reiterado em cada ano que para ns as jornadas cientficas so mais um momento de abertura da nossa instituio  sociedade e aos nossos parceiros, para juntos reflectirmos sobre informao da nossa especialidade, estudos tcnico-cientficos relacionados com a nossa actividade, o que nos permite estarmos atentos a outras sensibilidade e percepes, mantendo o contacto visual e analtico com opinies at contrrias, numa dialctica de permanente aprendizagem, visando aprimorar a nossa actuao nos domnios da concepo e implementao das polticas monetria e cambial, na nossa funo de reguladores e supervisores das instituies de crdito, sociedades financeiras e do sistema nacional de pagamentos. As primeiras Jornadas tiveram lugar em 2009, tendo sido analisados dois temas da autoria de quadros do Banco de Moambique e perante uma audincia reduzida a gestores e tcnicos da instituio, embora tenhamos convidado discussants externos ao Banco. Em 2010, as jornadas cientficas estiveram centradas na anlise e divulgao das nossas pesquisas no mbito da formulao e gesto da poltica monetria, em face de alteraes substanciais que empreendemos na orgnica e contedo do nosso Comit de Poltica Monetria (CPMO). Nesse ano, seleccionmos trs trabalhos para debate, todos da autoria de nossos gestores e tcnicos, perante uma audincia que contou j com a participao de convidados de instituies do Governo e da academia. Seguindo o gradualismo que adoptmos, no ano passado, as Terceiras Jornadas Cientficas foram alargadas a representantes de instituies do Governo, instituies acadmicas e de pesquisa econmica, analistas de especialidade e estudantes do ensino superior. Nesse evento, abordmos trs temas da autoria do staff do Banco de Moambique, designadamente, O Mecanismo de Transmisso da Poltica Monetria: Uma Investigao do Canal de Taxa de Juros em Moambique, Reflexo sobre as Metas Monetrias em Moambique e a Eficcia da Regra de Taylor em Moambique. Para a presente edio das Jornadas Cientficas, o Conselho de Administrao elegeu como tema central A taxa de Cmbio em Moambique, o qual se justifica pelo facto de assinalarmos este ano o 25 aniversrio da implementao da primeira reforma da taxa de cmbio em Moambique, inserida na implementao do PRE - Programa de Reabilitao Econmica. Como mencionei, esta temtica  sempre actual e transversal, despertando o interesse de um leque variado de sensibilidades e percepes, desde acadmicos ao cidado comum, sendo por isso importante debatermos e sabermos escutar a voz da pesquisa estruturada sobre esta matria. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Desde a proclamao da independncia em 1975, o nosso Pas j experimentou distintos regimes cambiais, em face das condies conjunturais especficas de cada momento, bem assim dos objectivos de poltica econmica perseguidos em cada etapa. O perodo de 1975 a 1986 foi caracterizado por um regime de cmbios fixos, no quadro de uma economia de planificao central marcada por inmeras dificuldades conjunturais, deteriorao da produo nacional, agravamento do endividamento pblico e escassez de divisas. Em onze anos de regime de taxa de cmbio fixa, a flutuao acumulada aproximou-se a 46%, correspondente a uma depreciao mdia anual de apenas 1,42%. As reservas internacionais neste perodo eram de apenas 39,5 milhes de Dlares americanos, montante capaz de cobrir menos de um ms de importaes que o pas realizava naquela poca. Chamo, contudo, a ateno para que no se avalie este perodo sem se contextualizar o ambiente de economia de guerra em que se estava mergulhado. Em 1987, na sequncia da adeso de Moambique ao Fundo Monetrio Internacional efectivada em 1984, inicia-se a implementao do Programa de Reabilitao Econmica (PRE). Este programa seguia o modelo tpico de ajustamento estrutural e de liberalizao econmica e a correco da taxa de cmbio constituiu a face mais visvel do programa, com duas etapas distintas:  A primeira, de desvalorizaes de grande intensidade (tambm conhecidas por terapia de choque), realizadas entre 1987 e 1988, numa base semestral. Recorde-se que a primeira desvalorizao ocorreu a 31 de Janeiro de 1987, quando pela voz do ento Primeiro-Ministro do nosso governo, o Metical sofreu a primeira desvalorizao de 442,5% face ao Dlar americano que era transaccionado no mercado oficial ao cmbio de 38,28 Meticais ao passar para 200 Meticais. Este processo prosseguiu at 1988, tendo em Outubro a taxa de cmbio atingido 620 Meticais por Dlar, traduzindo uma correco administrativa de 1.520% na nossa moeda, em cerca de dois anos.  Seguiu-se entre 1989 e 1992, o perodo de crawling peg ou desvalorizao deslizante, sem, contudo alterar-se a substncia do regime cambial em vigor que continuou a ser de taxas administradas ou fixas. O processo consistiu em pequenas desvalorizaes mensais, at 1990, seguidas por desvalorizaes dirias, entre 1991 e 1992, tendo a desvalorizao acumulada neste intervalo totalizado 59,9% no primeiro perodo e de 13%, no segundo. Foi neste perodo que foi criado o Mercado Secundrio de Cmbios, espao legal que veio a atrair operadores privados para um novo segmento do mercado cambial, muitos dos quais at ento vinculados ao mercado paralelo de divisas. Entre 1992 e 1993, levmos a cabo o processo de unificao cambial, etapa que foi marcada por um estreitamento do spread entre a taxa de cmbio oficial e a do mercado secundrio. Seguiu-se o perodo de 1993 a 2000, em que comemos a preparar as condies e os alicerces para a transio para o regime de cmbios flexveis, no contexto do aprofundamento da liberalizao poltica e econmica que o pas viveu, com a paz alcanada em 1992 e a realizao das primeiras eleies multipartidrias, em 1994. Em 1996, crimos formalmente o Mercado Cambial Interbancrio, que operou durante quatro anos em regime presencial e sem suporte tecnolgico de vulto. Passmos a transaccionar no mercado cambial divisas com os bancos comerciais existentes, resultando da uma taxa de cmbio que foi a gnese da actual taxa das cotaes do MCI. Convm destacar que no ano de 2000 inicimos a transio para instrumentos indirectos de controle monetrio, abandonando o sistema de limites de crdito e limites de activos internos lquidos, passando a poltica monetria a ser feita exclusivamente pelos instrumentos dos mercados, mormente, monetrio e cambial. A entrada de novos bancos privados no sistema bancrio impunha o aprofundamento das funcionalidades do mercado cambial interbancrio. Em 2005, com a assistncia tcnica de especialistas internacionais, introduzimos o sistema de cotaes Bid e Offer no mercado cambial interbancrio e regras de conduta para balizar a postura e tica dos dealers, sustentado por um sistema informtico que foi sendo constantemente aperfeioado no tempo, o qual permite realizar operaes em tempo real, com qualquer praa financeira do mundo. Este foi o culminar de um longo processo de reformas do nosso regime cambial e a partir de ento consolidmos o regime em que a taxa de cmbio  determinada pelas condies de procura e oferta no mercado. Convir recordar que no quadro desta reforma, ensaimos em 2005 a realizao de leiles de divisas no mercado cambial, com o intuito de melhor aferir o mecanismo de price discovering. Tratou-se duma experincia que acarretou resultados menos positivos, tendo o Metical naquele ano, registado uma elevada depreciao nominal, prxima de 20%. As cotaes do Metical, em cada momento do dia, so determinadas pelas condies de procura e oferta de divisas expressas pelos operadores autorizados a exercer actividades no nosso mercado cambial. Desde ento, as nossas intervenes no mercado tm vindo a ter em conta as condies de mercado e os seus objectivos esto estreitamente associados aos objectivos macroeconmicos estabelecidos, assentes em trs pilares essenciais: regulao da liquidez, inflao e posio das reservas internacionais. Assim, quando intervimos no mercado cambial, mais do que satisfazer a procura revelada de divisas, tambm perseguimos objectivos de poltica monetria ou alinhamentos necessrios na nossa taxa de cmbio  sua tendncia mais desejada a mdio prazo. O regime cambial flexvel foi reiterado e reforado com a Lei n 11/2009, de 11 de Maro, Lei Cambial, que consagrou a completa liberalizao das transaces correntes no pas, a exclusividade do sistema bancrio nacional para a intermediao das operaes com o exterior, mantendo sob tutela e jurisdio da autoridade cambial todas as operaes de capital. Previamente  adopo desta regulamentao, o pas foi sujeito ao escrutnio das instituies financeiras internacionais para avaliar e verificar a existncia de restries cambiais e prticas de taxas de cmbio mltiplas. Concluiu-se que Moambique adopta efectivamente um regime cambial flexvel, possibilitando a nossa adeso ao Artigo VIII dos Estatutos do FMI. Estes desenvolvimentos foram acompanhados pelo crescimento das exportaes totais de bens e servios, a uma taxa mdia anual de 16% nos ltimos dez anos o que teve reflexos positivos na melhoria da posio externa do pas, traduzida na queda do rcio do dfice da conta corrente em relao ao PIB, para menos de 10% em 2009, voltando a subir para 13,2% em 2011, em face do grande volume de importaes associadas ao elevado influxo de Investimento Directo Estrangeiro que tem vindo a verificar-se nos ltimos anos. As Reservas Internacionais Lquidas do pas, foram aumentando ano a ano, at posicionarem-se em cerca USD 2,7 bilies em Setembro ltimo, o equivalente a 5,9 meses de cobertura das importaes de bens e servios no factoriais e 6,5 meses se excluindo as importaes dos grandes projectos. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, O processo de reformas em Moambique, com impacto directo e indirecto no regime cambial, est bastante documentado e razoavelmente analisado na nossa instituio. Para alm de estudos de especialidade tambm levados a cabo por outros pesquisadores nacionais e estrangeiros. Orgulha-nos o facto de os nossos quadros terem j elaborado contribuies analticas e cientificas sobre o assunto, alguns dos quais passo a resumir para o benefcio dos nossos debates. Assim, encontramos em de Sousa, W. (1993), uma anlise do impacto da unificao cambial em Moambique, ocorrida em 1992 e a constatao de o processo ter sido caracterizado por significativas desvalorizaes efectivas reais, com ganhos reais de competitividade externa para o pas, concluindo que a competitividade s  efectiva quando ponderado todos os factores que a determinam, para alm da taxa de cmbio, nomeadamente, o regime de taxas e tarifas, a produtividade de trabalho e a inovao. J Pimpo, A. (1996) faz uma cronologia da evoluo da poltica cambial em Moambique, no perodo de 1975 a 1996, destacando os objectivos que a nortearam. Por seu turno, Saranga, J. no seu trabalho Taxa de Cmbio Real e os Produtos Agrcolas de Exportao (1996), analisou o impacto da taxa de cmbio real sobre o volume de exportaes de produtos agrcolas, com nfase para o algodo e castanha de caju, tendo concludo que o efeito era marginal, mostrando assim o facto de a pouca competitividade dos produtos agrcolas no estar dependente do comportamento da taxa de cmbio. Sobre a problemtica do alinhamento da taxa de cmbio em Moambique, h tambm a assinalar trabalhos cientficos relevantes j publicados, sendo de destacar o trabalho de Fabrizio, S. (1998), que avaliou a competitividade externa de Moambique para o perodo de 1980 a 1996, tendo constatado que em termos lquidos o Metical registou uma apreciao real efectiva entre 1980-1986, traduzindo em perdas reais de competitividade externa vis--vis os principais parceiros comerciais da regio, situao que no entanto foi revertida a partir de meados de 1987. A autora conclui que a taxa de cmbio real voltou a registar entre 1993 e 1997, perodos de relativa apreciao, mas no geral sem expresso na ptica de desalinhamento, uma vez que as flutuaes giraram em torno do seu equilbrio, em mdia, os 7%. Francis V. (2007), no seu artigo Export Performance and Competitiveness in Mozambique, avaliando o desalinhamento da taxa de cmbio real entre 1999 e 2006, conclui que no obstante os desalinhamentos observados, no geral a taxa de cmbio esteve em linha com os fundamentos econmicos do pas. Mais recentemente, no mbito da melhoria do quadro de implementao da poltica monetria, o nosso Departamento de Estudos Econmicos e Estatstica tem realizado diversas estimaes, incluindo economtricas, cujos resultados convergem para os j apresentados noutros trabalhos sobre os determinantes da inflao em Moambique, que mostram que a transmisso dos efeitos da taxa de cmbio para a inflao  rpida e de magnitude considervel. Este facto, leva a que estejamos sempre atentos aos movimentos desta varivel para evitar que a sua dinmica de curto prazo no tenha reflexos negativos no nvel geral de preos, mas tambm, no propicie perdas persistentes da competitividade externa dos nossos produtos de exportao. Caros Convidados Este debate tem lugar num momento caracterizado pela ocorrncia de uma crise econmica e financeira sem precedentes. Ainda assim, a economia moambicana apresenta uma considervel resilincia, registando taxas de crescimento acima dos 7%, superior  mdia da SADC e do continente africano. O crescimento da actividade econmica no pas tem vindo a ser sustentado pelo bom desempenho dos sectores da agricultura, construo, transportes e comunicaes, alavancados por elevados investimentos pblicos e privados, particularmente o investimento estrangeiro, na indstria de extraco mineira, dinamismo este que no entanto, ainda no tem sido totalmente ponderado nas estatsticas da produo total do pas. Por seu turno, a inflao medida pela variao anual do ndice de Preos da cidade de Maputo que regrediu para 5,46% em 2011, apresentou-se nos nove meses do presente ano estvel e baixa, fixando-se em 1,23%,  semelhana da inflao mdia que regrediu para 3,31%, aps 10,3% em Dezembro de 2011. Registmos uma considervel estabilidade cambial nos ltimos anos, sustentada, por um lado, pela boa coordenao das polticas monetria e fiscal, bem como pela macia entrada de capitais no sistema bancrio nacional, associada ao investimento directo estrangeiro que tem lugar no pas, com o advento da explorao dos recursos naturais. A taxa de cmbio  uma importante varivel da gesto macroeconmica e estimula a actividade econmica, impactando em especial no nosso caso, com o comportamento do nvel geral de preos. Para Pases como o nosso, uma depreciao excessiva para alm de no assegurar, a longo prazo, ganhos de competitividade, pode ter efeitos perniciosos sobre a produo domstica, se os agentes econmicos, perante os ganhos extraordinrios proporcionados pela taxa de cmbio, deixarem de investir na inovao e modernizao das suas unidades produtivas, direccionadas para a promoo da produtividade e na competitividade. O estudo da taxa de cmbio oferece vrias abordagens, que podem ir desde a compreenso da dinmica, determinantes, efeitos em outras variveis macroeconmicas, determinao do nvel de equilbrio e respectivo desalinhamento, bem como, o efeito e magnitudes do mecanismo de transmisso para a inflao e crescimento, incluindo o fenmeno do dutch disease. A nossa histria de reformas na rea cambial  longa assim como a anlise tcnica sobre esta temtica. Alguns dos trabalhos desenvolvidos sobre a realidade moambicana abordam dois principais assuntos relacionados com o comportamento do Metical, designadamente a questo do alinhamento ou desalinhamento da taxa de cmbio versus avaliao da ocorrncia do dutch desease. Muito se tem falado recentemente sobre o fenmeno da doena holandesa para o caso moambicano. So vrios os analistas e as percepes sobre este fenmeno, mas devo sublinhar que ns Banco de Moambique ainda no vislumbramos a ocorrncia desse fenmeno na economia moambicana. Desde o incio da recente explorao de recursos naturais, tudo o que est a acontecer situa-se ainda na esfera do investimento directo, esperando-se que a mdio prazo as receitas venham a alavancar uma maior independncia do nosso Oramento de Estado e maior robustez das nossas reservas internacionais. No artigo The Macroeconomic Challange of More Aid publicado pelo FMI na Revista Finance and Development, n 3 do volume 43, de Setembro de 2005, concluiu-se que a economia moambicana tem conseguido absorver complementarmente as entradas de ajuda externa, o que tem permitido evitar episdios de apreciao real, no havendo por isso, evidncias da doena holandesa. Nesta linha, Wazela, T. e Ornar, J. (2009), ambos tcnicos do Banco de Moambique, concluem que apesar da entrada considervel de fundos de ajuda externa so tnues os sinais de ocorrncia do Dutch desease ou doena holandesa, resultados compatveis com o trabalho do FMI publicado em 2006, com o ttulo Aid and the Equilibrium Exchange Rate - The case of Mozambique. A discusso em torno da doena holandesa, que antes era relacionada com a entrada de ajuda externa para apoio directo ao Oramento do Estado, muda-se agora para a explorao de recursos naturais e os fortes investimentos associados. Veja-se a este respeito as recentes inferncias do Professor Tyler Biggs. Mesmo assim, para o caso de Moambique, respeitando os resultados e opinies dos diferentes estudiosos e analistas, temos pautado por uma gesto cambial prudente, ajustando as nossas intervenes nos mercados, sempre com o intuito de influenciar e no determinar, o comportamento da taxa de cmbio, para nveis que assegurem no mdio prazo, ganhos reais de competitividade. Assim, desde a liberalizao da taxa em 1993, esta tem flutuado livremente e em torno do seu nvel de equilbrio, no havendo por ora, sinais da chamada doena holandesa no nosso Pas. No entanto, temos a conscincia de que o processo de explorao de recursos naturais no renovveis que o nosso pas acaba de iniciar exigir de ns ajustamentos considerveis na actuao da poltica monetria e cambial, por forma a assegurar que o esperado incremento massivo de receitas de exportaes resultante da implementao dos projectos em implantao, no ponha em causa a competitividade externa da taxa de cmbio, ou resulte na propalada doena holandesa. Neste domnio, reafirmo a nossa predisposio e compromisso de tudo fazermos visando a preservao e consolidao da estabilidade macroeconmica no pas, incluindo a cambial, condio essencial para a concretizao de mais e maiores investimentos e consequente promoo do crescimento econmico. Para esta edio, o jri seleccionou para apresentao pblica os seguintes trabalhos: Impacto das Variaes da Taxa de Cmbio na Balana Comercial de Moambique e  Crises Cambiais em Moambique e seus Determinantes . Antes de concluir, permitam-me que expresse o nosso orgulho por mantermos o nosso Metical estvel e competitivo no tempo. Orgulha-nos tambm o facto de termos mantido a nossa moeda nacional, o Metical, cada vez mais aceite universalmente, no apenas pelo seu poder liberatrio mas tambm pela pujana intrnseca que a mesma representa na economia global, regional e no comrcio transfronteirio, sem subalternizar o seu peso crescente nas transaces domsticas. A robustez do Metical  reflexo de todas as reformas multisectoriais que o pas vem realizando nos ltimos 25 anos e expressa as novas dinmicas e o equilbrio de foras que se geram na nossa economia e o seu posicionamento na regio e no mundo, despontando para o mundo com novos atributos e recursos e, da atraindo elevado interesse e investimento directo estrangeiro. No posso perder de vista as reformas que realizmos na circulao monetria desde 1987, introduzindo trs novas famlias do Metical e aliviando a economia e a contabilidade nacional com o corte de trs dgitos efectuado em 2006. Termino renovando a nossa expectativa de que os trabalhos que sero aqui apresentados nos proporcionem profcuos debates e troca de pontos de vista  volta da questo da taxa de cmbio em Moambique. Declaro assim abertas as Quartas Jornadas Cientficas do Banco de Moambique e desejo a todos participantes uma boa sesso de trabalhos. Muito Obrigado. Maputo, 30 de Outubro de 2012

Title: Intervention at the Lisbon 2012 Meeting
text: Bank of Mozambique The Challenges of Monetary Policy in the Context of Natural Resource Exploitation: The Case of Mozambique Dr. Ernesto Gouveia Gove Governor  Introduction Despite the economic and financial crisis that the world is experiencing, Mozambique continues to gain the confidence of different investors, becoming, in recent years, an desirable destination for foreign direct investment in Africa and the world. After twenty years of peace and a long process of macroeconomic adjustment, with various reforms aimed at improving the business environment, the country reaps the first fruits of the influx of foreign capital, associated with the beginning of the exploitation of natural resources, with emphasis on coal, in the preliminary phase of production and export, as well as gas, research and evaluation. In 2011, foreign direct investment in the extractive industry represented an approximate value of 17% of the Country's Gross Domestic Product, compared with approximately 5% in the period 2000 to 2008. The export of coal started in mid-2011 allowed revenue to exceed 5 billion Meticais in the first six months of 2012, with this ore occupying the second position in Mozambique's export product list after aluminum. The beginning of the exploitation of coal and other non-renewable natural resources poses new challenges to macroeconomic management and policies committed to the Central Bank. The high influx of capital, associated with the investment phase and, in the future, with export revenues, has been increasing the availability of foreign currency to the economy, thus constituting a challenge to the management of monetary policy and public finances. The immediate effect of improving the country's external reserve levels, far from meaning an end in itself in the complex macroeconomic management process, puts new paradigms on the stabilization and consolidation of public finances. The effect of natural resources on the economy is a subject much discussed in the economic literature and it can be affirmed that consensus is fragile. Several studies have found that resource-rich countries tend to experience modest growth rates in their economies compared to those less gifted due to the adverse effects of the abundance of natural resources, also known as "Dutch disease", sometimes associated with price volatility of raw materials international markets, or institutional fragility that can foment the phenomenon of corruption. Sachs and Warner (1995) show that economies starting with a high ratio of natural resource exports to GDP tend to grow more slowly in subsequent years compared to countries least dependent on natural resource exports when differences in the initial conditions of key factors are controlled economic growth. In this scenario, the abundance of natural resources would become a "curse", as it would lead to the occurrence of social, political and economic instability. However, there is a set of studies showing that there is no deterministic causal relationship between the abundance of natural resources and the levels of economic growth, even with examples of countries that have used their resources as catalysts for development. At present, the cases of Chile, Botswana, Indonesia and Norway which, having adopted economic policy measures and appropriate institutional reforms, have achieved high levels of economic growth over successive years, with a direct impact on the quality of life of its citizens, are well known as successful examples. This document aims to discuss the challenges of the Bank of Mozambique, as the central bank of the Republic of Mozambique, in the emergence of large-scale exploitation of non-renewable natural resources. The document is divided into four parts, including introduction. In the second part, the paper discusses the main channels or causes of the "curse of natural resources". In the third, it discusses the concrete case of Mozambique analyzing the macroeconomic context in which the exploitation of natural resources is taking place, the prospects, the impacts (or possible consequences), the main challenges and the role of the Bank of Mozambique in this process. In the last part, brief conclusions are presented.  Causes of the "Curse of Resources" The main challenge of economic policy management in countries with natural resources is to prevent the possibility of the occurrence of the so-called "resource curse". International evidence shows that the abundance of natural resources reduces the economic growth of some countries over a long period of time, and may even see cases of negative growth and socio-political instability, in contrast to the performance of the least endowed countries. Although international evidence shows the tendency to the possibility of the occurrence of the curse of resources, there is no consensus on the mechanisms or causes of it. The literature points to as causes of the "curse" of economic resources, such as the effects of the deterioration of terms of exchange (or Prebisch-Singer's hypotheses), "Dutch disease", the volatility of resource prices on the international market and weak positive externalities of the natural resources sector in relation to the other sectors of the economy, or even extra-economic factors, in particular the existence of weak institutions, the phenomenon of corruption, civil conflicts and the inequalities that arise in the distribution of income. This document only takes into account economic aspects , although the importance of extra-economic factors for poor countries is recognised.
