Title: End of the Economic Year 2012
text: Mr President of INE, Excellency Mr. Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency Former Governors of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellencies; Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Former Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Presidents of the Boards of Directors and Executive Committees of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations; Members of the Audit Board of the Bank of Mozambique; Dear Directors, Assistant Directors and other Managers of the Bank of Mozambique; Distinguished Guests Ladies and Gentlemen I would first of all like to greet everyone present at this traditional year-end toast ceremony in which our institution takes the preliminary assessment of the year that is about to end and shares with its partners and the general public the prospects for the new year. Let me begin my speech by addressing a special greeting to our Government for the numerous activities it carried out in 2012, as part of the implementation of its Five-Year Plan, with emphasis on actions with an impact on improving the business environment, for those that stimulate new opportunities for our economic actors to invest in investment in various sectors of activity as Activities generation of income, new jobs and greater competitiveness of our economy, with less external dependence. In an adverse situation and with limited resources, our Government has been able to elect measures that preserve the standard of living of the millions of Mozambican citizens, measures that mitigate the effects of the international crisis to which many of our compatriots are subject, because they still live on the threshold of poverty. The Government has done much to maintain peace and political stability and Macroeconomic values that are already assumed as part of our Mozambicanity and reinforce the credibility of our State in Africa and in the world. The environment of peace and stability has favored the capture of investments for the country. The exploration of mineral resources and hydrocarbons that we started, together with the public and private investments of ongoing infrastructure, has allowed the country's enormous potential to be relaunched, which in the long term will contribute to improving Mozambique's position on the global roadmap. These ventures and initiatives give substance to our economic growth, which we all increasingly desire to but strong, comprehensive and inclusive. I also take this moment to express our appreciation and recognition of the To credit institutions and financial corporations operating in our market, To public and private companies providing various goods and services to the financial sector, To economic and socio-professional associations, trade unions, To academic and research institutions and the media, for the invaluable collaboration they have provided to the Bank of Mozambique, which helps us to improve our performance and to carry out with zeal the mission entrusted to us. I extend my greetings to our cooperation partners and international financial institutions for committing to our country and our development agenda, also contributing to the success of numerous reforms that the country has been undertaking in the economic, social, financial and legal-legal spheres. Distinguished Guests Ladies, gentlemen, Economic Situation Macroeconomic Performance in 2012 The world still faces the threat of the international economic and financial crisis triggered in 2007, despite the exceptional and incentive measures taken by governments and central banks of the economies of the northern hemisphere to counter its effects. The recession in the more developed economies has had varying repercussions on the march of social and human development of the periphery economies, with a focus on those of the African continent, even though our economic growth, as with emerging market economies, remains thriving. will continue to adversely affect our balance of payments, international price volatility, restrictions on access to external credit by our fragile business sector, without neglecting the reduction in official financial aid to development programmes. 0 year 2012 continued to be marked by an adverse international conjuncture, but Mozambique's resilience persists, measure by the confidence of entrepreneurs of different latitudes that make our country a safe destination and attractive market for their investments. Gradually we are taking a major position in the statistics of foreign direct investment in Africa and the world, which everyone should be proud of. The latest information from the National Institute of Statistics, which does not weigh the recent dynamics of the extractive industry that emerges in the country, points out that the real growth of Mozambican Gross Domestic Product was close to 8.0% in the first half of 2012, which is in line with the initial expectation of the authorities of a growth of 7.5%. This performance has been sustained by the dynamism of the agriculture, construction, transport and communications sectors, leveraged by high public and private investments. The start of the exploration of mineral resources, broadens the mood and prospects that several analysts make of our economy, in the short and medium term, which are unanimous in considering that Mozambique is on the "ramp" of strong growth of broad base. It is up to us Mozambicans to make this growth endogenous, inclusive and dynamicized by a state budget less dependent on foreign aid. To this end, our institution has contributed in several areas of expertise to the urgency of preparing a development strategy that consolidates actions to combat poverty and integrates this agenda in a broader framework, addressing the emerging challenges of the exploitation of non-renewable natural resources, the focus that must be made on creating jobs for our youth, as well as establishing an appropriate link between the integration of the internal market, regional integration and the deepening of the internationalisation of the Mozambican economy. We are pleased to note that the country's new wave of growth occurs in an environment of peace, macroeconomic stability and the financial sector. After we faced strong inflationary pressure in 2010, the correction and adjustment measures we took had their effects in 2012. Thus, in the year in the past year we observed a downward behavior of inflation measured by the annual change in the Consumer Price Index of the city of Maputo, to a level of 2.46% until November 2012, which compared with 7.74% in the same period of 2011. Average annual inflation also fell to 2.36%, after 11.27% in November 2011. This trend is also observed in IPC Mozambique. The low inflation behavior in the eleven months of this year makes us confident that the target of 5.6% set for this year will be observed. Price stability in 2012 stems from a multitude of factors, of which, we highlight the dynamism of the real sector of the economy, the entrepreneurship of economic agents, the good coordination of policies, associated with the relative stability of the Metical vis-88-vis the currencies traded on our market, in a framework in which the cushions of the prices of some goods and services established to mitigate the impact of the international crisis continued to prevail, with emphasis on liquid fuel, water and energy prices. The fall in international prices of some of the goods we import also contributed to the inflation results this year. In 2012, we continued a monetary policy aimed at further expanding monetary and credit aggregates, in the face of stable behavior and in line with the established programme, of the main macro-financial indicators. The Monetary Policy Committee has strongly adopted a resource-freestance stance on interbank markets, respecting our commitments in terms of monetary base and net international reserves. Indeed, throughout the year, it decided six times to reduce the liquidity-in-the-MMI rate, totaling a drop of 5.5 percentage points to the current 9.5%. The Permanent Deposit Facility rate was reduced by 275 basis points during the year, placing it at 2.25% last November and the Mandatory Reserve coefficient received a clearance of 150 basis points, to the current 8.0%. These are the gains of macroeconomic stability that we all want to preserve. Although with some lag, which translates our transmission mechanism, proper to a developing financial market, these measures of the Bank of Mozambique were timidly monitored by commercial banks, despite being in the right direction. As a monetary authority and supervisors of the financial system, we recognize that there are challenges to our strategic objective of low and attractive interest rates, with competitive financial services and fair transaction costs, in a low inflation environment with financial stability. As a result of the monetary policy we have adopted, the expansion of bank credit to the private sector of the economy, which has been experiencing a sharp slowdown since late 2010, reversed its trend in 2012, rising from 6% in December 2011 to around 19% last November. However, we are not content with this growth, as there are still structural constraints on access to bank financing, particularly for the universe of our small and medium-sized Companies. To these, we continue to call for greater effort in the field of the organization of their accounting systems, following international standards, with audited accounts to facilitate the risk analysis of their financing projects, without neglecting that we all also have a responsibility to seek solutions that amplify access to credit for this important segment of our economy. Distinguished Guests; Ladies; Gentlemen Development Financial Sector and Payment System Since the beginning of the implementation in July 2011 of the new foreign exchange legislation, which enshrines the principle of liberalization of current transactions and reinforces the role of the national banking system in the intermediation of foreign operations, we have seen a greater availability of foreign exchange in the foreign exchange market, giving it greater fluidity. Of the supervisory actions we have carried out on credit institutions authorized to carry out transactions with abroad, we found it necessary to continue to invest in the ongoing training of their employees, some of whom without the necessary training for an adequate analysis of the various foreign operations that the counters receive daily. In 2012, we faced some periods of nervousness in the Metical exchange rate, associated with seasonality and the excessive concentration of import and liquidation operations of the net fuel bill. The dynamics of our economy demand annual imports of around US1 billion of this raw material and our foreign exchange market is in a position to meet this demand, although some operational aspects need to be improved. In close compliance with the flexible exchange rate principles enshrined in our exchange rate regime, the nominal depreciation of 9.7% that Metical recorded in 2012 against the US Dollar can be seen as an adjustment that the market has made to our external competitiveness, and exporters are expected to do their part, toasting our balance of payments with effective improvements in the quantities exported. Regarding the Rand, the Metical proved to be more stable (virtually nil variation), at a time when the South African currency, due to its greater integration into the international economy, recorded significant fluctuations in relation to the US Dollar, without neglecting other factors, such as the international trend in precious metal prices that South Africa produces and exports and the prolonged strikes that afflicted its mining sector. Despite the economic and financial crisis that the world is experiencing, Mozambique has become in recent years a privileged destination for foreign direct investment in Africa and the world, particularly in the natural resources sector. This investment, in its initial phase, exacerbates the current account deficit of our balance of payments. Foreign direct investment, which accounted for an average of 5% of GDP by 2009, has risen in the last two years to around 17%. In the first nine months of this year, our balance of payments recorded a net capital inflow in the form of foreign direct investment of US1,451 million, 330 million more than in the same period last year. Preliminary data from Mozambique's external position measured by the current account balance show a 70% deterioration to US1,802 million compared to the same period in 2011, mainly explained by the increase in demand for services by foreign direct investment projects. Removing the effect of these projects, the current account deficit increased less pronounced, by 36%, to 1,492 million Dollars. The worsening of the deficit was partially mitigated by the improvement in the balance of the goods account as a result of the increase in exports by 9.5% in the first nine months of the year, to a total of US2.6 02 million, where the export revenues of coal exported with a value of 313 million, which came to occupy the second position in all Mozambican exports, after aluminum. In turn, total imports grew by 5.1% to US4,263 million, of which US1,283 million was carried out by major projects. The country constituted net international reserves in the amount of US306 million, for a balance of US2,546 million, according to preliminary data reported on December 14, 2012, which is equivalent to about 5,6 6 months of coverage of imports of non-factor goods and services. Our interventions in the Market Interbank exchange rate resulted in gross sales of US625 million until December 14, 2012, of which a significant part was intended to support the settlement of the net fuel bill. Distinguished Guests Ladies Gentlemen At the level of the financial sector, we continue in the year in review to implement actions aimed at encouraging the increase and diversification of financial institutions operating in the country, as well as the expansion and scope of the services provided. Contrary to what is happening in other countries, we have seen the entry into the our financial system of new entrants, as well as investments of geographical expansion and modernization, demonstrating the soundness and stability of the sector. In 2012, we pointed to the entry of 19 new microcredit institutions, the opening of 39 new bank branches, for a total of 479 operating in 2012, covering all provincial capitals, municipalities and 62 of the 128 districts, or 4 more compared to 2011. Although we recognize and welcome the effort made by credit institutions in this area, there is no doubt that much remains to be done, because the demand for financial services by our population is indeferred, imposing the need for expansion to more places in our vast territory, where populations produce wealth and lack the support of banking, either for the deposit of your savings or for the investment. The Mozambican financial system has shown a degree of resilience to the indirect effects of the international financial crisis, to be measured by the robustness of the solvency ratio that by September 2012 stood at 19.1%, well above the minimum set by the Basel I criterion, while the ratio of unchanged credit decreased to less than 4% in September. In the wake of our commitment to the soundness of the Mozambican financial sector, we issued Notice No. 03/GBM/2012 of 28 November, which guides the institutions on migration to the Basel II criteria. 2013 hard work awaits us to begin simultaneous adoption of the Basel I and II criteria, preparing our institutions for the transition to the terms of Basel II from 1 January 2014. As with other countries, migration to Basel II will impose the need for minimum capital reinforcement, which will require our institutions to put in place appropriate methodologies for calculating capital requirements, whether for credit risk coverage and for the incorporation of new risks, operational risk and market risk. In turn, the modernization of our national payment system is a strategic objective of our role as the Central Bank. The computer platform of the Interbank Society of Services (SIMO) is already installed and ready for the connection of banks to SIMOrede. The pilot linking of the first ATM's and POS's last September, in the framework of the operationalisation of SIMO, was an important step towards the materialisation of this objective. Based on the atm number criterion, the number of institutions in productive and advanced phase of simonetwork integration tests already represent about 50% of the market. I take this opportunity to congratulate the banks that are at the forefront of this process for their effective commitment and I also welcome the efforts made, encouraging all other banks in the system to follow this irreversible march towards a fully integrated network that brings efficiency gains and economies of scale for users of financial intermediation services, reason for this project. The high degree of penetration of the mobile phone has created in the country, an opportunity for credit institutions to provide financial products using the technology of mobile phone service providers. Since 2011, the financial system has had an institution operating using the mobile phone network. In in 2012, we saw the introduction of new products and financial services accessed via mobile phone. These and other solutions that have been implemented are an excellent contribution of the institutions operating in the country to the development of our financial inclusion strategy, by ensuring rapid access of financial services to a wide layer of our population, which imposes new challenges in regulating this type of services. Ladies Gentlemen The economic outlook for 2013 points to the prevalence of an adverse and uncertain international environment, especially in the level of the more advanced economies, where the pace of expansion of economic activity is expected to slow down accompanied by increased unemployment. Uncertainty about ending the sovereign debt crisis in the Eurozone requires ongoing monitoring to ward off the dangers of contagion in our financial system. International Monetary Fund forecasts last October lower growth prospects economic 2012 and 2013. Thus, emerging and developing market economies could experience aggregate growth of 5.3%, while advanced economies could grow by only 1.3%, heavily penalised by developments in eurozone economies where the recession is expected to worsen Economic. In 2013, maintaining macroeconomic stability gains and the financial sector will remain our main objective. In this context, our action will be oriented to contribute to the final economic policy objectives set by the Government, which provide for annual inflation of 7.%, real GDP growth of 8.4% and an accumulation of international reserves that allow coverage of at least 3.8 months of coverage of imports of non-factoria goods and services. To this end, the Bank of Mozambique will continue to focus on the use of instruments available in the monetary and foreign exchange markets, complemented by prudential supervision, with a view to ensuring an expansion of total means of payment (M3) of around 19.3% and bank credit to the private sector around 19.0%. The monetary base, our operating variable, is expected to have growth of no more than 18.4%. In addition to the follow-up to the actions already initiated in recent years, we have planned for 2013 the following structural actions: i. Continue to improve monetary policy management by strengthening our forecasting and response capacity; ii. Continue to strengthen our role as supervisor and regulator of credit institutions, leading the transition to basel II criteria; iii. In partnership with credit institutions, continue the effort to bankare the national economy, modernize the national payment system and seek more competitive and transparent financial services prices; iv. Continue to adopt postures of prudence and diversification of the application of our international reserves with a view to reducing risks; v. In collaboration with other institutions and bodies, continue to stimulate the expansion of financial services using new technologies, aiming to accelerate financial inclusion in the country. Distinguished Guests Challenges Mozambique is undergoing profound structural transformations induced by the discovery and start of the exploitation of non-renewable natural resources. This poses new challenges to macroeconomic management in general and to policies committed to the Central Bank in particular. The Bank of Mozambique reaffirms its commitment to adopt a flexible monetary policy to ensure the consolidation of macroeconomic stability and the financial sector, in an environment of expected increase in investment and exports, safeguarding development of the various sectors of the economy and external competitiveness. The new cycle of our development requires greater empowerment of our institutions to lead the process of exploitation of natural resources, in defense of the national interest and future generations, calibrating, if necessary, our policies, so that they exercise more effectively the role that is expected of them in the national agenda for development. 0 Bank of Mozambique, in coordination with the Government and the private sector, will continue to make efforts to create conditions to ensure greater access to small and medium-sized enterprises and other segments of the population not banked. These challenges are enshrined in the proposal for a Financial Sector Development Strategy, which requires the preparation of a specific Strategy for Inclusion Financial. To this end, a working group has been set up at The Bank of Mozambique to ensure the implementation of the aspects inherent in this objective, including the preparation of a proposed regulation on electronic banking , access to and use of mobile financial services, as well as the preparation of indicators for the measurement and monitoring of financial inclusion in the country. In addition, our institution will continue to pay attention to actions to promote financial education in the context of financial consumer protection. Ladies and gentlemen On 31 December the legal course and the unlimited and full release value of the notes and coins of the first two families will end, namely the "People's Republic of Mozambique" family and the "Republic of Mozambique" family. I take this privileged stage to appeal to all those who have these denominations to make their deposit in banking establishments or exchange in the branches of the Bank of Mozambique, thus avoiding the loss of assets that will no longer have value from January 1, 2013. I rewelcome our greetings to economic agents and society at large who with their selfless effort have contributed to the country's economic development, giving substance to the efforts of the Government and monetary authority. I would also like to reiterate my appreciation to all the managers and technicians of the Bank of Mozambique whose devotion to work made possible the results achieved by our institution in 2012. I end by thanking all those present for their honorable presence at this balance sheet ceremony of the economic year about to end. I can only wish all present and your esteemed families, the staff and collaborators of the Bank of Mozambique and the financial sector and their families, happy holidays and a prosperous New Year. I invite you to accompany me in a toast for the health of our financial system, your health and our families! Maputo, 17 December 2012Ernesto Gouveia Gove

Permitam-me que inicie a minha interveno endereando uma saudao especial ao nosso Governo pelas inmeras actividades que levou a cabo em 2012, no quadro da implementao do seu Plano Quinquenal, com destaque para as aces com impacto na melhoria do ambiente de negcios, para as que estimulam novas Introduo e Saudaes Introduo e Saudaes Estendo as minhas saudaes aos nossos parceiros de cooperao e s instituies financeiras internacionais pelo cometimento para com o nosso Pas e a nossa agenda de desenvolvimento, contribuindo igualmente para o sucesso de inmeras reformas que o Pas tem vindo a empreender nas esferas econmica, social, financeira e jurdico-legal. Distintos Convidados Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Conjuntura Econmica Desempenho Macroeconmico em 2012 0 mundo ainda enfrenta a ameaa da crise econmica e financeira internacional deflagrada em 2007, no obstante as medidas excepcionais e de incentivo tomadas pelos Governos e bancos centrais das economias do hemisfrio norte para contrariar os seus efeitos. A recesso nas economias mais desenvolvidas tem tido reflexos variados na marcha do desenvolvimento social e humano das economias da periferia, com enfoque para as do continente africano, ainda que o nosso crescimento econmico,  semelhana do que sucede com as economias de mercado emergentes, continue a ser pujante. 0 espectro da recesso nos pases da Zona Euro, continuar a afectar negativamente a nossa balana de pagamentos, a volatilidade dos preos internacionais, as restries no acesso ao crdito externo por parte do nosso frgil sector empresarial, sem descurar a reduo da ajuda financeira oficial aos programas de desenvolvimento. 0 ano de 2012 continuou a ser marcado por uma conjuntura internacional adversa, mas a resilincia de Moambique persiste, a medir pela confiana de empreendedores de diferentes latitudes que fazem do nosso Pas destino seguro e mercado atractivo para os seus investimentos. Gradualmente vamos assumindo uma posio de relevo nas estatsticas do investimento directo estrangeiro, em frica e no mundo, o que a todos deve orgulhar. A ltima informao do Instituto Nacional de Estatstica, que no pondera a recente dinmica da indstria extractiva que desponta no Pas, aponta que o crescimento real do Produto Interno Bruto moambicano se situou prximo dos 8,0% no primeiro semestre de 2012, o que est em linha com a expectativa inicial das autoridades de um crescimento de 7.5%. Este desempenho tem vindo a ser sustentado pelo dinamismo dos sectores da agricultura, construo, transportes e comunicaes, alavancados por elevados investimentos pblicos e privados. O incio da explorao de recursos minerais, alarga o nimo e as perspectivas que vrios analistas fazem da nossa economia, no curto e mdio prazos, os quais so unnimes em considerar que Moambique est na rampa de um crescimento forte de base alargada. Compete-nos a ns moambicanos tornar este crescimento endgeno, inclusivo e dinamizado por um oramento de Estado menos dependente da ajuda externa. Para tanto, a nossa instituio tem contribudo em vrios fora de especialidade sobre a urgncia de prepararmos uma estratgia de desenvolvimento que consolide as aces de combate  pobreza e que integre esta agenda num quadro mais vasto, contemplando os desafios emergentes da explorao de recursos naturais no renovveis, a aposta que deve ser feita na criao de emprego para a nossa juventude, bem assim, que estabelea uma adequada ligao entre a integrao do mercado interno, a integrao regional e o aprofundamento da internacionalizao da economia moambicana. Apraz-nos constatar que a nova vaga de crescimento que o pas experimenta ocorre num ambiente de paz, estabilidade macroeconmica e do sector financeiro. Depois de em 2010 termos enfrentado uma forte presso inflacionria, as medidas de correco e ajuste que tommos surtiram em 2012 os seus efeitos. Assim, observamos no ano em revista um comportamento descendente da inflao medida pela variao anual do ndice de Preos no Consumidor da cidade de Maputo, para um nvel de 2.46% at Novembro de 2012, que compara com 7.74% em igual perodo de 2011. A inflao mdia anual tambm reduziu para 2.36%, aps 11,27% em Novembro de 2011. Esta tendncia  igualmente observada no IPC Moambique. O comportamento em baixa da inflao nos onze meses do corrente ano faz-nos estar confiantes em que a meta de 5.6% estabelecida para o presente ano ser observada. A estabilidade de preos em 2012 decorre de uma multiplicidade de factores, dos quais, destacamos o dinamismo do sector real da economia, o empreendedorismo dos agentes econmicos, a boa coordenao de polticas, associados  relativa estabilidade do Metical face s moedas transaccionadas no nosso mercado, num quadro em que continuaram a vigorar as almofadas aos preos de alguns bens e servios institudos para mitigar o impacto da crise internacional, com destaque para os preos dos combustveis lquidos, da gua e da energia. A queda dos preos internacionais de algumas mercadorias que importamos tambm concorreu para os resultados de inflao no presente ano. Em 2012, demos continuidade a uma poltica monetria orientada a uma maior expanso dos agregados monetrios e creditcios, em face de um comportamento estvel e em linha com o programa estabelecido, dos principais indicadores macro-financeiros. O Comit de Poltica Monetria insistentemente adoptou uma postura de libertao de recursos nos mercados interbancrios, respeitando os nossos compromissos em termos de base monetria e reservas internacionais lquidas. Com efeito, ao longo do ano, decidiu por seis vezes reduzir a taxa de cedncia de liquidez no MMI, totalizando uma baixa de 5.5 pontos percentuais, para os actuais 9,5%. A taxa da Facilidade Permanente de Depsitos foi reduzida em 275 pontos base durante o ano, posicionando-a em 2,25% em Novembro ltimo e o coeficiente de Reserva Obrigatria recebeu uma folga de 150 pontos base, para os actuais 8.0%. Estes so os ganhos da estabilidade macroeconmica que todos queremos preservar. Ainda que com algum desfasamento, que traduz o nosso mecanismo de transmisso, prprio de um mercado financeiro em desenvolvimento, estas medidas do Banco de Moambique foram timidamente acompanhadas pelos bancos comerciais, no obstante estarem na direco correcta. Como autoridade monetria e supervisores do sistema financeiro, reconhecemos existirem desafios em relao ao nosso objectivo estratgico de taxas de juro baixas e atractivas, com servios financeiros competitivos e custos de transaco justos, num ambiente de inflao baixa, com estabilidade financeira. Em resultado da poltica monetria que adoptmos, a expanso do crdito bancrio ao sector privado da economia, que vinha registando uma acentuada desacelerao desde finais de 2010, inverteu em 2012 a sua tendncia, subindo de 6% em Dezembro de 2011 para cerca de 19% em Novembro ltimo. Todavia, no nos contentamos com este crescimento, visto existirem ainda constrangimentos estruturais no acesso ao financiamento bancrio, particularmente pelo universo das nossas pequenas e mdias empresas. A estas, continuamos a apelar a um maior esforo no domnio da organizao do seus sistemas de contabilidade, obedecendo a padres internacionais, com contas auditadas para facilitar a anlise do risco dos seus projectos de financiamento, sem descurar que todos temos igualmente a responsabilidade de buscar solues que amplifiquem o acesso ao crdito por este segmento importante da nossa economia. Distintos Convidados; Minhas Senhoras; Meus Senhores, Desenvolvimento do Sector Financeiro e Sistema de Pagamentos Desde o incio da implementao, em Julho de 2011, da nova legislao cambial, que consagra o princpio da liberalizao das transaces correntes e refora o papel do sistema bancrio nacional na intermediao das operaes com o exterior, constatmos uma maior disponibilidade de divisas no mercado cambial, conferindo-lhe maior fluidez. Das aces de fiscalizao que realizmos s instituies de crdito autorizadas a realizar transaces com o exterior, constatmos ser necessrio continuar-se a apostar na formao permanente dos respectivos colaboradores, alguns dos quais sem o necessrio adestramento para uma adequada anlise das vrias operaes com o exterior que os balces diariamente recebem. Em 2012, enfrentmos alguns perodos de nervosismo na taxa de cmbio do Metical, associado  sazonalidade e  excessiva concentrao das operaes de importao e liquidao da factura de combustveis lquidos. A dinmica da nossa economia demanda importaes anuais em redor de mil milhes de dlares desta matria-prima e o nosso mercado cambial est em condies de satisfazer essa procura, ainda que seja necessrio melhorar alguns aspectos operacionais. Em estreita obedincia aos princpios de taxa de cmbio flexvel consagrados no nosso regime cambial, a depreciao nominal de 9.7% que o Metical registou em 2012 face ao Dlar americano pode ser encarada como um ajuste que o mercado efectuou a nossa competitividade externa, esperando-se que os exportadores faam a sua parte, brindando a nossa balana de pagamentos com melhorias efectivas nas quantidades exportadas. Relativamente ao Rand, o Metical mostrou-se mais estvel (variao praticamente nula), numa conjuntura em que a moeda sul-africana, devido  sua maior integrao na economia internacional, registou flutuaes expressivas em relao ao Dlar americano, sem descurar outros factores, como a tendncia internacional dos preos dos metais preciosos que a frica do Sul produz e exporta e as prolongadas greves que afligiram o seu sector mineiro. Apesar da crise econmica e financeira que o mundo atravessa, Moambique vem-se tornando nos ltimos anos, num destino privilegiado do investimento directo estrangeiro em frica e no mundo, particularmente no sector dos recursos naturais. Este investimento, na sua fase inicial, agrava o dfice da conta corrente da nossa balana de pagamentos. O investimento directo estrangeiro que representava at 2009 uma mdia 5% do PIB, ascendeu nos ltimos dois anos para cerca de 17%. Nos primeiros nove meses do corrente ano, a nossa balana de pagamentos registou uma entrada lquida de capitais sob forma de investimento directo estrangeiro, de 1.451 milhes de Dlares, mais 330 milhes que em igual perodo do ano transacto. Dados preliminares da posio externa de Moambique medida pelo saldo da conta corrente, mostra uma deteriorao em 70%, para 1.802 milhes de Dlares, comparativamente ao perodo homlogo de 2011, explicado, essencialmente, pelo aumento da demanda de servios especializados pelos projectos de investimento directo estrangeiro. Retirando o efeito destes projectos, o dfice da conta corrente regista um aumento menos pronunciado, em 36%, para 1.492 milhes de Dlares. O agravamento do dfice foi parcialmente atenuado pela melhoria do saldo da conta de bens em resultado do aumento das exportaes em 9.5% nos primeiros nove meses do ano, para um total de 2.602 milhes de Dlares, onde pontificaram as receitas de exportao de carvo mineral com um valor de 313 milhes, que passaram a ocupar a segunda posio no conjunto das exportaes moambicanas, depois do alumnio. Por seu turno, as importaes totais cresceram em 5.1%, para 4.263 milhes de Dlares, dos quais, 1.283 milhes realizadas pelos grandes projectos. O Pas constituiu reservas internacionais lquidas no montante de 306 milhes de Dlares, para um saldo de 2.546 milhes, de acordo com dados preliminares reportados a 14 de Dezembro de 2012, que equivale a cerca de 5.6 meses de cobertura de importaes de bens e servios no factoriais. As nossas intervenes no Mercado Cambial Interbancrio traduziram-se em vendas brutas de 625 milhes de Dlares at 14 de Dezembro de 2012, dos quais, parte significativa se destinou a apoiar a liquidao da factura de combustveis lquidos. Distintos Convidados Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores A nvel do sector financeiro, continuamos no ano em revista a implementar aces visando incentivar o aumento e a diversificao de instituies financeiras que operam no Pas, bem assim o alargamento e abrangncia dos servios prestados. Contrariamente ao que est a ocorrer em outros pases, assistimos  entrada no nosso sistema financeiro de novos operadores, bem assim  realizao de investimentos de expanso geogrfica e de modernizao, demonstrativo da solidez e estabilidade do sector. Com efeito, assinalmos, em 2012, a entrada de 19 novas instituies de microcrdito, a abertura de 39 novos balces de bancos, para um total de 479 em funcionamento em 2012, cobrindo todas as capitais provinciais, municpios e 62 dos 128 distritos, ou seja, mais 4 em relao a 2011. Ainda que reconheamos e saudemos o esforo realizado pelas instituies de crdito neste domnio, no restam dvidas que muito h por realizar, pois a demanda de servios financeiros pela nossa populao,  inadivel, impondo-se a necessidade de expanso para mais lugares do nosso vasto territrio, onde as populaes produzem riqueza e carecem do apoio da banca, quer para o depsito das suas poupanas, quer para o investimento. O sistema financeiro moambicano tem mostrado um grau de resilincia aos efeitos indirectos da crise financeira internacional, a medir pela robustez do rcio de solvabilidade que at Setembro de  se situou em 19.1%, muito acima do mnimo estabelecido pelo critrio de Basileia I, enquanto o rcio do crdito malparado regrediu para menos de 4% em Setembro. Na esteira do nosso cometimento com a solidez do sector financeiro moambicano, emitimos o Aviso n 03/GBM/2012, de 28 de Novembro, que orienta as instituies sobre a migrao para os critrios de Basileia II. Neste contexto, a partir de 1 de Janeiro de  um rduo trabalho nos aguarda para iniciarmos adopo simultnea dos critrios de Basileia I e II, preparando as nossas instituies para a transio para os termos de Basileia II, a partir de 1 de Janeiro de 2014.  semelhana do que sucedeu com os outros pases, a migrao para Basileia II ir impr a necessidade de reforo de capitais mnimos, o que vai exigir das nossas instituies a adopo de metodologias adequadas para o clculo dos requisitos de capitais, seja para a cobertura do risco de crdito, como para a incorporao de novos riscos, nomeadamente, o risco operacional e o risco de mercado. Por seu turno, a modernizao do nosso sistema nacional de pagamentos  um objectivo estratgico da nossa actuao como Banco Central. A plataforma informtica da Sociedade Interbancria de Servios (SIMO) encontra-se j instalada e pronta para a ligao dos bancos  SIMOrede. A ligao, em regime piloto, dos primeiros ATM's e POS's em Setembro ltimo, no quadro da operacionalizao da SIMO, constituiu um importante passo rumo  materializao deste objectivo. Com base no critrio de nmero de ATMs, o nmero de instituies em produtivo e em fase avanada de testes de integrao  SIMOrede representam j cerca de 50% do mercado. Aproveito esta ocasio para felicitar os bancos que esto na vanguarda deste processo, pelo seu cometimento efectivo e dou tambm nota positiva aos esforos empreendidos, encorajando a todos os demais bancos do sistema a seguirem esta marcha irreversvel, rumo a uma rede plenamente integrada que traga ganhos de eficincia e economias de escala para os utilizadores dos servios de intermediao financeira, razo de ser deste projecto. O elevado grau de penetrao do telemvel criou no Pas, uma oportunidade para as instituies de crdito fornecerem produtos financeiros com recurso a tecnologia dos provedores de servios de telefonia mvel. O sistema financeiro conta desde 2011 com uma instituio que opera com recurso  rede de telefonia mvel. Na sequncia, assistimos em 2012, a introduo de novos produtos e servios financeiros acedidos por via do telemvel. Estas e outras solues que vem sendo implementadas constituem um ptimo contributo das instituies que operam no pas para a dinamizao da nossa estratgia de incluso financeira, ao assegurar um rpido acesso dos servios financeiros para uma vasta camada da nossa populao, o que impe novos desafios em matria de regulamentao deste tipo de servios. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores, As perspectivas econmicas para 2013 apontam para a prevalncia de uma conjuntura internacional adversa e incerta, sobretudo ao nvel das economias mais avanadas, onde se espera um abrandamento do ritmo de expanso da actividade econmica acompanhada de aumento do desemprego. A incerteza quanto ao fim da crise de dvida soberana na Zona Euro requer monitoria permanente para afastar os perigos do efeito contgio no nosso sistema financeiro. Perspectivas e Programa Monetrio 2013 Perspectivas e Programa Monetrio 2013 Em 2013, a manuteno dos ganhos de estabilidade macroeconmica e do sector financeiro continuar a ser o nosso principal objectivo. Neste contexto, a nossa actuao ser orientada a contribuir para os objectivos finais de poltica econmica estabelecidos pelo Governo, que prevm uma inflao anual de 7.%, um crescimento real do PIB de 8,4% e uma acumulao de reservas internacionais que permita a cobertura de pelo menos 3,8 meses de cobertura de importaes de bens e servios no factoriais. Para tanto, o Banco de Moambique continuar a privilegiar o uso dos instrumentos disponveis nos mercados monetrio e cambial, complementados com a superviso prudencial, visando assegurar uma expanso dos meios totais de pagamento (M3) em redor de 19.3% e do crdito bancrio ao sector privado em redor de 19.0%. A base monetria, nossa varivel operacional, dever ter um crescimento no superior a 18.4%. Adicionalmente e no seguimento das aces j iniciadas nos ltimos anos, temos previstas para 2013 as seguintes aces de carcter estrutural:  Continuar a melhorar a gesto da poltica monetria, reforando a nossa capacidade de previso e de resposta;  Continuar a fortalecer o nosso papel de supervisor e regulador das instituies de crdito, liderando a transio para os critrios de Basileia II;  Em parceria com as instituies de crdito, prosseguir o esforo de bancarizao da economia nacional, a modernizao do sistema nacional de pagamentos e a busca de prerios dos servios financeiros, mais competitivos e transparentes;  Continuar a adoptar posturas de prudncia e de diversificao da aplicao das nossas reservas internacionais tendo em vista reduzir os riscos; v. Em colaborao com outras instituies e organismos, continuar a estimular a expanso dos servios financeiros com recurso  novas tecnologias, visando acelerar a incluso financeira no pas. Distintos Convidados Desafios Moambique est a conhecer profundas transformaes estruturais induzidas pela descoberta e incio da explorao de recursos naturais no renovveis. Este facto coloca novos desafios  gesto macroeconmica em geral e s polticas acometidas ao Banco Central, em particular. 0 Banco de Moambique reafirma o seu cometimento em adoptar uma poltica monetria flexvel para garantir a consolidao da estabilidade macroeconmica e do sector financeiro, num ambiente de esperado incremento do investimento e exportaes, salvaguardando o desenvolvimento equilibrado dos vrios sectores da economia e a competitividade externa. 0 novo ciclo do nosso desenvolvimento exige maior empoderamento das nossas instituies para liderarem o processo de explorao de recursos naturais, em defesa do interesse nacional e das futuras geraes, calibrando, se necessrio, as nossas polticas, para que elas exeram mais eficazmente o papel que delas se espera na agenda nacional pelo desenvolvimento. 0 Banco de Moambique, em coordenao com o Governo e com o sector privado, continuar a desenvolver esforos com o intuito de criar condies que assegurem um maior acesso ao crdito por parte das pequenas e mdias empresas e outros segmentos da populao no bancarizados. Estes desafios esto consagrados na proposta de Estratgia de Desenvolvimento do Sector Financeiro, que demanda a preparao de uma Estratgia especfica para a Incluso Financeira. Para o efeito, a nvel do Banco de Moambique foi criado um grupo de trabalho para assegurar a implementao dos aspectos inerentes a este objectivo, incluindo a preparao de uma proposta de regulamentao sobre a banca electrnica, o acesso e uso de servios financeiros mveis, bem como a preparao de indicadores para a mensurao e acompanhamento da incluso financeira no pas. Adicionalmente, a nossa instituio continuar a prestar ateno s aces de promoo da educao financeira, no mbito da proteco do consumidor financeiro. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores A 31 de Dezembro terminar o curso legal e o valor liberatrio ilimitado e pleno das notas e moedas das duas primeiras famlias, designadamente a famlia Repblica Popular de Moambique e a famlia Repblica de Moambique. Aproveito este palco privilegiado para apelar a todos os que tenham estas denominaes para proceder ao seu depsito nos estabelecimentos bancrios ou  troca nas filiais do Banco de Moambique, evitando deste modo a perca de activos que deixaro de ter valor a partir de 01 de Janeiro de 2013. Renovo as nossas saudaes aos agentes econmicos e  sociedade em geral que com seu esforo abnegado tm contribudo para o desenvolvimento econmico do pas, dando substncia aos esforos do Governo e da autoridade monetria. Quero ainda reiterar o meu apreo a todos os gestores e tcnicos do Banco de Moambique cuja devoo ao trabalho tornaram possveis os resultados alcanados pela nossa instituio em 2012. Termino agradecendo a todos os presentes pela honrosa presena nesta cerimnia de balano do exerccio econmico prestes a findar. Resta-me desejar a todos os presentes e vossas estimadas famlias, aos quadros e colaboradores do Banco de Moambique e do sector financeiro e suas famlias, votos de Festas Felizes e um Prspero Ano Novo.
