Title: Intervention at the Negcios Conference
text: THE ROLE OF MONETARY POLICY IN ENCOURAGING BANK CREDIT Dr. Ant97nio Pinto de Abreu - Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique Mr Deputy Minister for Industry and Trade, Excellency, National Directors and senior management of the Government, Distinguished Panel Members, Ladies and Gentlemen, First of all, I would like to thank the invitation given to us to participate in this important forum and to welcome, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, to the organizers of this event, for the initiative and honour they grant us to share with us our vision of the role of monetary policy in encouraging bank credit in Mozambique. Although the chosen theme may generate increased expectations among those present, due to the nature of the participants in this event and given the functions of the Institute for the Promotion of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises, it is humbly important to recognize that the relationship between Monetary Policy and Credit to the Economy is not always evident so easily - that is, the relationship between monetary policy and the volume and distribution of credit to the economy. At the theoretical level and in view of the prevailing economic model in Mozambique, monetary policy is the set of measures and actions carried out by the authorities for macroeconomic objectives, generally a level of prices or inflation; however, while the volume of credit to the economy can mirror the direct or indirect effects of monetary policy, the distribution (sectoral, territorial or population) of credit to the economy tends to respond better to micro-economic and fiscal aspects, to issues of choice or individual decision-making by the economic actors involved in the face of the constraints they face and to the incentives that may actually be in place Gifts. In direct control regimes, the volume of credit to the economy is determined a priori as a goal, as a limit, as a ceiling that cannot be transposed in the course of a previously established time. In indirect control regimes - as a rule using the operations of interbank markets - the volume of credit to the economy emerges as an ex post result of the implementation of a given policy. In the first case - that of quantitative credit limits - the monetary authority may even go into the detail of establishing credit cards by sectors of activity or for sectors considered as priorities. In the second case, such detail is simply impossible, since the claim is not determined ex ante, arising only a posteriori, as a result of the effects of the policy instruments that have been handled. Experience teaches that the use of credit limits always result - sooner or later , depending on the elasticity of each economy - in a maze of increasing inefficiency, because it represents a dismay to the initiative of economic operators by deholding them from their role as micro-economic decision-makers, and therefore it is not recommended to take their adoption for long periods of time, unless in well-delimited moments of adjustment or readjustment of the economy or even when it is advisable to cause a focused shock. In the case of Mozambique, we have had the privilege of knowing extensively in practice the two monetary policy approaches to which I referred - that of the setting and administration of credit limits to the economy, with selective sectoral credit plafonds, which was in effective use until the mid-1990s and extended to the year 2000; that of indirect action, with the use of interventions by the monetary authority through operations in interbank markets, which has been applied since 2001 and benefiting from successive improvements as the complexity of our economy grows and the capacity of the resources used in the Bank of Mozambique is strengthened. In any case, in mind the factors I described before as to the complexity of the main subject of the dissertation that is expected today from the Bank of Mozambique, I think that we would reduce the richness of the theme if we were limited only to the role of monetary policy per se - because it itself may face restrictions in an attempt to generate a desired impact on the volume and distribution of credit to the economy - which is why we add the issue to the the role of the central bank in encouraging credit to the economy, in order to capture and exploit the other tools available to the monetary authority - and indeed has - in pursuing the objective of adequate financing of the economy, in achieving its role as an entity that ultimately ensures the efficiency of financial intermediation. This conference comes at a time when the global economic and financial environment remains uncertain and a number to be taken into account by financial institutions in other geographical areas remain in a situation of turbulence or inactivity, despite the gradual return of the main financial markets to normality. However, in Mozambique, there is a great change in the economic and productive structure, induced by large investments and the beginning of the exploration of mineral resources, with emphasis on coal and gas. In the face of this reality, new opportunities arise and new demands are imposed on economic agents - both the State and the private sector and families - so this meeting is another opportune space for us to exchange ideas about the role to be played by the various actors at this important stage of our economy, which certainly makes this occasion of sublime importance for each of the institutions properly represented here. Ladies Gentlemen The Constitution of Mozambique enshrines to our institution the role of Central Bank of the Republic, which has the legal cover to act as a monetary authority, as a regulatory authority and supervisor of the financial system, as a foreign exchange authority and as an authority of the national payment system. The main objective of a law established for the Bank of Mozambique is to preserve the value of the national currency, understood as achieving low and controllable inflation levels, in an environment of exchange rate stability and stability in the functioning of the national financial system. In our action, we recognise that with low and persistent inflation at controllable levels, we create conditions for us to have more attractive interest rates in the country, an indispensable condition for the promotion of financial savings, and consequently the increase in the volume of resources available for bank financing to the private sector, as well as we believe that realistic interest rates at appropriate levels also make projects more competitive, more profitable, more banitable, and thus ensures the stimulus to productive investment. On the other hand, a monetary policy oriented towards low inflation promotes greater efficiency in the allocation and distribution of income in the economy, in addition to contributing to the fight against poverty, either by increasing investment or by protecting the purchasing power of the less favoured people. In other words, we assume that low inflation reflecting macroeconomic stability is a fundamental condition for fostering a favorable environment for the flourishing of economic activity, it is an incentive to establish lasting and profitable businesses. In this area, we have led policies that have allowed inflation to be between 6 and 8% in the last five years, with a higher level of between 12 and 17% in 2010, and the lowest level converging to 2% in 2012. It should be recalled that in that period it was only in one year that we recorded a low inflation of the year to double digits, or above 10%, precisely in 2010. However, in terms of average annual inflation, it was above 10% in 2008, 2010 and 2011, which shows how difficult it has been to ensure low and controllable inflation levels in the medium term. The causes of inflation have been explained in a timely manner by the Bank of Mozambique, through the communiqu8es of its Monetary Policy Committee, through its periodic reports and the public interventions of its representatives, and in particular his Excellency the Governor of the Bank, who is, by law, the sole responsibility of announcing monetary policy measures. Inflation in Mozambique is sensitive to the availability of food, is sensitive to changes in the exchange rates of the dollar and the rand, is sensitive to psychological factors among economic agents and the normal functioning of the economy and society. In the same 5-year period that we took merely as a reference, the currency and foreign exchange markets generally behaved in a stable manner, with an average annual exchange rate variation of around 5% and interest rates for active operations for the highest risk credits for a year, which exceeded 32% ten years ago, have fallen successively to current levels of around 20%, with the prime rate exceeding 25%, now well below 20%. EXCELLENCIES LADIES LADIES AND GENTLEMEN In a country that experiences development stages similar to those of Mozambique, we have to accept that the availability of financing to the economy does not automatically result from the manipulation of classic monetary policy instruments. There are structural factors to be taken into account and of great importance in achieving the noble objective of financial intermediation, such as the availability of financial institutions and products and services in the national territory, with economic actors and appropriate to the different sectors of activity. Aware of the need to undertake a new dynamic for the National Financial System and to adjust the monetary policy framework to the legal and institutional changes introduced in the late 1980s, the Bank of Mozambique has been undertaking a series of structural reforms, promoting the adequacy of legislation with a view to opening up the financial market to domestic and foreign private investors, to provide a favourable environment for the development of diversified products and services and to encourage the expansion of counters and financial services to rural areas. The results are visible and consolidated year after year: the number of institutions operating in the country, evolved from only three banks in 1992, to a total of 21 banks at present, with 529 branches or licensed branches or branches - 502 of which already in operation, covering all cities capitas, municipalities and a total of 63 districts. Just to give an idea of evolution, six years ago only 28 districts had a bank branch and Mozambique benefited from only 274 bank branches. Today, in addition to banks, we have 8 microbanks, 7 credit unions, 11 savings and loan organizations, 202 microcredit operators and 1 electronic money institution with more than 3,000 agents spread across the country. Initially the development of our financial system, was characterized by a strong tendency towards physical concentration and services provided by it in the main cities of the country. To reverse this situation, bearing in mind the idea that the financial system should cover places which, being potentially rich in terms of economic activities generating wealth and income, are not properly served from the point of view of locating banks or accessing intermediation in 2007, we launched the strategy of banking the economy, which includes a set of measures and various incentives, with the aim of promoting small finances, on the one hand, and setting banks in areas of the country with the lowest density of financial services, on the other. We are aware that bank credit plays an important role in the development of a country's business sector and no economy can survive on the fringes of banking. In fact, credit enables the acquisition of production facilities, raw materials and labor contracting, that is, it helps to cause the transformation of net capital into fixed capital or means of production. Still, we also keep in mind that policies aimed at keeping inflation low and bringing interest rates to affordable levels, or additionally ensuring the physical presence of banks where economic activity pulses, alone may not solve the problem, may not be the magic wand or the master key that opens the tap credit to the economy. There is also the question of the size of the market seen in two perspectives - on the one hand, the size of the credit market with real and capillary impact on the economy and, on the other hand, the ability of market operators to keep up with the growing needs of a rapidly developing economy. The first aspect relates to the trend towards dollarization that had proved virtually irreversible until the mid-last decade - banks preferred to do credit operations in foreign currency, thereby reducing the size of credit in national currency; economic operators with eligible projects chose to obtain credit in foreign currency allegedly because they faced lower and more predictable costs. We live years of foreign currency credit significantly surpassing domestic credit in national currency - it was the trap of dollarization taking over the balance sheets of the national bank. We had to change that. A difficult, complex process that required a lot of consultation, a lot of involvement from the private sector, the banks themselves, the presidion associations and the press itself. We had no fundamentalism against the business networks then established. We had only a duty to prevent risks, the duty to mitigate the effects of the uncertainty underlying the handling of an instrument that does not belong to us, the awareness that dollarization permanently harms small and medium-sized enterprises and ultimately favors the reproduction of established processes dominated by larger companies already experienced in dealing with the international market. It was necessary to amend the exchange law and introduce a regulation that would change the prevailing situation. Prudential measures had to be taken on credit granted in foreign currency. But it was necessary, above all, to talk to economic agents, to listen to and to address their concerns, to explain the meaning and objectives of our policy. As a result, the volume of credit in meticais has grown and is today the most important part of the internal assets of banks. With the growth of credit availability, there is also a potential reduction in interest rates. As a result, banks' propensity to specialise in foreign currency credit decreased from 42% in 2003 to 24% in 2012, as well as the percentage of banks specializing in promoting foreign currency deposit capture decreased from 33% in 2003 to 14% in 2012. In the same period, banks' capital rose considerably so that they can continue to leverage a constantly growing economy. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN The path I have set out in retrospect is only to illustrate that the Bank of Mozambique, recognizing the difficulties that national economic agents have been facing in accessing credit, has privileged at every moment the adoption of a monetary policy stance in line with with the promotion of greater growth of the national economy by reducing the costs of financial intermediation, banking of the economy, and consolidating coordination between fiscal and monetary policy. Indeed, the rate of monetisation of the economy grew from 20% in December 1999 to around 41% at the end of 2011, while the level of financial savings doubled in the same period, at the close of 2011 at 35%. Bank financing to the private sector took on the same trend, from 15% of GDP to 28% of GDP in the same period, and of the total granted by the banking system, about 75% was allocated to businesses , between small and medium- and medium-sized. In a context in which the availability and access to external financing are increasingly limited and difficult, the expansion of bank credit to the private sector has not only met the growing financing needs for the economy, but has also been instrumental in accelerating productive investment and, consequently, galvanising activity national economic economy, measured by gross domestic product, whose growth rates of the last five years exceed the 7% bar, placing the country in a narrowest group of fastest growing economies in Africa. By sectors, we continue to note that higher credit volume continues to flow to the trade (20%), transport and communications (10%) and construction (6.0%) sectors. Individuals, whose participation in the economy is also of importance, given that the increase in financing in this segment is important for stimulating consumption and consequently to the sales of companies, there has been a significant increase in the volume of financial resources from the national banking, with the final information available pointing to a weight of about 20% of the total. Despite the achievements described here in a remarkable advance towards the consolidation of the national financial system, we are aware that the challenges ahead are still enormous and will certainly be require all stakeholders to make a bold undertaking so that together we can find integrated and fruitful solutions. One of the important constraints to be highlighted on the financial sector side is the costs of financial intermediation that still remain relatively high, despite the efforts we have been making to make financial services more accessible and less costly to citizens. In this regard, it is urgent to note that there are a set of legal precepts and moral persuasion measures that the Bank of Mozambique has been favouring, with Notice No. 5/GBM/2009, which establishes the minimum services to be provided free of charge, as well as the requirements that institutions must observe in the disclosure, to the public, of commissions and other charges arising from the use of financial products and services, just one example of the measures we have been taking. The high costs of financial intermediation are justified in part by the risks that financial activity involves, especially in a society where information asymmetry and economic and social imbalances still persist. Despite the recognized role that Small and Medium Enterprises play in the development of the national economy, as an important source of job creation, income generation and in stimulating innovation and creativity, they still present structural organizational constraints that often hinder or hinder their access to credit together with financial institutions. Among several constraints I quote a few that I consider the most salient: Firstly, most small and medium-sized enterprises face the problem of decapitalisation, something that obviously apoquenta us, as a monetary authority, since companies are the foundation of our economy, an important source of state revenue and the thousands of families. I have no doubt that the solution of this problem requires a multifaceted intervention of institutions, but the main one, I believe is associativism as a way to combine synergies. Secondly, many of our companies do not have a commercial and tax register, do not have an organised accounting and have a poor history of connection with banking institutions. Additionally, they have high transaction costs and high mobility and do not present conventional collaterals. This does not help companies to increase their trust with banking due to the high asymmetry of information resulting from the lack of such information. Third, weak use of commercial contracts does not allow the maximization of the customer-supplier relationship, which can greatly contribute to the increase in transactions, without the use of bank financing. These constraints make it partly difficult for these companies to access bank financing, or to have to obtain bank financing at comparatively higher interest rates. However, thanks to the natural growth of businesses and the reforms that take place in various areas of our economy, it is worth noting the improvements that have been observed in the relationship between banking and business, the result of increasing confidence, thus contributing to the development of the national business sector, an important element in the creation of wealth and employment in the country, as well as in generating sources of income for many Mozambican families. Ladies Gentlemen Finally, I would like, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, to address our congratulations on the first anniversary of this "Journal", an unequivocal proof of our press's committing to provide diversified information in order to facilitate decision-making. Our wish is that this forum will serve not only as a means of exchanging ideas, but as a vehicle for disseminating the conclusions that will come out of this great assembly in such a way that more economic agents and society in general can have access to and reflect on the challenges ahead. Speaking at a forum in which, on the government side, the INSTITUTE for the PROMOTION OF SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES is a happy opportunity for me because, many years ago, in the first half of the 1990s, the Bank of Mozambique mobilized and directly managed financial resources from the World Bank for financing small and medium-sized enterprises, instrument which proved very useful for the reanimation of the economy after the peace agreements and for the building of a business fabric of national roots. Today the conditions are different, but the Bank of Mozambique reiterates its readiness, this time to provide the necessary collaboration for IPEME to fulfill its mission. Thank you very much Maputo, 15 April 2013
text_original: O PAPEL DA POLTICA MONETRIA NO INCENTIVO AO CRDITO BANCRIO Dr. Antnio Pinto de Abreu - Vice-Governador do Banco de Moambique Senhor Vice-Ministro da Indstria e Comrcio , Excelncia Senhores Directores Nacionais e quadros superiores do Governo, Senhores Membros do Painel Distintos Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Gostaria, em primeiro lugar, de agradecer o convite que nos foi formulado para participar neste importante frum e saudar, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, aos organizadores deste evento, pela iniciativa e pela honra que nos concedem de partilhar com os presentes a nossa viso sobre o papel da poltica monetria no incentivo ao crdito bancrio em Moambique. Muito embora o tema escolhido possa gerar acrescidas expectativas junto dos presentes, pela natureza dos participantes neste evento e dadas as funes do Instituto Para a Promoo das Pequenas e Mdias Empresas, importa humildemente reconhecer que nem sempre a relao entre a Poltica Monetria e o Crdito  Economia se evidencia assim to facilmente - ou seja, nem sempre  directa e imediatamente perceptvel a relao entre a poltica monetria e o volume e distribuio do crdito  economia. No plano terico e atendendo ao modelo econmico prevalecente em Moambique, a poltica monetria  o conjunto de medidas e aces levadas a cabo pelas autoridades visando objectivos macro-econmicos, geralmente um nvel de preos ou inflao; porm, no obstante o volume de crdito  economia puder espelhar os efeitos directos ou indirectos da poltica monetria, j a distribuio (sectorial, territorial ou populacional) do crdito  economia tende a responder melhor a aspectos de natureza micro-econmica e fiscal, a questes de escolha ou de deciso individual dos agentes econmicos intervenientes face aos constrangimentos que enfrentem e aos estmulos que possam eventualmente estar efectivamente presentes. Em regimes de controles directos, o volume de crdito  economia  determinado a priori como meta, como limite, como um tecto que no poder ser transposto no decurso de um tempo previamente estabelecido. Em regimes de controles indirectos - em regra com recurso s operaes dos mercados interbancrios - o volume de crdito  economia surge como um resultado ex post da implementao de uma determinada poltica. No primeiro caso - o dos limites quantitativos do crdito - a autoridade monetria pode at ir ao detalhe de estabelecer plafonds de crdito por sectores de actividade ou para sectores considerados prioritrios. No segundo caso, essa mincia  simplesmente impossvel, pois o crdito no se determina ex ante, surgindo apenas a posteriori, em consequncia dos efeitos dos instrumentos de poltica que tenham sido manuseados. A experincia ensina que o recurso aos limites de crdito redunda sempre - mais cedo ou mais tarde, consoante a elasticidade de cada economia - num labirinto de ineficincia crescente, pois representa um desalento  iniciativa dos agentes econmicos desresponsabilizando-os da sua funo de decisores no plano micro- econmico, no sendo por isso recomendvel a sua adopo por perodos de tempo longos, a no ser em momentos bem delimitados de ajustamento ou de reajustamento da economia ou ainda quando se queira provocar um choque focalizado. No caso de Moambique, temos tido o privilgio de conhecer vastamente na prtica os dois enfoques de poltica monetria a que me referi - o da fixao e administrao de limites de crdito  economia, com plafonds selectivos de crdito sectorial, que esteve em uso efectivo at meados da dcada de noventa e se estendeu ao ano de 2000; o da actuao por via indirecta, com recurso a intervenes da autoridade monetria por intermdio das operaes nos mercados interbancrios, que vem sendo aplicado desde 2001 e beneficiando de sucessivos aperfeioamentos a medida que cresce a complexidade da nossa economia e se refora a capacidade dos recursos empregues no Banco de Moambique. Seja como for, atento aos factores que antes descrevi quanto  complexidade do assunto principal da dissertao que se espera hoje do Banco de Moambique, julgo que diminuiramos a riqueza da temtica se nos circunscrevssemos apenas ao papel da poltica monetria per si - pois ela em si pode enfrentar restries na tentativa de gerar um impacto desejado sobre o volume e a distribuio do crdito  economia - convindo por isso que alarguemos o tema ao papel do banco central no incentivo ao crdito  economia, por forma a captar e explorar assim as demais ferramentas de que a autoridade monetria pode dispor - e de facto dispe - na prossecuo do objectivo de um adequado financiamento  economia, na consecuo do seu papel de entidade que zela, em ltima instncia, pela eficincia da intermediao financeira. Esta conferncia ocorre numa altura em que a conjuntura econmico- financeira global ainda permanece incerta e um nmero a ter em conta de instituies financeiras de outros espaos geogrficos continua em situao de turbulncia ou inactividade, apesar do retorno gradual dos principais mercados financeiros  normalidade. No entanto, em Moambique, assiste-se a uma grande mudana na estrutura econmica e produtiva, induzida pelos grandes investimentos e incio da explorao de recursos minerais, com destaque para o carvo e o gs. Perante esta realidade, novas oportunidades surgem e novas exigncias se impem aos agentes econmicos - quer ao Estado quer ao sector privado e s famlias - pelo que, o presente encontro constitui mais um espao oportuno para trocarmos ideias sobre o papel a ser desempenhado pelos diversos intervenientes nesta fase importante da nossa economia, o que, certamente, torna esta ocasio de importncia sublime para cada uma das instituies aqui condignamente representadas. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores, A Constituio de Moambique consagra  nossa instituio o papel de Banco Central da Repblica, que tem a cobertura legal para actuar como autoridade monetria, como autoridade reguladora e supervisora do sistema financeiro, como autoridade cambial e como autoridade do sistema nacional de pagamentos. O objectivo principal de lei estabelecido para o Banco de Moambique,  o da preservao do valor da moeda nacional, entendida como a consecuo de nveis de inflao baixos e controlveis, num ambiente de estabilidade cambial e de estabilidade no funcionamento do sistema financeiro nacional. Na nossa actuao, reconhecemos que com inflao baixa e persistente em nveis controlveis, criam-se condies para que tenhamos no pas, taxas de juro mais atractivas, condio indispensvel para a promoo da poupana financeira, e consequentemente o aumento do volume de recursos disponveis para o financiamento bancrio ao sector privado, assim como entendemos que taxas de juro realistas em nveis adequados tornam tambm os projectos mais competitivos, mais rentveis, mais bancveis, e deste modo, se assegura o estmulo ao investimento produtivo. Por outro lado, uma poltica monetria orientada para inflao baixa, promove uma maior eficincia na alocao e distribuio do rendimento na economia, para alm, de contribuir para o combate a pobreza, seja por via do aumento do investimento como pela proteco do poder de compra das pessoas menos favorecidas. Dito por outras palavras, assumimos que uma inflao baixa reflectindo estabilidade macroeconmica  condio fundamental para propiciar um ambiente favorvel ao florescimento da actividade econmica,  um incentivo ao estabelecimento de negcios duradouros e rentveis. Neste domnio, conduzimos polticas que permitiram que nos ltimos cinco anos a inflao se situasse, em termos mdios anuais, entre 6 e 8%, com um nvel mais alto entre 12 e 17% em 2010, e o nvel mais baixo convergindo para 2% em 2012. De recordar que nesse perodo foi apenas num ano que registamos uma inflao de dim de ano a dois dgitos, ou seja acima de 10%, precisamente em 2010. Todavia, em termos de inflao mdia anual, ela foi superior a 10% em 2008, em 2010 e em 2011, o que revela quo difcil tem sido assegurar, a mdio prazo, nveis de inflao baixa e controlvel. As causas da inflao tm sido explanadas tempestivamente pelo Banco de Moambique, atravs dos comunicados do seu Comit de Poltica Monetria, atravs dos seus relatrios peridicos e das intervenes pblicas dos seus representantes, e nomeadamente de Sua Excelncia o Governador do Banco, a quem cabe, por lei, a responsabilidade exclusiva de anunciar medidas de poltica monetria. A inflao em Moambique  sensvel  disponibilidade de bens alimentares,  sensvel s variaes das taxas de cmbio do dlar e do rand,  sensvel a factores psicolgicos junto dos agentes econmicos e ao funcionamento normal da economia e da sociedade. No mesmo perodo de 5 anos que tomamos meramente como referncia, a moeda e os mercados cambiais comportaram-se em geral de forma estvel, com uma variao cambial mdia anual em torno de 5% e as taxas de juro de operaes activas para os crditos de maior risco a um ano, que superavam os 32% h dez anos atrs, caram sucessivamente para nveis actuais em torno de 20%, com a prime rate, que era superior a 25%, situando-se agora bem abaixo dos 20%. EXCELNCIAS MINHAS SENHORAS MEUS SENHORES Num pas que experimente estgios de desenvolvimento semelhantes aos de Moambique, temos que aceitar que a disponibilidade de financiamento  economia no resulta automaticamente da manipulao dos instrumentos clssicos de poltica monetria. Existem factores estruturais a ter em conta e de grande relevo para a consecuo do objectivo nobre da intermediao financeira, como por exemplo, a disponibilidade de instituies e de produtos e servios financeiros no territrio nacional, junto dos agentes econmicos e adequados aos diferentes sectores de actividade. Ciente da necessidade de empreender uma nova dinmica ao Sistema Financeiro Nacional e de ajustar o quadro da poltica monetria s transformaes jurdico-institucionais introduzidas em finais dos anos 80, o Banco de Moambique vem encetando um conjunto de reformas estruturais, promovendo a adequao da legislao com vista a abrir- se o mercado financeiro a investidores privados nacionais e estrangeiras, a proporcionar um ambiente favorvel ao desenvolvimento de produtos e servios diversificados e a incentivar a expanso dos balces e dos servios financeiros s zonas rurais. Os resultados so visveis e consolidam-se ano aps ano: o nmero de instituies a operar no pas, evoluiu de apenas trs bancos em 1992, para um total de 21 bancos presentemente, com 529 agncias ou balces licenciados - 502 dos quais j em operao, cobrindo todas as cidades capitas, municpios e um total de 63 distritos. S para dar uma ideia de evoluo, h seis anos atrs apenas 28 distritos tinham agncia bancria e Moambique beneficiava de somente 274 balces de bancos. Hoje, para alm de bancos, temos 8 microbancos, 7 cooperativas de crdito, 11 organizaes de poupana e emprstimo, 202 operadores de microcrdito e 1 instituio de moeda electrnica com mais de 3.000 agentes espalhados pelo pas. Inicialmente o desenvolvimento do nosso sistema financeiro, vinha-se caracterizando por uma forte tendncia para a concentrao fsica e dos servios por este prestados nas principais cidades do pas. Para inverter esta situao, tendo presente a ideia de que o sistema financeiro deve abranger os locais que, sendo potencialmente ricos em termos de actividades econmicas geradoras de riqueza e rendimentos, no esto devidamente servidos do ponto de vista de localizao de bancos ou acesso  intermediao financeira, lanmos, em 2007, a estratgia de bancarizao da economia, que contempla um conjunto de medidas e diversos incentivos, com o intuito de promover as pequenas finanas, por um lado, e a fixao de bancos nas zonas do pas com menor densidade de servios financeiros, por outro. Temos a conscincia de que o crdito bancrio desempenha um papel importante no desenvolvimento do sector empresarial de um pas e nenhuma economia pode sobreviver  margem da banca. Na verdade, o crdito possibilita a aquisio de meios de produo, matrias-primas e contratao de mo-de-obra, ou seja, ajuda a provocar a transformao do capital lquido em capital fixo ou meios de produo. Ainda assim, temos tambm presente, que polticas tendentes a manter a inflao baixa e a trazer as taxas de juro para nveis comportveis, ou a adicionalmente assegurar a presena fsica dos bancos onde pulse a actividade econmica, por si ss podem no resolver o problema, podem no ser a varinha mgica ou a chave mestra que abra a torneira do crdito  economia. Coloca-se tambm a questo da dimenso do mercado encarada em duas perspectivas - por um lado, o tamanho do mercado de crdito com impacto real e capilar para a economia e, por outro lado, a capacidade dos operadores do mercado acompanharem as necessidades crescentes duma economia em franco desenvolvimento. O primeiro aspecto prende-se com a tendncia  dolarizao que se tinha mostrado praticamente irreversvel at meados da dcada passada - os bancos preferiam fazer operaes de crdito em moeda estrangeira, diminuindo assim o tamanho do crdito em moeda nacional; os agentes econmicos com projectos elegveis, optavam por obter crdito em moeda estrangeira alegadamente por enfrentarem custos mais baixos e mais previsveis. Vivemos anos de crdito em moeda estrangeira superando significativamente o crdito interno em moeda nacional - era a armadilha da dolarizao tomando conta dos balanos da banca nacional. Foi preciso mudar isso. Um processo difcil, complexo, que exigiu muita consulta, muito envolvimento do sector privado, dos prprios bancos, das associaes em presidiais e da prpria imprensa. No tnhamos nenhum fundamentalismo contra as redes de negcio ento estabelecidas. Tnhamos apenas o dever de prevenir riscos, o dever de mitigar os efeitos da incerteza subjacente ao manuseio de um instrumento que no nos pertence, a conscincia de que a dolarizao prejudica permanentemente as pequenas e mdias empresas e favorece em ultima instncia a reproduo dos processos j estabelecidos dominados pelas empresas de maior porte j experientes em lidar com o mercado internacional. Foi preciso alterar a lei cambial e introduzir um regulamento que mudasse a situao prevalecente. Foi preciso adoptar medidas prudenciais sobre o crdito concedido em moeda estrangeira. Mas foi preciso, acima de tudo, falar com os agentes econmicos, escutar e atender as suas preocupaes, explicar o sentido e os objectivos da nossa poltica. Como resultado, o volume de crdito em meticais cresceu e constitui hoje a parte mais importante do activo interno dos bancos. Com o crescimento da disponibilidade de crdito concorre-se tambm para a desejada reduo das taxas de juro. Como resultado ainda, a propenso dos bancos em se especializarem no crdito em moeda estrangeira, reduziu de 42% em 2003 para 24% em 2012, assim como a percentagem de bancos especializados em promover a captao de depsitos em moeda estrangeira reduziu de 33% em 2003 para 14% em 2012. No mesmo perodo, o capital dos bancos subiu consideravelmente para que possam continuar a alavancar uma economia em crescimento constante. MINHAS SENHORAS MEUS SENHORES O percurso que tracei em retrospectiva visa apenas ilustrar que o Banco de Moambique, reconhecendo as dificuldades por que os agentes econmicos nacionais tm vindo a enfrentar no acesso ao crdito, tem privilegiado a, cada momento, a adopo de uma postura de poltica monetria consentnea com a promoo de um maior crescimento da economia nacional atravs da reduo dos custos de intermediao financeira, bancarizao da economia, e consolidao da coordenao entre a poltica fiscal e monetria. Com efeito, o grau de monetizao da economia cresceu de 20% em Dezembro de 1999 para cerca de 41% no final de 2011, enquanto o nvel de poupana financeira duplicou no mesmo perodo, situando-se no fecho de 2011 em 35%. O financiamento bancrio ao sector privado, assumiu a mesma tendncia, tendo passado de 15% do PIB para 28% do PIB no mesmo perodo, sendo que do total concedido pelo sistema bancrio, cerca de 75% destinou-se s empresas, entre pequenas e mdias. Perante um contexto em que a disponibilidade e o acesso ao financiamento externo so cada vez mais exguas e difceis, a expanso do crdito bancrio ao sector privado permitiu, no apenas, preencher as necessidades crescentes de financiamento  economia, mas tambm, foi determinante para acelerar o investimento produtivo e consequentemente, galvanizar a actividade econmica nacional, medida pelo Produto Interno Bruto, cujas taxas de crescimento dos ltimos cinco anos superam a fasquia dos 7%, posicionando o pas num grupo restrito de economias que mais crescem em frica. Por sectores, continuamos a notar que maior volume de crdito continua a fluir para os sectores de comrcio (20%), transportes e comunicaes (10%) e construo (6,0%). Aos particulares, cuja participao na economia  tambm de relevo, dado que o aumento do financiamento a este segmento  importante para o estmulo ao consumo e consequentemente s vendas das empresas, tem vindo a conhecer-se um acrscimo significativo no volume de recursos financeiros provenientes da banca nacional, com a informao final disponvel a apontar para um peso de cerca de 20% do total. No obstante os feitos ora descritos constiturem um notvel avano rumo  consolidao do sistema financeiro nacional, estamos cientes de que os desafios pela frente, ainda so enormes e certamente iro exigir de todos os stakeholders um cometimento arrojado para que junto, possamos encontrar solues integradas e profcuas. Um dos constrangimentos importantes a realar do lado do sector financeiro prende-se com os custos de intermediao financeira que ainda permanecem relativamente elevados, apesar dos esforos que temos vindo a envidar no sentido de tornar os servios financeiros mais acessveis e menos onerosos aos cidados. A este respeito, urge referir que h um conjunto de preceitos legais e medidas de persuaso moral que o Banco de Moambique tem estado a privilegiar, sendo o Aviso n 5/GBM/2009, que estabelece os servios mnimos a serem prestados gratuitamente, bem como os requisitos que as instituies devem observar na divulgao, ao pblico, das comisses e demais encargos decorrentes da utilizao de produtos e servios financeiros, apenas um exemplo das medidas que temos vindo a adoptar. Os elevados custos de intermediao financeira, encontram justificao, em parte, pelos riscos que a actividade financeira envolve, sobretudo numa sociedade em que a assimetria de informao e os desequilbrios econmicos e sociais, ainda persistem. Apesar do reconhecido papel que as Pequenas e Mdias Empresas jogam no desenvolvimento da economia nacional, como importante fonte de criao de emprego, gerao de rendimentos e no estmulo  inovao e criatividades, estas ainda apresentam constrangimentos organizacionais estruturais que muitas vezes, emperram ou dificultam o seu acesso ao crdito juntos das instituies financeiras. De entre vrios constrangimentos passo a citar alguns que considero os mais salientes: Primeiro: a generalidade das pequenas e mdias empresas enfrentam o problema da descapitalizao, algo que obviamente nos apoquenta, enquanto autoridade monetria, dado que as empresas so o alicerce da nossa economia, uma importante fonte de receitas do Estado e o sustento de milhares de famlias. No tenho dvidas que a soluo deste problema requer uma interveno multifacetada de instituies, mas a principal, acredito passa pelo associativismo como forma de juntar sinergias. Segundo: muitas das nossas empresas no tm um registo comercial e fiscal, no apresentam uma contabilidade organizada e tm um histrico fraco de ligao com as instituies bancrias. Adicionalmente, apresentam elevados custos de transaco e elevada mobilidade e no apresentam colaterais convencionais. Este facto no ajuda as empresas a aumentar a sua confiana junto da banca, devido  elevada assimetria de informao que resulta da falta destas informaes. Terceiro: fraco uso de contratos comerciais no permite a maximizao da relao cliente-fornecedor, o que em muito pode concorrer para o aumento das transaces, sem o recurso ao financiamento bancrio. Estes constrangimentos dificultam em parte o acesso ao financiamento bancrio por parte destas empresas, ou ento a terem que obter financiamento bancrio a taxas de juro comparativamente mais altas. No entanto, merc do crescimento natural das empresas e das reformas que tm lugar em vrios domnios da nossa economia,  de se assinalar as melhorias que tm vindo a ser observadas na relao entre a banca e as empresas, fruto de uma confiana cada vez crescente, contribuindo deste modo para o desenvolvimento do sector empresarial nacional, elemento importante na criao de riqueza e emprego no pas, bem assim, na gerao de fontes de rendimentos para muitas famlias moambicana. Minhas Senhoras Meus Senhores Para terminar, gostaria de, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, enderear os nossos parabns pelo primeiro aniversrio deste Jornal, uma prova inequvoca do cometimento que a nossa imprensa tem em prover informao diversificada de modo a facilitar a tomada de deciso. O nosso anseio  de que este frum sirva no apenas como uma meio de troca de ideias, mas sim como um veculo para disseminao das concluses que sairo desta magna assembleia de tal sorte que mais agentes que econmicos e a sociedade em geral, possam ter acesso e reflectir em torno dos desafios que se colocam pela frente. Dissertar num frum em que do lado do Governo pontifica na sua organizao o INSTITUTO PARA A PROMOO DAS PEQUENAS E MDIAS EMPRESAS  para mim uma feliz oportunidade uma vez que, h muitos muitos anos, na primeira metade da dcada de noventa, o Banco de Moambique mobilizou e geriu directamente recursos financeiros provenientes do Banco Mundial para financiamento s pequenas e mdias empresas, instrumento que se revelou bastante til para a reanimao da economia aps os acordos de paz e para a edificao de um tecido empresarial de razes nacionais. Hoje as condies so outras, mas o Banco de Moambique reitera a sua disponibilidade, desta vez para prestar a necessria colaborao para que o IPEME cumpra com a sua misso. Muito obrigado Maputo, 15 de Abril de 2013

Title: V Scientific Days
text: Members of the Council of Ministers, Excellencies Mr Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency Mr. Tomaz Salomao, Former Executive Secretary of SADC, Excellency, Ladies And Gentlemen of the Bank of Mozambique; Representatives of Government Institutions, Financial Institutions, Academic Institutions and Research Centres; Dear Directors, Managers and Technicians of the Bank of Mozambique; Different representatives of the Media; Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen I would first like, on behalf of the Board of Directors and on my own behalf, to address all welcome greetings to the 5th Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique. It is an honour for us to welcome you to this annual forum that we take to work together to reflect, in an open and frank way, on issues of economic and financial interest for our country and for our institution. Your presence at this meeting testifies once again to the wide interest of this event with our partners, academics, researchers and the general public, in contributing ideas and knowing about issues of recognized relevance to the Bank of Mozambique, within the framework of its functions, as Central Bank of our country. Allow me to address a special greeting to Dr. Tomaz Salomao, a figure recognised for his experience in macroeconomic management and until very recently Executive Secretary of SADC, for accepting the invitation we have asked him to share with us his vision and thought, as the keynote speaker of the central theme we have selected for these Five Days - "Monetary Policy Framework in the Context of The Exploitation of Natural Resources". I am greeting the representatives of government institutions, financial institutions, academic institutions and research centres who have once again agreed to join us in this forum, which honours us greatly. On this occasion, I would like to express my thanks to the President and to the other Members of the Jury of these Fifth Scientific Days, who spared no effort to fulfil their mandate with exemption, care and rigour. I congratulate all the researchers who responded to the open invitation, launched by the Bank of Mozambique, for the disinterested participation, including those whose research proposals were not selected for the final phase of the competition. We knew from the outset that the theme of these Days was complex but timely, so the various ideas, reflections and perceptions will be welcomed by us. For the work selected as a finalist and which will be presented here, i congratulate you on the delivery and dedication in your preparation, which, of course, required its authors many hours of research and consultation. Ladies Gentlemen Our country is experiencing profound structural transformations associated with the process of exploitation of non-renewable natural resources, such as coal and gas. Although in the phase of deployment investments, their impacts begin to be tangible for our economy as a whole and, in particular, for the regions where these projects are taking place. After several years of peace-building and successful reforms in several areas, macroeconomic stability and the financial sector allows the country to focus on the new cycle of its development, with renewed optimism, to be illustrated by some indicators that I will summarize:  The country has lived in the last five years with an average single-digit inflation, and in the last three it has been less than 6%, which provides optimistic expectations regarding the future of the business of our economic agents;  Investor confidence in the Mozambican economy is growing, witnessed by the raising of large sums of private investment, which in 2012 exceeded the 5 billion mark. Direct investment in the extractive industry already accounts for 30% of Mozambican GDP, according to 2012 data, compared to 5% in the period 2000 to 2008;  The export of coal started in mid-2011 experienced strong growth in 2012, which resulted in revenue collection of USD 435 million, making this ore the second position in the country's export products;  Financial transactions involving assets represented by natural resources located on Mozambican soil generated revenues for the State in the form of capital gains taxes in a significant amount;  These projects have created numerous jobs, direct and indirect, especially for young graduates, thus enabling the generation of income for thousands of Mozambican families. Our generation has in its hands the historic opportunity, with the beginning of the exploitation of natural resources, to relaunch the country's economic activity to robust levels, sustained by greater diversification of the production and export base and, in the long term, contribute to accelerate the generation of employment and income for thousands of Mozambican families, as well as reducing external dependence. In the short term, the investment associated with these ventures will continue to aggravate our current account due to the import of various machinery and equipment, as well as the contracting of specialized services. Moreover, these projects require a muscular public investment in the infrastructure and logistics of flow, which includes the provision of energy, the improvement of the network of roads, bridges, ports and railways. Indeed, our balance of payments statistics show that the current account deficit, which was 13% of GDP in 2009, increased to 36% in 2012. Even repurging the direct effect of major projects, it is clear that the traditional sectors and the State have been increasing investment levels, and a significant part has been demanding significant imports, reflecting our current account. We are, however, convinced that, in the medium and long term, our balance of payments will reverse the current deficit trend of your current account, with the flow of exports more diversified than many studies and forecasts project. We are sure that the exploitation of natural resources poses important challenges to the macroeconomic management of the country, including policies under the responsibility of the central bank. Indeed, the influx of capital injects additional currency into the domestic economy, an element to be taken into account in macro-financial programming and in the calibration of the instruments at our disposal to regulate liquidity, in close coordination with fiscal and budgetary policies and instruments. Ladies My Lords The exploitation of natural resources also involves risks associated with what various authors call the "curse of resources". However, the theoretical analysis and successful experiences show that this phenomenon can be prevented, turning the hypothetical curse into a blessing. To this do so, it is essential that macroeconomic and sectoral policies are permanently synchronized and tailored to face this type of risk. On the monetary side, the most appropriate monetary policy framework should be considered and countercyclical policy measures adopted, aware that countries such as Mozambique will continue to take as a priority investments in socio-economic infrastructure sectors, both at times of high and at times of low natural resource prices in international markets. In this context, for the correct macroeconomic management and success of monetary policy, increasing coordination with fiscal policy is indispensable. In addition, it is urgent to protect the country's competitiveness in order to avoid, among other ills, the effects of the so-called "Dutch disease", guiding our policies towards a trend of real gains in mozambique's external competitiveness in the medium and long term, even if it is not exclusive to the behavior of the exchange rate, but also of other factors such as productivity, comparatively attractive taxation and reforms that make the business environment more competitive. It seems agreed that the financial sector plays a relevant role in promoting development, through a sound and competitive financial system, in an environment of attractive interest rates that stimulate quality credit for companies to compete in the foreign market and meet domestic demand. With a stable macroeconomic environment, it is legitimate to expect from our economic agents investment prospects that they induce the various sectors of our economy to greater productivity and efficiency. It is in this context that the election by the Bank of Mozambique, for the V Scientific Days, the theme "Monetary Policy Framework in the Context of the Exploration of Natural Resources" is framed. In our view, this is a topic of great interest and timeliness and its debate allows for an interaction of various perceptions and visions that will certainly be taken into account in the formulation and implementation of our policies. Under the Constitution of the Republic, the Bank of Mozambique is the central bank. The main mission assigned to it by the respective Organic Law is to preserve the value of the national currency and promote a solid and efficient national financial sector in an environment of low and controlled inflation. Only with low inflation can we have an environment conducive to savings, investment and expectations of more attractive interest rates. Low, controlled inflation serves the interests of society as a whole, especially the lower-income social groups. It is in this way that our macroeconomic policies have been oriented. The new cycle of economic development that the country starts will impose profound changes in the fabric, structure and dynamics of the various sectors of activity, and it is therefore important, where necessary, to adjust the framework of our policies. The risks and increasing unpredictability of the international environment lead us to be prudent in the profile of our policies, strengthening the supervisory and stability mechanisms of the financial sector, as well as the necessary safeguards for our national payment system, which is increasingly integrated into the global network. The activity of natural resource exploration undertakings, the expectations of revenues that are envisaged in the short and medium term horizon, is imposing a rapid adequacy of our financial sector so that it is an active agent of the accumulation process it generates. We therefore see with good eyes the partnerships that are created between international banks and banks operating in the Mozambican market. Dear Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen During these Scientific Days, we will also have the opportunity to hear the presentation and debate, the results of a research entitled "Shocks of Demand and Supply of Natural Resources on Macroeconomic Variables in Developing Countries - The Case of Mozambique", carried out by a group of national researchers, to whom, once again, I salute you for this hard work. After this introduction, I believe that the conditions for the open and frank presentation and discussion of the themes that are part of the agenda of these days are created. My expectation is that, from the debate, we will be able to draw lessons and contributions that will enable us to understand our policies at the current stage of the economic cycle that the country is going through. I hereby declare the Fifth Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique open. Thank you very much. Maputo, 27 September 2013
