Title: Scientific Days - Speech
text: Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Representatives of Government Institutions; Representatives of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations; Representatives of Academic Institutions and Research Centres; Directors, Managers and Technicians of the Bank of Mozambique; Representatives of the Media; Ladies and gentlemen Gentlemen It is with great satisfaction that the Bank of Mozambique welcomes you to this house for the Eighth Scientific Days of our institution, an event that takes place in the week that we celebrate another anniversary of the creation of Metical, our currency. I warmly greet all those present and I want you to know that, for the Bank of Mozambique, the days are a unique moment of interaction with the various segments of our society on diverse issues that are part of the universe of the mandate assigned to us as central bank. I take this opportunity to thank and congratulate all the researchers who, imbued with a spirit of mission, welcomed the invitation that the Bank of Mozambique made in September 2015, submitting their research proposals on the theme selected for this edition of our days. To the researchers whose research projects have been positively sanctioned by the Jury are our words of appreciation and encouragement, and to those who the Jury, in its high discretion, considered to be in a position for public presentation on these days, our congratulations. No doubt that were many hours of research and analysis, commitment and dedication in the preparation of the work that we are all looking forward to hearing and debating. On this occasion, I would like to greet the representatives of government institutions, credit institutions and financial corporations, academic institutions, research institutes and analysts of different specialities, for once again joining us on these scientific journeys. Allow me to express my special gratitude to Dr Salvador Namburete, who has unreservedly accepted our invitation to share with us his long and rich experience of governance and public manager in different sectors of our economy, but with a special imprint in promoting Mozambique's exports. Dr. Namburete today assumes the honors of The Eighth Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique and we certainly look forward to hearing his lesson and his rich teachings, which we think are important to socialize. I believe that Dr. Namburete will understand that the Bank of Mozambique prioritizes, in its strategy of action, the boosting of Mozambican exports, synonymous with reducing the country's external dependence. I am also very sorry to greet the members of the Jury, in the person of their President, Professor Matias Farahane, this time assisted by Dr. Saide Dade and Dr. Agostinho Machava, as vowels, for accepting the invitation we have formulated to play with professionalism and didactism the role of Jury selection and advice of the various research projects for these days. We are already accustomed to your rigorous scrutiny, which greatly honors our institution and credits this event. I could not fail to mention the discussions invited to these days, namely Professor Dr. Ragendra de Sousa and Dr. Faizal Carsane, to whom we address our sincere thanks for having promptly accepted the invitation we have addressed to them to share with this audience the analysis they consider relevant in the works that will be presented here, without neglecting that it is also up to you to animate the debate, that is intended to be frank, open and fruitful. Ladies and Gentlemen The scientific days are for us a time when our institution is open to criticism and debate of ideas on matters relevant to the economic and financial current affairs of our country, focusing on those that directly or indirectly contribute to the improvement of the process of formulation, implementation and management of policies of the central bank's competence. Our mission as monetary and exchange rate policy managers requires our institution to constantly learn and exchange vital information about the relationships that are established in the economy as a whole and in the behavior of the variables affecting the various sectors of the economy. It is in this context that the Board of Directors elected to the scientific days of 2016 quantities of the Mozambican external sector, which end up having an impact on the real sector of the economy, such as economic growth and employment, as well as in the monetary and foreign exchange sector, recognizing that exports interfere with GDP and are a primary source of foreign exchange generation for the country's exchange rate fund. In the adverse international situation we are experiencing, characterized by the fall in commodity prices that Mozambique exports, aggravated by the scenario of suspension of foreign aid from our international partners, exports are of particular importance to all of us, hence the theme "Contribution of exports to the economy of Mozambique" is current. As a result of the country's various shocks, the exchange rate pressure we are experiencing has been evident, which also generates pressure on the general level of prices, in a basically importing economy like ours and therefore heavily dependent on the outside world. After successive years of appreciable macroeconomic stability accompanied by robust economic growth, the most recent cycle of our development has been characterized slowing down our growth, with factors that, to some extent, condition the solid foundations of macroeconomic stability. The statistical information of the Country's Balance of Payments shows that in the last five years the average value of our exports was US3.685 million, of which approximately 1,509 million correspond to traditional exports. Among the products with the highest contribution to our exports in the last five years are aluminum (US1.095 million), coal (US365 million), electricity (US299 million), tobacco (US237 million), gas (US236 million), sugar (US123 million) and wood (US108 million). From 2013, our exports started a downward trend, culminating in 2015 with a reduction of 12.8%. But the export potential of Mozambican products is vast, including agricultural products that our farmers export to some neighbouring countries, so it is important that we look at how to boost the entire export-oriented production cycle, without neglecting a diversification of our economy, in order to also diversify our exports, whether in products or in markets. This is the way to sustainably minimise the funding gap experienced by the national economy. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen Gentlemen The fall in exports in recent years, not being properly compensated by a greater levelling of imports, greater rigidity of these or by domestic production that replaces it, imposes increased challenges to the domestic foreign exchange market and, therefore, to the objective of exchange rate stability. The increase in the country's burden on foreign countries in the face of an environment of lower foreign exchange influx is itself a generator of exchange rate volatility, in a context where the capacity to Central bank's intervention to mitigate these effects is limited to the current low level of the country's external reserves when viewed according to the months of import coverage. The current international conjuncture, characterized by the less favorable behavior of international prices of some commodities that Mozambique exports, namely aluminum, coal, natural gas and electricity, shows that the country needs to go through a strategy oriented towards the diversification of exports, as a way to reduce the impact of international price fluctuations of the raw materials we produce. To this end, the promotion of a value chain that allows some local processing not only contributes to the creation of more jobs, but multiplies the income of small and medium-sized enterprises called to take an active part in this process. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen Gentlemen The Bank of Mozambique has been focusing on various and current scientific days in the context of the recent dynamics of the Mozambican economy. For example, we highlight topics already analyzed in the last three editions, namely "More Appropriate Monetary Policy Regimes for Mozambique", "Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism in Mozambique" and "Monetary Policy Framework in the Context of Natural Resource Exploitation". The valuable contributions we have made from this forum help us to calibrate our policies and strategies of action, in addition to allowing a broad dialogue with different economic sensitivities and ways of thinking. The role of exports in the economy can be seen from different perspectives, as literature teaches us, namely between this and economic growth, in a perspective of elasticity or even analysis of the external competitiveness of the economy, among others. But i will not stretch about it, since we have followed a background intervention to be made by the illustrious Dr. Salvador Namburete. From the reading I made to the research papers that will be presented here, I found that their authors make two different approaches. One looks at the impact of our exports on the growth of the Mozambican economy in recent years and another looks at how the exchange rate change affects export behavior. No doubt our expectations regarding these presentations are high, but I don't think anyone in this room is waiting for a finished and final study. Therefore, I re-congratulate the two authors and wish a lot of inspiration in the presentation of the results of their research. In the end, I invite everyone present to a frank and uncomplex debate on the theme that is on the agenda in these days. Each and every one has something to convey and share, namely knowledge and experience, which will be the subject of our attention and study. With these words, I declare open the Eighth Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique under the theme "Contribution of Exports in the Economy of Mozambique". Thank you very much!
text_original: Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique; Senhores Representantes de Instituies do Governo; Senhores Representantes de Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras; Senhores Representantes de Instituies Acadmicas e de Centros de Investigao; Senhores Directores, Gestores e Tcnicos do Banco de Moambique; Senhores Representantes dos rgos de Comunicao Social; Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores  com enorme satisfao que o Banco de Moambique vos acolhe nesta casa para as Oitavas Jornadas Cientficas da nossa instituio, evento que decorre na semana em que comemoramos mais um aniversrio da criao do Metical, a nossa moeda. Sado vivamente todos os presentes e quero que saibam que, para o Banco de Moambique, as jornadas so um momento mpar de interaco com os vrios segmentos da nossa sociedade sobre temas diversos que integram o universo do mandato que nos est atribudo como banco central. Aproveito esta oportunidade para agradecer e felicitar a todos os investigadores que, imbudos de esprito de misso, acolheram favoravelmente o convite que o Banco de Moambique formulou em Setembro de 2015, submetendo as suas propostas de pesquisa em torno da temtica selecionada para a presente edio das nossas jornadas. Aos investigadores cujos projectos de pesquisa foram positivamente sancionados pelo Jri vo as nossas palavras de apreo e encorajamento, e queles que o Jri, no seu elevado critrio, considerou estarem em condies para a apresentao pblica nestas jornadas, as nossas felicitaes. Sem dvidas que foram muitas horas de pesquisa e anlise, empenho e dedicao na preparao dos trabalhos que estamos todos ansiosos por ouvir e debater. Gostaria, nesta ocasio, de cumprimentar os representantes das instituies do Governo, instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras, instituies acadmicas, institutos de pesquisa e analistas de diferentes especialidades, por mais uma vez se juntarem a ns nestas jornadas cientficas. Permitam-me que manifeste a minha especial gratido ao Dr. Salvador Namburete, que sem reservas aceitou o nosso convite para partilhar connosco a sua longa e rica experincia de governao e de gestor pblico, em diferentes sectores da nossa economia, mas com um cunho especial na promoo das exportaes de Moambique. O Dr. Namburete assume hoje as honras de Orador Principal das Oitavas Jornadas Cientficas do Banco de Moambique e por certo estamos ansiosos por escutar a sua lio e os seus ricos ensinamentos, que julgamos importante socializar. Julgo que o Dr. Namburete compreender que o Banco de Moambique prioriza, na sua estratgia de actuao, a dinamizao das exportaes moambicanas, sinnimo de reduo da dependncia externa do Pas. Cumpre-me igualmente saudar de forma muito especial os membros do Jri, na pessoa do seu Presidente, o Professor Dr. Matias Farahane, desta vez auxiliado pelo Dr. Sade Dade e pelo Dr. Agostinho Machava, na qualidade de vogais, por terem aceite o convite que formulmos para desempenharem com profissionalismo e didactismo o papel de Jri de seleco e aconselhamento dos vrios projectos de pesquisa para estas jornadas. Estamos j habituados ao vosso escrutnio rigoroso, que muito honra a nossa instituio e credibiliza este evento. No podia deixar de mencionar os discussants convidados para estas jornadas, nomeadamente o Professor Dr. Ragendra de Sousa e o Dr. Faizal Carsane, a quem endereo os nossos sinceros agradecimentos por terem prontamente aceite o convite que lhes enderemos para partilharem com esta audincia a anlise que consideram relevante nos trabalhos que sero aqui apresentados, sem descurar que tambm vos incumbe animar o debate, que se pretende franco, aberto e profcuo. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores As jornadas cientficas so para ns um momento em que a nossa instituio se abre  crtica e ao debate de ideias sobre matrias relevantes da actualidade econmico-financeira do nosso Pas, com enfoque para aquelas que directa ou indirectamente contribuem para a melhoria do processo de formulao, implementao e gesto das polticas da competncia do banco central. A nossa misso de gestores da poltica monetria e cambial exige da nossa instituio constante aprendizagem e troca de informaes vitais sobre as relaes que se estabelecem na economia, como um todo, e no comportamento das variveis que afectam os vrios sectores da economia.  neste contexto que o Conselho de Administrao elegeu para as jornadas cientficas de 2016 grandezas do sector externo moambicano, que acabam tendo impacto no sector real da economia, como o crescimento econmico e o emprego, assim como no sector monetrio e cambial, reconhecendo que as exportaes mexem com o PIB e so fonte primria de gerao de divisas para o fundo cambial do Pas. Na conjuntura internacional adversa que vivemos, caracterizada pela queda dos preos das matrias-primas que Moambique exporta, agravada pelo cenrio de suspenso da ajuda externa dos nossos parceiros internacionais, as exportaes assumem especial importncia para todos ns, da que o tema Contribuio das exportaes na economia de Moambique se mostre actual. Em resultado de diversos choques que o pas atravessa, tem sido evidente a presso cambial que vivemos, factor igualmente gerador de presso sobre o nvel geral de preos, numa economia basicamente importadora como a nossa e, por isso, bastante dependente do exterior. Aps anos sucessivos de aprecivel estabilidade macroeconmica acompanhada de um crescimento econmico robusto, o ciclo mais recente do nosso desenvolvimento tem sido caracterizado pela desacelerao do nosso crescimento, com factores que, de certo modo, condicionam os fundamentos slidos da estabilidade macroeconmica. A informao estatstica da Balana de Pagamentos do Pas mostra que nos ltimos cinco anos o valor mdio das nossas exportaes foi de 3.685 milhes de dlares, dos quais cerca de 1.509 milhes correspondem s exportaes tradicionais. Entre os produtos com maior contribuio nas nossas exportaes nos ltimos cinco anos destacam-se o alumnio (1.095 milhes de dlares), o carvo (365 milhes de dlares), a energia elctrica (299 milhes de dlares), o tabaco (237 milhes de dlares), o gs (236 milhes de dlares), o acar (123 milhes de dlares) e a madeira (108 milhes de dlares). A partir de 2013, as nossas exportaes iniciam uma tendncia para queda, culminando em 2015 com uma reduo de 12,8%. Mas o potencial de exportao de produtos moambicanos  vasto, incluindo produtos agrcolas que os nossos agricultores exportam para alguns pases vizinhos, sendo por isso importante analisarmos como dinamizar todo o ciclo de produo virada para a exportao, sem descurar uma diversificao da nossa economia, para tambm diversificarmos as nossas exportaes, seja em produtos, seja em mercados. Esta  a via para se minimizar, de forma sustentvel, o dfice de financiamento que a economia nacional experimenta. Ilustres Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores A queda das exportaes nos ltimos anos, no sendo devidamente compensada por um maior nivelamento das importaes, por maior rigidez destas ou por produo domstica que a substitua, impe desafios acrescidos ao mercado cambial domstico e, por conseguinte, ao objectivo de estabilidade cambial. O aumento dos encargos do Pas para com o exterior perante um ambiente de menor influxo de divisas  por si gerador de volatilidade cambial, num contexto em que a capacidade de interveno do banco central para mitigar esses efeitos est limitada ao actual baixo nvel das reservas externas do pas quando vistas em funo dos meses de cobertura das importaes. A actual conjuntura internacional, caracterizada pelo comportamento menos favorvel dos preos internacionais de algumas commodities que Moambique exporta, nomeadamente o alumnio, o carvo mineral, o gs natural e a energia elctrica, mostra que o Pas precisa enveredar por uma estratgia orientada para a diversificao das exportaes, como forma de reduzir o impacto das flutuaes de preos internacionais das matrias- primas que produzimos. Para tanto, a promoo de uma cadeia de valor que permita algum processamento local no s contribui para a criao de mais emprego, como multiplica a renda das pequenas e mdias empresas chamadas a tomar parte activa neste processo. Ilustres Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores O Banco de Moambique tem vindo a privilegiar nas suas jornadas cientficas temas diversos e actuais no contexto das dinmicas recentes da economia moambicana. A ttulo de exemplo, destacamos temas j analisados nas trs ltimas edies, designadamente Regimes de Poltica Monetria mais Apropriados para Moambique, Mecanismo de Transmisso da Poltica Monetria em Moambique e Quadro da Poltica Monetria no Contexto de Explorao de Recursos Naturais. As valiosas contribuies que temos recolhido deste frum ajudam-nos a calibrar as nossas polticas e estratgias de actuao, para alm de permitir um vasto dialogo com diferentes sensibilidades econmicas e formas de pensar. O papel das exportaes na economia pode ser visto sob diferentes prismas, como nos ensina a literatura, nomeadamente entre esta e o crescimento econmico, numa perspectiva de elasticidade ou mesmo de anlise da competitividade externa da economia, entre outros. Mas sobre isso no me vou alongar, visto termos a seguir uma interveno de fundo a ser feita pelo ilustre Dr. Salvador Namburete. Da leitura que fiz aos trabalhos de pesquisa que sero aqui apresentados, verifiquei que os seus autores fazem duas abordagens diferentes. Um se debrua sobre o impacto das nossas exportaes no crescimento da economia moambicana nos ltimos anos e outro analisa como a variao da taxa de cmbio afecta o comportamento das exportaes. Sem dvidas que so grandes as nossas expectativas em relao a estas apresentaes, mas julgo que ningum nesta sala aguarda por um estudo acabado e final. Por isso, renovo as minhas felicitaes aos dois autores e desejo muita inspirao na apresentao dos resultados das suas pesquisas. A terminar, convido todos os presentes para um debate franco e sem complexos em relao ao tema que est em pauta nestas jornadas. Todos e cada um tm algo por transmitir e partilhar, designadamente conhecimentos e experincias, que sero objecto da nossa ateno e estudo. Com estas palavras, declaro abertas as Oitavas Jornadas Cientficas do Banco de Moambique sob o tema Contribuio das Exportaes na Economia de Moambique. Muito Obrigado!

Title: Launch of the 2017 Series of Metical Banknotes
text: INTERVENTION OF ITS EXCIA. THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE ON THE OCCASION OF THE LAUNCH OF THE 2017 SERIES OF METICAL NOTES PRESS CONFERENCE MAPUTO, 17 MAY 2017 Your Excellese Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Dear Media Partners; Dear Guests; Ladies; Gentlemen; On behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf I would like, on this festive day, to celebrate the creation of the WB, to begin by addressing to all our warm welcome and thanking you for your presence, which greatly honors and sensitizes me. In 2006, the Bank of Mozambique reformed the national currency, adopting the third metical family, i.e. the "Bank of Mozambique" family. This family succeeded the first two, namely the "People's Republic of Mozambique" family and the "Republic of Mozambique" family, who finished their legal course on 31 December 2012. Some five years after the introduction of the third Metical family and the increasingly accelerated evolution of printing technologies coupled with the need to ensure more effective banknote protection, it was necessary to adjust the safety features in 2011. It was in this context that we had the honour of introducing the new banknotes with improved safety devices and equipped with elements that facilitate the identification of the various names through touch. Another milestone in the improvements made was the alteration of the substrate of the notes of 20 MT, 50 MT and 100 MT. The choice of these names resulted from the fact that they are banknotes of greater circulation and therefore subject to greater wear and tear. As a result of the research carried out with a view to enhancing the consistency of the notes, we chose to replace the paper substrate with the polymer, which is a synthetic material, particularly adjusted to humid climates. With the adoption of the new substrate, we have significantly reduced the costs associated with the replacement of degraded banknotes. We also comply with our plan to provide the public with sufficient grades and the necessary quality. It should be noted that, from 2011 to this part, we have not yet detected a single banknote contramade in polymer substrate, which is an unprecedented milestone even at the international level. In paper notes, counterfeits or counterfeits detected are easily identified 333 in plain sight. Distinguished Guests, Ladies, Gentlemen Good practice in these matters recommends that the characteristics and safety elements of banknotes be reviewed every five years. In this sense, it should be noted that from the assessment carried out by the Bank of Mozambique it was concluded that the security elements of the Metical notes remain robust. Approaching, however, another date of commemoration of the Metical, symbol of our sovereignty as a country, we believe that we are facing an opportunity for the launch of another series of the national currency, containing a new signature and date. It is in this context that I have the honor to announce the launch of the new metical series today, May 17, 2017, the date on which the creation of the Bank of Mozambique is celebrated, and the effective circulation of the new banknotes will take place on June 16, 2017 - the day of the Metical. The 2017 Series, like the 2011 Series, will not include coins. In this sense, coins bearing the date of 2006, at the time of the issuance of the "new Metical Family" will remain in circulation. In this sense, the circulation of the 2017 series will be simultaneous with the 2006 and 2011 series of Metical notes bearing the signatures of the Former Governors, namely Adriano Afonso Maleiane, dated June 16, 2006, and Ernesto Gouveia Gove, dated June 16, 2011, respectively. It should be noted that there will be no exchange process or deadline for the circulation of the notes of the 2006 and 2011 series. Dear Guests, Ladies and gentlemen, as can be seen, the security elements and, consequently, the reasons for the Metical notes put into circulation in 2011 remain, thus keeping in mind the praise of the values of our cultural, historical, faunistic and economic heritage. I end my speech by reiterating my thanks for your presence and appealing to everyone's participation in the dignification and conservation of metical notes and coins. By keeping our Metical, we save the country's borders. Thank you!

Title: Signing Ceremony of the Agreement for Standardization of the Calculation Base (Index) of the Banking System Interest Rate
text: INTERVENTION OF YOUR EXCELLENCY GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE On THE OCCASION OF THE SIGNING CEREMONY OF THE AGREEMENT FOR THE UNIFORMITY OF THE BASE OFCALCULATION (INDEXING) OF THE INTEREST RATE OF THE BANKING SYSTEM MAPUTO, 17 MAY 2017 Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique; Mr President of the Mozambican Banking Association; Presidents of the Boards of Directors and Executive Committees of Commercial Banks; Distinguished Guests, Ladies, and My Lords, Let me first of all convey, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my own behalf, our gratitude for your honorable presence in this act, which represents the culmination of a joint and concerted effort. I take this opportunity to express our appreciation to the Mozambican Association of Banks and to all credit institutions for their excellent collaboration over the course of several months of hard work that has made it possible to implement this Agreement, the formal signature of which we have all witnessed. This ceremony takes place exactly on the date when the Bank of Mozambique celebrates another year of its creation. We remain firm in our mission to ensure the stability of the national currency, an essential condition for economic operators to develop their activities and make investment decisions in an environment of greater predictability of economic and financial indicators. The mechanism for raising interest rates as well as their level is a pressing concern of economic agents, and the Bank of Mozambique cannot remain indifferent. In 1994, as part of the reforms introduced in the path of our country's support to the Breton Woods institutions, the first major reform was produced in the system for determining the interest rates applied in the operations of the financial system with the public. The Bank of Mozambique has ceased to fix them, and its determination is the responsibility of each financial institution operating in the Mozambican market, according to the risk assessment that each one makes, and should only report them to the central bank for its monitoring and measurement of the situation of the financial system. It was indeed an interest rate liberalisation in the context of the financial system reform process, which was also accompanied by the creation of the Interbank Money Market (MMI) in 1997 and the introduction of different instruments for banks to apply their liquidity, in particular the permanent liquidity lending and absorption facilities, fpc and FPD, respectively. In 1999, financial institutions initialled the MAIBOR Agreement to encourage the formation of an income curve for the Mozambican market and to deepen the maturity of the operations carried out. MAIBOR was being assumed by some banks as a benchmark for retail operations, but depending on changes in conjuncture, many banks began to index their retail operations at the rate of the Permanent Lending Facility (FPC), which was not supposed to happen, since this is a penalizing rate for transactions that are generated in the interbank money market. This resulted in the liberalized credit market operating with more than one benchmark for retail operations, depending on market expectations and constraints and the perception of each institution at any given time. The act we have just witnessed reflects an important step towards the crystallization of reforms introduced more than 20 years ago with regard to the determination of interest rates, and it is in line with international good practice, which adopts a single benchmark in the formation of the interest rate on credit operations. Indeed, in the context of promoting greater transparency in the process of setting interest rates in the market, coupled with the very mechanism for transmitting monetary policy that needs to improve, the Bank of Mozambique has held discussions in recent months with the Mozambican Association of Banks representing credit institutions and financial companies with the aim of obtaining a consensus methodology on which the indexer is based on which it will serve as a based on the formation of the Prime-Rate and then all credit rates of the market, which resulted in the formalization of the agreement for the Standardization of the Basis of Calculation of interest rate in the banking system. The Single Indexer will be the base rate for the calculation of the Prime Rate of the Financial System to be practiced in the variable interest rate credit operations contractualized between credit institutions and financial corporations with their clients. In the compilation of this indexer stands out the inclusion of the MIMO rate, our recently approved monetary policy interest rate, in order to ensure that the interest rates practiced by commercial banks, in transactions with their customers, are increasingly sensitive to monetary policy stimulus, thereby improving transmission mechanisms. A Cost Premium will be added to the Indexer, i.e. a market risk margin to constitute the Prime Rate of the Financial System. This premium, which will be calculated and informed by the Mozambican Association of Banks to the Bank of Mozambique, may change whenever the liquidity and risk conditions of the market so require. The Mozambican Financial System Prime Rate will be a single reference rate for Interest Rate credit operations Variable of the Mozambican financial system, composed of the sum of the Single Indexer and the Cost Premium. In the credit agreements for each particular client, the concrete risk of each transaction will be taken into account, this being the Credit Spread. It should be mentioned that this spread varies depending on the risk of each transaction, and can be added or subtracted from the Prime Rate of the Financial System. The present agreement signed between the Bank of Mozambique, the Mozambican Association of Banks and twenty Credit Institutions, enters into effectiveness on June 1, 2017, revoking the MAIBOR Agreement. It has a mandatory clause for all new contracts or for cases of refinancing or renegotiation of contracts already in force. The Bank of Mozambique assumes the function of advertising Prime Rate to the public, and credit institutions have the duty to provide information to their clients at each counter and on the websites of each institution, the value of the credit spread that each one practices, for each credit category. Distinguished Guests Ladies Gentlemen The main recipient of this agreement is the consumer of banking services. We believe that the public wants and expects from all institutions to respect and implement the agreed terms, so, as supervisors and regulators of the financial system, we are committed to ensure that this agreement is rigorously implemented. Today we have just offered the public an instrument that enables them to better understand the mechanism for setting up the interest rate, empowering them in dialogue with credit institutions and financial society. We hope that transparency and competition will prevail in the Mozambican financial system, which makes room for liquidity and solvency to remain at appropriate levels, allowing the financial system to contribute more actively to the development of the national economy. I conclude by reiterating our thanks, congratulating all the signatories of the agreement and registering a very special recognition to the technical team that worked tirelessly until the conclusion of the final version of the Agreement. Thank you so much for the attention given! Maputo, 17 May 2017
text_original: INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELENCIA O GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE POR OCASIO DA CERIMNIA DE ASSINATURA DO ACORDO PARA A UNIFORMIZAO DA BASE DE CLCULO (INDEXANTE) DA TAXA DE JURO DO SISTEMA BANCRIO MAPUTO, 17 DE MAIO DE 2017 Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique; Senhor Presidente da Associao Moambicana de Bancos; Senhores Presidentes dos Conselhos de Administrao e Comisses Executivas dos Bancos Comerciais; Distintos Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, e Meus Senhores, Permitam-me, antes de mais, transmitir, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome pessoal, a nossa gratido pela vossa honrosa presena neste acto que representa o culminar de um esforo conjunto e concertado. Aproveito esta ocasio para expressar o nosso apreo  Associao Moambicana de Bancos e a todas as instituies de crdito pela excelente colaborao que prestaram ao longo dos vrios meses de trabalho rduo que tornou possvel a concretizao deste Acordo cuja assinatura formal acabamos todos de testemunhar. Esta cerimnia ocorre exactamente na data em que o Banco de Moambique comemora mais um ano da sua criao. Continuamos firmes na nossa misso de garantir a estabilidade da moeda nacional, condio essencial para que os agentes econmicos desenvolvam as suas actividades e tomem as decises de investimento num ambiente de maior previsibilidade dos indicadores econmicos e financeiros. O mecanismo de formao das taxas de juro, bem como o seu nvel  preocupao premente dos agentes econmicos, e o Banco de Moambique no pode ficar indiferente. Em 1994, no quadro das reformas introduzidas na senda da adeso do nosso pas s instituies de Breton Woods produziu-se a primeira grande reforma no regime de determinao das taxas de juro aplicadas nas operaes do sistema financeiro com o pblico. O Banco de Moambique deixou de as fixar, passando a sua determinao a ser responsabilidade de cada instituio financeira que opera no mercado moambicano, de acordo com a avaliao de risco que cada uma faz, devendo apenas report-las ao banco central para sua monitoria e aferio da situao do sistema financeiro. Tratou-se na verdade de uma liberalizao da taxa de juro, no mbito do processo de reformas no sistema financeiro, que foi tambm acompanhada pela criao do Mercado Monetrio Interbancrio (MMI), em 1997 e a introduo de diferentes instrumentos para os bancos aplicarem a sua liquidez, nomeadamente as facilidades permanentes de cedncia e de absoro de liquidez, vulgo FPC e FPD, respectivamente. Em 1999, as instituies financeiras rubricaram o Acordo de Adeso  MAIBOR, com vista a incentivar a formao de uma curva de rendimentos para o mercado moambicano e aprofundar a maturidade das operaes realizadas. A MAIBOR foi sendo assumida por alguns bancos como um indicador de referncia para as operaes a retalho, mas consoante alteraes de conjuntura, muito bancos passaram a indexar as suas operaes de retalho  taxa da Facilidade Permanente de Cedncia (FPC), o que era suposto no acontecer, visto que esta  uma taxa penalizadora das transaces que se geram no mercado monetrio interbancrio. Tal resultou que o mercado de crdito liberalizado passasse a operar com mais do que um indicador de referncia para as operaes a retalho, dependendo das expectativas e de condicionalismos de mercado e da percepo de cada instituio em cada momento. O acto que acabmos de testemunhar traduz um passo importante para a cristalizao das reformas introduzidas h mais de 20 anos no que tange  determinao das taxas de juro, e o mesmo est alinhado com as boas prticas internacionais, que adopta uma referncia nica na formao da taxa de juro das operaes de crdito. Com efeito, e no mbito da promoo de uma maior transparncia no processo de fixao das taxas de juro no mercado, associado ao prprio mecanismo de transmisso da poltica monetria que importa melhorar, o Banco de Moambique manteve discusses, nos ltimos meses, com a Associao Moambicana de Bancos em representao das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras com o objectivo de obter uma metodologia de consenso sob o qual assenta o indexante que servir de base a formao das Prime-Rate e de seguida de todas as taxas de crdito do mercado, do que resultou a formalizao do acordo para a Uniformizao da Base de Clculo da Taxa de Juro no Sistema Bancrio. O Indexante nico ser a taxa de base para o clculo da Prime Rate do Sistema Financeiro a ser praticada nas operaes de crdito de Taxa de Juro Varivel contratualizadas entre as Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras com os seus clientes. Na compilao deste indexante destaca-se a incluso da taxa MIMO, a nossa taxa de juro de poltica monetria, recentemente aprovada, com vista a assegurar que as taxas de juro praticadas pelos Bancos Comerciais, nas operaes com os seus clientes, sejam cada vez mais sensveis aos estmulos da poltica monetria, melhorando, desta forma, os mecanismos de transmisso. Ser adicionado um Prmio de Custo ao Indexante, ou seja uma margem de risco de mercado para constituir a Prime Rate do Sistema Financeiro. Este prmio, que ser calculado e informado pela Associao Moambicana de Bancos ao Banco de Moambique, pode alterar sempre que as condies de liquidez e de risco do mercado o exijam. A Prime Rate do Sistema Financeiro Moambicano ser uma taxa nica de referncia para operaes de crdito de Taxa de Juro Varivel do sistema financeiro moambicano, composta pela soma do Indexante nico e do Prmio de Custo. Nos contratos de crdito para cada cliente em particular, ser tomado em conta o risco concreto de cada operao, sendo isto o Spread de crdito. Convm mencionar que esse spread varia em funo do risco de cada operao, podendo ser adicionado ou subtrado da Prime Rate do Sistema Financeiro. 0 presente acordo assinado entre o Banco de Moambique, a Associao Moambicana de Bancos e vinte Instituies de Crdito, entra em efectividade no dia 1 de Junho de 2017, revogando o Acordo da MAIBOR. Ele possui uma clusula mandatria para todos os novos contractos ou para os casos de refinanciamento ou renegociao de contractos j em vigor. O Banco de Moambique assume a funo de publicitar a Prime Rate para o pblico, cabendo as instituies de crdito o dever de informao aos seus clientes em cada balco e nas pginas electrnicas de cada instituio, o valor do spread de crdito que cada uma pratica, para cada categoria de crdito. Distintos Convidados Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, O destinatrio principal deste acordo  o consumidor dos servios bancrios. Estamos em crer que o pblico almeja e espera de todas as instituies o respeito e implementao dos termos acordados, pelo que, na nossa qualidade de supervisores e reguladores do sistema financeiro, assumimos desde j o compromisso de velarmos pela rigorosa implementao deste acordo. Acabamos de oferecer hoje ao pblico um instrumento que o habilita a melhor entender o mecanismo de formao da taxa de juro, capacitando-o no dilogo com as instituies de crdito e sociedade financeiras. Ns esperamos que a transparncia e concorrncia prevaleam no sistema financeiro moambicano, o que abre espao para que a liquidez e solvabilidade se mantenham em nveis adequados, permitindo ao sistema financeiro contribuir de forma mais activa para desenvolvimento da economia nacional. Termino reiterando os nossos agradecimentos, felicitando a todos os signatrios do acordo e registando um reconhecimento muito especial  equipa tcnica que trabalhou incansavelmente at a concluso da verso final do Acordo. Muito obrigado pela ateno dispensada! Maputo, 17 de Maio de 2017

Title: Press Conference Transcript - MPC, October 26, 2017
text: in Mozambique October 26, 2017 About a year ago, on 21 October 2016, we made monetary policy decisions that defined the roadmap for our position in terms of interest rates and other instruments to date. On that day, we deliberated in the Monetary Policy Committee a substantial increase in interest rates in order to deal with inflationary pressures and the currency crisis. I would like to take this opportunity to thank the press that has been accompanying us since then and transmitting to society the difficult decisions we have been making in order to control inflationary risks. We continue to follow the same path and today's decisions reflect this trajectory. In view of the behaviour of inflation, the CPMO considers that there is room for a moderate drop in interest rates having deliberated: 1. Reduce the monetary policy interest rate, MIMO rate, by 50 basis points, to 21.0%; 2. Reduce the interest rate of the Permanent Liquidity-Of-Liquidity Facility (FPC) by 50 basis points to 22.0%; 3. Reduce the interest rate of the Permanent Deposit Facility (FPD) by 50 basis points to 15.5%; 4. Reduce the Mandatory Reserves coefficient for domestic and foreign currency liabilities by 100 basis points to 14.0%. Depending on developments in economic and financial indicators and risk factors, the CPMO may take the necessary corrective measures before the next meeting of the body, scheduled for 20 December 2017 From June to October, we have taken two important measures to strengthen the strength, transparency and discipline of the market and our credit institutions. On the one hand, we have reinforced the obligation for credit institutions to disclose solvency and liquidity ratios to the public. Thus, information on these indicators becomes available more frequently to the public so that they can monitor the health of credit institutions. On the other hand, the Bank of Mozambique begins to publish the definitive sanctions imposed on credit institutions and financial corporations. Key Challenges for Decision Making 1. There are always a number of risks both domestically and internationally. At national level: i) uncertainty as to the magnitude of the adjustment of tax policy in the face of confirmation of the maintenance of the freezing and suspension of direct external aid to the State budget. ii) uncertainty as to the impact of the price adjustment of liquid fuels and other managed goods and services; iii) uncertainty about climate effects. At international level we have identified two factors already known since the last CPMO meeting and certainly since June. i) the impact of the political situation in South Africa, our largest economic and trade partner; ii) the impact of commodity price volatility with effects on domestic prices and the balance of payments According to the latest publication by the National Institute of Statistics (INE), GDP continues to grow moderately and recorded relatively weak growth in the 1st half of this year (3%), compared to the 2016 period (above 5%). We also recorded a deterioration in the economic climate indicator in August for the second month in a row, instifing that economic activity will remain below potential. We also see the continued fall in annual inflation, a trend expected to continue until December 2017, thanks to metical stability and weak aggregate demand. The diffusion index, which indicates the proportion of products with positive monthly price change, has begun for the first time to show a slightly positive trend since October 2016. This, in turn, indicates the beginning of the trend of inflationary risks. The Metical has remained stable since the last CPMO, continuing to favor the fall in inflation. The economic situation of the country is reflected in the behaviour of the currency vis-88-vis the currencies of our partners, in particular the US dollar and the rand. In relation to state indebtedness, domestic debt (which is already high) continues with an increasing trend, having increased by about 5 billion meticais to about 100 billion meticais as a result, essentially, of increased use of Treasury Bills. The trade balance remains favourable reflecting the positive impact of exchange rate stability and reserve behaviour. The trade balance, which is traditionally loss-making, is increasingly decreasing. In the third quarter of 2016 we had a deficit of almost USD 1.5 billion, having fallen to about USD 378 million in the same period of 2017. This is an extremely sharp adjustment led by exports, in particular those of major projects. Imports have fallen substantially, but not as much as the increase in exports, with a drop of just over USD 100 million, which in turn greatly helps our trade balance, in particular, and the balance of payments in general. We also have positive news that reflects the combination of the trade balance account, capital account and capital flow, in particular direct investment, which continues to increase. Gross reserves are around USD 2.5 billion, which equates to a little more than 6 months of imports of goods and services. This means that we are at a comfortable level of reserves, a level that is internationally established in 6 months, this being a practice and not a legal definition. A country with this reserve level is considered to be able to deal with normal debt service payments. The prospects for a slowdown in inflation in the current year to single digits prevail, but there are still risks of worsening inflationary pressures. For 2018, some inflationary risks are foreseen. We, as legislators, are tasked with closely monitoring these risks and taking the necessary measures to ensure that these risks do not materialize. It is important to understand that as the Central Bank we have an extremely conservative attitude towards inflationary risks and our goal as central bank is to achieve low inflation. High inflation is a serious problem in society. The poor get poorer and the rich get richer. Inflation creates enormous social tensions and we as the Central Bank will continue to take the necessary steps to ensure that this inflation, which could eventually arise, does not materialize and does not harm all these efforts that we have been making since the last twelve months or more. Thank you very much QUESTION SESSION 1. Reduction of prime rate The definition of prime rate also includes a part of the interest rate that reflects monetary policy decisions in particular the repo rate and is associated with the MIMO rate. Therefore, you can expect the prime rate to decrease. However, this is not the only component of the prime rate. In an ideal scenario, without changes, the prime rate should also fall as a result of the measures taken if other equally determining factors for the prime rate do not change. This is our expectation, but it is a combination of policy, market and credit institution decisions. 0 Bank does not force a prime rate. 2. Unsustainability of interest rates It is our understanding as the Central Bank that interest rates remain high and although we have been reducing them, they are not yet at the desired levels. We predicted that at this time of year short-term interest rates would be at relatively lower levels. However, due to a combination of factors, both domestic and international as well as other risk factors, conditions were not created for this to happen. Interest rates are a very sensitive subject that we have debated intensely and emotionally, with all the necessary passion. We constantly look at ways to reduce interest rates to the levels desired by society and which are indeed necessary. However, this decision is not limited to monetary policy, there is also the fiscal part and reforms. The process of fiscal consolidation, and certain reforms that have been underway, has been slower than anticipated. These conditions are imperative for lowering interest rates, at the risk of backing down on reserves, exchange rate volatility and even increasing inflation. Inflation today is on its way to single digits as a result of the caution we have been taking, so we will continue to be cautious. We naturally want to reduce interest rates even more than we have already done and we will not hesitate to do so when the conditions are in the open. However, as I mentioned earlier , there are still inflationary risks, and we are not sure in what magnitude. In fulfilling the mandate entrusted to us by the legislator, if the technical assessment of the situation is such that it requires us to take certain measures to maintain low and stable inflation, we will do so. In a way, the reduction in interest rates is not a decision that the Central Bank makes at random, it reflects an analysis of the conditions of society at all times. 3. Domestic debt The level of domestic debt is clearly high. Sometimes we are alarmed when we see certain sustainability indicators, but ultimately it is the market that decides. Who buys the debt is the market and this market can be both banks and credit institutions or even citizens. When debt grows it is our obligation to keep up with the market reaction, as it may not be willing to buy the debt. However, it is not a question of having an established number which, when exceeded, indicates the deterioration of the debt. By way of example, each bank has a different number because each institution has limits on the purchase of state debt. For various reasons, both internal and own risk management, holders of such securities decide at different times the purchase of the debt. 4. Inclusion of climate effects in BM forecasts It would be hard to do that. Our region is prone to climate problems. Our ability to predict climate aspects also reflects the ability of those who make these forecasts. If it is difficult for these to predict, it means that for us with BM it would be much more difficult yet since it is not only up to us. The ability to make predictions in these areas depends on other professionals and not economists. 5. Excessive band liquidity Excess liquidity is associated with the growth of reserves. The Bank of Mozambique increased its foreign reserves and, in return, injected meticais into the economy, which caused the increase in liquidity. This increase also reflects the behaviour of state activities as a Government, as the Central Bank and as a company when they spend more and when they finance themselves. It also reflects credit behaviour in our economy. Credit remains weak and with relatively modest growth, which means that excess liquidity, which should go to the economy, is still in liquidity instruments. Liquidity is not necessarily cash, it is mostly applied to government instruments and Reverse Repo, which we call short-term instruments, on Treasury Bonds and also on Treasury Bills. Ideally, this excessive liquidity would be applied to the economy, but it is not up to us to decide, we cannot force the market or direct credit. What we do is signal, but ultimately it is the credit institutions that must make these decisions through their risk assessment and their business plans. 6. Uncertainty about state funding in 2018 The IMF has decided to maintain the freezing of funding to our country in 2018. That's no longer a risk, it's a certainty and has already been made public. Donors, in turn, claim that without a program with the fund they are not willing to resume aid, which means the continuity of the problems we had in 2016. The budget is under great pressure and despite all the effort that the Tax Authority has made, it is not possible, in the short term, to offset these cuts in foreign aid to the country. It is not for the BM to make the necessary decisions to compensate for this type of adjustment derived from the cancellation of external aid. It is the task of the Government led by the Ministry of Finance. Certainly, the Government is working hard to deal with this situation and to find necessary measures from the point of view of expenditure, revenue, financing and debt restructuring. 7. Question of Probity in the Moza case I have already spoken extensively on this matter. My position remains, nothing has changed. I have nothing to add or withdraw from what I have already explained. As i'm responsible, it's a closed matter. As regulator, we delivered Moza on July 28th. For me it was particularly a source of great pride to be able to successfully complete this complicated and difficult operation that would have put us in a very complicated situation. We work hard, we have been criticized, but this is part of the democratic process. As regulators we have to take action regardless of the comments. I, in particular, make 100% of the decisions I've made. For me it was a successful decision, it was the right and necessary decision. People are free to criticize, I repeat I have not benefited from anything in this operation nor my colleagues. This was the miraculously right decision because it required a lot of work and creativity on our part to come to this positive outcome. This is a decision I'm proud of. The process is complete and irreversible. When we made the delivery of the Bank we treated Moza like any bank, I do not comment on bci, about BIM and I will no longer comment on Moza which for us is a bank that works today in normality. We took out of the system a systemic risk that seriously distressed us. Nothing was done by mistake. Everything was done intentionally 8. Why Kuhanha's reports are not available for public consultation This is not the BM's decision, it's Kuhanha's decision. Kuhanha is a private law company. It is not governed by the same laws as the Bank. Surely everything they do is provided for in the laws that govern it. There is no illegality in Kuhanha. 9. Investor selection criteria - Moza case There was a criterion for the recapitalization of Moza and investors who did not meet the requirements were excluded. These investors did not meet the necessary conditions to invest in Moza and any other bank in the system. They were a source of instability and risk that we were not willing to take. These investors could bring serious problems to the country and it is up to the state's regulator and public institutions to ensure that investors entering our institutions meet the necessary integrity requirements. Otherwise we're on the world's blacklist and that has serious consequences. When we get on the list it's extremely difficult to get out. In my experience, no country that made that list has been able to get out. 10. Mozambique can live another year without help We can certainly live, but it will be a difficult life. Due to the decision taken by the IMF we live in an environment of even higher risks. This, in turn, requires tax and other reforms of even deeper economic competitiveness . It is something serious and we have to work more intensively, to double the efforts and energies to deal with this new reality which is to achieve positive results by walking practically alone from a budgetary point of view. On the other hand, this complicates our monetary policy management capacity, and our projections also reflect this. 11. Translate single-digit inflation into numbers That is not important at the moment, keep in mind that we are coming from 25% inflation. I remember that in October 2016, when we made the big decisions, the expectation was also around inflation. We tend to be a little reluctant about that and we focus on the numbers. We have already been on our way to inflation that would reach 30% by the end of the year if we had not been draconian and taken the almost unprecedented measures we have taken. If you'd asked me at the time where we were going to end up, I confess we've finished better than my expectations. At the time of uncertainty there are many variants and it would not be fair for us to indicate a number. The great news we have to convey is that with inflation of 25% that walked, without taking action, to 30% by the end of the year, today we have inflation, at the end of 2017, single digits. 12. Growth forecast for 2019 On the fiscal side, a combination of measures from the point of view of revenue management, the various components of expenditure (current and non-current) of reforms is necessary, especially with regard to competitiveness. The government recently passed a new business sector law that will certainly be a powerful tool in consolidating the accounts of public companies. Further efforts are being made outside the country with regard to restructuring foreign debt. A number of measures are being taken, however, I do not consider myself the right person to answer that question. This is a response that is incumbent upon the Minister who oversees this portfolio. 13. Risk factors There are significant risks that we could encounter in a double-digit inflation situation in 2018, so we are prepared to do whatever is necessary to make this material. Theoretically it is easy to talk about cutting expenses, increasing revenues, but the implementation itself is complex. There are many interest groups. We need to be aware of the situation and take the necessary measures in case of materialisation of risks. It's a big win for us to come up with single-digit inflation. Mozambique and Angola have one of the highest inflations on the continent and, at regional level, we are seen as a source of instability. With the exception of Mozambique and Angola, inflation in many countries in the region is below 10%. We must do our part to contribute to the stability of the region and I can assure you that our neighbours follow what we are doing. I'm sure they'll applaud when we get into the low inflation club as a result of the effort and sacrifice society has made to make it happen. When inflation is high prices are also priceless hindering investments and business in the country. We have to take that risk so that society and our partners work with us in a normal situation.
text_original: TRANSCRIO CPMO 26 de Outubro de 2017 H cerca de um ano atrs, no dia 21 de Outubro de 2016, tomamos decises de Poltica Monetria que definiram o roteiro da nossa posio em termos de taxas de juro e outros instrumentos, at a data. Nesse dia, deliberamos, no Comit de Poltica Monetria, um aumento substancial das taxas de juro de forma a lidar com as presses inflacionrias e a crise cambial. Quero aproveitar esta ocasio para agradecer a imprensa que tem, desde essa data, nos acompanhado e transmitindo a sociedade as decises difceis que temos estado a tomar de forma a controlar os riscos inflacionrios. Continuamos a seguir o mesmo caminho e as decises de hoje reflectem essa trajectria. Tendo em conta o comportamento da inflao, o CPMO considera haver espao para uma baixa moderada das taxas de juro tendo deliberado:  Reduzir a taxa de juro de poltica monetria, taxa MIMO, em 50 pontos base, para 21,0%;  Reduzir a taxa de juro da Facilidade Permanente de Cedncia de Liquidez (FPC) em 50 pontos base, para 22,0%;  Reduzir a taxa de juro da Facilidade Permanente de Depsitos (FPD) em 50 pontos base, para 15,5%;  Reduzir o coeficiente de Reservas Obrigatrias para os passivos em moeda domstica e estrangeira em 100 pontos base, para 14,0%. Dependendo da evoluo dos indicadores econmico-financeiros e dos factores de risco, o CPMO poder tomar as medidas correctivas necessrias antes da prxima reunio do rgo, agendada para o dia 20 de Dezembro de 2017 Desde Junho at Outubro, tomamos duas medidas importantes de forma a fortalecer a solidez, transparncia e disciplina do mercado e das nossas instituies de crdito. Por um lado, reforamos a obrigatoriedade de as instituies de crdito divulgarem ao pblico os rcios de solvabilidade e de liquidez. Deste modo, a informao sobre esses indicadores passa a estar disponvel com maior frequncia ao pblico para que este possa acompanhar a sade das instituies de crdito. Por outro lado, o Banco de Moambique passa a publicar as sanes definitivas aplicadas as instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras. Principais Desafios para a tomada de decises  Existe sempre uma srie de riscos quer a nvel domstico quer a nvel internacional. A nvel nacional:  a incerteza quanto a magnitude do ajuste da poltica fiscal perante a confirmao da manuteno do congelamento e suspenso da ajuda externa directa ao Oramento do Estado.  a incerteza quanto ao impacto do ajuste de preos dos combustveis lquidos e outros bens e servios administrados;  a incerteza quanto aos efeitos climticos. A nvel internacional identificamos dois factores j conhecidos desde a ultima reunio do CPMO e certamente desde Junho.  o impacto da situao poltica na frica do Sul, nosso maior parceiro econmico e comercial;  o impacto da volatilidade dos preos das commodities com efeitos nos preos domsticos e na balana de pagamentos De acordo com a mais recente publicao do Instituto Nacional de Estatsticas (INE), o PIB continua a crescer de maneira moderada tendo registado um crescimento relativamente fraco no 1- semestre deste ano (3%), comparativamente ao perodo homologo de 2016 (acima de 5%). Registamos igualmente uma deteriorao do indicador do clima econmico no ms de Agosto, pelo segundo ms consecutivo, indiciando que actividade econmica continuar abaixo do potencial. Verificamos ainda a queda contnua da inflao anual, tendncia que se espera que se mantenha at Dezembro de 2017, merc da estabilidade do Metical e da fraca procura agregada. O ndice de difuso, que indica a proporo de produtos com variao mensal positiva de preos, comeou, pela primeira vez, a demonstrar uma tendncia ligeiramente positiva, desde Outubro de 2016. Isto, por sua vez, indica o incio da tendncia de riscos inflacionrios. O Metical manteve-se estvel desde o ltimo CPMO, continuando a favorecer a queda da inflao. A situao econmica do pas  reflectida no comportamento da moeda vis--vis as moedas dos nossos parceiros, em particular o dlar americano e o rand. Em relao ao endividamento do Estado, a dvida interna (que j  alta) continua com uma tendncia crescente, tendo aumentado em cerca de 5 mil milhes de meticais para cerca de 100 mil milhes de meticais como resultado, essencialmente, de uma maior utilizao de Bilhetes de Tesouro. A balana comercial continua favorvel reflectindo o impacto positivo da estabilidade do cmbio e do comportamento das reservas. A balana comercial que  tradicionalmente deficitria, apresenta uma tendncia cada vez mais decrescente. No terceiro trimestre de 2016 tnhamos um dfice de quase USD 1.5 bilies, tendo cado para cerca de USD 378 milhes, em igual perodo de 2017. Este  um ajuste extremamente acentuado liderado pelas exportaes, em particular, as dos grandes projectos. As importaes caram substancialmente, mas no tanto quanto a subida das exportaes, tendo registado uma queda de um pouco mais de USD 100 milhes, o que por sua vez ajuda bastante a nossa balana comercial, em particular, e a balana de pagamentos, no geral. Temos tambm notcias positivas que reflectem a combinao da conta da balana comercial, conta capital e o fluxo de capitais, em particular o investimento directo, que continua a aumentar. As reservas brutas situam-se em cerca de USD 2.5 bilies, o que equivale a um pouco mais de 6 meses de importaes de bens e servios. Isso significa que estamos a um a nvel confortvel de reservas, nvel esse que  internacionalmente estabelecido em 6 meses, sendo esta uma prtica e no de uma definio legal. Considera-se que um pas que tenha esse nvel de reserva, tem capacidade para lidar com pagamentos normais de servios da dvida. Prevalecem as perspectivas de desacelerao da inflao no ano corrente para um dgito, porm existem ainda riscos de agravamento de presses inflacionrias. Para 2018, esto previstos alguns riscos inflacionrios. Ns, na qualidade de legisladores, estamos incumbidos de acompanhar de perto esses riscos e tomar as medidas necessrias para assegurar que esses riscos no se materializem.  importante entender que como Banco Central temos uma postura extremamente conservadora em relao aos riscos inflacionrios e o nosso objectivo como Banco Central  alcanar uma inflao baixa. A inflao alta  um problema srio na sociedade. Os pobres ficam mais pobres e os ricos ficam mais ricos. A inflao cria tenses sociais enormes e ns como Banco Central continuaremos a tomar as medidas necessrias para que esta inflao, que poderia eventualmente surgir, no se materialize e no prejudique todos esses esforos que temos vindo a tomar desde os ltimos doze meses ou mais. Muito obrigado SESSO DE PERGUNTAS  Reduo da prime rate A definio de prime rate inclui tambm uma parte da taxa de juro que reflecte decises de poltica monetria sobretudo a taxa repo e est associada a taxa MIMO. Sendo assim,  de esperar que a prime rate reduza. No entanto, esta no  a nica componente da prime rate. Num cenrio ideal, sem alteraes, a prime rate tambm deveria cair como resultado das medidas tomadas, caso outros factores igualmente determinantes para a prime rate no se alterem. Esta  nossa expectativa, porm trata-se de uma combinao de decises de poltica, de mercado e das instituies de crdito. 0 Banco no fora uma prime rate.  Insustentabilidade das taxas de juro  nosso entender como Banco Central que as taxas de juro continuam altas e apesar de termos vindo a reduz-las, estas ainda no se encontram nos nveis desejados. Prevamos que nesta poca do ano as taxas de juro de curto prazo estivessem a nveis relativamente mais baixos. No entanto, devido a uma combinao de factores, quer domsticos quer internacionais bem como outros factores de risco, as condies no estavam criadas para que isso acontecesse. As taxas de juro constituem um assunto muito sensvel o qual temos debatido intensa e emocionalmente, com toda a paixo necessria. Indagamos constantemente formas de reduzir as taxas de juro para os nveis desejados pela sociedade e que so de facto necessrios. No entanto, esta deciso no se limita a poltica monetria, existe tambm a parte fiscal e as reformas. 0 processo da consolidao fiscal, e certas reformas que tem estado a decorrer, foi mais lento do que previsto. Estas condies so imperativas para a reduo das taxas de juro, sob o risco de retrocedermos em matria de reservas, volatilidade cambial e ainda aumentar a inflao. A inflao hoje est a caminho de um dgito como resultado da cautela que temos tido, da que continuaremos a ser prudentes. Queremos naturalmente reduzir as taxas de juro mais ainda do que j fizemos e no hesitaremos em faz-lo quando as condies estiverem criadas. No entanto, como havia referido anteriormente, existem ainda riscos inflacionrios, e no sabemos ao certo em que magnitude. No cumprimento do mandato que nos foi incumbido pelo legislador, se a avaliao tcnica da situao for tal que nos obrigue a tomar certas medidas com vista a manter uma inflao baixa e estvel, assim o faremos. Em suma, a reduo das taxas de juro no  uma deciso que o Banco Central tome de forma aleatria, ela reflecte uma anlise das condies da sociedade em todo o momento.  Dvida interna 0 nvel da dvida interna  claramente alto. Por vezes alarmamo-nos quando vemos certos indicadores de sustentabilidade, mas em ltima estncia  o mercado que decide. Quem compra a dvida  o mercado e este mercado podem ser tanto os bancos como as instituies de crditos ou ainda os cidados. Quando a dvida cresce  nossa obrigao acompanhar a reaco do mercado, pois este pode no estar disposto a comprar a dvida. Porm, no se trata de ter um nmero estabelecido que quando ultrapassado indica a deteriorao da dvida. A ttulo de exemplo, cada banco tem um nmero diferente porque cada instituio tem limites de compra da dvida do Estado. Por vrias razes, quer internas quer de gesto prpria de risco, os detentores desses ttulos decidem em alturas diferentes a compra da dvida.  Incluso dos efeitos climticos nas previses do BM Seria difcil isso acontecer. A nossa regio  propensa a problemas climticos. A nossa capacidade de prever aspectos climticos reflecte tambm a capacidade daqueles que fazem essas previses. Se  difcil para estes prever, isso significa que para ns com BM seria muito mais difcil ainda visto que no depende somente de ns. A capacidade de fazer previses nessas reas depende de outros profissionais e no de economistas.  Liquidez de banda excessiva 0 excesso de liquidez est associado ao crescimento das reservas. 0 Banco de Moambique aumentou as suas reservas estrangeiras e, em troca, injectou meticais na economia, o que causou o aumento de liquidez. Este aumento reflecte tambm o comportamento das actividades do Estado como Governo, como Banco Central e como empresa quando gastam mais e quando se financiam. Reflecte igualmente o comportamento do crdito na nossa economia. 0 crdito continua fraco e com um crescimento relativamente modesto, o que faz com que o excesso de liquidez, que devia ir para a economia, fique parado em instrumentos de liquidez. A liquidez no  necessariamente em dinheiro, ela  aplicada maioritariamente em instrumentos do Governo e nas Reverse Repo, que chamamos de instrumentos de curto prazo, nas Obrigaes do Tesouro e tambm nos Bilhetes de Tesouro. 0 ideal seria que essa liquidez excessiva fosse aplicada na economia, mas isso no cabe a ns decidir, no podemos forar o mercado nem direcionar o crdito. 0 que fazemos  sinalizar, mas em ltima estncia so as instituies de crdito que devem tomar essas decises atravs da sua avaliao de risco e dos seus planos de negcio.  Incerteza quanto ao financiamento do Estado em 2018 0 FMI decidiu manter o congelamento do financiamento ao nosso pas em 2018. Isso j no  um risco,  uma certeza e j foi tornado pblico. Os doadores, por sua vez, afirmam que sem um programa com o fundo no esto dispostos a retomar a ajuda, o que significa a continuidade dos problemas que tivemos em 2016. 0 oramento est sob grande presso e apesar de todo o esforo que a Autoridade Tributria tem feito, no  possvel, no curto-prazo, compensar estes cortes da ajuda externa ao pas. No compete ao BM tomar as decises necessrias para compensar esse tipo de ajuste derivado do cancelamento da ajuda externa.  tarefa do Governo liderado pelo Ministrio das Finanas. Certamente que o Governo trabalha arduamente para lidar com esta situao e encontrar medidas necessrias do ponto de vista de despesa, receitas, financiamento e reestruturao da dvida.  Questo da Probidade no caso Moza Eu j me pronuncie exaustivamente sobre esse assunto. A minha posio mantm-se, nada mudou. No tenho nada a acrescentar nem a retirar ao que j expliquei. No que me compete  um assunto encerrado. Como regulador, fizemos a entrega do Moza no dia 28 de Julho. Para mim foi particularmente um motivo de muito orgulho conseguirmos concluir com sucesso essa operao complicada e difcil que teria nos colocado numa situao bastante complicada. Trabalhamos arduamente, fomos criticados, mas isso faz parte do processo democrtico. Como reguladores temos que tomar medidas, independentemente dos comentrios. Eu, particularmente, assumo a 100% as decises que tomei. Para mim foi uma deciso de sucesso, foi a deciso acertada e necessria. As pessoas so livres de criticar, repito no me beneficiei em nada nessa operao nem os meus colegas. Essa foi a deciso milagrosamente certa porque requereu muito trabalho e criatividade da nossa parte para chegar a esse desfecho positivo. Esta  uma deciso da qual me orgulho. O processo est concludo e  irreversvel. Quando fizemos a entrega do Banco tratamos o Moza como qualquer banco, no comento sobre o BCI, sobre o BIM e no vou mais comentar sobre o Moza que para ns  um banco que funciona hoje na normalidade. Tiramos do sistema um risco sistmico que nos angustiava seriamente. Nada foi feito por engano. Tudo foi feito de forma intencional  Porqu os relatrios de venha da Kuhanha no esto disponveis para consulta pblica Isso no  deciso do BM mas sim da Kuhanha. A Kuhanha  uma sociedade de direito privado. Ela no  regida pelas mesmas leis do Banco. Certamente tudo que fazem est previsto nas leis que a rege. No h nenhuma ilegalidade na Kuhanha.  Critrios de seleco de investidores - caso Moza Houve um critrio para a recapitalizao do Moza e os investidores que no cumpriam os requisitos foram excludos. Esses investidores no reuniram as condies necessrios para investir no Moza e em nenhum outro banco no sistema. Constituam uma fonte de instabilidade e risco que no estvamos dispostos a assumir. Estes investidores poderiam trazer problemas srios para o pas e compete ao regulador e as instituies pblicas do estado, assegurar que os investidores que entram nas nossas instituies renam os requisitos de integridade necessrios. Caso contrrio entramos para a lista negra do mundo e isso tem consequncias srias. Quando entramos para a lista  extremamente difcil sair. Pela minha experincia, nenhum pas que entrou nessa lista conseguiu sair.  Moambique pode viver mais um ano sem ajuda Certamente podemos viver, mas ser uma vida difcil. Devido a deciso tomada pelo FMI vivemos um ambiente de riscos ainda mais elevados. Isso, por sua vez, requer reformas fiscais e outras de competitividade na economia ainda mais profundas.  algo srio e temos que trabalhar de forma mais intensa, duplicar os esforos e energias para lidar com essa nova realidade que  alcanar resultados positivos caminhando praticamente sozinhos do ponto de vista oramental. Por outro lado, isto complica a nossa capacidade de gesto da poltica monetria as nossas projeces tambm reflectem isso.  Traduzir a inflao de um dgito em nmeros Isso no  importante neste momento, tenhamos em mente que estamos a vir de uma inflao de 25%. Recordo-me que em Outubro de 2016, quando tomamos as grandes decises, a expectativa tambm era em torno da inflao. Temos tendncia a ser um pouco relutantes em relao a isso e concentramo-nos nos nmeros. J estivemos a caminho de uma inflao que chegaria a 30% no final do ano se no tivssemos sido draconianos e tomado as medidas quase inditas que tomamos. Se tivessem me perguntado na altura onde iramos terminar, confesso que terminamos melhor que a minha expectativa. No momento de incertezas existem muitas variantes e no seria justo que indicssemos um nmero. A grande notcia que temos a transmitir  que com uma inflao de 25% que caminhava, sem tomada de medidas, para 30% at o final do ano, hoje temos uma inflao, no final de 2017, de um dgito.  Previso de crescimento para 2019 Do lado fiscal  necessria uma combinao de medidas do ponto de vista da administrao de receitas, das vrias componentes das despesas (correntes e no correntes), de reformas, sobretudo no tocante a competitividade. O governo aprovou recentemente uma nova lei do sector empresarial que certamente constituir um instrumento poderoso na consolidao das contas das empresas pblicas. Esforos adicionais esto a ser feitos fora do pas no que toca a restruturao da dvida externa. Vrias medidas esto a ser tomadas, no entanto, no me considero a pessoa indicada para responder a essa questo. Esta  uma resposta que compete ao Ministro que tutela essa pasta.  Factores de risco Existem riscos significantes que poderamos encontrar numa situao de inflao de dois dgitos em 2018, por isso estamos preparados para fazer o que for necessrio para que isso no se materialize. Teoricamente  fcil falar em corte de despesas, aumento de receitas, mas a implementao em si  complexa. Existem muitos grupos de interesse.  necessrio estarmos atentos para a situao e tomar as medidas necessrias em caso de materializao dos riscos.  uma grande vitria para ns chegar a uma inflao de um dgito. Moambique e Angola tem uma das inflaes mais altas do continente e, a nvel regional, somos vistos como uma fonte de instabilidade. Com excepo de Moambique e Angola a inflao em muitos pases da regio est abaixo dos 10%. Temos que fazer a nossa parte de modo a contribuir para a estabilidade da regio e posso lhes garantir que os nossos vizinhos acompanham o que estamos a fazer. De certeza que estes iro aplaudir quando entrarmos no clube de inflao baixa como resultado do esforo e sacrifcio que a sociedade fez para que isso acontecesse. Quando a inflao  alta os preos tambm so instveis dificultando investimentos e negcios no pas. Temos que tirar esse risco para que a sociedade e nossos parceiros trabalhem connosco em situao de normalidade.

Title: End of the Economic Year 2017
text: INTERVENTION OF YOUR EXCELENCEROGeRIO ZANDAMELA, GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE ON THE OCCASION OF THE TOAST ALRELATED TO THE END OF THE ECONOMIC YEAR LOCATION: BM'S OFFICE Maputo, 18 December 2017 Former Governors of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellencies Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Former Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Representatives of State Institutions, Representatives of International Cooperation Partners, Presidents of the Boards of Directors and Executive Committees of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, Directors and other Managers of the Bank of Mozambique Distinguished Guests; Ladies, and My Lords, Good afternoon! It is with high honor that, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, I greet all those present at this year-end toast ceremony, which takes place for the first time in our new facilities, wishing everyone to enjoy the beauty of the view that this building provides. With this event we intend to make the preliminary balance of 2017 and prospect the year 2018, in macroeconomic terms. On this balance sheet occasion, I would like to thank the Government, credit institutions and financial corporations operating in the country, the private sector , economic and socio-professional associations, the academic community, international cooperation partners and the media, for their continued collaboration with the Bank of Mozambique, which has contributed to a large extent to a large extent. to fulfill our mission to preserve the value of our currency, the Metical, and ensure the stability of the financial sector . Ladies, ladies and gentlemen, In the year that is about to end, there was a gradual return to normality of economic and financial indicators, which had degraded substantially in the previous year. These improvements are largely a reflection of the vigorous measures we have taken to re-place macroeconomic stability, which have also been called for important measures and reforms initiated by our Government in the framework of public policies aimed at stabilising our economy. Thus, annual inflation, as measured by the evolution of mozambique's general price index, slowed significantly from the peak of 27%, observed in November 2016, to 7.15% in the same month of 2017, reflecting the effect of restrictive monetary policy on aggregate demand, without neglecting the fiscal consolidation measures implemented by the Government on various price subsidies, in a context where domestic fruit and vegetable production has increased. Throughout 2017, The Metical exchange rate against the major international currencies traded in the Mozambican foreign exchange market was quite stable, with Metical recording a significant recovery, such as the price against the U.S. Dollar, which fell from almost 80.00 meticais in September 2016 to about 60.00 meticais per U.S. dollar, currently. The introduction of the reference exchange rate and the principle of exchange rate uniqueness favoured the desideratum of exchange rate stability, in addition to strengthening transparency and competitiveness in the market. Our international reserves increased substantially in the year under review, thanks to improved Mozambican exports and the confidence of economic agents.
