To these factors, in addition, the recent entry of capital gains in favour of the State in the amount of US352 million, bringing the balance of our gross reserves to just over THREE trillion dollars to date, with the level of coverage of imports of non-factorious goods and services close to 7 months, when in December 2016 this indicator was slightly below 3 months. Ladies and gentlemen, in the first quarter of 2017 we changed the mechanism for formulating and implementing monetary policy, introducing the monetary policy interest rate, MIMO rate, which guides the interbank monetary market intervention mechanism, replacing the monetary base, until then the operational variable of monetary policy. The MIMO rate is the basis for determining the single indexing that all banks have undertaken to adopt in the process of determining loan interest rates, through the agreement initialled between the Bank of Mozambique, the commercial banks and the Mozambican Association of Banks. From this index, the financial system started to have a uniform prime interest rate, and its regular disclosure by the vast public allowed to strengthen transparency, as well as promote greater competitiveness in the market. After the interventions we made in 2016 to two credit institutions, in view of the serious solvency problems they had, today our financial system is more robust and capitalised to cope with shocks, with the solvency ratio of the system around 20%, well above the 8% regulated by the Basel I and II principles. robust and robust, under prudential measures we have strengthened the minimum capital for credit institutions, with emphasis on the minimum share capital of banks, we have changed the composition of the credit institutions' own funds, we have increased the prudential ratios and limits of credit institutions, with emphasis on increasing the solvency ratio of banks, and introduced the liquidity ratio to monitor liquidity levels in the banking system. In so that citizens can measure on their very two-off the level of robustness of the institutions, we have introduced the from March this year the requirement for banks to regularly publish information on their solvency and liquidity levels. We also introduce the principle of publication by the Bank of Mozambique of the name of financial institutions that have been penalised as a result of infringements they have committed in the performance of their duties. In the field of the implementation of the Financial Sector Development Strategy, and more specifically with regard to the materialization of the objectives of our National Financial Inclusion Strategy, we have operationalized the National Committee for Financial Inclusion, with the formalization of the working groups and the holding of its first working meeting. We are convinced that, with this stage, the conditions are created for the further improvement of the levels of financial inclusion in the country, especially with regard to physical or electronic access to financial services provided by financial institutions and territorial expansion at the level of districts and localities. Within the framework of the issuing function, and taking the opportunity of the commemorative date of our coin, we launched the 2017 Series of Notes of the Metical, which maintains the same characteristics of quality and safety as the previous 2011, presenting only as new elements the signature and the date. On the other hand, in the ongoing effort to improve internal working conditions, and with a view to continuing to ensure an appropriate provision of services to the State and banking institutions, while ensuring adequate preparation for regional integration, were inaugurated by His Excellency Mr. President of the Republic Filipe Jacinto Nyusi, here at the seat of the Bank of Mozambique a complex of three modern buildings, internationally required standards to the banking industry. Ladies and gentlemen, With the aim of creating greater synergies between foreign and national investment, within a framework of greater equal opportunities, within the scope of the powers that the Government has given us we have issued very recently a Notice introducing significant changes in the Exchange Rate Regulation, aimed at providing greater flexibility and speed in transactions with the outside, without respecting the principles of registration, duty of verification and full exercise of the function of foreign exchange authority reserved to the Bank of Mozambique. Moreover, in this wake, we had already liberalized at the beginning of the year the limits of the use of electronic payment cards by all customers of the Mozambican financial system, until then set at 700,000 meticais. It is our belief that these steps give greater responsibility to all actors in foreign exchange transactions, but on the other hand they have an immeasurable multiplier effect on the further growth of investments in our country, whether by foreign economic agents or by nationals. Despite the positive results I have just underlined, macroeconomic stability needs to be strengthened. Thus, relaunching economic activity to the average growth patterns we had been experiencing will continue to require reforms, fiscal discipline and selfless work from all Mozambicans. Until the third quarter of this year, the economy grew only 3%, when, in the 8 years prior to 2016, it had been growing around 7%. In addition, despite the efforts made in the tax collection, state revenues remain below what is necessary to finance expenditure, resonating from the suspension of direct support to the budget by donors and cooperation partners, an aspect that poses increased challenges to the tax sector. Ladies, ladies and gentlemen, for the coming year, monetary policy will be geared towards maintaining low and controlled inflation at the single digit level, with room, yet and on the size and speed of the implementation of the projected fiscal reforms, so that it is suficipentemente flexible and prudently decompressed, thus contributing to the private sector of the economy being the main beneficiary of the few financial resources that our system has, which, if it comes to fruition, will reflect the joint effort of all of us for the sake of the recovery of our economy in the near future. At the level of the financial sector, we will strengthen macroprudential surveillance to monitor the potential risks that may affect it, as well as microprudential, so that all institutions comply with international good practice and strictly comply with our recommendations and standards, within the framework of onsite and offsite supervision on the basis of basel II principles and risk, to prevent the degradation of the financial health of institutions. Also in the context of efforts to maintain financial stability, we will introduce regulatory reforms aimed at mitigating the risk arising from the growing exposure of Mozambican financial institutions to foreign operations. These prudential measures are in line with that advocated by the Basel Committee for strengthening supervision in the field of cross-border activity of the institutions, given their potential to transmit external shocks to the financial systems of the countries concerned. We will also submit to the Government a proposal to revise the Law of Credit Institutions and Financial Companies, more adjusted to a banking resolution regime appropriate for the Mozambican case and following international good practice, which will make our action more flexible in case of need for intervention to correct situations of instability of credit institutions. However, the achievement of these objectives requires the contribution of all of us - the financial system, companies and the government - so that it is possible to overcome the risks that are envisaged in the short to medium term horizon, both domestic and international lyconitude, which, if not taken care of, can put at risk all the stability reached. In our view, the main challenges for the materialisation of the objectives already announced include maintaining a lasting peace, continuing fiscal consolidation efforts already initiated with the recent package of rationalisation of expenditure, the non-occurrence of climate shocks and the stability of commodity prices on the international market. I will therefore end my speech, thanking everyone for their presence and making wishes for happy feasts and a prosperous 2018 for all of you and your esteemed families! Thank you so much for your attention! Maputo, 18 December 2017
text_original: INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELENCIA ROGRIO ZANDAMELA, GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE POR OCASIO DO BRINDE ALUSIVO AO ENCERRAMENTO DO ANO ECONMICO LOCAL: SEDE DO BM Maputo, 18 de Dezembro de 2017 Antigos Governadores do Banco de Moambique, Excelncias Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique Senhores Antigos Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique Senhores Representantes de Instituies do Estado Senhores Parceiros de Cooperao Internacional Senhores Presidentes dos Conselhos de Administrao e das Comisses Executivas das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras Senhores Directores e demais Gestores do Banco de Moambique Distintos Convidados; Minhas Senhoras, e Meus Senhores, Boa tarde!  com elevada honra que, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome, cumprimento todos os presentes nesta cerimnia de brinde de fim de ano, que tem lugar pela primeira vez nas nossas novas instalaes, desejando a todos que desfrutem, de seguida, da beleza da vista que este edifcio proporciona. Com este evento pretendemos fazer o balano preliminar de 2017 e perspectivar o ano de 2018, em termos macroeconmicos. Nesta ocasio de balano, gostaria de enderear os nossos agradecimentos ao Governo, s instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras que operam no Pas, ao sector privado, s associaes econmicas e socioprofissionais,  comunidade acadmica, aos parceiros de cooperao internacional e  comunicao social, pela contnua colaborao prestada ao Banco de Moambique, a qual tem contribudo, em grande medida, para o cumprimento da nossa misso de preservar o valor da nossa moeda, o Metical, e assegurar a estabilidade do sector financeiro. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, No ano que est prestes a findar, assistiu-se a um retorno gradual  normalidade dos indicadores econmicos e financeiros, que se haviam degradado substancialmente no ano anterior. Estas melhorias so, em grande parte, o reflexo das medidas vigorosas que tommos visando repor a estabilidade macroeconmica, que contaram tambm com o concurso de medidas e reformas importantes encetadas pelo nosso Governo, no quadro de polticas pblicas orientadas  estabilizao da nossa economia. Desta forma, a inflao anual, medida pela evoluo do ndice geral de preos de Moambique, desacelerou significativamente do pico de 27%, observado em Novembro de 2016, para 7,15% em igual ms de 2017, traduzindo o efeito da poltica monetria restritiva sobre a procura agregada, sem descurar as medidas de consolidao fiscal implementadas pelo Governo em matria de subsdios diversos aos preos, num contexto em que a produo interna de frutas e vegetais incrementou. Ao longo de 2017, a taxa de cmbio do Metical face s principais moedas internacionais transaccionadas no mercado cambial moambicano apresentou-se bastante estvel, estando o Metical a registar uma recuperao assinalvel, a exemplo da cotao contra o Dlar dos Estados Unidos da Amrica, que baixou de quase 80,00 meticais em Setembro de 2016 para cerca de 60,00 meticais por dlar dos Estados Unidos da Amrica, actualmente. A introduo da taxa de cmbio de referncia e do princpio de unicidade de taxa de cmbio favoreceu o desiderato de estabilidade cambial, para alm de ter reforado a transparncia e a competitividade no mercado. As nossas reservas internacionais incrementaram substancialmente no ano em revista, merc da melhoria das exportaes moambicanas e da confiana dos agentes econmicos. A estes factores acresce mencionar a entrada recente de mais-valias a favor do Estado no valor de 352 milhes de dlares dos Estados Unidos da Amrica, elevando o saldo das nossas reservas brutas para pouco mais trs bilies de dlares at a presente data, estando o nvel de cobertura de importaes de bens e servios no factoriais prximo de 7 meses, quando em Dezembro de 2016 este indicador se situava ligeiramente abaixo de 3 meses. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, No primeiro trimestre de 2017 altermos o mecanismo de formulao e implementao da poltica monetria, tendo introduzido a taxa de juro de poltica monetria, taxa MIMO, que guia o mecanismo de intervenes no Mercado Monetrio Interbancrio, em substituio da base monetria, at ento a varivel operacional da poltica monetria. A taxa MIMO constitui a base para a determinao do indexante nico que todos os bancos se comprometeram a adoptar no processo de determinao das taxas de juro de emprstimo, atravs do acordo rubricado entre o Banco de Moambique, os bancos comerciais e a Associao Moambicana de Bancos. A partir desse indexante, o sistema financeiro passou a ter uma taxa de juro prime uniforme, e a sua divulgao regular pelo vasto pblico permitiu reforar a transparncia, assim como promover uma maior competitividade no mercado. Depois das intervenes que fizemos em 2016 a duas instituies de crdito, em face dos graves problemas de solvabilidade que as mesmas apresentavam, hoje o nosso sistema financeiro se mostra mais slido e capitalizado para fazer face a choques, estando o rcio de solvabilidade do sistema em redor de 20%, bem acima dos 8% regulamentados pelos princpios de Basileia I e II. Ainda na perspectiva de continuar a ter um sistema financeiro mais robusto e slido, no mbito das medidas prudenciais reformos os capitais mnimos para as instituies de crdito, com destaque para o capital social mnimo dos bancos, altermos a composio dos fundos prprios das instituies de crdito, elevmos os rcios e limites prudenciais das instituies de crdito, com destaque para o incremento do rcio de solvabilidade dos bancos, e introduzimos o rcio de liquidez para monitorar nveis de liquidez no sistema bancrio. Para que os cidados possam aferir por si ss o nvel de robustez das instituies, introduzimos a partir de Maro deste ano a obrigatoriedade de os bancos publicarem regularmente a informao sobre os seus nveis de solvabilidade e de liquidez. Introduzimos, igualmente, o princpio de publicao, pelo Banco de Moambique, do nome das instituies financeiras que tenham sido penalizadas em decorrncia de infraces que tenham cometido no exerccio das respectivas funes. No domnio da implementao da Estratgia de Desenvolvimento do Sector Financeiro, e mais concretamente no que concerne  materializao dos objectivos da nossa Estratgia Nacional de Incluso Financeira, operacionalizmos o Comit Nacional de Incluso Financeira, com a formalizao dos grupos de trabalho e a realizao do seu primeiro encontro de trabalho. Estamos convictos de que, com esta etapa, esto criadas as condies para a continuao da melhoria dos nveis de incluso financeira no Pas, principalmente no que diz respeito ao acesso fsico ou electrnico aos servios financeiros prestados pelas instituies financeiras e  expanso territorial ao nvel dos distritos e localidades. No mbito da funo emissora, e tomando o ensejo da data comemorativa da nossa moeda, lanmos a Srie 2017 de notas do Metical, que mantm as mesmas caractersticas de qualidade e segurana que a anterior de 2011, apresentando apenas como novos elementos a assinatura e a data. Por outro lado, no esforo permanente de melhoria das condies internas de trabalho, e tendo em vista continuar a garantir uma apropriada prestao de servios ao Estado e s instituies bancrias, ao mesmo tempo assegurando uma adequada preparao para a integrao regional, foram inaugurados por Sua Excelncia Senhor Presidente da Repblica Filipe Jacinto Nyusi, aqui na sede do Banco de Moambique um complexo de trs edifcios modernos, que respondem aos padres exigidos internacionalmente  indstria bancria. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Com o objectivo de criar maiores sinergias entre o investimento estrangeiro e nacional, num quadro de maior igualdade de oportunidades, no mbito das competncias que o Governo nos atribuiu emitimos muito recentemente um Aviso que introduz alteraes significativas no Regulamento Cambial, orientadas a proporcionar maior flexibilidade e celeridade nas transacces com o exterior, sem perigar os princpios de registo, de dever de verificao e de exerccio pleno da funo de autoridade cambial reservada ao Banco de Moambique. Alis, nesta esteira, j havamos liberalizado nos princpios do ano os limites de utilizao de cartes de pagamento electrnico por todos os clientes do sistema financeiro moambicano, at ento fixado em setecentos mil meticais.  nossa convico que estes passos conferem maior responsabilidade a todos os intervenientes nas transacces cambiais, mas, por outro lado, tm um efeito multiplicador incomensurvel na dinamizao dos investimentos no nosso pas, seja por agentes econmicos estrangeiros, seja por nacionais. No obstante os resultados positivos que acabo de sublinhar, a estabilidade macroeconmica precisa de ser reforada. Assim, relanar a actividade econmica para os padres mdios de crescimento que vnhamos registando vai continuar a exigir reformas, disciplina fiscal e trabalho abnegado de todos os moambicanos. At ao terceiro trimestre do presente ano, a economia cresceu apenas 3%, quando, nos 8 anos anteriores a 2016, a mesma vinha crescendo em redor de 7%. Adicionalmente, apesar dos esforos empreendidos na colecta de impostos, as receitas do Estado continuam aqum do necessrio para financiar as despesas, ressentindo-se da suspenso do apoio directo ao oramento por parte dos doadores e parceiros de cooperao, aspecto que coloca desafios acrescidos ao sector fiscal. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Para o ano que se avizinha, a poltica monetria ser orientada para a manuteno de uma inflao baixa e controlada, ao nvel de um dgito, havendo espao, ainda assim e na dimenso e velocidade da execuo das reformas fiscais projectadas, para que a mesma seja sufcentemente flexvel e prudentemente descomprimida, contribuindo deste modo para que o sector privado da economia seja o principal beneficirio dos poucos recursos financeiros que o nosso sistema possui, o que, a concretizar-se, reflectir o esforo conjunto de todos ns a bem da retoma da nossa economia a breve trecho. Ao nvel do sector financeiro, reforaremos a vigilncia macroprudencial, para monitorarmos os riscos potenciais que possam afect-lo, bem assim a microprudencial, para que todas as instituies observem as boas prticas internacionais e cumpram rigorosamente com as nossas recomendaes e normas, no mbito da superviso onsite e offsite com base nos princpios de Basileia II e no risco, visando evitar a degradao da sade financeira das instituies. Ainda no mbito dos esforos de manuteno da estabilidade financeira, vamos introduzir reformas regulatrias visando mitigar o risco decorrente da crescente exposio das instituies financeiras moambicanas s operaes com o exterior. Estas medidas prudenciais esto alinhadas com o preconizado pelo Comit de Basileia para o reforo da superviso no domnio da actividade transfronteirica das instituies, dado o seu potencial para transmitir choques externos aos sistemas financeiros dos pases envolvidos. Submeteremos, igualmente, ao Governo uma proposta de reviso da Lei das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras, mais ajustada a um regime de resoluo bancria adequado para o caso moambicano e seguindo as boas prticas internacionais, o que ir flexibilizar a nossa actuaco em caso de necessidade de interveno para correco de situaes de instabilidade das instituies de crdito. Contudo, o alcance destes objectivos exige a contribuio de todos ns - o sistema financeiro, as empresas e o governo -, para que seja possvel vencer os riscos que se vislumbram no horizonte de curto a mdio prazos, tanto de conjuntura domstica como de conjuntura internacional, os quais, se no acautelados, podem colocar em risco toda a estabilidade alcancada. Em nosso entender, os principais desafios para a materializao dos objectivos j anunciados incluem a manuteno de uma paz duradoura, a continuao dos esforos de consolidao fiscal j iniciados com o recente pacote de racionalizao de despesas, a no ocorrncia de choques climticos e a estabilidade dos preos das mercadorias no mercado internacional. Termino, assim, a minha interveno, agradecendo a presena de todos e formulando votos de festas felizes e um prspero 2018 para todos vs e as vossas estimadas famlias! Muito obrigado pela ateno! Maputo, 18 de Dezembro de 2017

Title: Speech at the Inauguration of the Moza Banco Agency in Lichinga
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENcy THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, ROGeRIO ZANDAMELA INAUGURATION OF MOZA BANCO IN AGENCY Lichinga Lichinga, 26 January 2018 Mr Governor of the Province of Niassa, Excellency, Mr President of the City Council of Lichinga, Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency, Honourable Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Mr President of the Board of Directors of Moza Banco, Honourable Members of the Board of Directors of Moza Banco, Dear Representatives of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and gentlemen, I extend my greetings to all those present at this opening ceremony of moza banco's first branch in the city of Lichinga, and I thank you, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, for the invitation that was given to us to participate in this event, which has the happy coincidence that it will take place at a time when the bank's managers and technicians are in this part of the country, in the context of the holding of the Advisory Board of our institution. Let me address our congratulations to Moza Banco, its employees, managers and members of the board of directors, represented by its President, Dr. Joao Figueiredo, for the initiative to open this agency. As you know, Moza Banco faced very difficult moments, which were the health of the entire financial system, which forced us, as a regulatory institution, to make an intervention in October 2016. Therefore, the opening of this agency is a clear reconfirmation of what we have been saying, that is, that we have succeeded, with the support and patience of all Mozambicans, to successfully complete the intervention process, thus returning this institution to the market with adequate stability and liquidity. In this context, we would like to call on the managers of this institution to guide them with rigour and prudence in management, always pondering between territorial expansion, in response to our calls for the bankof the country, and its financial capacity. We believe that the opening of this agency will improve the indicators of financial inclusion, which in niassa province have very low levels when compared to the rest of the country. Just to illustrate, at the end of 2017 the province of Niassa had a total of 20 branches, representing less than 3% of the country's total of 679, 64 ATM, out of a total of 1507, and only about 153,000 bank accounts, for more than four million nationwide. These figures mirror the supply gap of financial institutions in Niassa, which is compounded when we assess the potential of their economic activity. Moreover, the study we presented this morning on our Advisory Board reveals a huge potential for the production and marketing of agricultural products, which will certainly require an increasing presence of credit institutions in this province. The implementation of this agency is an effective stimulus to healthy competition between the financial institutions located here, and, in this way, a contribution to improving the quality of banking services provided to economic operators and the general population. I also use this opportunity to welcome the commitment of credit institutions authorized to operate in Mozambique, which, as moza banco here today provides us, have been contributing to the provision of financial services in decent and secure conditions. The economic agents and the population of this city, which from today on, have another bank branch, which will certainly further boost economic activity through financial intermediation, thereby contributing to the development of niassa province, the city of Lichinga and the country. I end my speech by reiterating our congratulations to Moza Banco and wishing it many successes. Thank you very much! Maputo, 26 January 2018
text_original: INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELNCIA O GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE, ROGRIO ZANDAMELA INAUGURAO DA AGNCIA DO MOZA BANCO EM LICHINGA Lichinga, 26 de Janeiro de 2018 Senhor Governador da Provncia de Niassa, Excelncia Excelentssimo Senhor Presidente do Conselho Municipal da Cidade de Lichinga, Senhor Vice-Governador do Banco de Moambique, Excelncia Excelentssimos Senhores Administradores do Banco de Moambique, Excelentssimo Senhor Presidente do Conselho de Administrao do Moza Banco, Excelentssimos Senhores Membros do Conselho de Administrao do Moza Banco, Estimados Representantes das Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras, Distintos Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Apresento as minhas saudaes a todos os presentes nesta cerimnia de inaugurao da primeira agncia do Moza Banco na cidade de Lichinga, e agradeo, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome, o convite que nos foi formulado para participar neste evento, que tem a feliz coincidncia de ocorrer numa altura em que os gestores e tcnicos do Banco se encontram nesta parte do Pas, no contexto da realizao do Conselho Consultivo da nossa instituio. Permitam-me que enderece as nossas felicitaes ao Moza Banco, seus colaboradores, gestores e membros do conselho de administrao, representados pelo seu Presidente, Dr. Joo Figueiredo, pela iniciativa de abertura desta agncia. Como  do conhecimento de Vossas Excelncias, o Moza Banco enfrentou momentos muito difceis, que perigavam a sade de todo o sistema financeiro, o que nos obrigou, como instituio reguladora, a fazer uma interveno em Outubro de 2016. Assim sendo, a abertura desta agncia  uma clara reconfirmao do que temos vindo a dizer, ou seja, que conseguimos, com o apoio e a pacincia de todos os moambicanos, concluir o processo de interveno com sucesso, devolvendo assim esta instituio ao mercado com estabilidade e liquidez adequada. Neste contexto, gostaramos de apelar aos gestores desta instituio a pautarem por rigor e prudncia na gesto, ponderando sempre entre a expanso territorial, em resposta aos nossos apelos para a bancarizao do pas, e a sua capacidade financeira. Acreditamos que a abertura desta agncia ir melhorar os indicadores de incluso financeira, que na provncia de Niassa apresentam nveis muito baixos, quando comparados com o resto do pas. S para ilustrar, em finais de 2017 a provncia de Niassa apresentava um total de 20 agncias, o que representa menos de 3% do total de 679 existentes no pas, 64 ATM, de um total de 1507, e apenas cerca de 153 mil contas bancrias, para mais de quatro milhes em todo o pas. Estes nmeros espelham o dfice de oferta de instituies financeiras em Niassa, o que  agravado quando avaliamos o potencial da sua actividade econmica. Alis, o estudo que apresentmos na manh de hoje, no nosso Conselho Consultivo, revela um potencial enorme de produo e comercializao de produtos agrcolas, que, certamente, vai exigir uma cada vez maior presena de instituies de crdito nesta provncia. A implantao desta agncia constitui um efectivo estmulo  concorrncia saudvel entre as instituies financeiras aqui localizadas, e, por essa via, um contributo para a melhoria da qualidade dos servios bancrios prestados aos agentes econmicos e  populao em geral. Uso ainda esta oportunidade para saudar o empenho das instituies de crdito autorizadas a operar em Moambique, as quais,  semelhana do que o Moza Banco hoje aqui nos proporciona, tm estado a contribuir para o provimento de servios financeiros em condies condignas e de segurana. Esto tambm de parabns os agentes econmicos e a populao desta cidade, que, a partir de hoje, passam a contar com mais uma agncia bancria, que ir com certeza impulsionar ainda mais a actividade econmica atravs da intermediao financeira, contribuindo desse modo para o desenvolvimento da provncia de Niassa, da cidade de Lichinga e do pas. Termino a minha interveno reiterando as nossas felicitaes ao Moza Banco e desejando- lhe muitos sucessos. Muito obrigado! Maputo, 26 de Janeiro de 2018

Title: Press Conference Transcript - MPC, February 26, 2018
text: in Mozambique The CPMO met today, February 26, 2018, to assess recent macroeconomic developments, domestic and international, until February 23, 2018, as well as the projections of the main macroeconomic indicators for the end of this year, having taken monetary policy measures considered appropriate. The continued improvement of the inflation outlook for the medium term justifies the further reduction in interest rates. Thus, the CPMO deliberated:  Reduce the monetary policy interest rate, MIMO rate, by 150 basis points, to 18.0%;  Reduce the interest rate of the Permanent Liquidity-Of-Liquidity Facility (FPC) by 150 basis points to 19.0%;  Reduce the interest rate of the Permanent Deposit Facility (FPD) by 150 basis points to 12.5%; Furthermore, in view of the pressure observed in the foreign exchange market, the CPMO deliberated: Increase the coefficient of Mandatory Reserves for liabilities in foreign currency, by 800 basis points, to 22.0%, having maintained the coefficient for liabilities in national currency at 14.0%. The agency considers that the pressure on the foreign exchange market reflects the combined effects of the volatility of the main currencies in the international market and the adjustment to the paradigm of greater opening of capital flows, contemplated in the new regulation of the Exchange Law. Depending on developments in economic and financial indicators and risk factors, the CPMO may take the necessary corrective measures before the next meeting of the body, scheduled for 30 April 2018. Between December 2017 and February 2018, the Board of Directors took the following measures:  Notice No. 19/2017 on the Financial Services Commissionand Charges Scheme; and  Notice No 20/2017 on Exchange Standards and Procedures Main challenges of the decisions of the Monetary Policy Committee At home we have, firstly, the effect of the heavy rains that have affected the country and, secondly, the sustainability of debt. Internationally we have the volatility of commodity and dollar prices in international markets. In 2017, GDP grew moderately around 3%. The sectoral distribution of GDP is mainly led by the growth of the primary sector in agriculture, fisheries and extractive sector which has experienced extremely strong growth followed by tertiary growth in its components of trade, transport, financial services and others. The graph [of quarterly GDP developments] shows us this moderate GDP growth in 2017, which, although moderate, is within the region's standards and, in particular, above the average of our SADC partners, which recorded GDP growth of 2.8%, compared to Mozambican GDP growth of 3.7%. The economic climate recovered substantially in the fourth quarter of 2017, measured by the optimism of entrepreneurs regarding the prospects of economic activity, in particular in its price, employment and other factors including demand. Inflation continues to slow. In January it was around 3.84%. A year ago we had an annual level of inflation, annual inflation, above 20%, having fallen substantially, which is reflected in the reduction in the cost of living of consumers, of the Mozambican citizen. Purchasing power has been added to the country's consumers. It is therefore positive news that clearly affects the optimism that is observed within entrepreneurs. The risk factor that was represented by high and unstable inflation today has significantly reduced. Core inflation is below aggregate overall inflation. Excluding fruits and vegetables, factors that tend to have higher volatility or seasonality, inflation is 2.36% well below overall inflation of 2.84%. The big challenge we have had since January 2018 is that the foreign exchange market is under relatively increasing pressure over time. The metical shows mixed behavior having devalued 12.28%, against the dollar, 1.68% against the Rand and appreciated against the Euro. Also in this period of pressurethe Central Bank sold foreign exchange in the foreign exchange market, in net terms, which means that in January and February sales were higher than purchases in the amount of more than 87.5 million dollars, which means that the Central Bank lost reserves in that amount. However, in general, until a certain point in the first quarter of the year, with the exception of last year, seasonality always shows a relative loss of reserves. It is the dry period from the point of view of our exports. Traditionally we exportless in the Iquarter compared to the remaining quarters of the year. In this particular case, the situation is slightly different because there are other factors that are added to the seasonality of exports. Meanwhile, the current account deficit continues to improve, having reduced from around USD 4 million in 2016 to USD 2,542 million in 2017, representing a 35% drop in the current account deficit. This is good news and implies an overall improvement in our external account due in large part to large projects that continue to export large volumes of goods. When major projects are excluded, exports are up modestly 8%. Including major projects growth increases to 54%. Imports of goods and services grew by 9.5% while imports from large projects declined. Domestic debt remained high raising sustainability issues and increased from 98 billion meticais in December to 104.6 billion meticais in February. Interbank Money Market interest rates continue to fall and converge on the MIMO rate, reinforcing the flag element of the MIMO rate. This phenomenon has become quite noticeable this year as with the substantial drop in inflation expectations, all other rates have fallen, including BTs. In 2016, for 364-day BTs the rate was more or less than 27%, compared to 91-day BTs, which was 24%, and the MIMO rate at the time was lower than that. With the successes achieved in the area of inflation and the improvement in inflation expectations has made rates begin to converge and are now practically at the same level. Short-term and one-year rates are virtually at the same level. This is an important fact of the success and credibility of monetary policy that has been achieved with much effort from all of us. The increased liquidity has decreased. In the past, one of the major challenges we had was the increasing liquidity in the market. Today, after several months, we have a substantial reduction in liquidity in the banking market. Liquidity fell substantially from almost 36 billion in January to 14 billion in February, while in 2016 it was only growing. We were living what we call long liquidity, which is excess liquidity. We are moving towards a situation of lower liquidity in the market due, in a way, to the behavior of the foreign exchange market. A considerable part of this liquidity that came out of the interbank market entered the interbank foreign exchange market through the purchase of foreign exchange by banking and economic agents. There is a fall of more than USD 300 million in a short period of time in terms of bank liquidity. Credit to the economy is in snare. As monetary aggregates grow, credit to the economy continues to slow, with the rest of the credit going to the public sector. That is why we say it is important to adjust the tax bills to create space for available credit to pass more to the private sector. While credit to the private sector fell the public sector was the largest consumer of credit. For 2018 we expect single-digit inflation, as we said in our communique in December, and continued moderate GDP growth. I will end my presentation here of the deliberations of the Monetary Policy Committee today and I put myself at your disposal to clarify any matter relating to the deliberations of the Monetary Policy Committee. QUESTION SESSION First of all, I would like to clarify that from this year on, at cpmo meetings we will limit to discussing and clarifying issues related to the deliberations of the body. It does not mean that we will not answer the other questions, but this is not the appropriate forum. We will have the opportunity to at least twice a year discuss other issues that are not related to the CPMO in a more open way. We will follow international practice, which is to limit the CPMO to the deliberations of the body and the other matters we deal with separately. We're not doing anything different. It's common practice. So we haven't lost focus, as there are already other forums to deal with other issues.  On the increase in public debt Clearly it is growing and when that happens there are sustainability issues. This is not the first time we have discussed this subject here and I remember that when we talked about it one of you asked how sustainability was defined, if there was a number and what would then be the magical value that alerts the system. My answer was that there were several discussions in this, even academic, that look at past experiences to define more or less what is considered sustainable. There are also several indicators for this, but ultimately it depends on the willingness of economic operators, in particular banks and other investors, to want to buy this debt from the state. State debt is an asset in someone's portfolio (banks, pension funds and other investors) when they think the debt is starting to reach worrying levels they stop buying. All these institutions (banks, pension funds, investors) have scripts that set the maximum amount of investment for each type of debt. When that time comes they stop. The state is starting to get into trouble. We don't know when this is going to happen. This depends on economic agents and varies from country to country depending on the risks involved. When debt begins to rise from one level to another we begin to think, to what extent economic agents will be willing to continue to put that instrument into the portfolio as an investment asset for you.  Fees for the use of ATM services This issue has been much debated at the banking level. It was a one-sided decision and it doesn't come as a surprise, it's part of a warning. First there was a recognition that these rates remained constant in meticais for a long time and given inflation and given population growth, these were not aligned. The bank took the initiative to contact us and questioned the sustainability of the financial services it was providing in the face of the rates in force, hence the revision of the value. However, what is not said here is that it is necessary to be aware that this value of 9.5meticais is not charged every time the customer uses the ATM. In the first two movements of the month the service is free. This fee of 9.5 meticais can only be charged from the 3to move of the month. We will have to see if that guidance is being met. I take this opportunity to inform you that the Bank of Mozambique has a department for complaints of abusive behavior on the part of the bank, the Department of Behavioral Supervision that is present here. This department is open to the public, and it can call, write, send letters and, with this information, it will be ascertained which banks do not comply with this notice and will be taken the necessary measures to enforce, including fines. The Bank of Mozambique has a fines regime and now the fines are published so that the company knows which institutions are being fined. Spread this news to the entire population and let us work hard to make this a reality. Clarification When we say that the Bank of Mozambique has lost foreign currency, it is because it has sold foreign currency to the market. However, it is good to clarify that although we lost foreign exchange in the amount of 97.5 million we still have a comfortable level of reserves. Today the country's gross reserves are USD 3,170 billion, which corresponds to more than 7 months of import. There is no reason to panic about it as long as our policies are well aligned.  External debt The only new factor in foreign debt is hidden debt. Foreign debt, excluding hidden debts, is well-addressed through past restructuring paid. The only factor that hinders the scenario of this sustainability are hidden debts. I will not comment on the external debt debate. Let the lawyers debate and decide on the legality of this debt. That's a legal issue. This debate is not only in Mozambique. The discussion with creditors about the nature of the debt continues, with those who question the legality of the debt and who does not. Right now I have no opinion on this subject and if I did, I wouldn't say it.  Rand Ascent The Reserve Bank has virtually the same exchange rate and fluctuation regime, has no exchange rate target. The rand floats just like the metical. This is part of the normal functioning of the market and does not mean the beginning of a new trend itself. Of course, if the rand appreciates in relation to the metical, the metical, in turn, depreciates and the imported goods become more expensive from the rand's point of view. But it also means that we will import less from the South African area and import from other countries where competitiveness is greatest. That's the kind of gymnastics you have to do. For now, it can be said that this behaviour is part of a normal adjustment to a political change that is currently underway in South Africa. I would call this a correction, not necessarily the beginning of a new trend, but a correction to the natural balance (which we don't know which one will be) that depends on many other factors. 4.1. Implication of the rand rise in Inflation South Africa is not Mozambique's only partner. Imports in dollars are as much or more important in inflation relative to Rand, which does not mean that the rand is not important. The Rand, the Dollar and the Euro are currencies that count towards the behavior of inflation. We cannot look at a currency in isolation and worry about its individual impact on inflation.  ATM Rate Control Mechanism There are mechanisms, but in order for us to do our job well, we count on the collaboration of consumers. If there is abusive behavior of the bank outside the Notice, the BM has tools to investigate and decide whether it is a penalty, whether it is the first violation or if it was a mistake. Some might claim that their system hasn't been modified, or a system problem. It's a joint effort that we all have to do.  Crisis In April 2017, when we made the first interest rate cut, I said we were at the beginning of the end of the crisis and you made a lot of noise saying that the Governor is crazy. I believe what you said. We looked at the indicators and they indicated that we had reached the peak and that we could only improve from that and that's what we saw. We continue to lower interest rates in peace of mind, with caution and today we are confirming that the country is coming out of the crisis. There is no doubt about it, we are even better because we have the element peace, tranquility, which I want to believe, will turn into effective peace soon. All this further reinforces what we already knew in April. This statement was fair based on a cautious observation, it was not a propagandistic statement. Looking at the figures in April we came to the conclusion that we were comfortable with the measures we had and found that we were finally on the path to a slow exit from the crisis. That's what's happening. I reaffirm that we are better than I thought in April, because we have the factor peace, political tranquility that at the time were not well equated  Loans granted to the Government What are the limits and what is the existing margin. Our organic law passed by the legislature provides for the government to ask for advances. Advances are set at 10% of government revenues from two years ago and can range to around 15 billion, which has been the case over the past two years. The government must be between 5 and 6 billion. This value is aligned. It's not a favor, the state has the right to do so, it's provided for by law.
text_original: Transcrio da Conferncia de Imprensa O CPMO reuniu-se hoje, dia 26 de Fevereiro de 2018, para apreciar os desenvolvimentos macroeconmicos recentes, domsticos e internacionais, at 23 de Fevereiro de 2018, bem como as projeces dos principais indicadores macroeconmicos para o final do corrente ano, tendo tomado as medidas de poltica monetria consideradas adequadas. A contnua melhoria das perspectivas de inflao para o mdio prazo justifica o prosseguimento da reduo das taxas de juro. Assim, o CPMO deliberou:  Reduzir a taxa de juro de poltica monetria, taxa MIMO, em 150 pontos base, para 18,0%;  Reduzir a taxa de juro da Facilidade Permanente de Cedncia de Liquidez (FPC) em 150 pontos base, para 19,0%;  Reduzir a taxa de juro da Facilidade Permanente de Depsitos (FPD) em 150 pontos base, para 12,5%; Ainda, em face da presso que se observa no mercado cambial, o CPMO deliberou: Aumentar o coeficiente de Reservas Obrigatrias para os passivos em moeda estrangeira, em 800 pontos base, para 22,0%, tendo mantido o coeficiente para os passivos em moeda nacional em 14,0%. O rgo entende que a presso no mercado cambial reflecte os efeitos conjugados da volatilidade das principais divisas no mercado internacional e do ajustamento ao paradigma de maior abertura dos fluxos de capitais, contemplados no novo regulamento da Lei Cambial. Dependendo da evoluo dos indicadores econmico-financeiros e dos factores de risco, o CPMO poder tomar as medidas correctivas necessrias antes da prxima reunio do rgo, agendada para o dia 30 de Abril de 2018. Entre Dezembro de 2017 e Fevereiro de 2018, o Conselho de Administrao tomou as seguintes medidas:  Aviso n. 19/2017 sobre o Regime de Comisses e Encargos dos Servios Financeiros; e  Aviso n. 20/2017 sobre as Normas e Procedimentos Cambiais Principais desafios das decises do Comit de Poltica Monetria A nvel domstico temos, em primeiro lugar, o efeito das chuvas intensas que tem afectado o pas e, em segundo lugar, a sustentabilidade da dvida. A nvel internacional temos a volatilidade dos preos das commodities e do dlar nos mercados internacionais. Em 2017, o PIB registou um crescimento moderado ao redor dos 3%. A distribuio sectorial do PIB  liderada essencialmente pelo crescimento do sector primrio na vertente de agricultura, pesca e sector extractivo que registou um crescimento extremamente forte seguido do tercirio nas suas componentes de comrcio, transporte, servios financeiros e outros. O grfico [da evoluo trimestral do PIB] mostra-nos este crescimento moderado do PIB em 2017 que, apesar de moderado, est dentro dos padres da regio e, em particular, acima da mdia dos nossos parceiros da SADC que registaram, no seu todo, um crescimento de PIB de 2,8%, comparado ao crescimento do PIB moambicano de 3.7%. O clima econmico recuperou substancialmente, no quarto trimestre de 2017, medido atravs do optimismo dos empresrios no que diz respeito as perspectivas da actividade econmica, em particular nas suas componentes de preos, emprego e outros factores incluindo procura. A inflao continua a desacelerar. Em Janeiro andava ao redor de 3.84%. H um ano tnhamos um nvel de inflao anual, inflao homloga, acima dos 20%, tendo cado substancialmente, o que se reflecte na reduo do custo de vida dos consumidores, do cidado moambicano. O poder de compra foi acrescentado aos consumidores do pas. Portanto, so notcias positivas que afectam claramente o optimismo que se observa no seio dos empresrios. O factor de risco que era representado por uma inflao elevada e instvel hoje reduziu significativamente. O core inflation encontra-se abaixo da inflao geral agregada. Excluindo as frutas e vegetais, factores que tm tendncia a uma maior volatilidade ou sazonalidade, a inflao se situa a 2.36% bem abaixo da inflao geral de 2.84%. O grande desafio que temos, desde Janeiro de 2018, prende-se ao facto de o mercado de cmbio estar a registar uma presso relativamente crescente ao longo do tempo. O metical apresenta um comportamento misto tendo desvalorizado 12,28%, em relao ao dlar, 1,68% em relao ao Rand e apreciado relativamente ao Euro. Ainda neste perodo de presses o Banco Central vendeu divisas no mercado de cmbio, em termos lquidos, o que quer dizer que em Janeiro e Fevereiro as vendas foram superiores as compras no valor de mais de 87,5 milhes de dlares, o que significa que o Banco Central perdeu reservas nesse valor. Porm, no geral, at um certo momento, no primeiro trimestre do ano, com a excepo do ano passado, a sazonalidade mostra sempre uma relativa perda de reservas.  o perodo seco do ponto de vista das nossas exportaes. Tradicionalmente exportamos menos no Io trimestre em relao aos restantes trimestres do ano. Nesse caso, em particular, a situao  ligeiramente diferente pois existem outros factores que se agregam na sazonalidade das exportaes. Entretanto, o dfice da conta corrente continua a melhorar, tendo reduzido de cerca de USD 4 milhes, em 2016, para USD 2.542 milhes, em 2017, o que representa uma queda do dfice da conta corrente em 35%. Isso so boas noticias e implica uma melhoria, no geral, da nossa conta externa devido, em grande parte, aos grandes projectos que continuam a exportar grandes volumes de bens. Quando excludos os grandes projectos, as exportaes registam um crescimento modesto de 8%. Incluindo os grandes projectos o crescimento aumenta para 54%. As importaes de bens e servios cresceram 9,5% enquanto as importaes dos grandes projetos registaram um aqueda. A dvida interna continuou elevada levantando questes de sustentabilidade e aumentou de 98 mil milhes de meticais, em Dezembro, para 104,6 mil milhes de meticais, em Fevereiro. As taxas de juro do Mercado Monetrio Interbancrio continuam em tendncia de queda e a convergir para a taxa MIMO, reforando o elemento sinalizador da taxa MIMO. Este fenmeno tomou-se bastante visvel este ano visto que com a queda substancial nas expectativas de inflao, todas as outras taxas caram, incluindo os BTs. Em 2016, para os BTs de 364 dias a taxa era mais ou menos de 27%, comparando com BTs de 91 dias que era de 24%, sendo que a taxa MIMO na altura era inferior a essa. Com os sucessos alcanados na rea da inflao e a melhoria nas expectativas de inflao tem feito com que as taxas comecem a convergir e, actualmente, encontram-se praticamente ao mesmo nvel. As taxas de curto prazo e de um ano esto praticamente ao mesmo nvel. Isso  um dado importante do sucesso e da credibilidade da poltica monetria que foi alcanada com muito esforo de todos ns. A liquidez ampliada reduziu. No passado, um dos grandes desafios que tnhamos era a liquidez crescente no mercado. Hoje, passados vrios meses, temos uma reduo substancial da liquidez no mercado bancrio. A liquidez reduziu substancialmente de quase 36 mil milhes, em Janeiro, para 14 mil milhes, em Fevereiro, enquanto que em 2016 esta s crescia. Estvamos a viver aquilo que chamamos de liquidez longa, que  o excesso de liquidez. Estamos a caminhar para uma situao de menor liquidez no mercado devido, de certa forma, ao comportamento do mercado de cmbio. Parte considervel desta liquidez que saiu do mercado interbancrio entrou no mercado interbancrio de cmbio atravs da compra de divisas pela banca e pelos agentes econmicos. Nota-se uma queda de mais de USD 300 milhes num curto perodo de tempo no que se refere a liquidez bancria. O crdito  economia est em queda. Enquanto os agregados monetrios crescem, o crdito a economia continua a desacelerar, sendo que o resto do crdito  destinado ao sector pblico. Da que dizemos ser importante ajustar as contas fiscais para criar espao para que o crdito disponvel possa passar mais ao sector privado. Enquanto o crdito ao sector privado caiu o sector pblico foi o maior consumidor de crdito. Para 2018 esperamos uma inflao de um dgito, como afirmamos no nosso comunicado em Dezembro, e continuao de um crescimento moderado do PIB. Termino aqui a minha apresentao das deliberaes do Comit de Poltica Monetria hoje reunido e me coloco a vossa disposio para esclarecer qualquer questo relacionada com as deliberaes do Comit de Poltica Monetria. SESSO DE PERGUNTAS Antes de mais gostaria de esclarecer que a partir deste ano, nas reunies do CPMO limitaremos a discutir e esclarecer questes relacionadas com as deliberaes do rgo. No significa que no iremos responder s outras questes, mas este no  o frum apropriado. Teremos a oportunidade de, pelo menos, duas vezes ao ano, discutir de uma maneira mais aberta outras questes que no esto relacionadas ao CPMO. Vamos seguir a prtica internacional, que  limitar o CPMO s deliberaes do rgo e os restantes assuntos tratamos separadamente. No estamos a fazer nada diferente.  a prtica comum. Assim no perdemos o foco, pois j existem outros fruns para lidar com outras questes.  Sobre o aumento da dvida pblica Claramente est a crescer e quando isso acontece levantam-se questes de sustentabilidade. Esta no  a primeira vez que discutimos esse assunto aqui e me recordo que quando falamos disso um de vocs perguntou como se definia sustentabilidade, se havia um nmero e qual seria ento o valor mgico que alerta o sistema. A minha resposta foi que existiam vrias discusses em tomo disso, at acadmicas, que olham para experincias passadas para definir mais ou menos o que  considerado sustentvel. Existem tambm vrios indicadores para isso, mas, em ltima instncia, depende da vontade dos operadores econmicos, em particular bancos e outros investidores, de querer comprar essa dvida do Estado. A dvida do Estado  um activo na carteira de algum (bancos, fundos de penses e outros investidores), quando estes acham que a dvida comea a atingir nveis preocupantes eles param de comprar. Todas essas instituies (bancos, fundo de penses, investidores) tem guies que fixam o montante mximo de investimento para cada tipo de dvida. Quando chega esse momento eles param. O Estado comea a ter problemas. No sabemos quando isto vai acontecer. Isso depende dos agentes econmicos e varia de pas para pas dependendo dos riscos envolvidos. Quando a dvida comea a aumentar saindo de um nvel para outro comeamos a pensar, at que ponto os agentes econmicos estaro dispostos a continuar a por na carteira esse instrumento como uma activo de investimento para si.  Taxas de utilizao dos servios da ATM Este assunto foi muito debatido a nvel da banca. Foi uma deciso unilateral e no vem como uma surpresa, faz parte de um aviso. Primeiro houve um reconhecimento que estas taxas se mantiveram constantes em meticais por muito tempo e dada a inflao e dado o crescimento da populao, estas no estavam alinhadas. A banca tomou a iniciativa de nos contactar e questionou a sustentabilidade dos servios financeiros que estava a fornecer face das taxas em vigor, da a reviso do valor. Porm, o que no se diz aqui  que  preciso ter conscincia que esse valor de 9.5meticais no  cobrado cada vez que o cliente usa a ATM. Nos primeiros dois movimentos do ms o servio  gratuito. Esta taxa de 9.5 meticais s pode ser cobrada a partir da 3a movimentao do ms. Teremos que observar se essa orientao est a ser cumprida. Aproveito a oportunidade para informar que o Banco de Moambique dispe de um departamento para reclamaes de comportamento abusivo por parte da banca, o Departamento de Superviso Comportamental que est aqui presente. Este departamento est aberto ao pblico, sendo que este pode telefonar, escrever, mandar cartas e, com essa informao, ser averiguado quais so os bancos que no cumprem com esse aviso e sero tomadas as medidas necessrias para fazer cumprir, incluindo multas. O Banco de Moambique tem um regime de multas e agora as multas passam a ser publicadas para que a sociedade saiba quais as instituies que esto a ser multadas. Espalhem esta notcia  toda a populao e trabalhemos j untos para que isso se tome uma realidade. Esclarecimento Quando dizemos que o Banco de Moambique perdeu divisas  porque vendeu divisas ao mercado. Porm,  bom esclarecer que apesar de termos perdido divisas no valor de 97.5 milhes continuamos com um nvel confortvel de reservas. Hoje as reservas brutas do pas esto a USD 3.170 mil milhes o que corresponde a mais de 7 meses de importao. No h razo para pnico nessa matria desde que as nossas polticas estejam bem alinhadas.  Dvida Externa O nico factor novo da dvida externa so as dvidas ocultas. A dvida externa, excluindo as dvidas ocultas, est bem equacionada atravs de restruturaes passadas pagas. O nico factor que vem atrapalhar o cenrio dessa sustentabilidade so as dvidas ocultas. Em relao ao debate da dvida externa no vou comentar. Deixemos que os juristas debatam e decidam sobre a legalidade dessa dvida. Essa  uma questo legal. Esse debate no se verifica apenas em Moambique. A discusso com os credores sobre a natureza da dvida mantm-se, havendo quem ponha em causa a legalidade da dvida e quem no ponha. Neste momento no tenho opinio sobre esse assunto e se tivesse no diria.  Subida do Rand O Reserve Bank tem praticamente o mesmo regime de cmbio e flutuao, no tem objectivo de cmbio. O rand flutua assim como o metical. Isso faz parte do funcionamento normal do mercado e no significa o incio de uma nova tendncia em si. Naturalmente, se o rand aprecia em relao ao metical, o metical, por sua vez, deprecia e os bens importados ficam mais caros do ponto de vista do rand. Mas isso significa tambm que vamos importar menos da zona da frica do Sul e importar de outros pases onde a competitividade  maior.  esse tipo de ginstica que tem que se fazer. Por enquanto, pode se dizer que esse comportamento  parte de um ajustamento normal  uma mudana poltica que est em curso, neste momento, na frica do Sul. Chamaria a isso de uma correco, no necessariamente o incio de uma nova tendncia, mas uma correco para o equilbrio natural (que no sabemos qual ser) que depende de muitos outros factores. 4.1. Implicao da subida do rand na Inflao A frica do Sul no  o nico parceiro de Moambique. As importaes em dlares so tanto ou mais importantes na inflao em relao ao Rand, o que no significa que o rand no seja importante. O Rand, o Dlar e o Euro so moedas que contam para o comportamento da inflao. No podemos olhar para uma moeda de forma isolada e nos preocupar com o seu impacto individual na inflao.  Mecanismo de Controlo das Taxa de ATM Existem sim mecanismos, mas para que possamos fazer bem o nosso trabalho, contamos com a colaborao dos consumidores. Title: Speech at the Inaugural Lecture of the Pedagogical University
text: Dl MOTTO BETWEEN THE ABUNDANCE OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC GROWTH: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES. INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENcy THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, ROGeRIO LUCAS ZANDAMELA,ON THE OCCASION OF THE OPENING OF THE ACADEMIC YEAR OF THE PEDAGOGICAL UNIVERSITY"INAUGURAL CLASS" MAPUTO, 2 DE AAARcO DE 2018 Let me, first of all, welcome all present and address my sincere thanks to Prof. Doctor Jorge Ferrao, Rector of the Pedagogical University, for honoring me with this exciting and at the same time prestigious invitation to be here today, surrounded by so many young people, who will certainly be the future leaders of our country. It is a great honour for me to be with you in this room and to be able to share some of my ideas and reflections on the economy of Mozambique, leaving a little of the sphere of the performance of the Bank of Mozambique, but focusing on an equally important theme for the future of our country, and above all for our youth. I admit this is the first time I've taught an inaugural class at a university. Perhaps that's why this moment will make me retreat to times that are already there, when I - still a college student, with all the strength and will that youth have to change the world, eager to obtain new knowledge, after participating in several lectures, I felt that many of them had not said anything new. When I look at the faces of many students present here, I review this desire to hear something new. I must confess, however, that I will not say anything that you have not heard in other lectures. Perhaps it is more emphatic, but, as previously announced, the theme I propose to address is very connected with the current situation that we are living in Mozambique: "The dilemma of having many natural resources and still not achieving the desirable levels of economic growth." I will do my dissertation around three central dimensions: first, I want to remind you about the potential of natural resources that Mozambique has; second, I will demonstrate, by taking advantage of international experiences, that not always having abundant natural resources is synonymous with robust and inclusive growth, hence the notion of dilemma; third, focusing on some factors that contribute to this, I will try to argue that, although Mozambique has abundant natural resources, we continue to have below desirable development patterns. Having said that, I will come up with some challenges, which, if resolved, could be an important platform for inclusive and sustainable growth. Let me then begin by presenting to you what Mozambique is talking about, so that we can all start from the same basis of analysis. Mozambique has a privileged geographical location, along the eastern coast of Southern Africa, with a coastline of about 2,300 km, which, in addition to fishing and tourist potential, makes it a perfect pivot in international trade and an important route from the countries neighbouring hinterland to the rest of the world. Demographic indicators from the 2017 census indicate that the country has a high workforce potential, with a total of 28.8 million inhabitants and a population density of 36.1 inhabitants perkm2. However, only about 51% of Mozambique's population is literate and about 70% live in rural areas and practice activities related to agriculture, fishing and subsistence livestock. Mozambique is also blessed by the allocation of natural resources, which highlights the existence of 36 million hectares of fertile land, conducive to the practice of agriculture, and in recent years agriculture has been the main source of income, representing about 25% of GDP. In fact, a total of six strategic corridors with potential for the development of agriculture have been identified, but which are still underutilized, specifically Nacala, Zambezi Valley, Beira, Pemba and Lichinga, Limpopo and Maputo. We also identified 12 important product chains and agricultural value for the production, among others, of rice, soybeans, corn, sugarcane, cotton and cashew nuts, as well as for cutting and processing wood, but which are underdeveloped. The country also has a high potential for the production of hydroelectric, wind and geothermal energy, being seen as a potential solution for reducing the electricity deficit in the SADC region. In this context, projects such as the Cahora Bassa Hydroelectric Power Plant, the Massingir Dam, the Benga, Nkondezi and Moatize thermal power plants stand out, in addition to the project still in the construction portfolio of the Mpanda Nkuwa dam. Mozambique has also distinguished itself by its wealth in terms of mineral resources, and in this sense has attracted large investors to develop large projects in the area of the extractive industry, with emphasis on the exploration of: (i) natural gas in the Rovuma basin (one of the world's largest reserves of natural gas); (ii) natural gas in the provinces of Inhambane and Sofala; (iii) coal in Moatize, tete province; well so (iv) of the areas of extraction of gold, heavy sands and precious stones such as ruby, in the central and northern areas. As you can see, Mozambique has been blessed with a vast potential for natural resources. But what does international experience on an abundance of resources vis-a-vis economic growth tell us? According to unctad reported information on foreign direct investment flows in Africa, which amounted to USD 59.4 billion in 2016, Mozambique was part of the group of the six African economies that received the most flows that year, and was the second in the SADC region, second only to Angola. Of the total EI flows received by the African continent, the majority went to the extractive sector, with an enhancement to natural gas, oil and coal, which shows the great link between The IDE in Africa and the extraction of natural resources. However, looking at the current situation of most African countries, it is noted that the effect of this investment is not the most desired, as the levels of development of their economies remain low, while poverty indicators have not reduced enough. Some academics criticize the fact that the region still faces constraints in terms of human capabilities, capital and good governance, despite the abundance of natural resources in Africa. The concentration of foreign direct investment flows in sectors geared towards the extraction of natural resources means that most economies marginalise other strategic sectors, showing the international experience that agriculture and manufacturing have been the most sacrificed. Indeed, the growth of African economies that receive the most flows of foreign direct investment, such as Angola, Nigeria and Ghana, is dependent on the extraction and export of natural resources, with no added value and little impact on other sectors of the economy. This scenario results in a weak diversification of the production base of African economies, which makes them dependent and vulnerable to the behavior of international commodity prices. Thus, when the global economy is in a growth phase, it requires greater consumption of these goods, stimulating the growth of their prices, and vice versa, which directly affects the revenues of the exporting African countries, in this case, and makes the behaviour of their economies very volatile. This form of exploration, concentrated on one or a few products, and intensely, poses serious sustainability problems over time, especially if we take into account that many of the resources are not renewable, such as oil, natural gas and coal. The information available shows that the dilemma between the abundance of natural resources and growth or poverty can also be a reality in Mozambique if it is not properly addressed. Indeed, the high economic growth observed in Mozambique in recent decades of around 7% per year has not been sufficiently inclusive to generate the positive externalities necessary for the effective improvement of the lives of the majority of the population. Recently published data on the assessment of poverty and well-being in Mozambique show that about 46.1% of the population still lived below the poverty line in 2014, equivalent to a total of 11.8 million inhabitants, the same number observed in 1996 (12 million). In the same period, according to data from the Household Budget surveys, the inequality in income distribution (as measured by the well-known Gini coefficient) increased from 0.4 in 1996 to 0.47 in 2014. Additionally, gross domestic product per capita, i.e. the income that each of the 29 million Mozambicans is assumed to have (if all had the same income) has not changed in recent years, having settled at USD 430 in 2017, according to IMF estimates. In the evaluation of the Human Development Index of a total of 188 countries, Mozambique was ranked 181in 2016, being in the group of the ten least developed countries in the world, being the worst ranked of the CPLP countries and the SADC region. The country also stands out in the group of 10 countries with the lowest infrastructure development in Africa, occupying position 45, in a total of 54 African economies evaluated by the Infrastructure Development index in Africa, and is in the group of countries with the highest perception of corruption in the world, occupying position 142, a total of 176 economies analyzed by the Corruption Perception index. The even more important aspect to highlight is the fact that the economic structure has hardly changed in recent years, whereas, with the exception of the extractive industry and financial services sectors, which have seen an improvement from major projects, the production base has continued to be dominated by the agriculture sector, mostly representing about 25% of GDP, while the remaining sectors maintained the same structure as 18 years ago. So what to do? I believe that the first major challenge is to integrate civil society, with particular emphasis on the younger layers, in the debate on how to create a national wealth fund that allows transforming the gains made by the exploitation of non-renewable natural resources into the generation of renewable resources. It is essential that the use of revenue stemming from the exploitation of non-renewable natural resources does not constitute an exclusive decision of economic policy makers, used to address immediate needs, but rather to reflect the intentions of the different spheres of civil society and the communities from which those resources are extracted. And in this respect, I would like to insist that you young people must now start to create an active critical mass, sounding and capable of demanding greater participation in the process of defining the rules that will dictate the use of the proceeds of the exploitation of natural resources and in the choice of the most appropriate development model for our country, which still has many basic needs to be resolved, but which must also guarantee wealth for generations to come. There are several models already tested in other countries that could serve as an example. It is vital that you are empowered - and universities are a good place to do so - and appropriate your future, now starting a hard work of actively monitoring policy-making processes to ensure that your interests are reflected in the policy measures to be implemented. Take the attention that it is your right, as a result of the future of this country, to demand greater rigour and discipline of current policymakers in the use of revenues from the exploitation of natural resources, ensuring that these gains are used for the construction of priority infrastructure for the country, for the generation of human capital, through investments in education and technologies, increasing the productivity of the national workforce and promoting the creation of renewable resources. Only in this way can we achieve a transformation of the productive structure of the economy and generate gains and opportunities for generations to come. It is also important to ensure that government authorities consolidate an environment of peace and political stability, a factor that will enable economic actors to develop their productive and commercial links in a scenario of security and free movement of people and goods in different regions of the country. In addition, it is a priority to adopt reforms that enable the continuous improvement of the business environment, enabling a diversified and inclusive development of the business fabric. The current business environment is more oriented towards large projects, whose financial strength and trading capacity allow them to access special regimes, which facilitate their operations, while the remaining business segment deals with a little developed business environment and with various constraints. According to Doing Business 2018, Mozambique belongs to the group of countries where it is difficult to start a venture, standing at position 134 out of a total of 190 economies, standing behind economies such as Mauritius, Botswana and South Africa. This, moreover, is reinforced by data from the Business Census, which indicate that, over a 12-year horizon, the number of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the ones that promote the most jobs, has decreased by 1,681 to 26,793 in 2016, while large companies, which are mostly capital intensive, have almost tripled, 905 in 2016. Combined with this, it is also necessary to attract and support foreign direct investment projects on a more diversified basis. Although the country is noted for the substantial increase in EDE, it has not been promoting the desired economic transformation, since the largest proportion of these investments is destined to the natural gas and coal sectors, to the detriment of areas of high potential such as agriculture, fishing, livestock, manufacturing and tourism. Indeed, in the period 2010-2017, about 69% of The EII went to the extractive industry for the exploration of coal and natural gas, making the economy vulnerable to the volatility of international prices of these commodities. It is urgently up to us in the financial system to fulfil the important task of increasing the levels of financial inclusion of our population, given the potential that financial services have to boost the growth of economies by promoting income-generating activities, savings and new investments, in addition to contributing to improving living and social conditions. It is to our knowledge that Mozambique has a low level of financial inclusion and an underdeveloped financial system, partly due to the weak coverage of the banking network, which affects mostly urban areas and only 94 districts, out of a total of 154, largely due to the high transaction costs and infrastructure deficit, which makes it difficult to set up bank branches in some parts of the country. This scenario means that, according to FINSCOPE 2014, only 20% of the adult population has access to formal financial products and services in Mozambique. These levels of financial inclusion can be improved by betting  development of financial services and products based on the use of information and communication technologies, which outsmart the need for the physical presence of banking units in hard-to-reach places and allow reaching a wide range of the population that does not have access to formal financial services;  implementation of financial education activities, so that the population acquires the necessary knowledge to better exploit the potential of existing financial services; and  strengthening the consumer protection framework by improving public confidence in the financial system. Associated with the previous point, it is also necessary to promote domestic savings, since it has been insufficient to finance domestic investment needs. Indeed, the deficit between savings and domestic investment in 2014 was close to 40% of GDP, making the country vulnerable and dependent on the savings of the rest of the world, mainly in the form of foreign direct investment, which has been growing in recent years. At the public sector level , the scarcity of funds is also evident, as the domestic revenues collected by the state have not been sufficient to cover public spending, putting public finances in a chronic deficit position. This scenario makes the country dependent on foreign aid in the form of donations and credits to finance the public deficit. In recent years, public debt has grown substantially to unsustainable levels, largely due to hidden debts, which still need to be resolved. I realize that these challenges are not easy to solve and that success in overcoming them depends, above all, on the effort and commitment of all of us, especially young people, who are the pillar of our development. I end by thanking you for your attention and wishing all the students present here many successes in academic life and assimilating the knowledge to be the transforming agents of our economy, applying your entire knowledge to make Mozambique a country with a stronger, stronger and more inclusive growth, both socially and economically. Maputo, 02 March 2018
text_original: Dl LEMA ENTRE A ABUNDNCIA DE RECURSOS NATURAIS E O CRESCIMENTO ECONMICO: DESAFIOS E OPORTUNIDADES. INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELNCIA O GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE, ROGRIO LUCAS ZANDAMELA, POR OCASIO DA ABERTURA DO ANO LECTIVO DA UNIVERSIDADE PEDAGGICA AULA INAUGURAL MAPUTO, 2 DE AAARO DE 2018 Permitam-me, em primeiro lugar, que sade a todos os presentes e enderece os meus sinceros agradecimentos ao Prof. Doutor Jorge Ferro, Magnfico Reitor da Universidade Pedaggica, por me honrar com este aliciante e ao mesmo tempo prestigiante convite para estar aqui, hoje, rodeado de tantos jovens, que certamente sero os futuros dirigentes do nosso pas. , para mim, uma grande honra estar convosco nesta sala e poder partilhar algumas das minhas ideias e reflexes sobre a economia de Moambique, saindo um pouco da esfera da actuao do Banco de Moambique, mas centrando-me num tema igualmente importante para o futuro do nosso pas, e acima de tudo para a nossa juventude. Admito que  a primeira vez que profiro uma aula inaugural numa Universidade. Talvez por isso, este momento me faa recuar para tempos que j l vo, quando eu - ainda estudante universitrio, com toda a fora e vontade que a juventude tem para mudar o mundo, vido de obter novos conhecimentos, aps participar em vrias palestras, sentia que muitas delas no tinham dito nada de novo.
