Talvez seja mais enftico, mas, como foi anunciado previamente, o tema que proponho abordar tem muita ligao com a actualidade que estamos a viver em Moambique: O dilema de ter muitos recursos naturais e, mesmo assim, no alcanar os nveis de crescimento econmico desejveis. Vou fazer a minha dissertao em torno de trs dimenses centrais: primeiro, pretendo recordar-vos sobre o potencial de recursos naturais que Moambique possui; segundo, irei demonstrar, socorrendo-me das experincias internacionais, que nem sempre ter recursos naturais em abundncia  sinnimo de ter um crescimento robusto e inclusivo, da a noo de dilema; terceiro, focando alguns factores que concorrem para isso, tentarei argumentar que, apesar de Moambique possuir recursos naturais em abundncia, continuamos com padres de desenvolvimento abaixo dos desejveis. Posto isto, irei avanar com alguns desafios, que, se resolvidos, podero constituir uma plataforma importante para um crescimento inclusivo e sustentvel. Permitam-me, ento, que comece por apresentar-vos de que Moambique estamos a falar, para que todos partamos da mesma base de anlise. Moambique possui uma localizao geogrfica privilegiada, junto da costa oriental da frica Austral, com uma linha costeira de cerca de 2.300 km, o que, para alm do potencial pesqueiro e turstico, o torna num piv perfeito a nvel do comrcio internacional e numa rota importante dos pases vizinhos da hinterlndia para o resto do mundo. Os indicadores demogrficos do censo de 2017 indicam que o pas conta com um elevado potencial de fora de trabalho, com um total de 28,8 milhes de habitantes e uma densidade populacional de 36,1 habitantes por km2. No entanto, apenas cerca de 51% da populao de Moambique  alfabetizada e cerca de 70% reside nas zonas rurais e pratica actividades relacionadas com a agricultura, pesca e pecuria de subsistncia. Moambique  ainda abenoado pela dotao de recursos naturais, de onde se destaca a existncia 36 milhes de hectares de terras frteis, propcias para a prtica da agricultura, sendo que, nos ltimos anos, a agricultura constituiu a principal fonte de rendimento, representando cerca de 25% do PIB. Com efeito, foi identificado um total de seis corredores estratgicos com potencial para o desenvolvimento da agricultura, mas que ainda se encontram subaproveitados, especificamente Nacala, Vale do Zambeze, Beira, Pemba e Lichinga, Limpopo e Maputo. Foram tambm identificadas 12 importantes cadeias de produto e valor agrcola para a produo, entre outros, de arroz, soja, milho, cana-de-acar, algodo e castanha de caju, bem como para o corte e processamento de madeira, mas que se encontram pouco desenvolvidas. 0 pas detm ainda um elevado potencial para a produo de energia hidroelctrica, elica e geotrmica, sendo visto como uma potencial soluo para a reduo do dfice de energia elctrica na regio da SADC. Neste mbito, destacam-se projectos como a Hidroelctrica de Cahora Bassa, a barragem de Massingir, as centrais trmicas de Benga, Nkondezi e Moatize, para alm do projecto ainda em carteira de construo da barragem de Mpanda Nkuwa. Moambique tem-se distinguido tambm pela sua riqueza em termos de recursos minerais, tendo, neste sentido, atrado grandes investidores para desenvolverem grandes projectos na rea da indstria extractiva, com destaque para a explorao de: (i) gs natural na bacia do Rovuma (uma das maiores reservas mundiais de gs natural); (ii) gs natural nas provncias de Inhambane e Sofala; (iii) carvo mineral em Moatize, na provncia de Tete; bem assim (iv) das reas de extraco de ouro, areias pesadas e pedras preciosas como o rubi, nas zonas centro e norte. Como podem notar, Moambique foi abenoado com um vasto potencial de recursos naturais. Mas o que nos diz a experincia internacional sobre abundncia de recursos vis--vis o crescimento econmico? De acordo com a informao reportada pela UNCTAD sobre os fluxos de investimento directo estrangeiro em frica, que ascendiam aos USD 59.4 bilies no ano de 2016, Moambique fez parte do grupo das seis economias de frica que mais fluxos recebeu naquele ano, e foi a segunda na regio da SADC, ficando atrs apenas de Angola. Do total dos fluxos de IDE recebidos pelo continente Africano, a maioria destinou-se ao sector extractivo, com realce para o gs natural, petrleo e carvo, o que mostra a grande ligao entre o IDE em frica e a extraco dos recursos naturais. Entretanto, observando a situao actual da maioria dos pases africanos, nota-se que o efeito desse investimento no  o mais desejado, pois os nveis de desenvolvimento das suas economias continuam baixos, ao mesmo tempo que os indicadores de pobreza no reduziram o suficiente. Alguns acadmicos criticam o facto de a regio ainda enfrentar constrangimentos em termos de capacidades humanas, capital e boa governao, apesar da abundncia de recursos naturais em frica. A concentrao de fluxos de investimento directo estrangeiro nos sectores orientados para a extraco dos recursos naturais faz com que a maior parte das economias marginalize os outros sectores estratgicos, mostrando a experincia internacional que a agricultura e a indstria transformadora tm sido os mais sacrificados. Com efeito, o crescimento das economias africanas que mais fluxos de investimento directo estrangeiro recebem, a exemplo de Angola, Nigria e Gana,  dependente da extraco e exportao de recursos naturais, sem nenhum valor acrescentado e com pouca repercusso noutros sectores da economia. Este cenrio resulta numa fraca diversificao da base produtiva das economias africanas, o que as torna dependentes e vulnerveis ao comportamento dos preos internacionais das mercadorias. Assim, quando a economia global est numa fase de crescimento, requer um maior consumo dessas mercadorias, estimulando o crescimento dos seus preos, e vice-versa, o que afecta directamente as receitas dos pases africanos exportadores, no caso vertente, e torna o comportamento das suas economias muito voltil. Esta forma de explorao, concentrada em um ou em poucos produtos, e de forma intensa, coloca srios problemas de sustentabilidade no tempo, principalmente se tomarmos em considerao que muitos dos recursos no so renovveis, como so os casos do petrleo, do gs natural e do carvo. A informao disponvel mostra que o dilema entre a abundncia de recursos naturais e o crescimento ou pobreza tambm pode ser uma realidade em Moambique, se no for devidamente enfrentado. Com efeito, o elevado crescimento econmico observado nas ltimas dcadas em Moambique, de cerca de 7% por ano, no foi suficientemente inclusivo para gerar as externalidades positivas necessrias para a melhoria efectiva da vida da maioria da populao. Dados recentemente publicados sobre a avaliao da pobreza e bem-estar em Moambique mostram que cerca de 46,1% da populao ainda vivia abaixo da linha de pobreza em 2014, o equivalente a um total de 11,8 milhes de habitantes, o mesmo nmero observado em 1996 (12 milhes). No mesmo perodo, segundo os dados dos inquritos ao Oramento familiar, a desigualdade na distribuio do rendimento (medida pelo conhecido coeficiente de Gini) aumentou de 0,4 em 1996 para 0,47 em 2014. Adicionalmente, o produto interno bruto per capita, ou seja, o rendimento que se supe que cada um dos 29 milhes de moambicanos tenha (se todos tivessem o mesmo rendimento) no mudou nos ltimos anos, tendo-se fixado em USD 430 em 2017, segundo estimativas do FMI. Na avaliao do ndice de Desenvolvimento Humano, de um total de 188 pases, Moambique encontrava-se classificado na posio 181 em 2016, situando-se no grupo dos dez pases menos desenvolvidos do mundo, sendo o pior classificado dos pases da CPLP e da regio da SADC. O pas destaca-se ainda no grupo dos 10 pases com o menor desenvolvimento de infra-estruturas em frica, ocupando a posio 45, num total de 54 economias africanas avaliadas pelo ndice de Desenvolvimento de Infra-estruturas em frica, e encontra-se no grupo dos pases com maior percepo de corrupo do mundo, ocupando a posio 142, num total de 176 economias analisadas pelo ndice de Percepo de Corrupo. O aspecto ainda mais importante a destacar  o facto de a estrutura econmica praticamente no se ter alterado nos ltimos anos, em que, com a excepo dos sectores da indstria extractiva e dos servios financeiros, que observaram uma melhoria decorrente dos grandes projectos, a base produtiva continuou a ser dominada pelo sector da agricultura, maioritariamente de subsistncia, representando cerca de 25% do PIB, enquanto os restantes sectores mantiveram a mesma estrutura de h 18 anos atrs. Sendo assim, o que fazer? Considero que o primeiro grande desafio passa por integrar a sociedade civil, com especial destaque para as camadas mais jovens, no debate sobre como criar um fundo de riqueza nacional que permita transformar os ganhos obtidos pela explorao de recursos naturais no renovveis em gerao de recursos renovveis.  fundamental que a utilizao das receitas resultantes da explorao dos recursos naturais no renovveis no constitua uma deciso exclusiva dos formuladores de poltica econmica, usada para resolver as necessidades imediatas, mas sim que seja um reflexo das intenes das diferentes esferas da sociedade civil e das comunidades de onde esses recursos so extrados. E, neste aspecto, quero insistir que vocs, jovens, devem comear a criar agora uma massa crtica activa, sonante e capaz de exigir uma maior participao no processo de definio das regras que vo ditar a utilizao das receitas da explorao dos recursos naturais e na escolha do modelo de desenvolvimento mais adequado para o nosso pas, que ainda tem muitas necessidades bsicas por resolver, mas que tem tambm de garantir riqueza para as geraes vindouras. H vrios modelos j testados noutros pases que podero servir de exemplo.  fundamental que sejam empoderados - e as Universidades so um bom local para isso - e se apropriem do vosso futuro, iniciando agora um trabalho rduo de monitoria activa dos processos de formulao de polticas, de modo a certificar que os vossos interesses estejam reflectidos nas medidas de poltica a serem implementadas. Assumam que  vosso direito, na qualidade do futuro deste pas, exigir um maior rigor e disciplina dos actuais formuladores de polticas na utilizao das receitas de explorao dos recursos naturais, garantindo que estes ganhos sejam usados para a construo de infra-estruturas prioritrias para o pas, para a gerao de capital humano, atravs de investimentos em educao e tecnologias, que elevem cada vez mais a produtividade da fora de trabalho nacional e promovam a criao de recursos renovveis. S assim  que se poder atingir uma transformao da estrutura produtiva da economia e gerao de ganhos e oportunidades para as geraes vindouras.  igualmente importante assegurar que as autoridades governamentais consolidem um ambiente de paz e de estabilidade poltica, factor que vai permitir que os agentes econmicos possam desenvolver as suas ligaes produtivas e comerciais num cenrio de segurana e de livre circulao de pessoas e bens, nas diferentes regies do pas. Adicionalmente,  prioritrio adoptar reformas que activem a melhoria contnua do ambiente de negcios, possibilitando um desenvolvimento diversificado e inclusivo do tecido empresarial. 0 actual ambiente de negcios  mais orientado para os grandes projectos, cuja pujana financeira e capacidade de negociao lhes permitem aceder aos regimes especiais, que facilitam as suas operaes, enquanto o remanescente segmento empresarial lida com um ambiente de negcios pouco desenvolvido e com vrios constrangimentos. Segundo o Doing Business de 2018, Moambique pertence ao grupo dos pases onde  difcil iniciar um empreendimento, situando-se na posio 134, de um total de 190 economias, posicionando-se atrs de economias como Maurcias, Botswana e frica do Sul. Este facto, alis,  reforado pelos dados do Censo de Empresas, que indicam que, num horizonte de 12 anos, o nmero de micro, pequenas e mdias empresas, que so as que promovem mais postos de emprego, reduziu em 1.681, passando para 26.793 em 2016, enquanto as grandes empresas, que so maioritariamente intensivas em capital, quase que triplicaram, passando para 905 em 2016. Combinado com este facto,  tambm necessrio atrair e apoiar projectos de investimento directo estrangeiro numa base mais diversificada. Apesar de o pas se notabilizar pelo aumento substancial do IDE, este no tem estado a promover a transformao econmica desejada, visto que a maior proporo destes investimentos se destina aos sectores de gs natural e carvo, em detrimento de reas de elevado potencial como a agricultura, a pesca, a pecuria, a manufactura e o turismo. Efectivamente, no perodo de 2010-2017, cerca de 69% do IDE destinava-se  indstria extractiva para a explorao de carvo e gs natural, tornando a economia vulnervel  volatilidade dos preos internacionais destas mercadorias. A ns, do sistema financeiro, cabe-nos cumprir com urgncia a misso importante de aumentar os nveis de incluso financeira da nossa populao, dado o potencial que os servios financeiros possuem de dinamizar o crescimento das economias atravs da promoo de actividades geradoras de rendimento, poupana e novos investimentos, para alm de contribuir para a melhoria das condies de vida e sociais.  do nosso conhecimento que Moambique possui um baixo nvel de incluso financeira e um sistema financeiro subdesenvolvido, em parte decorrente da fraca cobertura da rede bancria, que atinge maioritariamente as zonas urbanas e apenas 94 distritos, dum total de 154, muito por conta dos elevados custos de transaco e do dfice de infra-estruturas, que dificulta a instalao de agncias bancrias em alguns pontos do pas. Este cenrio faz com que, segundo o FINSCOPE 2014, apenas 20% da populao adulta tenha acesso a servios e produtos financeiros formais em Moambique. Estes nveis de incluso financeira podem ser melhorados, atravs da aposta  no desenvolvimento de servios e produtos financeiros baseados na utilizao das tecnologias de informao e comunicao, que contornam a necessidade de presena fsica de unidades bancrias em locais de difcil acesso e permitem atingir uma vasta gama da populao que no tem acesso a servios financeiros formais;  na implementao de actividades de educao financeira, de modo que a populao adquira os conhecimentos necessrios para melhor explorar o potencial dos servios financeiros existentes; e  no reforo do quadro de proteco do consumidor, melhorando a confiana da populao no sistema financeiro. Associado ao ponto anterior,  tambm necessrio promover a poupana domstica, uma vez que a mesma tem sido insuficiente para financiar as necessidades domsticas de investimento. Efectivamente, o dfice entre a poupana e o investimento domstico em 2014 situou-se prximo de 40% do PIB, fazendo com que o pas se torne vulnervel e dependente das poupanas do resto do mundo, principalmente na forma de investimento directo estrangeiro, que tem estado a crescer nos ltimos anos. A nvel do sector pblico, tambm  patente a escassez de fundos, na medida em que as receitas domsticas arrecadadas pelo Estado no tm sido suficientes para cobrir a despesa pblica, colocando as finanas pblicas numa posio crnica de dfice. Este cenrio faz com que o pas seja dependente da ajuda externa na forma de donativos e crditos, para financiar o dfice pblico. Nos ltimos anos, a dvida pblica cresceu substancialmente para nveis insustentveis, muito por conta das dvidas ocultas, que ainda precisam de ser resolvidas. Percebo que estes desafios no so fceis de solucionar e que o sucesso para os ultrapassar depende, sobretudo, do esforo e comprometimento de todos ns, em particular dos jovens, que so o pilar do nosso desenvolvimento. Termino agradecendo a vossa ateno e desejando a todos os estudantes aqui presentes muitos sucessos na vida acadmica e que assimilem os conhecimentos para serem os agentes transformadores da nossa economia, aplicando o vosso inteiro saber para tornar Moambique um pas com um crescimento mais firme, slido e inclusivo, quer social, quer economicamente. Maputo, 02 de Maro de 2018

Title: Speech on the Launch of the Pilot Project for Tourism Revenue Control
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENCY THE VICE-GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, VICTOR PEDRO GOMES ON THE OCCASION OF THE LAUNCH OF THE PILOT PROJECT FOR THE CONTROL OF TOURISM REVENUES MAPUTO, APRIL 2, 2018 Prime Minister, Your Excellency Minister for Culture and Tourism, Excellency Minister of the Interior, Excellency Madam Deputy Minister for Culture and Tourism, Excellency, Mr President of the Tax Authority of Mozambique Mr President of the National Institute of Statistics Your Excellese Ly, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, Exmos. Gentlemen Cultural Agents and Tour Operators, Dear Guests, Ladies and gentlemen, let me first, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, welcome all present at this launch ceremony of the Pilot Project for Effective Control of The Flow of Revenue abroad and Dialogue with Cultural Agents and Tour Operators. I extend special greetings to our Government, which has been undertaking the coordination of the different economic sectors in the search for better solutions for the country, and His Excellency Silva Dunduro, Minister of Culture and Tourism, for hosting this important event. I would also like to greet all the tour operators and cultural agents present here, as well as the managers and technicians of the Bank of Mozambique and the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, who have worked hard to implement this project until the current launch phase. Distinguished Guests, Ladies and gentlemen, At the end of December 2017, the Bank of Mozambique, in the exercise of its function as foreign exchange authority, issued a legal provision establishing rules and procedures to be observed in the performance of foreign exchange operations. Among other aspects, this provision eliminates the mandatory conversion of 50% of export revenue repatriated to the country and transfers to credit institutions part of the capital operations that were carried out by the Bank of Mozambique. The principle of repatriation provided for in the Exchange Law, however , remained. For the special case of tourism, the regulation also establishes that all receipts resulting from the provision of hotel and tourism services by residents must occur through accounts in banks operating in the country. We are aware that the foreign exchange area is very dynamic and that, depending on the stage of development, the network of relations between foreign and national investors can change, and consequently tourist movements also change. These factors can change the dynamics of financial flows between the country and abroad, so we remain committed to printing the flexibility necessary for the creation, maintenance and updating of standards and intervention instruments increasingly adjusted to reality. Data from the last five years show that the tourism sector has been gaining relative importance in external sector statistics. Tourism revenues in our Balance of Payments show an increasing trend, reaching US151 million in 2017, which, compared to 2016 data, represents an increase of 39.6%. This dynamic that the tourism sector has been experiencing in the Balance of Payments is related, among other factors, to the marketing policy triggered by the institutions of that sector. However, difficulties prevail in capturing information on tourism revenues, due to at least two main reasons. On the one hand, the weak culture of information provision, both by economic agents and by cultural agents and tour operators; on the other hand, the fact that the billing of some tourism services is still not made using the national banking system. It is in this context that we believe that the pilot project launched today will, in the medium term, boost the collection of export revenues from tourism, since institutional mechanisms of work and coordination will be created for the proper implementation of reforms imbued with the regulations issued. In the end, I hope that this project will be successful and that its results will contribute, as we hope, to maximising revenues to strengthen our economy. Thank you so much for your attention! Maputo, 02 April 2018.
text_original: INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELNCIA O VICE- GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE, VICTOR PEDRO GOMES POR OCASIO DO LANAMENTO DO PROJECTO- PILOTO DE CONTROLO DE RECEITAS DO TURISMO MAPUTO, 02 DE ABRIL DE 2018 Senhor Primeiro-Ministro, Excelncia Senhor Ministro da Cultura e Turismo, Excelncia Senhor Ministro do Interior, Excelncia Senhora Vice-Ministra da Cultura e Turismo, Excelncia Excelentssimo Senhor Presidente da Autoridade Tributria de Moambique, Excelentssimo Senhor Presidente do Instituto Nacional de Estatstica, Excelentssimo Senhor Secretrio Permanente do Ministrio da Cultura e Turismo, Exmos. Senhores Agentes Culturais e Operadores Tursticos, Caros convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Permitam-me que, em primeiro lugar, em nome do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome, sade a todos os presentes nesta cerimnia de lanamento do Projecto-piloto de Controlo Eficaz do Fluxo de Receitas no Exterior e Dilogo com Agentes Culturais e Operadores Tursticos. Dirijo saudaes especiais ao nosso Governo que tem vindo a empreender a coordenao dos diferentes sectores econmicos na busca de melhores solues para o Pas, e a Sua Excelncia Silva Dunduro, Ministro da Cultura e Turismo, por hospedar este importante evento. Gostaria de cumprimentar ainda todos os operadores tursticos e agentes culturais aqui presentes, bem como os gestores e tcnicos do Banco de Moambique e do Ministrio da Cultura e Turismo, que trabalharam arduamente para a concretizao deste projecto, at  actual fase de lanamento. Distintos Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e meus Senhores, Em finais de Dezembro de 2017, o Banco de Moambique, no exerccio da sua funo de autoridade cambial, emitiu um dispositivo legal que estabelece normas e procedimentos a observar na realizao de operaes cambiais. Entre outros aspectos, esse dispositivo elimina a obrigatoriedade de converso de 50% da receita de exportao repatriada para o Pas e transfere para as instituies de crdito parte das operaes de capitais que eram realizadas pelo Banco de Moambique. O princpio do repatriamento previsto na Lei Cambial, entretanto, manteve-se. Estamos conscientes de que a rea cambial  muito dinmica e de que, dependendo do estgio de desenvolvimento, a rede de relaes entre investidores estrangeiros e nacionais pode alterar-se, e consequentemente os movimentos tursticos tambm mudam. Esses factores podem alterar a dinmica dos fluxos financeiros entre o pas e o estrangeiro, pelo que mantemos o compromisso de imprimir a flexibilidade necessria para a criao, manuteno e actualizao de normas e instrumentos de interveno cada vez mais ajustados  realidade. Os dados dos ltimos cinco anos mostram que o sector do turismo tem vindo a ganhar importncia relativa nas estatsticas do sector externo. As receitas de turismo constantes na nossa Balana de Pagamentos apresentam uma tendncia crescente, tendo em 2017 atingido a cifra de 151 milhes de Dlares, o que, comparado com os dados de 2016, representa um aumento de 39.6%. Essa dinmica que o sector de turismo vem registando na Balana de Pagamentos est relacionada, entre outros factores, com a poltica de marketing desencadeada pelas instituies desse sector. Contudo, prevalecem dificuldades na captao de informao sobre as receitas do turismo, devido, pelo menos, a duas principais razes. Por um lado,  fraca cultura de prestao de informao, quer por parte dos agentes econmicos, quer por parte dos agentes culturais e operadores tursticos; por outro, ao facto de a facturao de alguns servios de turismo continuar a no ser feita com recurso ao sistema bancrio nacional.  neste contexto que acreditamos que o Projecto-piloto em lanamento hoje ir, a mdio prazo, impulsionar a captao de receitas de exportao do turismo, uma vez que estaro criados mecanismos institucionais de trabalho e de coordenao para uma adequada implementao das reformas imbudas nos normativos emitidos. A terminar, fao votos para que este projecto seja bem-sucedido e para que os seus resultados contribuam, como esperamos, para maximizar as receitas para fortalecer a nossa economia. Muito obrigado pela ateno! Maputo, 02 de Abril de 2018.

Title: Transcription of the Press Conference of the Monetary Policy Committee (CPMO) on April 11, 2018
text: in Mozambique 11 April 2018 We are gathered here at our usual press conference to announce the deliberations of the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Mozambique. I would like to take this solemn occasion to congratulate my fellow journalists on the passage of the 40Q anniversary. I would also like to thank you for the existing partnership with BM. Through journalists we have had the opportunity not only to communicate with the public about our decisions and market actions, but also to receive, through journalists, the reactions, concerns and anxieties of our people. It's clearly a noble profession. You must be proud of the role you play, of the public service you are playing in our society, this society that still faces many challenges that you, better than anyone else, know. Going to the central theme, I must say that the most important decision of the CPMO is on the MIMO rate, the rate of intervention in the money market. Given the favourable behaviour of the inflation indicator in recent months and its alignment with our projection of single-digit inflation at the end of the year, significantly below 10%, we are comfortable reducing the monetary policy interest rate (MIMO rate) by 150 basis points, from 18.00% to 16.50%. We also took the decision to reduce the Permanent Liquidity Facility (FPC) interest rate from 100 basis points to 18% and to keep the Deposit Facility (FPD) interest rate at 12.5%, as well as maintain mandatory reserve coefficients in national currency as in foreign currency at 14% and 22% respectively. Depending on the evolution of economic and financial indicators and risk factors, the CPMO is prepared to take the necessary measures to respond to any contingency that may occur in the market. Since the last CPMO, held on February 26, to date, we have issued 3 Notices, which constitute the regulatory instrument of the Central Bank system: 1 Code of Conduct of Credit Companies and Financial Institutions  Advertising of Financial Products and Services  Conditions of Movement of the Specific Export Revenue Account. MAIN CHALLENGES At the domestic level it remains the sustainability of public debt and the evolution of the prices of managed goods and at international level we have the manifestation of protectionism in international trade, with particular relevance to the United States, which in turn has an impact in other countries, causing this climate of uncertainties and anxieties in international trade, and the volatility of the dollar and commodity prices, in particular our export and import products which are coal, import natural gas, cotton, etc. CONTEXT The economic climate seen by our operators remains positive having risen for the sixth consecutive month. This indicator shows how the entrepreneurs surveyed view the prospects for employment, demand and activity, and remains consistent for the sixth consecutive month. This also signals that economic activity continues to respond gradually, which is a positive fact. INFLATION The National Statistical Office has regularly updated us on the behaviour of inflation and this remains extremely low. The latest inflation data show that in March annual inflation was 3%., a significantly low figure compared to the same period last year (above 21%). It is a substantial drop in inflation considering that at peak time in 2016 it reached about 27%. When we exclude certain price factors, such as fruits and vegetables and managed prices, some of which are volatile and others are controlled by policy decisions such as managed prices, we observe that inflation (1.34%) is significantly below general inflation (3%). FOREIGN EXCHANGE MARKET In the past we have had a heated debate here about the foreign exchange market, indicating a certain external concern since the foreign exchange market, having enjoyed for several months began a new trend of depreciation and volatility of the currency. The exchange rate began to depreciate at an increasing rate in the foreign exchange market having caused some anxiety in society. We said at the time that this was due to a number of factors, namely the paradigm shift as a result of the introduction of a new regulation of the foreign exchange law and the seasonality of our net export revenues. The first quarter of the year is the period that, for obvious reasons, we export less, export revenues compared to imports of goods and services are much lower and the exchange rate usually depreciates. We take measures considering, above all, the volatility, among them, (i) the increase of mandatory reserves to 22%, about 800 basis points, (ii) sale of previously announced currencies and for the purchase of fuel and (iii) opening up the market for the import of fuels from the point of view of access to foreign exchange. Traditionally, the Bank of Mozambique only sold foreign currency to banks that were registered with the fuel import union that were traditionally BIM and BCI. What we did was open this sale to every bank as long as they met the necessary conditions, regardless of whether or not you are affiliated with the Union. Conditions for moving the export revenue-specific account In summary we can observe that the behavior of the exchange rates of commercial banks with the public, depreciates until reaching the level of 62.74MZN/USD on 10 and 11 March. As a result of the measures taken in the foreign exchange market we began to observe a certain normality in the behavior that was manifested through the reversal of the trend and the volatility of the exchange rate. Today, I can quietly say that the market is relatively stable, the anxiety that existed of the banking and workers about the behavior of the exchange rate is practically controlled. Banks' exchange rates tend to converge. In the period of exchange rate volatility to which we refer (February), exchange rates began to behave in a non-aligned manner and today, as a result of stability and greater tranquility in the market, they begin to converge so that the reference rate and the average rate of commercial banks with the public are practically Aligned. The only rate that continues to behave differently, because it has its particularities, is the exchange rate. Part of the measures we took was that Aas rates were completely out of line, volatility was significant, we had to act and today we are satisfied with the results achieved. RESERVES The level of international reserves in the country is comfortable. Gross reserves remain above the 7 months of import, above the recommended levels of 6 months, which is very good given the uncertainties, challenges and risks we have today. We need to be careful, have margins to be able to deal with emergency situations that may occur. The fact that we faced volatility at the beginning of the year, in a situation where we had a high level of reserves, allowed us to face this situation calmly, without worries and anxieties from the regulator's point of view. This scenario would have been different if our reserves were at low levels. The last reading of our gross reserves was 3.26 billion. TAX RISK The risk remains high. The indicators defined in terms of domestic debt show that this risk continues to grow having increased from 104 697 million meticais in February to 107 823 million meticais at the end of March. INTERBANK MONEY MARKET Interest rates continued to fall. For the first time in several years there was a reversal of behavior. Interbank market interest rates are lower than the BM's benchmark rate, showing that, for the first time, the market and banking are aligned with our regulatory view of reducing rates. We started the cycle of interest rate reduction in April 2017 and have done so in a continuous manner consistent with our expectation of reduced inflation over the course of 2018 and 2019. From a market point of view, this was not the case, the market did not believe in it, there was no confidence, as a result we had a relatively growing curve despite the BM stating that the inflation projection was of a fall the bank opted for the rise. Today, several years later, there is a clear harmony between the mercad, in terms of expectation, and the BM. LIQUIDITY The potential liquidity is around 160 billion meticais and is essentially applied to Treasury And Treasury Bills, the rest of which is in the interbank system. Generally speaking, all the liquidity of the system is practically in these instruments. Credit and monetary aggregates remain stagnant, maintaining the same reading we had in February. GROSS DOMESTIC PRODUCT AND INFLATION GDP will continue to grow moderately, according to our internal projections, and inflation will be at 1 digit, below 10%. In other words, what we want to say is that under normal conditions, if we continue to do our job as normal, we expect inflation at the end of 2018 to be single digits with moderate GDP growth. Q&A SESSION IMPLICATIONS OF THE INCREASE OF THE FED RATE TO 1.75% The increase will have an impact on the short-term capital flow. For us the capital flows with impact in our country are medium and long term, essentially direct investment in the form of buying and building companies. This interest rate will have a relatively marginal impact because we are not yet integrated into short-term flows in our economy. ACTIVE INTEREST RATES PRACTICED BY COMMERCIAL BANKS ARE NOT ALIGNED WITH THE BEHAVIOR OF BM RATES 0 BM as monetary authority has control over certain components of the active rate that banks practice with their customers and, as it has been observed, that component of the final rate to the consumer, in our part, has been falling. However, we are aware that the rates practiced by the bank have not reduced in the same proportion, nor to the desired levels. When we go up the rate, commercial banks go up in the same proportion, but when we reduce the rate they no longer do so in the same proportion. This is a legitimate debate. We're working with the bank to deal with these situations. At this point it would be premature to say what we are going to achieve, but there is work going on. Our attitude has been towards collaboration, not confrontation. We could make unilateral decisions because the Bank has all the powers to do so, but that is not what we want. Sustainable solutions are those in which one party tries to understand the behavior of the other party in order to work together. Ultimately we want the well-being of our consumer. There is, therefore, work that is underway that also includes spread issues to know how trading banks calculate their spread, what the criteria are, so we know what their behavior will be when we raise rates. We have a BM team working together with a team from the Banking Association on this matter. CLARIFICATION ON SANCTIONS ON COMMERCIAL BANKS We do not have any feedback that commercial banks are appealing in the courts. All the fines have been paid. These are infringements that have occurred over a number of periods, but the sanctions were imposed last year. I would like to point out that we are guided by collaboration with the bank, that there is no confrontation, we could even have been more rigorous than we were, but what we want is to signal a certain concern, we want the bankto improve its behaviour. These are credit institutions that are managing our citizens' savings and we have to ensure that they work with the best standards of transparency within national and international law and practices. The bank will have to get used to this because we will regularly sanction institutions that are not complying with the rules and we will publish these sanctions in the media. This is a new reality and is part of the discipline of the market. It is important that society and shareholders know what is happening. The banks are working with us on this. FUEL PRICES Although it is not the bank dealing with the issue of fuel prices I can clearly state there is now greater flexibility in relation to fuel prices. The elimination of subsidies allows prices to fall depending on international prices. 0 fuel is a good that like so many others has price variations. If international prices rise/fall, local fuel prices should also rise/fall. Not checking this behavior carries a very high price for society and for our public finances, because when international prices go up and ours does not go up it means that someone will have to pay the difference, in that case the state through taxes that instead of being used for health, for roads or other priority goods are subsidising the consumption of this good. RISKS ON MONEY LAUNDERING This is not an opportune time, I will take note of this and I will ask colleagues in the area of financial education to respond in due course. We have a specific department for financial education, what we can do is include this story in one of our financial education programs so that the public can better understand what is happening. We are being rigorous in order to make our square a financial square of rigour and seriousness in this matter and, to that end, we are working with the bank which is the primary beneficiary. Here we are also in a scenario of collaboration and non-confrontation, banking wants to contribute to our system and everything has to be done within the rules and practices provided for in our national and international laws, regulations and practices. EVOLUTION OF MANAGED PRICES At the moment we do not have the ability to predict prices, but if the factors affecting transport costs, etc. go up and the consumer price is not adjusted, someone has to pay. And when that doesn't happen, it's the tax money that has to subsidize it. Society may even decide in this way, but the bill is high on this type of subsidy. It is necessary to become aware of the cost of the account and to ensure that certain prices begin to respond to the costs implied in the production of these goods and services. Thank you
text_original: TRANSCRIO CPMO 11 de Abril de 2018 Estamos aqui reunidos na nossa habitual conferncia de imprensa para anunciar as deliberaes do Comit de Poltica Monetria do Banco de Moambique. Queria aproveitar esta ocasio solene para dar os parabns aos colegas jornalistas pela passagem do 40Q aniversrio. Queria igualmente agradecer pela parceria existente com o BM. Atravs dos jornalistas temos tido a oportunidade no s de comunicar com o pblico sobre as nossas decises e actuaes do mercado, mas tambm de receber, atravs dos jornalistas, as reaces, preocupaes e as ansiedades do nosso povo.  claramente uma profisso nobre. Vocs devem estar orgulhosos do papel que desempenham, do servio pblico que esto a exercer na nossa sociedade, esta sociedade que enfrenta ainda vrios desafios que vocs, melhor do que ningum, conhecem. Indo ao tema central, devo dizer que a deciso mais importante do CPMO  sobre a taxa MIMO, a taxa de interveno no mercado monetrio. Tendo em conta o comportamento favorvel do indicador da inflao nos ltimos meses e o seu alinhamento com a nossa projeco de uma inflao, no final do ano, de um dgito, significativamente abaixo de 10%, sentimo-nos confortveis em reduzir a taxa de juro de poltica monetria (taxa MIMO) em 150 pontos base, de 18.00% para 16,50%. Tomamos igualmente a deciso de reduzir a taxa de juro de Facilidade Permanente de Cedncia de liquidez (FPC) de 100 pontos base para 18% e manter a taxa de juro da Facilidade Permanente de Depsito (FPD) em 12.5%, bem como manter os coeficientes de reserva obrigatrias em moeda nacional como em moeda estrangeira em 14% e 22 % respectivamente. Dependendo da evoluo dos indicadores econmico-financeiros e dos factores de risco, o CPMO est preparado para tomar as medidas necessrias para responder a qualquer contingncia que possa acontecer no mercado. Desde o ltimo CPMO, realizado a 26 de Fevereiro, at hoje, emitimos 3 Avisos, que constituem o instrumento de regulamentao do sistema do Banco Central: 1 Cdigo de Conduta das Sociedades de Crdito e Instituies Financeiras  Publicidade dos Produtos e Servios Financeiros  Condies da Movimentao da Conta Especfica de Receita de Exportao. PRINCIPAIS DESAFIOS A nvel domstico continua a ser a sustentabilidade da dvida pblica e a evoluo dos preos dos bens administrados e a nvel internacional temos a manifestao do proteccionismo no comrcio internacional, com particular relevncia para os Estados Unidos, que por sua vez tem impacto em outros pases, provocando este clima de incertezas e ansiedades no comrcio internacional, e a volatilidade do dlar e dos preos das commodities, em particular os nossos produtos de exportao e importao que so o carvo, o gs natural de importao, o algodo, etc. CONTEXTO 0 clima econmico visto pelos nossos operadores continua positivo tendo subido pelo sexto ms consecutivo. Este indicador mostra como os empresrios inquiridos veem as perspectivas de emprego, procura e de actividade, e continua consistente pelo sexto ms consecutivo. Isso tambm sinaliza que a actividade econmica continua a responder gradualmente, facto positivo. INFLAO 0 Instituto Nacional de Estatstica tem nos actualizado regularmente sobre o comportamento da inflao sendo que esta continua extremamente baixa. Os ltimos dados sobre a inflao mostram que, em Maro, a inflao homloga era de 3%., valor significativamente baixo comparado a igual perodo do ano passado (acima de 21%).  uma queda substancial da inflao considerando ainda que na altura de pico, em 2016, atingiu cerca de 27%. Quando exclumos certos factores de preo, como frutas e vegetais e preos administrados, sendo que uns so volteis e outros so controlados por decises de poltica como  o caso dos preos administrados, observamos que a inflao (1,34%) fica significativamente abaixo da inflao geral (3%). MERCADO CAMBIAL No passado tivemos aqui um debate caloroso sobre o mercado cambial, com indicao de uma certa preocupao externa uma vez que o mercado cambial, depois de ter apreciado por vrios meses iniciou uma nova tendncia de depreciao e volatilidade da moeda. O cmbio comeou a depreciar a uma velocidade crescente no mercado cambial tendo causado uma certa ansiedade na sociedade. Para ns os fluxos de capitais com impacto no nosso pas so de mdio e longo prazo, essencialmente investimento directo em forma de compra e construo de empresas. Title: Speech at the Opening of the 10th Scientific Conference of the Bank of Mozambique
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENCY THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, DOCTOR ROGeRIO ZANDAMELA On THE OCCASION OF THE OPENING OF the "X SCIENTIFIC DAYS OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE" MAPUTO, 15 JUNE 2018 Mr Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency Former Governors of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellencies, Honourable Members of the Diplomatic Corps, Honourable Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Honourable Representatives of Public Institutions, Distinguished Representatives of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, Representatives of Academic Institutions and Research Centres, Directors, Managers and Technicians of the Bank of Mozambique, Representatives of the Media, Distinguished Guests, Ladies, gentlemen, good morning! It is with great satisfaction that I greet, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, all those present in these "Tenth Scientific Days of the WB", which take place, as usual, in the week of the Metical, our national currency. We therefore reiterate our call on the entire Mozambican society to keep the notes and coins of the Metical, thus helping the Bank of Mozambique in its effort to make banknotes available that are increasingly safe and resistant. Today, we pride ourselves on seeing metical increasingly robust in relation to other currencies. Let me welcome, with particular appreciation and gratitude, to Dr. Ernesto Gove, former Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, for having promptly accepted the invitation we have formulated to be the keynote speaker of this edition of scientific days. I would also like to thank Professor Dr. Matias Farahane, President of the Jury, as well as his Vowels, Prof. Dr. Engineer Lourino Chemane, Dr. Saide Dade and Dr. Fernando Cuche, who spared no effort to evaluate the submitted works, with professionalism and engagement. I am very much listening to all the researchers, but in particular those who have been selected and selected, who have worked hard and have been willing to share their research projects with us. Distinguished guests, Ladies, Gentlemen, 0 theme chosen for this edition of the Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique, which constitute a moment of mutual learning, is "The Role of Digital Financial Services in Financial Inclusion: Challenges and Opportunities". This is a topical issue for the financial industry, as the digitisation of financial services has taken on unprecedented prominence and has received increasing attention in how to do business in the financial system around the world. The achievement of the objectives of our National Financial Inclusion Strategy depends to a large extent on progress in the digitisation of financial services, as the experiences of reference countries in this area, such as Kenya, show us. Aware of this correlation, very recently we launched the incubator of financial technologies, which we hope will contribute to the process of revolution of the digitization of financial services in Mozambique in the coming years. We are aware that this can only be achieved through the full collaboration of the multiple actors involved, including the regulatory body, financial institutions and other digital service providers, as well as consumers. In this context, these Days are a unique opportunity for us together to reap subsidies to better respond to the challenges and opportunities inherent in the digitization of financial services, maximizing their benefits and minimizing the associated risks. Ladies Gentlemen In the present Scientific Days, the Jury selected two research papers that will be presented here by two young Mozambicans. The first presentation will deal with "The Use of Mobile Phones as Access Points to Financial Products and Services", by Mr. Jose Ganhane, who, for the second consecutive time, reaches the final stage of our days. The second presentation is an analysis of the "Sustainable Digital Financial Inclusion Models for Our Country", authored by Mr. Silvano Castanheira. Despite the diversity of approaches, stimulated by the complexity of the theme, the work that will be presented here is unanimous as to the role that digital financial services play in promoting financial inclusion and in the economic and social development of the country. Considering the diversity of participants present in this great room and the timeliness of the theme, we are aware that the debate that will follow the presentations will bring teachings valid for all of us. I am also convinced that, like previous editions, we will share knowledge and experience that will contribute to the formulation of appropriate policies, aiming at achieving the economic and social development of the country. Thus, I declare open the Tenth Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique. Thank you very much!

Title: Transcription of the Press Conference of the Monetary Policy Committee (CPMO) on June 18, 2018
text: in Mozambique03/2018 18 June 2018 This is our 3rd meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (CPMO) of the WB. After this we will have even more 3 for the rest of the year, namely in August, October and November. As is practical we meet today and take some deliberations. Considering the short-term inflation outlook as well as their medium-term projection, indicators continue to point to a figure around a single digit. Considering all the underlying risks, the BM Monetary Policy Committee decided:  Reduce the monetary policy interest rate, MIMO rate, by 75 basis points, to 15.75 %. With this measure, policy interest rates, in terms of percentage points, fell beyond the 600 basis points (pb) of the increase we had in October 2016. This represents the continuation of the path of decreasing rates that began in April 2017.  In addition, we also evaluated the other rates and decided to keep the interest rate of the Permanent Liquidity-Holding Facility (FPC) at 18%, reduce the interest rate of the Permanent Deposit Facility (FPD) by 50bp to 12% and maintain the Mandatory Reserves coefficient for liabilities in national currency and foreign currency by 14.00% and 22.00%, respectively. As always, depending on the evolution of economic and financial indicators and considering risk factors, the CPMO may take the necessary corrective measures before the next meeting which is in principle scheduled for 30 August 2018. Since the last CPMO, which took place in April, we have published a Notice related to the updating of prudential limits and the concentration of risks of credit institutions. MAIN CHALLENGES FOR DECISION-MAKING As always, we have challenges at home and internationally. At the domestic level we have the uncertainties as to the rigor of the fiscal consolidation measures necessary to mitigate the risks associated with the sustainability of public debt, in the context of the election cycles in 2018, which are the municipal elections and, in 2019, the presidential and governors elections. The second domestic challenge concerns uncertainties about the trend in the prices of liquid fuels and other managed service goods such as water, energy, semi-collective transport, toll, interest rates, etc. At the international level we have added a challenge totaling three, namely: i) the likely impact of growing trade tension between major economies, in particular the United States, Europe and some emerging economies including China, Brazil, Mexico and others; (ii) the impact of commodity price volatility, with effects on domestic prices and the balance of payments which, depending on price behaviour, may affect the trajectory of our balance of payments as well as domestic prices; and (iii) the Metical exchange rate which remains volatile against the dollar, which in turn may affect the evolution of economic and financial indicators for the future. In relation to GDP (gross domestic product), according to data published by the National Institute of Statistics (INE), we have moderate GDP growth in the first quarter of 2018 of 3.2% driven by agriculture, minerals and trade. The most interesting fact here, from the narrative point of view, is that while in the first quarter of 2017 GDP grew 4.7%, in fact, the sector that contributed the most to this growth was that of mining, which, in the first quarter, grew by almost 60%. This growth practically boosted GDP in 2017. What we are seeing in 2018 is a further diversification of economic growth. Virtually all sectors of the economy are growing, with the exception of electricity and water. That's good news from the point of view of the economy as a whole. This is the big change from the narrative from 2017 to 2018. We expect this narrative to continue until the end of the year. As for inflation, it continues on its decreasing trajectory, as I said early on. Our expectation is that by the end of the year we will have inflation around one digit. According to THE INE data, currently annual inflation is at 3.26% and inflation averages 7.64%. Average inflation continues to fall and will continue to fall until the end of December. At the last meeting, average inflation had not yet reached a single digit, although it was close. The goal has already been reached. So there is greater convergence between end-of-period inflation and average inflation. This is good news because it shows that our projections, based on the information we have, are realistic and it is almost certain that we can achieve the goal of having single-digit inflation in 2018. This is important because inflation has actually increased by 3.26%, which is a low value, and this takes into account the high adjustment we have had in managed prices, in particular liquid fuels. If they notice, liquid fuel prices have been adjusted by almost 20%. Despite this we have inflation that shows that other products, in particular cereals, fruits and vegetables have had negative growth and, if we exclude the behavior of managed prices, we have seen that underlying inflation is practically around 1% rather than 3.26%. From the point of view of monetary policy this is the most relevant inflation because we have to exclude seasonal or policy factors. In fact the adjustment of administrative prices is also a policy decision. METICAL In line with what we observed at the last CPMO meeting in April, the Metical continues to appreciate the major currencies, in particular the Dollar, the Euro and the Rand. The good news is the exchange rate is virtually the same as it was at the close of 2017. We are in a stable environment from the point of view of the foreign exchange market, particularly from the point of view of our exchange rate. BALANCE OF PAYMENTS The trade balance, which is the balance of imports and exports of goods, continues to behave positively. In the first quarter of 2018, exports grew more than imports, a growth of almost USD 194 million, for exports, against a growth of USD 82 million, of imports, which reflects a strengthening of our trade balance. This is also reflected in the foreign exchange market as it means a greater entry of foreign exchange into the market and banking, which allows our currency to continue to appreciate and also allows the BM to strengthen its reserve position. The largest export products were coal, aluminum, electrical cables, rubies and heavy sands. In imports we have the usual products, which are consumer products, intermediate products, etc. Despite positive trade balance behaviour, the current account, which also includes services, has deteriorated due to increased payments for services abroad, in particular to large companies. The deficit in the balance of services, which in the first quarter of 2017 was 325 million, increases the deficit to 555 million and has affected the current account from a deteriorating point of view. Despite the improvement in the balance of goods, the deficit of which has fallen, the balance of services increased considerably which implied an increase in the current account deficit from USD 811 million in the first quarter of 2017 to USD 964 million. The financial account of direct investments continues to fall, but other forms of investment have strengthened and generally compensated for the fall in direct investment. Our reserves have benefited from this positive environment in foreign trade, and today we have a situation of comfortable gross reserves that have grown, albeit slightly. In the first quarter, the position was 3.225 billion and is now 3.335 billion. It is a modest but positive growth in the context in which we find ourselves, which leads us to a situation of sufficient gross reserves to cover a little more than 7 months of import, which is certainly above the recommended minimum that is 6 months. 'Re we have exchange rate stability, rates and we also have a strengthening of our international reserves. It is a positive moment in the market in this respect. As for public indebtedness, we don't have good news. We define public indebtedness in terms of bonds, Treasury Bills (BT) and treasury bonds, also including bm advances. The deficit has increased by almost 10 billion meticais since the beginning of the year, and on the last day of May it was 105.5 billion meticais, equivalent to just over 112% of GDP. This is the weight of domestic debt as a function of GDP. It is good to point out that this domestic debt does not include everything that is debt. There are certain components of domestic debt that are not yet included in certain goods contracts, server contracts and delays. This to say that the actual number is relatively higher than this, because here only captures the debt in BT bonds and advances from the BM. Turning back rates: interbank market rate developments have seen a slight change, but the yield curve of our interest rates remains negative, however not as much as seen in April. ACTIVE RATES It is the fees applied to retail credit operations, those in which we ask for credit lines in banking. These rates have been relatively modest, however, we continue to have a relative rigidity in these rates. Retail interest rates fell from around 38% to 28.78 %, a drop of just over 3.5 percentage points (pp), while the deposit rate fell sharply , which is almost an extension of that range. Active rates are not falling as much as passive rates. On the other hand, the prime rate continues to fall, more sharply than banks' interest rates. The evolution of private credit, as well as other households, remains stagnant, in line with the reading of the last session of the CPMO. Credit to the private sector remains stagnant as well as other monetary aggregates, in a context where public indebtedness, i.e. public sector credit continues to grow, while public sector credit falls (crowding out). Finally, with regard to the 2018 projections, we continue with the outlook we had in the last CPMO, low and stable inflation, around a single digit at the end of the year and moderate GDP growth. QUESTION SESSION DEBT RELATIONSHIP WITH THE ELECTORAL CYCLE Domestic debt remains high (the figures show that this excludes other outstanding debts) around 12%. Foreign debt is around 100% and public sector debt around 110 -112% of GDP. It is an extremely high debt, which raises questions in the light of sustainability. Nothing new so far. The relationship between this debt and the electoral cycle is not a new thing, nor intrinsic to Mozambique. In all countries that go through election cycles, including the United States, taking action at that time is complicated. The scope for taking fiscal adjustment measures necessary to mitigate these debts in order to generate the benefits necessary to be able to control the growth of this debt that is very high is very limited when we approach the election period, which is the period in which we are. As I said, it's nothing specific to Mozambique. And general information. This does not mean that nothing will be done, but space is very limited in this context. It is part of the democratic process, there are elections and politicians have sensitivity in these moments to deal with difficult decisions, something common in all countries. REDUCTION OF INVESTMENT IN THE ELECTORAL CYCLE In most of the countries I've been to, every time there's an election cycle investors always expect, because they don't know who's going to win the election and what the priorities of the new team will be. There's always a reduction in investment at that time. And a period of uncertainty on the part of investors and they hope to be clear about the application of values and areas of investment, taking into account the priorities of the government. CROWDING OUT PERSPECTIVES This is not an easy issue because we cannot reduce fees through administrative measures. As I have explained in the past, part of the rates component has to do with the behavior of policy rates, but on the other hand, we have a market-related component of ours. At the current juncture, rates remain high and are necessary in order to have the kind of macroeconomic stability and balance we need. However, we expect rates to continue to fall, some significantly, as is the case with the prime rate, whose fall is significantly more pronounced relative to retail interest rates. There's good news, but we want the news to be even better. For this we need to be patient, because these measures take some time to produce results, but the signal is good, the direction is correct, the intensity could be better. It is not an easy thing, it is not just up to the WB, it depends on other factors outside our control, on a whole exercise of reforms, on the behaviour of public finances, fiscal consolidation and other things. All of this has an impact on crowding out. GROSS DOMESTIC PRODUCT The World Bank's perspective is no different from ours. We have a GDP that grows moderately, we have an internal debt with some factors that are not included, but there is work that is being done by the government to determine the level of indebtedness with suppliers in particular and others. We don't have the numbers right now. It's something that's out of our control. But there is certainly work going on, because the debt will have to be paid and the government wants to pay, but it has to determine the legitimacy of those debts. It's almost a detective's job, it's not just looking at the papers, it's necessary to find out what you've actually received. EXPECTED PERCENTAGE OF GROWTH The numbers are weighted by a number of factors. We have several scenarios. We can say 3.5%, 4.5% or 5%, depending on the manifestation of the various risk factors we mentioned, which will have an impact on debt. The same is the case for inflation. What I can say about that is that it will be single digits. It is not by chance that we do not give the number, I know they would like me to declare an exact number but we are not in a position to do so. The conditions for doing this type of analysis are not created. But we are sure of one thing: we can reach a digit. That's good news for us in the context of our economy. That's the only thing I can guarantee right now. INFORMATION TRANSMITTED BY THE MOZAMBIQUE CHANNEL On this subject is present the Director of Internal Audit who, in due course, can help clarify and may realize that there is nothing unusual about what was written in the report. LIQUIDATOR COMMISSION OF OUR BANK What happens, in fact, is that the work has not stopped and it is important to underline this. In some institutions where we have already done this work in 2018, smaller institutions have not even appointed a committee. The work was done by ourselves. We are currently rethinking the best way to deal with this matter. Whether on the basis of a commission or whether it will be a liquidator working with the bm employees. I want to be frank and open about it: these things are complicated because they involve costs. The more people are used in these things, the higher the costs and the less money available to refund people. Part of the decision also has to do with the weighting of these factors. There's always the risk. We pay those who work, those who owe money and nothing left. We had to ponder and in my opinion it was one of the elements that weighed the most. Lastly we have to protect the final creditor, the depositors, and for that to happen we have to have the necessary resources available. In short, the work continues and it is important that it takes place in the shortest possible period of time. I recently dealt with a settlement that lasted 15 years. That's not acceptable. The Commission that was working did the best it could under the conditions in which it was working, but ultimately we had to protect the assets. The bankrupt mass. PENALTIES FOR MOZA MANAGERS Everyone has collaborated and continues to cooperate. For us here at BM this is a past matter. There is an interest of everyone, including the sanctioned people, in strengthening our system. It's part of market discipline. There is no market economy without sanctions. A sanctions-free market economy becomes anarchy. When there are deviations the regulator does what it has to do and takes the necessary measures to rectify these deviations and even to send a message to realize that there are consequences for certain behaviors. We appreciate all the collaboration we have received from Moza managers and everyone who has worked on our team for this outcome. QUESTIONABLE DEBTS As I said earlier there is ongoing work to be developed by the Ministry of Finance and the Treasury. We don't have the values, and I don't think they do. They're still working. If they had already shared it with us. ARMED CONFLICT OF SLENDER CABLE IS NOT TAKEN AS A RISK As you may know, the information available about the Cabo Delgado conflict is limited to all of us. So it's not a risk yet. We are not in a position to assess whether it is significant or not. At this time, based on the information we have, we classify it as insignificant. And all I can say. We don't have enough information yet. There was much more clarity about the conflict in the past (in the central area), about the impact it had on the country's economic activity and on communication between north and south. It was much easier to assess and consider this kind of risk. This conflict of Cabo Delgado is recent. It is still being studied and we are not experts to measure this conflict. We still don't have enough information for that. Thank you

Title: Speech on the Launch of the Renewable Energy Credit Line
text: SPEECH OF HIS EXCELLENCY THE VICE-GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, DR. VeaCTOR PEDRO GOMES On THE OCCASION OF THE LAUNCH OF THE BCI CREDIT LINEFOR THE FINANCING OF RENEWABLE ENERGY PRODUCTS AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY (RE/EE) MAPUTO, 09 JULY 2018 Mr Minister for Land, Environment and Rural Development, Your Excellency, Your Excellency, Mr President of the Board of Directors of BCI, Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany, Your Excellency, Gentlemen Members of the Diplomatic Corps, Excellencies Your Honourable Presidents of Executive Committees and other representatives of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, Your Excelleres, Representatives of Government Institutions, Honourable Representatives of the media. Distinguished guests. Ladies Gentlemen First of all, I would like to thank, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, the invitation addressed to us by BCI to participate in this ceremony and witness the launch of the renewable energy and energy efficiency product financing line. On this solemn occasion, I would like to extend our greetings to all present in this room, in particular bci managers and technicians for launching this important vehicle for our economy. Allow me to extend our greetings to the German Government, our cooperation partner, represented by KfW, for its leading role in financing this initiative. Ladies Gentlemen The launch of this financing line today reflects the commitment of the financial sector in promoting Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises operating in the renewable energy sector, an important segment in contributing to inclusive and sustainable growth in our country. Let me go back in time and recall the history of the funding line that is now peaking. This funding line is part of the financing agreement for the "Sustainable Economic Development Programme - Promotion of the Financial Sector", signed in 2012 between the governments of Mozambique and Germany. Under this program, the German Government, represented by KfW, provides financial support, and the Government of Mozambique, represented by the Bank of Mozambique, implements the credit lines for the promotion of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency products. This is how the Bank of Mozambique identified, through a public tender, the financial institutions that would work on the implementation of the project, and BCI was one of those institutions. The implementation agreement was signed in 2014. It is therefore with great satisfaction that we witness today the launch of the credit line for the promotion of Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency products, an important component to boost our economic growth. Renewable energy is a viable alternative at a time when there is increasing efforts for countries to reduce their dependence on fossil fuels. We are convinced that the development of renewable energy products will have a major impact on society, not only by improving the environment, but also by enabling the creation of new jobs, as well as conducting further research into new technologies to improve energy efficiency. Title: Speech at the Signing of the Second Addendum to the Contract for the Construction of the Auto Silo between the Maputo Municipal Council and the Bank of Mozambique
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENCYROGeRIO ZANDAMELA, GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE On THE OCCASION OF THE SIGNING OF THE SECOND AGREEMENT FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF THE AUTO SILO BETWEEN THE MAPUTO CITY COUNCIL AND THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE MAPUTO, 18 JULY 2018 Mr President of the Maputo City Council, Excellency Mr. Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency Honourable, Administrators of the Bank of Mozambique, Honourable Councillor of the Maputo City Council, Dear managers and technicians of the Bank of Mozambique and the Maputo City Council, Ladies and Gentlemen, it is with high honour that, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on behalf of me, address to all present the wishes of welcome to this signing ceremony of the second addition to the contract for the construction of the auto silo between the Bank of Mozambique and the Maputo City Council. I extend a special greeting to our guest of honor, His Excellency David Simango, President of the Maputo City Council, for the excellent work he has done to give our beautiful capital city an ever better image. The event that we witness today symbolizes the institutional cooperation between our two institutions and reinforces the strategic partnership formalized in May 2008, with the conclusion of the Agreement, which today undergoes its second addition to continue with the work of building to house the Municipal Balcony, the Sports Raffle Stand and its respective parking lot. For the Bank of Mozambique, as a financier, the construction of this project is important to create safe and decent conditions for parking and providing services to the municipalities of Maputo, so it was with great satisfaction that we learned that the work has already been consigned on the last nine of this month. I am sure that the addendum we have just signed will accelerate the achievement of the intended short-term objectives. I would therefore like to make known here the appreciation of the Bank of Mozambique for the efforts made by the Maputo City Council, in the person of its President, for the materialisation of this solemn act, reiterating our support in the spirit of transparency in this amendment. Finally, I address my thanks to the technical teams that, on behalf of the two institutions, lent their knowledge and dedication to the achievement of this noble objective for the well-being of the citizens of Maputo. Thank you very much!

Title: Speech at the Signing of the Cooperation Protocol between the Bank of Mozambique and the Ministry of Culture
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENcy OGOVERNADORDO BANCO DE MOcAMBIQUE,Dr. ROGeRIO ZANDAMELA ON THE OCCASION OF THE SIGNING OF THE COOPERATION BETWEEN THE BM AND MICULTUR 3 MAPUTO, 20 AUGUST 2018 Minister for Culture and Tourism, Excellency Your Excellese Ly Ministry of Culture and Tourism Honourable Representative of the National Institute of Statistics Your Excellese Confederation of Economic Associations Dear Managers and Technicians of the Bank of Mozambique and the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, Dear guests, Ladies and gentlemen, Let me, first of all, welcome, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, to all present at this signing ceremony of the cooperation protocol between the Bank of Mozambique and the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. Secondly, I would like to address a special greeting to His Excellency Silva Dunduro, Minister of Culture and Tourism for the work he has undertaken to promote Culture and Tourism in our country, as well as for his commitment to the materialisation of the protocol we have just signed. To all the managers and technicians of the two institutions who, directly or indirectly, have contributed to the materialisation of this Act, I express our appreciation. For the Bank of Mozambique, this protocol represents an important step towards improving the statistical information reported in our Balance of Payments, and its implementation will boost the materialization of some devices issued by the Bank of Mozambique, which establish the standards and procedures to be observed in the execution of foreign exchange operations, in the field of tourism operations. As the authority responsible for compiling the Balance of Payments, we also consider that the protocol we have just signed is of increased importance, as it will improve the collection of data on international travel services, an important category for assessing the evolution of tourism revenues and expenses. Currently, the data of our Balance of Payments indicate that tourism revenues amount to US151 million, a value clearly below the real potential of the country, so we hope that the implementation of this Protocol will bring significant improvements in this framework. It is our wish that the relations of cooperation between our institutions will be strengthened and serve the purpose of stimulating and stimulating the planning process and improving competitiveness in the tourism sector , thus contributing to the creation of a favorable business environment in the country. I end my speech by hopeing that this protocol will be successful and produce the results we aim to achieve in the process of collecting and compiling tourism statistics, which will certainly contribute to the development of the sector in particular and the economy in general. Thank you so much for your attention!
