Title: Speech at the Opening of the 5th Supervision Meeting of Central Banks of Portuguese-Speaking Countries
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENCY THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, Dr. ROGeRIO ZANDAMELA ON THE OCCASION OF THE SIGNING OF THE NEW AGREEMENT ON INDEXING OF THE MOZAMBICAN BANKING SYSTEM MAPUTO, 14 SEPTEMBER 2018 Mr. Vice-Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency, Honourable Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Mr President of the Mozambican Association of Banks, Honourable Presidents of the Boards of Directors and Executive Committees of credit institutions and financial corporations. Dear Managers of the Bank of Mozambique, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and gentlemen, First of all, I would like to thank, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, the presence of all at this signing ceremony on the indexing of interest rates in the banking system between the Bank of Mozambique, the Mozambican Association of Banks and credit institutions and financial corporations. Secondly, I would like to take this opportunity to address a word of appreciation to all credit institutions and financial corporations for their deep involvement in the work that culminated in the production of the agreement we have just signed. We would like to point out that, although this is a new agreement, the central objectives that led to the signing of the former remain valid. It is our understanding that, after 15 months of implementation of the single indexing agreement, we have accumulated enough experience that deserved to be incorporated into the understandings reached in 2017, with a view to optimising the model and making the nature of this instrument more transparent and perceptible to society as a whole. We are convinced that the improvements we have made to the agreement we have just initialled create the conditions for the mechanism for the formation of interest rates to be more transparent, making room for credit interest rates to more closely monitor the risk profile that our market faces, without neglecting greater alignment with signals issued by the central bank. We have no doubt that this agreement does not fully respond to the expectations of Mozambican society, which calls for lower and competitive credit interest rates, but I can assure you that, under its new terms, we will soon be able to witness a bearish revision in the cost premium by around 80 basis points. In addition, with the implementation of this Agreement, the Bank of Mozambique, as a regulator, will be better able to monitor the movements of interest rates of credit institutions, because in the new terms of this instrument are specified the different portions that enter into the mechanism for defining the indexing and interest rates of the system as a whole, which includes a cost premium. If we remember, the old agreement provided that the credit interest rate applied by credit institutions and financial corporations to their clients resulted from the sum between the single indexer, a cost premium and a spread reflecting not only the risk profile of the client, but also the business. The new agreement maintains that structure, but disaggregates the elements that make up the cost premium and specifies the spread component that identifies the risk profile of the borrowers, defined on the basis of standard conditions by credit category. In this way, the movements of the cost premium will depend on the changes in the Country Rating , the Default Credit Ratio, the Saneado Credit Ratio and the Mandatory Reserve Coefficient for Liabilities in National Currency. On the other hand, the credit spread to be disclosed by each credit institution will be based on a set of criteria standardized by the banking industry, giving the customer space to better negotiate and decide on the conditions of access to bank financing. Ladies and gentlemen, Despite these advantages, we are aware that the agreement we have just signed is not yet a perfect and finished product. There are aspects that we should continue to improve throughout the implementation process, so we have agreed to make improvements and revisions to its terms from time to time. We believe that the greatest challenge, as in any agreement, lies in its proper implementation, so we call on all actors to strictly comply with this agreement, with professionalism, honesty, transparency and, above all, in a didactic way. I end my speech by giving special thanks to the joint technical teams of the Mozambican Association of Banks, credit institutions and financial corporations and the Bank of Mozambique, who worked hard to materialize this Agreement. Thank you so much for your attention!
text_original: INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELNCIA O GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE, Dr. ROGRIO ZANDAMELA POR OCASIO DA ASSINATURA DO NOVO ACORDO SOBRE INDEXANTE NICO DO SISTEMA BANCRIO MOAMBICANO MAPUTO, 14 DE SETEMBRO DE 2018 Senhor Vice-Governador do Banco de Moambique, Excelncia Excelentssimos Senhores Administradores do Banco de Moambique, Excelentssimo Senhor Presidente da Associao Moambicana de Bancos, Excelentssimos Senhores Presidentes dos Conselhos de Administrao e das Comisses Executivas das instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras. Caros Gestores do Banco de Moambique, Ilustres Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Quero, em primeiro lugar, agradecer, em nome do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome, a presena de todos nesta cerimnia de assinatura do novo acordo sobre o indexante das taxas de juro no sistema bancrio, entre o Banco de Moambique, a Associao Moambicana de Bancos e as instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras. Em segundo lugar, gostaria de aproveitar esta ocasio para enderear uma palavra de apreo a todas as instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras, pelo seu profundo envolvimento nos trabalhos que culminaram com a produo do acordo que acabamos de assinar. Gostaramos de assinalar que, pese embora tratar-se de um novo acordo, mantm-se vlidos os objectivos centrais que nortearam a assinatura do primeiro.  nosso entendimento que, aps 15 meses de implementao do acordo sobre indexante nico, acumulmos experincia suficiente que merecia ser incorporada nos entendimentos alcanados em 2017, tendo em vista optimizar o modelo e tornar a natureza deste instrumento mais transparente e perceptvel para toda a sociedade. Estamos convictos de que as melhorias que introduzimos no acordo que acabamos de rubricar criam as condies para que o mecanismo de formao das taxas de juros seja mais transparente, abrindo espao para que as taxas de juros de crdito acompanhem mais fielmente o perfil de risco que o nosso mercado enfrenta, sem descurar um maior alinhamento com os sinais emitidos pelo banco central. No temos dvidas de que o presente acordo no responde cabalmente aos anseios da sociedade moambicana, que clama por taxas de juros de crdito mais baixas e competitivas, mas posso assegurar que, por fora dos seus novos termos, poderemos testemunhar brevemente uma reviso em baixa no prmio de custo em cerca de 80 pontos base. Adicionalmente, com a implementao do presente acordo, o Banco de Moambique, na qualidade de regulador, estar em melhores condies de monitorar os movimentos das taxas de juros das instituies de crdito, pois nos novos termos do presente instrumento so especificadas as diferentes parcelas que entram no mecanismo de definio do indexante e das taxas de juro do sistema no seu todo, que inclui um prmio de custo. Se nos lembramos, o antigo acordo previa que a taxa de juro de crdito aplicada pelas instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras aos seus clientes resultava da soma entre o indexante nico, um prmio de custo e um spread reflectindo, no s o perfil de risco do cliente, como do negcio. Com efeito, o novo acordo mantm essa estrutura, mas desagrega os elementos que compem o prmio de custo e especifica a componente do spread que identifica o perfil de risco dos muturios, definido com base em condies padronizadas por categoria de crdito. Desta forma, os movimentos do prmio de custo dependero das alteraes do Rating do Pas, do Rcio do Crdito em Incumprimento, do Rcio de Crdito Saneado e do Coeficiente de Reservas Obrigatrias para Passivos em Moeda Nacional. Por outro lado, o spread de crdito a ser divulgado por cada instituio de crdito ser baseado num conjunto de critrios padronizados pela indstria bancria, dando espao ao cliente para melhor negociar e decidir sobre as condies de acesso ao financiamento bancrio. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Apesar destas vantagens, estamos conscientes de que o acordo que acabamos de assinar no  ainda um produto perfeito e acabado. H aspectos que deveremos continuar a aprimorar ao longo do processo de implementao, da que tenhamos acordado em realizar melhorias e revises aos seus termos, de tempos em tempos. Entendemos que o maior desafio, como em qualquer acordo, est na sua correcta implementao, pelo que apelamos a todos os intervenientes para o cumprimento rigoroso deste acordo, com profissionalismo, honestidade, transparncia e, acima de tudo, de forma didctica. Termino a minha interveno prestando um agradecimento especial s equipas tcnicas conjuntas da Associao Moambicana de Bancos, das instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras e do Banco de Moambique, que trabalharam afincadamente para a materializao do presente acordo. Muito obrigado pela ateno!

Title: Speech at the Signing of the New Agreement on the Single Benchmark of the Mozambican Banking System
text: 19 TO 21 SEPTEMBER 2018 MAPUTO - MOZAMBIQUE Representatives of the Central Banks of the Community of Portuguese Language Ladies and gentlemen of the Board of Administration of the Bench of Mozambique Tables of the Bank of Mozambique, Distinguished guests, Ladies, Gentlemen, Very good morning! 19 TO 21 SEPTEMBER 2018 MAPUTO - MOZAMBIQUE It is with great honor and great satisfaction that, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, I greet all present at the 5th Meeting of Supervision of the Central Banks of portuguese-speaking countries, addressing our welcome wishes to Maputo, our capital city. To the illustrious representatives who visit us for the first time, I am pleased to share with you that Mozambique has some of the best seafood delights you can find in the world, so I recommend that in the intervals of the works enjoy our cuisine and the beauty that the city offers. For the Bank of Mozambique, hosting an event of such importance in our country, and in particular in our capital city, is a great pride. I take this opportunity to express our thanks for the preference. 19 TO 21 SEPTEMBER 2018 MAPUTO - MOZAMBIQUE Distinguished guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, This meeting takes place in a context of recovery of our economy, in which the main economic indicators show signs of returning to normality, after a troubled period, between 2014 and 2016. Thanks to monetary and fiscal policy measures, we are pleased to share that economic activity has improved its performance and is increasingly diversified, although still below its potential, with gross domestic product growing by 3.7% in 2017 and 3.4% in the first half of this year. 19 TO 21 SEPTEMBER 2018 MAPUTO - MOZAMBIQUE Inflation, the primary objective of our monetary policy, has receded below 5% in the last eight months; our international reserves have recovered for about 7 months of import coverage; The Metical exchange rate against the Dollar stabilized at around 60 meticais, after reaching 80 meticais in 2016; and our financial sector remains solid and robust, contributing about 6% of gross domestic product. At the level of the financial system, in 2017 the Bank of Mozambique took action to strengthen the existing regulatory framework, ensure greater robustness of the financial system and raise the level of transparency of the financial system, including the increase in the share capital of banks, from 70,000 to 1,700,000 thousand meticais, and the solvency ratio of banks, from 8% to a minimum of 12%. 19 TO 21 SEPTEMBER 2018 MAPUTO - MOZAMBIQUE Currently, our banking system is composed of 19 banks, all under the supervision of the Bank of Mozambique, and 70.3% of their share capital is held by foreign financial groups. The existence of foreign financial groups in Mozambique contributes, on the one hand, to increased competition, diversity and availability of financial products, and, on the other hand, to the development of industry in terms of technology, products and services provided, as well as to integration into the global economy. In the meantime, we are aware that the strong presence of these foreign groups also has implications for banking regulation and supervision, and discussion of issues such as 'cross-border supervision' is inevitable. 19 TO 21 SEPTEMBER 2018 MAPUTO - MOZAMBIQUE In the Mozambican legal framework, cross-border supervision is a reality consisting of the establishment of memoranda of understanding, participation in the colleges of supervisors, joint inspections with other central banks, as well as the holding of events of this nature. Another topical issue of great interest to supervisors is cybersecurity, a challenge that arises from the rapid technological evolution and globalization of the economy, recorded in recent decades. It is therefore relevant to establish a cyber risk governance structure at the level of regulatory and supervisory authorities with the purpose of ensuring the establishment of a resilient cybersecurity environment. 19 TO 21 SEPTEMBER 2018 MAPUTO - MOZAMBIQUE It is our expectation that these and other topics will be addressed and discussed in a frank and open way at this meeting, and that here are also shared essential tools that supervisors need to fulfill their function of regulating and supervising the financial system. Moreover, it is already a tradition that the CPLP Central Bank Supervision Meeting should be a forum for interaction between the supervisors of our community, enhancing the commitment to cooperation and contributing to the harmonisation of working methodologies and the measurement of common risks, so we hope that this meeting will not escape the rule. 19 TO 21 SEPTEMBER 2018 MAPUTO - MOZAMBIQUE Thus, it is with high honor that I declare open the 5th Meeting of Supervision of the Central Banks of the CPLP, reiterating the wishes of a fruitful discussion! Thank you for your attention!

Title: Speech at the New Year's Toast with the National Financial System
text: INTERVENTION OF YOUR EXCELENCEROG83RIO ZANDAMELA, GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE ON THE OCCASION OF THE TOAST ALRELATED TO THE END OF THE ECONOMIC YEAR LOCAL: SILO AUTO Maputo, 21 December 2018 Mr. Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Your Excellency, Mr. Administrators of the Bank of Mozambique, Your Excellency, Representatives of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, Dear Managers of the Bank of Mozambique, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Women Gentlemen, very good afternoon! It is with high honor that, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, I greet all those present at this traditional meeting for the year-end toast with the national financial system. I extend our greetings to all our partners, including government institutions, credit institutions and financial corporations, economic and socio-professional associations, the academic community, international cooperation partners and the media. As usual, on this occasion we carry out a preliminary assessment of the year about to end and present our prospects for the coming new year. It should be mentioned that our assessment of the 2018 economic situation does not differ much from the balance sheet we have recently made at the opening of our Advisory Board in the city of Quelimane, since there we have not made significant changes there. Ladies, gentlemen, the economic situation of 2018 was marked by the consolidation of macroeconomic stability that began in 2017, after the strong measures taken in 2016. Indeed, inflation, the main objective of our monetary policy, has stabilized at levels below five per cent throughout the year. It was on the basis of these results and our expectations about the future behaviour of this indicator that our monetary policy in 2018 was geared towards the reduction of interest rates, a stimulus factor for economic activity in general, and for our small and medium-sized enterprises in particular. The fall in the reference interest rate, the MIMO rate, which occurred five times over the course of this year, totalling 525 basis points, to the current level of 14.25%, was aimed at signalling to commercial banks that the economy is in a position to reduce the credit interest rates granted to its customers. In this respect, we are working with the Mozambican Association of Banks and commercial banks to further improve the mechanism for determining credit interest rates, materialized with the signing of the indexing agreement in 2017, subsequently reinforced this year with the signing of an added product. We are certain that the current stance of lowering interest rates in the context of monetary policy management has contributed to economic activity maintaining some momentum, although gross domestic product continues to grow moderately and below its potential. Specifically, by the third quarter of 2018, GDP grew by 3.2 percent, about twice as much as the increase recorded in the same quarter last year. This year's economic growth was determined by the positive performance of the mining , agriculture, trade and services, fisheries and manufacturing sectors, unlike last year, which depended only on the mining sector. 0 return on the stability of our economy has been promoting greater demand for imports, which until September this year increased compared to the same period of 2017 by 730 million exports increased by approximately US 410 million. In 2018, our performance in the foreign exchange market was to carry out specific interventions to meet fuel import needs and correct excessive exchange rate volatility. The balance of gross international reserves remained above US3 trillion, enough to cover about 7 months of imports of goods and services. In turn, metical's exchange rate against the currencies of our main partners, especially the U.S. dollar, remained generally stable throughout the year, around 60 meticais, with some moments of volatility at the beginning of the year and part of the third quarter. As far as the financial sector is concerned, we have been working continuously, in collaboration with commercial banks, to ensure their stability and soundness. We introduced the liquidity ratio and continued to monitor the implementation of the quarterly publication measure by commercial banks to report on solvency and liquidity levels. From this monitoring we can see that our financial system remains solid, healthy and adequately capitalized, although the average of the unnormal credit exceeds 12 percent in the last six months. In relation to our financial relationship with abroad, between 2015 and 2017 we registered significant losses of business counterparties in the relationship with the corresponding banks. This situation was caused, among other things, by the sharp increase in the country's risk in the international market, and by the perception of business partners that the Bank of Mozambique itself was part of the problem, which put the country at high risk of exclusion from the international payment system. However, from 2017, with the notorious resumption of macro-financial stability associated with the reforms implemented by the Bank of Mozambique and the Government, it was possible to gradually recover a considerable part of the counterparts of business with the corresponding banks, in an environment of continuity of internal reforms and deepening of the association with international good practices in the field. Ladies and gentlemen, as part of the implementation of the Financial Sector Development Strategy, we have been working to modernise our payment system and improve levels of financial inclusion in the country. In this sphere, we have very recently faced a crisis that has affected our payment system in the components of electronic transactions carried out using bank cards, ATMand and mobile accounts, negatively affecting thousands of bank customers, especially those outside the country. An interim solution is already in implementation, while the definitive solution is being developed by a new provider, EURONET, with which we signed a contract on the 10th of this month for the licensing, implementation and maintenance of a computer system for interbank electronic payments. Our expectation is that the new provider, given its size, experience and international exposure, will offer quality services and meeting the needs of our payment system, with the support and cooperation of all of us. Distinguished Guests, Ladies Gentlemen, the positive results achieved in 2018 fuel our short- and medium-term expectations of a significant improvement in the country's economic climate. For 2019, we will calibrate monetary and exchange rate policy instruments so that inflation is around single digits. We will maintain our commitment to the flexible exchange rate regime, which will serve as an adjustment for unexpected exchange shocks, and interventions may occur to correct excessive and undesirable volatility. At the level of the financial sector, we will remain vigilant to ensure that institutions continue to comply with international good practice and strictly comply with the recommendations and standards emanating from our institution. As for the national payment system, we will continue to implement the legislation in force aimed at the effective materialisation of the single payment network, with a view to reducing transaction costs for bank customers, thereby improving financial inclusion rates. Our research will be focused on topics related to natural resources. It is in this context that in March we will organise, in partnership with the International Monetary Fund, a high-level international seminar on "Sovereign Wealth Funds", and our annual Scientific Days scheduled for June will also deal with the same theme. We are aware that the realisation of these objectives will depend not only on the action of the Bank of Mozambique, and I therefore call for the contribution and participation of all our partners - the financial system, companies and the government - as well as the general public. Distinguished guests, Ladies, ladies and gentlemen, allow me to conclude my speech by thanking everyone for their presence and making my wishes for happy feasts and a prosperous 2019 for all of you and your esteemed families! Thank you so much for your attention!

Foi na base desses resultados e das nossas expectativas sobre o comportamento futuro deste indicador que a nossa poltica monetria em 2018 foi orientada para a reduo das taxas de juro, factor de estmulo  actividade econmica em geral, e para as nossas pequenas e mdias empresas em particular. A queda da taxa de juro de referncia, a taxa MIMO, que ocorreu por cinco vezes ao longo do presente ano, numa magnitude total de 525 pontos base, para o nvel actual de 14,25%, visava sinalizar aos bancos comerciais que a economia apresenta condies para a reduo das taxas de juro de crdito concedido aos seus clientes. Nesta matria, estamos a trabalhar com a Associao Moambicana de Bancos e os bancos comerciais, para continuar a aperfeioar o mecanismo de determinao das taxas de juro de crdito, materializado com a assinatura do acordo sobre o indexante, em 2017, posteriormente reforado no presente ano com a assinatura de uma adenda. Estamos certos de que a actual postura de reduo das taxas de juro, no mbito da gesto da poltica monetria, tem contribudo para que a actividade econmica mantenha algum dinamismo, embora o Produto Interno Bruto continue a crescer de forma moderada e abaixo do seu potencial. Concretamente, at ao terceiro trimestre de 2018, o PIB cresceu em 3,2 por cento, cerca de duas vezes mais o aumento registado no trimestre homlogo do ano passado. 0 crescimento econmico deste ano foi determinado pelo desempenho positivo dos sectores de extraco mineira, agricultura, comrcio e servios, pesca e indstria transformadora, contrariamente ao do ano passado, que dependia apenas do sector de extraco mineira. 0 retorno da estabilidade da nossa economia tem estado a promover uma maior procura por importaes, que at Setembro deste ano aumentaram em relao ao perodo homlogo de 2017 em 730 milhes de dlares, tendo as nossas exportaes aumentado em aproximadamente 410 milhes de dlares. Em 2018, a nossa actuao no mercado cambial foi no sentido de realizar intervenes pontuais para suprir as necessidades de importao de combustvel e corrigir a volatilidade excessiva da taxa de cmbio. 0 saldo das reservas internacionais brutas manteve-se acima de 3 bilies de dlares, o suficiente para cobrir cerca de 7 meses de importaes de bens e servios. Por seu turno, a taxa de cmbio do Metical em relao s moedas dos nossos principais parceiros, com destaque para o dlar norte- americano, manteve-se em geral estvel ao longo do ano, em torno de 60 meticais, com registo de alguns momentos de uma certa volatilidade no incio do ano e numa parte do terceiro trimestre. No que diz respeito ao sector financeiro, temos estado a trabalhar continuamente, em colaborao com os bancos comerciais, para garantir a sua estabilidade e solidez. Introduzimos o rcio de liquidez e continumos a monitorar a implementao da medida de publicao trimestral, por parte dos bancos comerciais, de informao sobre os nveis de solvabilidade e de liquidez. Dessa monitoria podemos constatar que o nosso sistema financeiro continua slido, saudvel e adequadamente capitalizado, apesar de o crdito malparado, em mdia, superar os 12 por cento, nos ltimos seis meses. Em relao ao nosso relacionamento financeiro com o exterior, entre 2015 e 2017 registmos perdas significativas de contrapartes de negcios na relao com os bancos correspondentes. Tal situao foi causada, de entre outros aspectos, pelo aumento acentuado do risco pas no mercado internacional, e pela percepo dos parceiros de negcios de que o prprio Banco de Moambique era parte do problema, o que colocou o pas sob elevado risco de excluso do sistema de pagamentos internacional. Porm, a partir de 2017, com a retoma notria da estabilidade macrofinanceira associada s reformas implementadas pelo Banco de Moambique e pelo Governo, foi possvel recuperar gradualmente parte considervel de contrapartes de negcios com os bancos correspondentes, num ambiente de continuidade de reformas internas e aprofundamento da adeso s boas prticas internacionais na matria. Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, No mbito da implementao da Estratgia de Desenvolvimento do Sector Financeiro, temos vindo a trabalhar para modernizar o nosso sistema de pagamentos e melhorar os nveis de incluso financeira no pas. Nesta esfera, enfrentmos muito recentemente uma crise que afectou o nosso sistema de pagamentos, nas componentes de transaces electrnicas efectuadas com recurso aos cartes bancrios, ATM e contas mveis, afectando negativamente milhares de clientes bancrios, principalmente os que se encontravam fora do pas. Uma soluo provisria j est em implementao, enquanto a definitiva est sendo desenvolvida por uma nova provedora, a EURONET, com que assinmos um contrato no dia 10 do corrente ms para o licenciamento, implementao e manuteno de um sistema informtico para pagamentos electrnicos interbancrios. A nossa expectativa  de que o novo provedor, dada a sua dimenso, experincia e exposio internacional, ir oferecer servios de qualidade e  altura das necessidades do nosso sistema de pagamentos, com o apoio e cooperao de todos ns. Ilustres Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Os resultados positivos alcanados em 2018 alimentam as nossas expectativas de curto e mdio prazos, de uma melhoria significativa da conjuntura econmica do pas. Para 2019, calibraremos os instrumentos de poltica monetria e cambial para que a inflao se situe em torno de um dgito. Manteremos o nosso compromisso com o regime de taxa de cmbio flexvel, que servir de ajuste para os choques cambiais no esperados, podendo ocorrer intervenes para corrigir a volatilidade excessiva e indesejvel. Ao nvel do sector financeiro, continuaremos vigilantes para garantir que as instituies continuem a observar as boas prticas internacionais e cumpram rigorosamente as recomendaes e normas emanadas pela nossa instituio. Quanto ao sistema nacional de pagamentos, continuaremos a implementar a legislao em vigor visando a materializao efectiva da rede nica de pagamentos, tendo em vista a reduo dos custos das transaces para os clientes bancrios, melhorando assim os ndices de incluso financeira. A nossa pesquisa estar orientada para temas relacionados com os recursos naturais.  neste contexto que, em Maro, vamos organizar, em parceria com o Fundo Monetrio Internacional, um seminrio internacional de alto nvel sobre Fundos Soberanos, e as nossas Jornadas Cientficas anuais agendadas para Junho versaro tambm sobre a mesma temtica. Estamos conscientes de que a materializao desses objectivos depender no apenas da aco do Banco de Moambique, pelo que apelo  contribuio e participao de todos os nossos parceiros - o sistema financeiro, as empresas e o Governo -, bem como do pblico em geral. Muito obrigado pela ateno!

Title: Speech at the Opening of the Workshop on "The Use of Financial Investigations and Intelligence in Countering Wildlife Trafficking"
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENCY THE GOVERNOR OF THE BANK OF MOZAMBIQUE, Dr. ROGeRIO ZANDAMELA POR OCASIaO DA ABERTURA DO WORKSHOP SOBRE THE USE OF FINANCIALINVESTIGATIONS AND INTELLIGENCE IN COUNTERING WILDLIFETRAFFICKING MAPUTO, March 4, 2019 Expensive participants, Distinguished guests, Ladies Gentlemen Very good morning! It is with high honor that, on behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, I greet all present at this seminar on the use of financial research and intelligence in combating the trafficking of wild flora and fauna. First of all, I would like to express our deep thanks to the organisers, in particular the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), for the honorable invitation that has been addressed to us to deliver this opening speech. The topic under discussion is of great interest to the Bank of Mozambique, and our presence today symbolizes precisely the relevance we give to the topic. Distinguished guests, Ladies and gentlemen, The illicit trade in wild flora and fauna is increasingly recognized as a form of international organized crime, generating billions of dollars in profits for smuggling syndicates. The financial flows of this crime end up flowing into the financial system through increasingly sophisticated money laundering and corruption schemes, which require equally sophisticated forms of combat. For African countries, which are still struggling with serious budget problems, the illicit trade in wild flora and fauna represents a major loss of revenue. This loss occurs mainly because the main tourist attractions are decimated, and large amounts of wood is transacted without tax considerations to the state. Ladies, and Gentlemen More than listing the problems, the most important thing at this stage is to take action to combat this illicit trade, increasingly sophisticated the techniques of our investigation. We understand that combating this type of crime, because it involves a sophisticated transnational modus operandi , necessarily involves international cooperation, involving multiple agencies and tracking the entire supply chain. In the current era of information technologies, the involvement of the financial sector in the investigation of such crimes is crucial because it allows the financial flows arising from these transactions to be traced. By following the "money path," financial institutions can help map criminal networks and provide law enforcement and law enforcement officials with the information they can provide to support investigations. In each nation, the fight involves recognizing the problem and committed to the cause, strengthening communication between public security agencies and fighting corruption. This means that the authorities involved in combating illicit trade should not act as islands, as cooperation with other institutions and the promotion of joint investigations involving law enforcement and order agents, customs, financial investigation units and financial institutions are essential. In this context, it is important to note that the Government of Mozambique is committed to the cause, being part of the signatories of the London Conference on combating the illicit trade in wild flora and fauna, held in October 2018. As part of our actions, as regulators of the financial system, we have been relentless in implementing severe measures against violations of money laundering law as a way of educating and discouraging the use of the financial system for illicit transactions. In this process, we have maintained healthy cooperation and coordination with other government institutions, namely our financial intelligence unit, the GIFiM. Distinguished guests, Our expectation is that the information that will be shared in this workshop and the exchange of experiences that will follow it are important ingredients for a frank debate among the participants, resulting in concrete solutions to this problem. Let me end my speech by renewing our thanks for the invitation and reiterating the Bank of Mozambique's commitment to combating illicit trade, given its implications for the financial system. Thank you very much!

Title: Intervention at the Opening of the Seminar "Preparing Mozambique for the Era of Natural Gas"

text: Minister for Economy and Finance , Excellency Former Governors of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellencies Mr. Vice-President, African Development Bank , Excellence Honourable Members of the Diplomatic Corps, Your Honours, Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, DignissimosAntigosAdministradoresdoBanco de Mocambique, Your Excellese representatives of public institutions, Distinguished Representatives of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations , Representatives of Academic Institutions and Research Centres , Dear Directors,ManagersandTechnicians of the Bank of Mozambique, Distinguished Guests, Ladies, Gentlemen , Very good morning! It is with great satisfaction that, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, I greet all those present at this eleventh edition of the "Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique", an event that usually takes place in June of each year in week of the Celebration of Metical Day. Let me begin my speech by expressing special thanks to Dr. Matthew Magala, Vice-President of the African Development Bank, for having welcomed and without reservation the invitation to him we have formulated to be the Main Speaker of this edition of scientific days, even in the face of an overly populated agenda. In the same way, I would like to thank Dr. Ibraimo Mussagy, professor at the Catholic University of Beira, for having led with professionalism, rigor, exemption and engagement the independent team that evaluated the works that will be presented here, which includes as vowels Dr. Faizal Carsane and Dr. Luis Quepe. This event would not have materialized without the delivery and professionalism of our organizing team. So I express my thanks to all the members of the organisation, as well as to all those who have directly and indirectly contributed to the implementation of this edition. Ladies , gentlemen , For this edition, the Scientific Days are " Sovereign Funds in Mozambique : Opportunities and Challenges". From the Perspective of the Bank of Mozambique, this reflection is of great importance and timeliness for the country, given that we are moving in great strides towards the start of the exploitation of non- with a focus on natural gas. It was in this spirit that we organised, between 27 and 28 March 2019, in partnership with the International Monetary Fund, the first International High Level Seminar on the same subject. From that seminar, there was a consensus among the participants, namely that there is a need to establish a sovereign wealth fund in Mozambique in anticipation of natural gas exploration revenues, and by deepening the technical details for this purpose. The present Scientific Days are thus an opportunity to share technical and scientific knowledge, in order to better respond to the challenges inherent in the process of creating a fund for the management of revenues of resources, definition of their objectives and governance structure, establishment of mechanisms for supervision and supervision, delineation of borders of responsibilities between stakeholders, among others. The independent jury has selected for debate three research papers that will be presented here, from a universe of 22 (twenty-two) proposals submitted. Despite the different approaches followed by the authors, the results converge on the need to create a sustainable revenue management mechanism exploitation of non-renewable resources and their vital importance for achieving the country's inclusive and social development, differing only in the time horizons of its implementation. Given the relevance of the theme and the heterogeneity of the profiles of participants present here, we are confident that we will have an open, frank and fruitful debate, and that, like previous editions, we will share knowledge and experiences that contribute to the formulation of appropriate policies, ultimately aiming to boost the country's economic development. Thus, I declare open the Eleventh Scientific Days of the Bank of Mozambique. Thank you so much for your attention!

O Jri independente seleccionou para debate trs trabalhos de pesquisa que sero aqui apresentados, de um universo de 22 (vinte e duas) propostas submetidas. No obstante as diferentes abordagens seguidas pelos autores, os resultados convergem para a necessidade de criao de um mecanismo sustentvel de gesto das receitas de explorao de recursos no renovveis e a sua importncia vital para o alcance do desenvolvimento inclusivo e social do pas, diferindo apenas nos horizontes temporais da sua implementao. Tendo em conta a relevncia do tema e a heterogeneidade dos perfis de participantes aqui presentes, estamos confiantes de que teremos um debate aberto, franco e profcuo, e que,  semelhana das edies anteriores, partilharemos conhecimentos e experincias que iro contribuir para a formulao de polticas adequadas, visando, em ltima instncia, impulsionar o desenvolvimento econmico do pas. Assim, declaro abertas as Dcimas Primeiras Jornadas Cientficas do Banco de Moambique. Muito obrigado pela ateno!

Title: Intervention at the Opening of the Evaluation Seminar of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy (ENIF)
text: Your Excellere, Resident Director of the World Bank in Mozambique, Mr Deputy Executive Director of the Alliance for Financial Inclusion, Madam President of the Insurance Supervision Institute of Mozambique, Your Excellere, Administrator of the Bank of Mozambique, Honourable Representatives of national and international financial institutions, associations and cooperation partners, and other members of the National Committee for Financial Inclusion, Distinguished guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, On behalf of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, I would like to greet all present and welcome the opening of the World Bank Mission and the Alliance for Financial Inclusion (AFI), which is now taking place and which is intended to be a time of medium-term evaluation of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2016-2022. With this assessment, we will have the opportunity to check the progress made, present the necessary recommendations and set priorities for the second phase of implementation for the period 2019 to 2022. As is known to all present, the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion was approved and disseminated in 2016 by the Mozambican Government, having benefited from contributions from the various entities represented here. The main objective of this strategy is to provide a structured approach to the establishment, on the one hand, of priority policies and actions, and, on the other hand, of monitoring, evaluation and coordination mechanisms between the various actors, with a view to making significant progress in the construction of a financially included company in Mozambique. Ladies and gentlemen , The National Financial Inclusion Strategy sets out the following goals to be highlighted:  By 2018 and 2022, 40% and 60% of the adult population, respectively, with physical or electronic access to financial services provided by a financial institution;  By 2018 and 2022, 75% and 100% of the country's districts, respectively, covered by at least one access point to formal financial services; and  By 2018 and 2022, 55% and 75% of the Mozambican population, respectively, with at least one access point services less than 5 km from the place of residence or work. In the objectives recommended in the Strategy , several actions have been implemented and in progress, with emphasis on the following actions , at the level of the financial sector:  establishing a legal and regulatory framework for the protection of the financial consumer, through either a code of conduct for credit institutions and financial corporations, and advertising financial products and services;  establishment of a legal and regulatory framework for the development of the activity implemented by electronic money institutions, money remittance operators and financial technology institutions, including fintechs;  establishing a legal and regulatory framework for the operationalisation of simplified bank accounts;  establishing a regulatory framework for the expansion of simplified microinsurance products;  Creation of an incubator for fintechs, launched in May 2018, a space where financial technology institutions can develop and test their ideas for a financially included company; and  Start of the capture and compilation of data on access to financial services, through a georeferenced platform for mapping financial services;  Development of microinsurance products oriented to MSMEs, farmers, mukheristas, market sellers and low-income population. Ladies, gentlemen , The implementation of the actions just mentioned led to the improvement of financial inclusion indicators, with emphasis on the following:  the achievement of a level of economy banking of 32.7% and an adult population level with electronic money accounts of 51.3% in 2018, against 25.1% and 23.1% in 2015, respectively;  64% of the country's districts covered with at least one access point to financial services, compared to 58% in 2015;  The global financial inclusion index, an indicator that weights the levels of geographic, demographic and use of financial products and services stood at 14.5 points in 2018, against 14.7 in 2015 and 13.2 in 2011;  Of the 154 districts in the country, 65% have at least one bank branch, 84% have at least one electronic money and POS institution, 59% of districts have at least one ATM and 24% of districts have at least one point of contact with an insurance institution;  The insurance market has now been responsible for a production level of around 13 trillion meticais in gross premiums issued, corresponding to an insurance penetration rate in the economy of around 1.5%;  The country had a stock market capitalization index of 8.6% of GDP in 2018, compared to 7.8% in 2015. Ladies, gentlemen , It is in this context that today, three years after the launch and implementation of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, we have come together to begin the medium-term evaluation process for the period 2016-2018, which is an opportunity to reflect on on the progress made in this period and to jointly identify the challenges and opportunities to achieve the goals we propose to achieve by the year 2022. To this end, we count on this Mission, in addition to the representatives of the World Bank and the Alliance for with representatives of the central banks of Ghana and Uganda, countries with experience in deviseing financial inclusion policies and will support the ongoing Strategy evaluation process. Thus, convinced that the exchange of experiences and knowledge, as well as the frank and open debate during this Mission, could contribute to the achievement of the objectives of improving financial inclusion in our country, I have the honour of declare open the Mission for evaluation of the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion 2016-2022. Thank you very much, thank you very much. Maputo, 08 July 2019
text_original: Excelentssimo Senhor Director Residente do Banco Mundial em Moambique, Excelentssimo Senhor Director Executivo Adjunto da Aliana para a Incluso Financeira, Excelentssima Senhora Presidente do Instituto de Superviso de Seguros de Moambique, Excelentssima Senhora Administradora do Banco de Moambique, Dignssimos Senhores representantes de instituies financeiras, de associaes e parceiros de cooperao nacionais e internacionais, e demais membros do Comit Nacional de Incluso Financeira, Distintos convidados, Minhas Senhoras, e Meus Senhores, Em nome do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome, quero saudar a todos os presentes e dar as boas-vindas  abertura da Misso do Banco Mundial e da Aliana para a Incluso Financeira (AFI), que tem hoje lugar e que se pretende seja um momento de avaliao de mdio prazo da Estratgia Nacional de Incluso Financeira 2016-2022. Minhas Senhoras, Meus senhores, A implementao das aces acabadas de referir conduziram  melhoria dos indicadores de incluso financeira, com destaque para os seguintes:  O alcance de um nvel de bancarizao da economia de 32,7% e um nvel de populao adulta com contas de moeda electrnica de 51,3%, em 2018, contra 25.1% e 23,1% em 2015, respectivamente;  64% dos distritos do pas cobertos com pelo menos um ponto de acesso aos servios financeiros, contra 58% em 2015;  O ndice de incluso financeira global, indicador que pondera os nveis de acesso geogrfico, demogrfico e utilizao dos produtos e servios financeiros situou-se em 14,5 pontos em 2018, contra 14,7 em 2015 e 13,2 em 2011;  Dos 154 distritos existentes no pas, 65% possuem pelo menos uma agncia bancria, 84% possuem pelo menos uma instituio de moeda electrnica e POS, 59% dos distritos possuem pelo menos um ATM e 24% dos distritos possuem pelo menos um ponto de contacto com uma instituio seguradora;  O mercado segurador passou a ser responsvel por um nvel de produo de cerca de 13 bilies de meticais em prmios brutos emitidos, o correspondente a uma taxa de penetrao dos seguros na economia de cerca de 1.5%;  O pas contou em 2018 com um ndice de capitalizao bolsista de 8,6% do PIB, contra 7,8% em 2015. Minhas Senhoras, Meus senhores,  neste contexto que hoje, passados trs anos desde o lanamento e implementao da Estratgia Nacional de Incluso Financeira, nos reunimos para dar incio ao processo de avaliao de mdio prazo referente ao perodo 2016-2018, sendo esta uma oportunidade para reflectirmos sobre os avanos realizados neste perodo e identificarmos de forma conjunta os desafios e oportunidades com vista ao alcance das metas que nos propomos alcanar at ao ano de 2022. Para o efeito, contamos, na presente Misso, para alm dos representantes do Banco Mundial e da Aliana para a Incluso Financeira, com representantes dos bancos centrais do Gana e Uganda, pases com experincia no desenho e implementao de polticas de incluso financeira e que iro apoiar no processo de avaliao da Estratgia ora em curso. Assim, convicto de que a troca de experincias e de conhecimentos, bem como o debate franco e aberto durante esta Misso, podero contribuir para o alcance dos objectivos de melhoria da incluso financeira no nosso pas, tenho a honra de declarar aberta a Misso para Avaliao da Estratgia Nacional de Incluso Financeira 2016-2022. Title: Intervention at the Inauguration of the Xai-Xai Branch
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENcy OGOVERNADORDO BANCO DE MO82AMBIQUE,Dr. ROG83RIO ZANDAMELA On THE OCCASION OF THE INAUGURATION OF THE DEXAI-XAI BRANCH XAI-XAI, August 8, 2019 Mr President of the Republic of Mozambique, Excellency Minister for Economy and Finance, Excellency Madam Governor of Gaza Province, Excellency Mr President of the Municipality of Xai-Xai, Excellency Madam President of the Xai-Xai Municipal Assembly, Excellency Mr. Vice-Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency Excellency, Honourable Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Distinguished Representatives of Credit Institutions and Financial Societies, Distinguished Guests, Ladies, Gentlemen, All Protocol Observed Very good morning! Firstly, On behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, I would like to thank you for your presence at this opening ceremony of the Bank of Mozambique Branch in the city of Xai-Xai, Gaza Province. Allow me to express special thanks to His Excellency the President of the Republic of Mozambique, Filipe Jacinto Nyusi, who honours us with his presence, despite his very busy agenda. My thanks extend to His Excellencies the Governor of Gaza Province, Stella Zeca, and the President of the Municipal Council of the city of Xai-Xai, Em92dio Xavier, for the collaboration shown by the institutions they lead, from the beginning of the implementation of this project to date, as well as to the Bank team, led by our Deputy Governor, Victor Gomes, who in collaboration with the Provincial Government of Gaza and the Municipal Council of Xai-Xai made this ceremony possible. I would also like to address my words of appreciation to all the technical team involved in the construction of this building, for the high level of commitment and dedication they have put into all the work leading up to this act, and so to all the citizens of Xai-Xai, who have patiently endured for about five years the constraints inherent in a work of this dimension. Ladies and gentlemen, the inauguration of this Branch is part of the actions that the Bank of Mozambique has been carrying out, with a view to expanding its physical presence throughout the national territory, in order to respond better and more effectively, on the one hand, to the concerns of economic agents, and, on the other, to respond better and more effectively, on the one hand, to the concerns of economic agents, and, on the other, to to the present and future challenges of our economy. Gaza province was, until today, one of two that did not yet have a branch of the Bank of Mozambique operating. Thus, with this inauguration we have taken another firm step in our purpose of being present in all the provinces of our vast country. The Branch that we inaugurate today will operate in a building built from scratch, with a modern and functional architecture that will give the city of Xai- Xai a new aspect and its urban configuration a greater value. Occupying a total area of 11,000 square meters, this building, which represents a heritage of all Mozambicans, was implanted with patterns of resilience to the effects of climate change, which cyclically affect our country, and in particular the city of Xai-Xai. It consists of two blocks with four floors each, which receive shared services, namely the public service desks, the auditorium, the clearing room, the library, the meeting rooms and the cafeteria. Additionally, it has two cellars, one for the treasury and the other for the car park, and is also equipped with a centralized technical management system, responsible for controlling the air conditioning process. I end my speech by making the hope that the citizens of Xai-Xai, in particular, will make the most of the presence of the Bank of Mozambique at this point in the country and contribute to the preservation of this building, our collective heritage. Thank you very much!

Title: End of the Economic Year 2019
text: INTERVENTION OF HIS EXCELLENCYROGeRIO ZANDAMELA, GOVERNOR OF BANCODE MOcAMBIQUE ON THE OCCASION OF THE TOAST ALRELATED TO THE END OF THE ECONOMIC YEAR Maputo, 16 December 2019 Mr. Deputy Governor of the Bank of Mozambique, Excellency Honourable, Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Honourable Representatives of Credit Institutions and Financial Corporations, Dear Managers of the Bank of Mozambique, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Women Gentlemen, very good afternoon! It is with high honor that, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, I greet all those present at this traditional meeting for the year-end toast with the national financial system. In particular, I greet all our partners, without whom it would not be possible to carry out our mission, namely government institutions, financial institutions, economic and socio-professional associations, the academic community, international cooperation partners and social communication. As usual, on this occasion we make a preliminary assessment of the year about to end and present our prospects for the next new year. Ladies, gentlemen, Very recently, at the opening of our Advisory Council which took place in the city of Xai-Xai, we had the opportunity to take stock of our performance. Our evaluation today will be no different from that presented at that time, so I will dispense with the details and focus on the most recent developments, starting with the characterization of the conjuncture. At the domestic level, the situation was characterized by the drop in the supply of goods and services resulting from tropical cyclones Idai and Kenneth, by the sharpness of military instability in the north and center regions of the country and by the increase in aggregate demand resulting from the holding of general elections on a larger scale. In the international context, we highlight the worsening trade tensions and geopolitical conflicts as well as the prolonged deadlock in discussions on the UK's withdrawal from the European Union, which have negatively affected commodity prices and the pattern of world trade. Ladies Gentlemen, it is in the face of this framework that we have implemented reforms and appropriate measures to strengthen macroeconomic stability and the financial system, of which I will highlight the following. In monetary and exchange rate policy, in view of the significant improvement in our inflation projections for the medium term, we have reduced the monetary policy interest rate twice from 14.25 per cent at the beginning of the year to the current 12.75 per cent. In addition, we have reduced the proportion of deposits in national currency that commercial banks are required to keep at the Bank of Mozambique for precautionary reasons, from 14 to 13 percent. However, in view of the worsening of external risks and aiming to give greater weight to Metical, we have increased the proportion of foreign currency deposits that banks are required to keep in the Bank of Mozambique, from 27 to 36 percent. In order to further strengthen the use of the national currency and protect citizens from potential foreign exchange losses, we have strengthened the prohibition of foreign currency payments in domestic transactions and established criteria for the movement of accounts in foreign currency. In the context of financial stability, we continued to monitor the activities of credit institutions and financial corporations through ordinary and sporadic inspections, including money laundering and terrorist financing. In order to improve transparency and competitiveness among credit institutions, we have introduced the obligation to provide information on their clients' deposits before and during their establishment, as well as the obligation to publish, quarterly, the information of their solvency levels liquidity. In the field of promoting financial inclusion, we have completed the tests and regulation of the first group of technology initiatives on the business maturation platform, also known as the sandbox, and, in collaboration with the actors of the financial system, we approved the rural banking project, which will allow the opening of accounts of 100,000 producers in the provinces of Niassa, Tete, Manica and Zambezia. We continued to implement and deepen reforms within our institution, highlighting the introduction of regulations that prevent the entry into the bank of direct family members, up to the fifth degree, of managers from the level of director. We continued to favor the opening of internal competitions for the provision of vacancies for management positions and we kept the promotion of external competitions transparent to fill vacancies for technicians. Distinguished Guests, Ladies, Ladies, Gentlemen, Our preliminary assessment of the impacts of the measures and reforms we implemented in 2019 is very positive, to be assessed by the good performance of the indicators under our purview. Inflation remained low and stable, around 2 per cent, in line with our single-digit medium-term target and substantially below the Southern African Development Community (SADC) convergence target of 3 to 7 per cent. International reserves increased to about 7 months of import coverage, a level comfortably above acceptable minimum standards of 3 months. The exchange rate remained relatively stable, and, in the current context of a flexible exchange rate regime, fluctuated in the band between 60 and 65 meticais per dollar. The solvency ratio of the banking system remained robust at around 25 per cent, well above the 12 per cent minimum set, against a background of a reduction in unsettled credit. Credit to the private sector expanded, after the contraction in 2018, with total credit growing in cumulative terms up to October, at 6 percent and credit in national currency increased around 11 percent. Ladies, gentlemen, for 2020, we remain committed to fighting inflation. Our outlook points to the continued price stability, which is based on stable inflation at single-digit levels, within the SADC convergence band, although relatively above this year's level. With regard to economic activity, we anticipate greater momentum in 2020, with gross domestic product accelerating to around 4 per cent. This forecast is based on post-cyclone reconstruction actions, the regularization of debts to suppliers of goods and services to the State, the increase in credit to the private sector and the boost of investment in the oil and gas sector. We will remain committed to the flexible exchange rate, so that we can absorb exogenous shocks, and we will consolidate reforms in the foreign exchange market, so that the exchange rate reflects the demand and supply of foreign exchange in the domestic market. In this context, we hope that our international reserves will remain at comfortable levels and may cover more than 5 months of imports of goods and services, excluding transactions from major projects. Also in 2020, we will implement a new interbank payment platform under the contract with Euronet, which will mark a turning point in Mozambique's history. The new infrastructure will be safer , stronger, with greater coverage of transactions and will allow greater interoperability across the financial system, including among electronic money institutions. Aware of the challenges posed by cybersecurity risks, we will work with financial institutions to create a 33 regulatory and supervisory framework that makes the industry increasingly resilient, starting with the meeting already scheduled for February 2020. We will conclude, in 2020, the technical work aimed at the implementation in our country of a transparent model for the management of revenues from mineral resources, also known as sovereign wealth fund. This technical work will result in a proposal that will serve as the basis for discussions at political level and with all actors, including civil society. At the level of interbank markets, after we have temporarily suspended transactions using long-term exchange rates in foreign currency purchase and sale operations, we will reopen the derivatives market segment, introducing appropriate legislation in line with the international experiences collected in order to allow the coverage of market risks, in particular foreign exchange, by banks and other actors in foreign exchange operations. Following the actions already initiated in recent years, in 2020 we will continue to strengthen the stability of our financial system and stimulate the expansion of financial services using new technologies, with a view to increasing the levels of access and use of financial services and products in the country. We also project, for 2020, a set of cultural, sporting and scientific activities alusive to the celebration of the forty-fifth anniversary of the Bank of Mozambique and the fortieth anniversary of the creation of metical. On this occasion, allow me to make the official launch of the festivities, appealing to the active participation of the entire financial system. We are aware that the materialisation of these objectives does not depend solely on the actions of the Bank of Mozambique, but above all on the collaboration and engagement of all our partners, namely the financial sector , the private sector , the government and the general public. Distinguished Guests, Ladies, Ladies and Gentlemen, I end my speech by thanking you all for your presence and expressing my wishes for happy feasts and a prosperous year 2020 for all of you and your esteemed families! For the attention paid, thank you very much! Maputo, 16 December 2019
text_original: INTERVENO DE SUA EXCELNCIA ROGRIO ZANDAMELA, GOVERNADOR DO BANCO DE MOAMBIQUE POR OCASIO DO BRINDE ALUSIVO AO ENCERRAMENTO DO ANO ECONMICO Maputo, 16 de Dezembro de 2019 Senhor Vice-Governador do Banco de Moambique, Excelncia Excelentssimos Senhores Administradores do Banco de Moambique, Excelentssimos Senhores Representantes de Instituies de Crdito e Sociedades Financeiras, Caros Gestores do Banco de Moambique, Distintos Convidados, Minhas Senhoras e Meus Senhores, Muito boa tarde!  com elevada honra que, em nome do Conselho de Administrao do Banco de Moambique e em meu nome, sado a todos os presentes neste tradicional encontro para o brinde de fim de ano com o sistema financeiro nacional. De forma especial, sado a todos os nossos parceiros, sem os quais no seria possvel realizarmos a nossa misso, nomeadamente, as instituies governamentais, as instituies financeiras, as associaes econmicas e socio- profissionais, a comunidade acadmica, os parceiros de cooperao internacional e a comunicaco social. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Muito recentemente, por ocasio da abertura do nosso Conselho Consultivo que teve lugar na cidade de Xai-Xai, tivemos a oportunidade de efectuar um balano da nossa actuaco. A nossa avaliao, hoje, no ser diferente daquela apresentada nessa altura, pelo que dispensarei os detalhes e privilegiarei os desenvolvimentos mais recentes, comeando pela caracterizao da conjuntura. Ao nvel domstico, a conjuntura foi caracterizada pela quebra da oferta de bens e servios resultante dos ciclones tropicais Idai e Kenneth, pela agudizao da instabilidade militar nas regies norte e centro do pas e pelo aumento da procura agregada decorrente da realizao de eleies gerais numa escala maior. Na conjuntura internacional, temos a destacar o agravamento das tenses comerciais e conflitos geopolticos bem como o impasse prolongado nas discusses sobre a retirada do Reino Unido da Unio Europeia, que afectaram negativamente os preos das mercadorias e o padro do comrcio mundial. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Foi perante este quadro que implementmos reformas e medidas adequadas, visando o reforo da estabilidade macroeconmica e do sistema financeiro, das quais irei destacar as que se seguem. No mbito da poltica monetria e cambial, em face da melhoria significativa das nossas projeces de inflao para o mdio prazo, reduzimos a taxa de juro de poltica monetria por duas vezes, passando de 14,25 por cento, no incio do ano, para os actuais 12,75 por cento. Adicionalmente, reduzimos a proporo dos depsitos em moeda nacional que os bancos comerciais so obrigados a manter no Banco de Moambique por motivos precaucionais, de 14 para 13 por cento. Entretanto, perante o agravamento dos riscos externos e visando conferir maior peso ao Metical, incrementmos a proporo dos depsitos em moeda estrangeira que os bancos so obrigados a manter no Banco de Moambique, de 27 para 36 por cento. Com o objectivo de fortalecer ainda mais o uso da moeda nacional e proteger os cidados de potenciais perdas cambiais, reformos a proibio de pagamentos em moeda estrangeira nas transacces domsticas e estabelecemos critrios para a movimentao das contas em moeda estrangeira. No mbito da estabilidade financeira, continumos a fazer a monitoria da actividade das instituies de crdito e sociedades financeiras atravs de inspeces ordinrias e espordicas, incluindo em matrias de branqueamento de capitais e financiamento do terrorismo. Visando melhorar a transparncia e a competitividade entre as instituies de crdito, introduzimos a obrigatoriedade de estas prestarem informao sobre os depsitos dos seus clientes, antes da sua constituio e durante a sua vigncia, bem como a obrigatoriedade de publicarem, trimestralmente, as informaes dos seus nveis de solvabilidade e liquidez. No domnio da promoo da incluso financeira, conclumos os testes e o regulamento do primeiro grupo de iniciativas tecnolgicas na plataforma de maturao de empresas, tambm conhecida como sandbox, e, em colaborao com os actores do sistema financeiro, aprovmos o projecto de bancarizao rural, que permitir a abertura de contas de 100 mil produtores nas provncias de Niassa, Tete, Manica e Zambzia. Continumos a implementar e a aprofundar reformas dentro da nossa instituio, sendo de destacar a introduo de normativos que impedem a entrada no banco de familiares directos, at ao quinto grau, de gestores a partir do nvel de director. Continumos a privilegiar a abertura de concursos internos para o provimento de vagas para cargos de gesto e mantivemos a promoo de concursos externos transparentes para o preenchimento de vagas para tcnicos. Distintos Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, A nossa avaliao preliminar dos impactos das medidas e reformas que implementmos em 2019  bastante positiva, a avaliar pelo bom desempenho dos indicadores sob a nossa alada. A inflao manteve-se baixa e estvel, em torno de 2 por cento, em linha com o nosso objectivo de mdio prazo de um dgito e, substancialmente, abaixo da meta de convergncia da Comunidade de Desenvolvimento da frica Austral (SADC), de 3 a 7 por cento. As reservas internacionais incrementaram para cerca de 7 meses de cobertura das importaes, nvel confortavelmente acima dos padres mnimos aceitveis, de 3 meses. A taxa de cmbio manteve-se relativamente estvel, tendo, no contexto actual de regime cambial flexvel, flutuado na banda entre 60 e 65 meticais por dlar. O rcio de solvabilidade do sistema bancrio manteve-se robusto, em torno de 25 por cento, bem acima do mnimo de 12 por cento estabelecido, num contexto de reduo do crdito malparado. O crdito ao sector privado expandiu, depois da contraco verificada em 2018, tendo o crdito total crescido, em termos acumulados at Outubro, em 6 por cento e o crdito em moeda nacional aumentado em torno de 11 por cento. Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Para 2020, mantemos o compromisso de combater a inflao. As nossas perspectivas apontam para a continuidade da estabilidade de preos, consubstanciada numa inflao estvel em nveis de um dgito, dentro da banda de convergncia da SADC, embora relativamente acima do nvel deste ano. Relativamente  actividade econmica, prevemos uma maior dinmica em 2020, podendo o produto interno bruto acelerar para cerca de 4 por cento. Esta previso  fundamentada pelas aces de reconstruo ps-ciclones, pela regularizao das dvidas aos fornecedores de bens e servios ao Estado, pelo incremento do crdito ao sector privado e pelo impulso do investimento no sector do petrleo e gs. Continuaremos comprometidos com o regime de cmbio flexvel, para termos capacidade de absorver os choques exgenos, e iremos consolidar as reformas no mercado cambial, de modo a que a taxa de cmbio reflicta a procura e oferta de divisas no mercado domstico. Neste quadro, perspectivamos que as nossas reservas internacionais permaneam em nveis confortveis, podendo cobrir acima de 5 meses de importaes de bens e servios, excluindo as transaces dos grandes projectos. Ainda em 2020, iremos implementar uma nova plataforma de pagamentos interbancrios ao abrigo do contrato com a Euronet, que marcar uma viragem na histria de Moambique. A nova infra-estrutura ser mais segura, slida, com maior cobertura de transaces e permitir maior interoperabilidade em todo o sistema financeiro, incluindo entre as instituies de moeda electrnica. Atentos aos desafios impostos pelos riscos de segurana ciberntica, iremos trabalhar com as instituies financeiras visando a criaco de um 3 3 quadro regulatrio e de superviso que torne a indstria cada vez mais resiliente, comeando com o encontro j agendado para Fevereiro de 2020. Iremos concluir, em 2020, os trabalhos tcnicos visando a implementao no nosso pas de um modelo transparente para a gesto das receitas provenientes dos recursos minerais, tambm conhecido por fundo soberano. Desses trabalhos tcnicos resultar uma proposta que servir de base para as discusses ao nvel poltico e com todos os intervenientes, incluindo a sociedade civil. Ao nvel dos mercados interbancrios, aps termos suspendido, temporariamente, as operaes com recurso a taxas de cmbio a prazo nas operaes de compra e venda de moeda estrangeira, iremos reabrir o segmento de mercado de derivativos, introduzindo legislao apropriada e em linha com as experincias internacionais recolhidas, de modo a permitir a cobertura de riscos de mercado, em particular o cambial, por parte dos bancos e demais intervenientes nas operaes cambiais. No seguimento das aces j iniciadas nos ltimos anos, em 2020 continuaremos a reforar a estabilidade do nosso sistema financeiro e a estimular a expanso dos servios financeiros com recurso s novas tecnologias, tendo em vista incrementar os nveis de acesso e uso dos servios e produtos financeiros no pas. Projectamos ainda, para 2020, um conjunto de actividades culturais, desportivas e cientficas alusivas  celebrao do quadragsimo quinto aniversrio do Banco de Moambique e ao quadragsimo aniversrio da criao do Metical. Nesta ocasio, permitam-me fazer o lanamento oficial das festividades, apelando  participao activa de todo o sistema financeiro. Estamos conscientes que a materializao destes objectivos no depende exclusivamente da actuao do Banco de Moambique, mas sobretudo da colaborao e engajamento de todos os nossos parceiros, nomeadamente, o sector financeiro, o sector privado, o Governo e o pblico em geral. Distintos Convidados, Minhas Senhoras, Meus Senhores, Termino a minha interveno agradecendo a presena de todos e manifestando os meus votos de festas felizes e um prspero ano de 2020 para todos Vs e as Vossas estimadas famlias! Pela ateno dispensada, muito obrigado! Maputo, 16 de Dezembro de 2019

Title: Intervention at the Official Launch Ceremony of the Georeferenced Mapping of Access Points to Financial Services
text: Your Excellere, Resident Director of the World Bank in Mozambique, Minister for Transport and Communications, Excellency Madam Deputy Minister for Economy and Finance, Excellency Madam Coordinator of the Space Development Program of the Ministry of Transport and Communications, Sir, Director-General of the Communications Regulatory Authority of Mozambique, Mr. President of the Mozambican Association of Banks, Your Excellese, Executive Director of the Financial Sector Deepening Mozambique, Honourable Members of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique, Presidents of the Boards of Directors and Executive Committees of financial institutions, Honourable Representatives of credit institutions and financial corporations , Distinguished Guests, Ladies, Gentlemen , Very good morning! Firstly, on behalf of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Mozambique and on my behalf, to greet all present and to welcome this Official Launch Ceremony of Georeferenced Mapping (GIS) of Access Points to Financial Services; This ceremony reflects the commitment of the country, and in particular of the Government , with the implementation of the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion 2016-2022, developed under the Financial Sector Development Strategy 2013-2022; This ceremony aims to officially launch the GIS mapping project of access points for the collection of data on financial services, as well as the presentation of the state of view of this collection with gis platform, started in 2018. Ladies, gentlemen, The GIS mapping of access points to financial services is part of Pillar 1 of the National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2016-2022, referring to the Access and Use of Financial Services; The main objective of this project is to improve the combined analysis capacity of access points to financial services with other socio-economic potential of the country provided by the platform. In addition, the project aims to contribute to improving the formulation and monitoring of public and private policies for the extension of financial activity to rural areas, and consequently increasing the levels of financial inclusion of the country; It should be noted that the implementation of this project is due to the effort made by the Ministry of Transport and Communications, to whom we extend our deep thanks for the training of the technicians of the Bank of Mozambique and representatives of financial institutions; This thanks extend to The FSDMoc and the World Bank for the support granted for the implementation of this project, and to representatives of the financial system, for their involvement in the data collection process , the results of which will be presented here. Dear guests , Ladies, Gentlemen, The Georeferenced Mapping Project, which today comes to an end, began in December 2017, when the Bank of Mozambique held the auscultation meeting to the financial sector and obtained consensus on the capture of georeferenced data to the same database; It was in this context that, on January 19, 2018, the Cooperation Protocol between the Bank of Mozambique and the Ministry of Transport and Communications was concluded through the Space Development Program. This protocol aimed to implement actions for mapping access points to financial services and products, using the Geographic Information System managed by the Ministry of Transport and Communications; We are very pleased to announce today that, in the context of the implementation of the Cooperation Protocol, the following actions have been implemented: In March 2018, the Ministry of Transport and Communications initiated the first phase of training actions in the use of the GIS platform, aimed at the financial system, namely banks, microbanks, credit unions and electronic money institutions; In August 2018, clarification sessions were held on the data collection process using GIS technology, where certificates were delivered and the Data Collection Manual. In November 2018, we witnessed the start of the capture of existing access points, including bank branches, microbanks and credit unions, bank agents, electronic money agents, ATM and POS; and In February 2019, the second phase of training actions was carried out with financial corporations and representatives of the Branches of the Bank of Mozambique, to support the process of capturing access to representations of exchange offices, savings and credit organizations, and microcredit operators. The capture of georeferenced information began shortly after the end of the formation. Distinguished guests, It is our understanding that the capture of access points to financial services for the same database can, on the one hand, contribute to the monitoring of the previously defined financial inclusion goals, and, on the other, serve as support in policy making and decision-making processes in matters of financial inclusion. It is in this context that the Bank of Mozambique intends to issue a Notice that provides for the mandatory mapping of access points to financial services, with a view to ensuring greater involvement of credit institutions and electronic money in the process. We are aware that the quality control of the data and information that feeds the GIS platform, including the timing factor, is a permanent and important challenge for us to maximise the potential that this platform offers us. It is our expectation that this ceremony will serve as a basis for greater awareness of the importance of this project and for the continuity of data collection at the level of financial institutions. We also hope to identify, through the results presented, potential solutions for the expansion of access points to financial services in the country, with a greater focus on rural areas. Finally, let me congratulate everyone present at this ceremony for their active participation in identifying solutions for the completion of this public utility project. Thank you very much! Maputo, 28 February 2020.
